conclude.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to decide or believe sth as a result of what you have heard or seen（断定；推断出；作出结论）；(formal) to come to an end; to bring sth to an end（（使）结束，终止）；(formal) to arrange and settle an agreement with sb formally and finally（达成，订立，缔结（协定））

conclusion.meaning: something that you decide when you have thought about all the information connected with the situation（结论；推论）；the end of sth such as a speech or a piece of writing（结束；结果；结尾；结局）；the formal and final arrangement of sth official（签订；达成；缔结）；to make a decision about sb/sth too quickly, before you know or have thought about all the facts（匆忙下结论；贸然断定）

conclusive.meaning: proving sth, and allowing no doubt or confusion（结论性的；不容置疑的；确凿的）；con·clu·sive·ly AW /kənˈkluːsɪvli; NAmEkənˈkluːsɪvli/ adv. to prove sth conclusively（确凿地证明某事）

concoct.meaning: to make sth, especially food or drink, by mixing different things（调制，调合，配制（尤指食物或饮料））；to invent a story, an excuse, etc.（虚构，杜撰，编造（故事、借口等））

concomitant.meaning: (formal) happening at the same time as sth else, especially because one thing is related to or causes the other（（尤指相关联的或有因果关系的事）同时发生的，伴随的，相伴的）；(formal) a thing that happens at the same time as sth else（同时发生的事；伴随（或相伴）的事物）

concrete.meaning: made of concrete（混凝土制的）；based on facts, not on ideas or guesses（确实的，具体的（而非想像或猜测的））；a concrete object is one that you can see and feel（有形的；实在的）；con·crete·ly /ˈkɒŋkriːtli; NAmEˈkɑːŋkriːtli/ adv. noun ★ [U] building material that is made by mixing together cement, sand, small stones and water（混凝土）

concurrence.meaning: agreement（同意；一致）；an example of two or more things happening at the same time（同时发生；同时出现）

concurrent.meaning: existing or happening at the same time（并存的；同时发生的）；con·cur·rent·ly AW /kənˈkʌrəntli; NAmEkənˈkɜːrəntli/ adv. The prison sentences will run concurrently.（所判的几个刑期合并执行。）

condemn.meaning: to express very strong disapproval of sb/sth, usually for moral reasons（（通常因道义上的原因而）谴责，指责）；to say what sb's punishment will be（宣判；判处（某人某种刑罚））；to force sb to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation（迫使 … 接受困境（或不愉快的状况））；to say officially that sth is not safe enough to be used（宣告使用 … 不安全）

condemnation.meaning: an expression of very strong disapproval（谴责；指责）

condensation.meaning: drops of water that form on a cold surface when warm water vapour becomes cool（凝结的水珠）；the process of a gas changing to a liquid（（气体）冷凝，凝结）；(formal) the process of making a book, etc. shorter by taking out anything that is not necessary（（书等的）简缩）

condense.meaning: to change from a gas into a liquid; to make a gas change into a liquid（（由气体）冷凝；（使气体）凝结）；if a liquid condenses or you condense it, it becomes thicker and stronger because it has lost some of its water（（使）浓缩，变浓，变稠）；to put sth such as a piece of writing into fewer words; to put a lot of information into a small space（简缩；压缩（文字、信息等））

condenser.meaning: a device that cools gas in order to change it into a liquid（冷凝器）；a device that receives or stores electricity, especially in a car engine（（尤指汽车发动机内的）电容器）

condition.meaning: the state that sth is in（状态；状况）；the state of sb's health or how fit they are（健康状况）；an illness or a medical problem that you have for a long time because it is not possible to cure it（（因不可能治愈而长期患有的）疾病）；the circumstances or situation in which people live, work or do things（（居住、工作或做事情的）环境，境况，条件）

conditional.meaning: depending on sth（附带条件的；依 … 而定的）；(grammar 语法) expressing sth that must happen or be true if another thing is to happen or be true（条件的）；con·di·tion·al·ly /kənˈdɪʃənəli; NAmEkənˈdɪʃənəli/ adv. The offer was made conditionally.（这个报价附有条件。）；a sentence or clause that begins with if or unless and expresses a condition（条件句，条件从句（由 if 或 unless 引导的））

conditioner.meaning: a liquid that makes hair soft and shiny after washing（护发剂；护发素）；a liquid, used after washing clothes, that makes them softer（（洗衣后用的）柔顺剂）

condolence.meaning: sympathy that you feel for sb when a person in their family or that they know well has died; an expression of this sympathy（吊唁；慰唁）

condor.meaning: a large bird of the vulture family, that lives mainly in S America（神鹰，大秃鹰（主要栖居在南美洲））

conducive.meaning: making it easy, possible or likely for sth to happen（使容易（或有可能）发生的）

conduct.meaning: (formal) to organize and/or do a particular activity（组织；安排；实施；执行）；to direct a group of people who are singing or playing music（指挥（歌唱或音乐演奏））；(formal) to lead or guide sb through or around a place（带领；引导；为（某人）导游）；(formal) to behave in a particular way（举止；表现）

conductance.meaning: the degree to which an object allows electricity or heat to pass through it（电导（率）；（热）传导性）

conduction.meaning: the process by which heat or electricity passes through a material（（热或电等能量的）传导）

conductor.meaning: a person who stands in front of an orchestra, a group of singers etc., and directs their performance, especially sb who does this as a profession（（管弦乐队、合唱队等的）指挥；职业指挥）；a person who is in charge of a train and travels with it, but does not drive it（列车长）；(BrE) a person whose job is to collect money from passengers on a bus or check their tickets（（公共汽车的）售票员）；(physics 物) a substance that allows electricity or heat to pass along it or through it（导体（导电或导热等的物质））

cone.meaning: a solid or hollow object with a round flat base and sides that slope up to a point（（实心或空心的）圆锥体）；a solid or hollow object that is shaped like a cone（（实心或空心的）圆锥形物）；a plastic object shaped like a cone and often red and white, or yellow, in colour, used on roads to show where vehicles are not allowed to go, for example while repairs are being done（锥形警告路标（常为红白色或红黄色的塑料锥形物，表示在维修道路等时禁止车辆通行））；a piece of thin crisp biscuit shaped like a cone, which you can put ice cream in to eat it（（盛冰淇淋的）锥形蛋卷筒）

confederacy.meaning: a union of states, groups of people or political parties with the same aim（联盟；同盟；联邦）

confederate.meaning: a person who helps sb, especially to do sth illegal or secret（同谋；同伙；从犯；共犯）；belonging to a confederacy（联盟的；同盟的；联邦的）

confer.meaning: to discuss sth with sb, in order to exchange opinions or get advice（商讨；协商；交换意见）；to give sb an award, a university degree or a particular honour or right（授予，颁发（奖项、学位、荣誉或权利））

conference.meaning: a large official meeting, usually lasting for a few days, at which people with the same work or interests come together to discuss their views（（通常持续几天的大型正式）会议，研讨会）；a meeting at which people have formal discussions（（正式）讨论会，商讨会）；(especially NAmE) a group of sports teams that play against each other in a league（体育协会（或联合会））

confess.meaning: to admit, especially formally or to the police, that you have done sth wrong or illegal（供认，坦白，承认（错误或罪行））；to admit sth that you feel ashamed or embarrassed about（承认（自己感到羞愧或尴尬的事））；(especially in the Roman Catholic Church（尤指罗马天主教会）；to tell God or a priest about the bad things you have done so that you can say that you are sorry and be forgiven（忏悔；悔过；告罪；告解）

confession.meaning: a statement that a person makes, admitting that they are guilty of a crime; the act of making such a statement（供词；供状；认罪；供认；坦白）；a statement admitting sth that you are ashamed or embarrassed about; the act of making such a statement（（对使自己羞愧或尴尬的事的）表白，承认）；(especially in the Roman Catholic Church（尤指罗马天主教会）；a private statement to a priest about the bad things that you have done（（向神父作的）告罪，告解）

confide.meaning: to tell sb secrets and personal information that you do not want other people to know（（向某人）吐露（秘密、隐私等））

confidence.meaning: the feeling that you can trust, believe in and be sure about the abilities or good qualities of sb/sth（信心；信任；信赖）；a belief in your own ability to do things and be successful（自信心）；the feeling that you are certain about sth（把握；肯定）；a feeling of trust that sb will keep information private（（对某人会保守秘密的）信任，信赖）

confident.meaning: feeling sure about your own ability to do things and be successful（自信的；有自信心的）；feeling certain that sth will happen in the way that you want or expect（肯定的；确信的；有把握的）

confidential.meaning: meant to be kept secret and not told to or shared with other people（机密的；保密的；秘密的）；(of a way of speaking（说话的方式）；showing that what you are saying is private or secret（隐密的；秘密的）；trusted with private or secret information（受信任的；委以机密的）

configuration.meaning: (formal or technical 术语) an arrangement of the parts of sth or a group of things; the form or shape that this arrangement produces（布局；结构；构造；格局；形状）；(computing 计) the equipment and programs that form a computer system and the way that these are set up to run（（计算机的）配置）

confine.meaning: to keep sb/sth inside the limits of a particular activity, subject, area, etc.（限制；限定）；to keep a person or an animal in a small or closed space（监禁；禁闭）；to have to stay in bed, in a wheelchair, etc.（使离不开（或受困于床、轮椅等））

confined.meaning: (of a space or an area（空间或地区）；small and surrounded by walls or sides（狭窄而围起来的）

confinement.meaning: the state of being forced to stay in a closed space, prison, etc., the act of putting sb there（禁闭；监禁；关押）；(formal or old-fashioned) the time when a woman gives birth to a baby（分娩；产期）

confirm.meaning: to state or show that sth is definitely true or correct, especially by providing evidence（（尤指提供证据来）证实，证明，确认）；to make sb feel or believe sth even more strongly（使感觉更强烈；使确信）；to make a position, an agreement, etc. more definite or official; to establish sb/sth firmly（批准（职位、协议等）；确认；认可）；to make sb a full member of the Christian Church（（给某人）施放坚振，施坚信礼）

confirmation.meaning: a statement, letter, etc. that shows that sth is true, correct or definite（证实；确认书；证明书）；a ceremony at which a person becomes a full member of the Christian Church（坚振；坚振礼；坚信礼）；a Jewish ceremony similar to a bar mitzvah or bat mitzvah but usually for young people over the age of 16（受戒礼（通常为 16 岁以上犹太年轻人举行的仪式））

conflate.meaning: (formal) to put two or more things together to make one new thing（合并；合成；混合）

conflict.meaning: a situation in which people, groups or countries are involved in a serious disagreement or argument（冲突；争执；争论）；a violent situation or period of fighting between two countries（（军事）冲突；战斗）；a situation in which there are opposing ideas, opinions, feelings or wishes; a situation in which it is difficult to choose（抵触；矛盾；不一致）；a situation in which sb has two jobs, aims, roles, etc. and cannot treat both of them equally and fairly at the same time（利益（或利害）冲突）

confluence.meaning: (technical 术语) the place where two rivers flow together and become one（（河流的）汇合处，汇流处，交汇处）；(formal) the fact of two or more things becoming one（（事物的）汇合，汇聚，汇集）

conform.meaning: to behave and think in the same way as most other people in a group or society（顺从，顺应（大多数人或社会）；随潮流）；to obey a rule, law, etc.（遵守，遵从，服从（规则、法律等））；to agree with or match sth（相一致；相符合；相吻合）

conformity.meaning: (formal) behaviour or actions that follow the accepted rules of society（（对社会规则的）遵从，遵守）；following the rules of sth; conforming to sth（遵循（规则）；与 … 相符合（或一致））

confront.meaning: (of problems or a difficult situation（问题或困境）；to appear and need to be dealt with by sb（使 … 无法回避；降临于）；to deal with a problem or difficult situation（处理，解决（问题或困境））；to face sb so that they cannot avoid seeing and hearing you, especially in an unfriendly or dangerous situation（面对；对抗；与（某人）对峙）

confrontation.meaning: a situation in which there is an angry disagreement between people or groups who have different opinions（对抗；对峙；冲突）

confucian.meaning: based on or believing the teachings of the Chinese philosopher Confucius（儒家的；儒学的；孔子学说的）

confuse.meaning: to make sb unable to think clearly or understand sth（使糊涂；使迷惑）；to think wrongly that sb/sth is sb/sth else（（将 … ）混淆，混同）；to make a subject more difficult to understand（使更难于理解）

confused.meaning: unable to think clearly or to understand what is happening or what sb is saying（糊涂的；迷惑的）；not clear or easy to understand（不清楚的；混乱的；难懂的）

confusing.meaning: difficult to understand; not clear（难以理解的；不清楚的）

confusion.meaning: a state of not being certain about what is happening, what you should do, what sth means, etc.（不确定；困惑）；the fact of making a mistake about who sb is or what sth is（混淆；混同）；a feeling of embarrassment when you do not understand sth and are not sure what to do in a situation（困窘；尴尬；局促不安）；a confused situation in which people do not know what action to take（（让人不知所措的）混乱局面，乱成一团）

congenial.meaning: (of a person（人）；pleasant to spend time with because their interests and character are similar to your own（意气相投的；志趣相投的；合得来的）；(of a place, job, etc.（地方、工作等）；pleasant because it suits your character（相宜的；合意的；适宜的）

congenital.meaning: (of a disease or medical condition（疾病或病理状况）；existing since or before birth（先天的；天生的）；existing as part of a person's character and not likely to change（生性的；生就的）；(of a person（人）

congested.meaning: crowded; full of traffic（拥挤的；挤满的；（交通）堵塞的）；(of a part of the body（身体部位）；blocked with blood or mucus（充血的；黏液阻塞的）

congestion.meaning: the state of being crowded and full of traffic（（交通）拥塞；塞车）；(medical 医) the state of part of the body being blocked with blood or mucus（充血；瘀血；黏液阻塞）

conglomerate.meaning: (business 商) a large company formed by joining together different firms（联合大公司；企业集团）；(formal) a number of things or parts that are put together to form a whole（合成物；组合物；聚合物）；(geology 地) a type of rock made of small stones held together by dried clay（砾岩）

congratulate.meaning: to tell sb that you are pleased about their success or achievements（向（某人）道贺；祝贺）；to feel pleased and proud because you have achieved sth or been successful at sth（（为成就或成功）感到高兴，感到自豪）

congratulation.meaning: a message congratulating sb (= saying that you are happy about their good luck or success)（祝贺；恭贺；贺辞）；used when you want to congratulate sb（（用以向人祝贺）祝贺，恭喜）；the act of congratulating sb（祝贺）

congregate.meaning: to come together in a group（群集；聚集；集合）

congress.meaning: a large formal meeting or series of meetings where representatives from different groups discuss ideas, make decisions, etc.（代表大会）；(in the US and some other countries（美国及一些其他国家）；the name of the group of people who are elected to make laws, in the US consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives（国会；议会）；used in the names of political parties in some countries（（用于某些国家的政党名称）国民大会）

congressional.meaning: related to or belonging to a congress or the Congress in the US（代表大会的；（美国）国会的）

congruent.meaning: (geometry 几何) having the same size and shape（全等的；叠合的）；(formal) suitable for sth; appropriate in a particular situation（适合的；适当的；恰当的；相称的）

conifer.meaning: any tree that produces hard dry fruit called cones. Most conifers are evergreen (= have leaves that stay on the tree all year).（针叶树）；con·ifer·ous /kəˈnɪfərəs; NAmEkəˈnɪfərəs/ adj. coniferous trees/forests（针叶树/林）

conjunction.meaning: (grammar 语法) a word that joins words, phrases or sentences, for example ‘and’, ‘but’, ‘or’（连词，（台）连接词）；(formal) a combination of events, etc., that causes a particular result（（引起某种结果的事物等的）结合，同时发生）；(astronomy 天) the fact of stars, planets, etc. passing close together as seen from the earth（（恒星、行星等的）合）；(formal) together with（与 … 一起）

connect.meaning: to join together two or more things; to be joined together（（使）连接；联结）；to join sth to the main supply of electricity, gas, water, etc. or to another piece of equipment（使 … 连接；接通）；to join a computer to the Internet or a computer network（使（计算机）连接（到互联网或计算机网络））；to notice or make a link between people, things, events, etc.（注意到 … 有关联；把 … 联系起来）

connected.meaning: (of two or more things or people（两个或以上的事物或人）；having a link between them（有联系的；相关的）

connection.meaning: something that connects two facts, ideas, etc.（（两种事实、想法等的）联系，关联）；the act of connecting or the state of being connected（联结；接通；连接）；a point, especially in an electrical system, where two parts connect（连接点；（尤指电力系统的）接头）；a train, bus or plane at a station or an airport that a passenger can take soon after getting off another in order to continue their journey（转车；转机；联运）

connective.meaning: (medical 医) that connects things（连接的；联结的）；(grammar 语法) a word that connects two parts of a sentence（连接词；关联词）

connoisseur.meaning: an expert on matters involving the judgement of beauty, quality or skill in art, food or music（鉴赏家；鉴定家；行家）

conquer.meaning: to take control of a country or city and its people by force（占领；攻克；征服）；to defeat sb, especially in a competition, race, etc.（（尤指比赛、赛跑等中）击败，战胜）；to succeed in dealing with or controlling sth（（成功地）对付，克服，控制）；to become very popular or successful in a place（在（某地）很受欢迎；在（某地）成功）

conqueror.meaning: a person who conquers（征服者；占领者；胜利者）

conquest.meaning: the act of taking control of a country, city, etc. by force（征服；占领）；an area of land taken by force（占领（或征服）的地区）；(usually humorous) a person that sb has persuaded to love them or to have sex with them（（爱情或性方面）被俘虏的人）；the act of gaining control over sth that is difficult or dangerous（（对困难、危险等的）控制）

conscience.meaning: the part of your mind that tells you whether your actions are right or wrong（良心；良知）；a guilty feeling about sth you have done or failed to do（内疚；愧疚）；the fact of behaving in a way that you feel is right even though this may cause problems（凭良心）；(formal) believing your actions to be fair（（认为行为）公正地，公平地，凭良心）

conscientious.meaning: taking care to do things carefully and correctly（勤勉认真的；一丝不苟的）；con·scien·tious·ly /ˌkɒnʃiˈenʃəsli; NAmEˌkɑːnʃiˈenʃəsli/ adv. She performed all her duties conscientiously.（她认真负责地履行自己的所有职责。）

conscious.meaning: aware of sth; noticing sth（意识到；注意到）；able to use your senses and mental powers to understand what is happening（神志清醒的；有知觉的；有意识的）；(of actions, feelings, etc.（行为、感情等）；deliberate or controlled（慎重的；有意的；刻意的）

consciousness.meaning: the state of being able to use your senses and mental powers to understand what is happening（清醒状态；知觉）；the state of being aware of sth（觉察；感觉；意识）；the ideas and opinions of a person or group（观念；看法）

conscription.meaning: the practice of ordering people by law to serve in the armed forces（征募；征兵）

consecutive.meaning: following one after another in a series, without interruption（连续不断的）

consensus.meaning: an opinion that all members of a group agree with（一致的意见；共识）

consent.meaning: permission to do sth, especially given by sb in authority（同意；准许；允许）；agreement about sth（同意；赞同）；an official document giving permission for sth（正式批准文件；批文）；(rather formal) to agree to sth or give your permission for sth（同意；准许；允许）

consequence.meaning: a result of sth that has happened（结果；后果）；(formal) importance（重要性）；(formal) as a result of sth（由于；作为 … 的结果）

consequent.meaning: happening as a result of sth（随之发生的；作为结果的）

consequently.meaning: as a result; therefore（因此；所以）

conservation.meaning: the protection of the natural environment（（对自然环境的）保护）；the official protection of buildings that have historical or artistic importance（（官方对历史或艺术建筑的）保护；文物保护）；the act of preventing sth from being lost, wasted, damaged or destroyed（防止流失（或浪费、损害、毁坏）；保存；保护）

conservatism.meaning: the tendency to resist great or sudden change（保守；守旧）；the political belief that society should change as little as possible（保守主义）；the principles of the Conservative Party in British politics（（英国）保守党的原则）

conservative.meaning: opposed to great or sudden social change; showing that you prefer traditional styles and values（保守的；守旧的）；connected with the British Conservative Party（（英国）保守党的）；(of an estimate（估计）；lower than what is probably the real amount or number（低于实际数量的；保守的）

conservatory.meaning: (BrE) a room with glass walls and a glass roof that is built on the side of a house. Conservatories are used for sitting in to enjoy the sun, and to protect plants from cold weather.（（靠房屋一侧用玻璃建造的）温室，暖房）；a school or college at which people are trained in music and theatre（音乐（或戏剧）专科学校（或学院））

conserve.meaning: to use as little of sth as possible so that it lasts a long time（节省；节约）；to protect sth and prevent it from being changed or destroyed（保护；保存；保藏）；jam containing large or whole pieces of fruit（（含有大块或整块水果的）果酱，蜜饯）

consider.meaning: to think about sth carefully, especially in order to make a decision（（尤指为作出决定而）仔细考虑，细想）；to think of sb/sth in a particular way（认为；以为；觉得）；to think about sth, especially the feelings of other people, and be influenced by it when making a decision, etc.（体谅；考虑到；顾及）；(formal) to look carefully at sb/sth（端详；注视）

considerable.meaning: great in amount, size, importance, etc.（相当多（或大、重要等）的）

considerably.meaning: much; a lot（非常；很；相当多地）

considerate.meaning: always thinking of other people's wishes and feelings; careful not to hurt or upset others（考虑周到的；为（他人）着想的；体谅的；体贴的）

consideration.meaning: (formal) the act of thinking carefully about sth（仔细考虑；深思；斟酌）；something that must be thought about when you are planning or deciding sth（（作计划或决定时）必须考虑的事（或因素、原因））；the quality of being sensitive towards others and thinking about their wishes and feelings（（对他人的）考虑周到，体谅，顾及）；(formal) a reward or payment for a service（报酬；酬金；支付款）

considering.meaning: used to show that you are thinking about a particular fact, and are influenced by it, when you make a statement about sth（考虑到；就 … 而言；鉴于）

consign.meaning: to put sb/sth somewhere in order to get rid of them/it（（为摆脱而）把 … 置于，把 … 交付给）；to put sb/sth in an unpleasant situation（把 … 置于（令人不快的境地）；打发；发落）；to give or send sth to sb（交给；交付；寄送）

consignment.meaning: a quantity of goods that are sent or delivered somewhere（装运的货物；运送物）；the act of sending or delivering sb/sth（发送；投递；递送）

consist.meaning: (formal) to have sth as the main or only part or feature（存在于；在于）；to be formed from the things or people mentioned（由 … 组成（或构成））

consistency.meaning: (approving) the quality of always behaving in the same way or of having the same opinions, standard, etc; the quality of being consistent（一致性；连贯性）；the consistency of a mixture or a liquid substance is how thick, smooth, etc. it is（黏稠度；密实度；平滑度；坚实度）

consistent.meaning: (approving) always behaving in the same way, or having the same opinions, standards, etc.（一致的；始终如一的）；happening in the same way and continuing for a period of time（连续的；持续的）；in agreement with sth; not contradicting sth（与 … 一致的；相符的；符合的；不矛盾的）；(of an argument or a set of ideas（论点或一系列的观点）

consolation.meaning: a thing or person that makes you feel better when you are unhappy or disappointed（使感到安慰的人（或物）；安慰；慰藉）

console.meaning: to give comfort or sympathy to sb who is unhappy or disappointed（安慰；抚慰；慰藉）；a flat surface which contains all the controls and switches for a machine, a piece of electronic equipment, etc.（（机器、电子设备等的）控制台，操纵台，仪表板）

consolidate.meaning: to make a position of power or success stronger so that it is more likely to continue（使加强；使巩固）；(technical 术语) to join things together into one; to be joined into one（（使）结成一体，合并）；con·soli·da·tion consolidation consolidations /kənˌsɒlɪˈdeɪʃn; NAmEkənˌsɑːlɪˈdeɪʃn/ noun [U] the consolidation of power（权力的巩固）

consonant.meaning: (phonetics 语音) a speech sound made by completely or partly stopping the flow of air being breathed out through the mouth（辅音；（台）子音）；a letter of the alphabet that represents a consonant sound, for example ‘b’, ‘c’, ‘d’, ‘f’, etc.（辅音字母，（台）子音字母）；(formal) agreeing with or being the same as sth else（（与 … ）一致的，符合的，相同的，和谐的）

consort.meaning: the husband or wife of a ruler（（统治者的）配偶）；a group of old-fashioned musical instruments, or a group of musicians who play music from several centuries ago（一组古乐器；（演奏几世纪前音乐的）一组乐师）；(formal) to spend time with sb that other people do not approve of（厮混；鬼混）

consortium.meaning: a group of people, countries, companies, etc. who are working together on a particular project（（合作进行某项工程的）财团，银团，联营企业）

conspicuous.meaning: easy to see or notice; likely to attract attention（易见的；明显的；惹人注意的）；con·spicu·ous·ly /kənˈspɪkjuəsli; NAmEkənˈspɪkjuəsli/ adv. Women were conspicuously absent from (= there were surprisingly few women on) the planning committee.（规划委员会里没有女性委员，惹人注意。）；con·spicu·ous·ness /kənˈspɪkjuəsnəs; NAmEkənˈspɪkjuəsnəs/ noun [U] IDM conˌspicuous by your ˈabsence not present in a situation or place, when it is obvious that you should be there（（本应在场）因缺席而招人注意）

conspiracy.meaning: a secret plan by a group of people to do sth harmful or illegal（密谋策划；阴谋）

constable.meaning: (in the US（美国）；a peace officer with some of the powers of a police officer, typically in a small town（（通常指小城镇的）警员，治安官）

constabulary.meaning: (in Britain) the police force of a particular area or town（（英国某地区或城镇的）警察部队）

constant.meaning: happening all the time or repeatedly（连续发生的；不断的；重复的）；that does not change（不变的；固定的；恒定的）；(technical 术语) a number or quantity that does not vary（常数；常量）

constantly.meaning: all the time; repeatedly（始终；一直；重复不断地）

constellation.meaning: a group of stars that forms a shape in the sky and has a name（星座）；(formal) a group of related ideas, things or people（一系列（相关的想法、事物）；一群（相关的人））

constituency.meaning: a district that elects its own representative to parliament（（选举议会议员的）选区）；the people who live in and vote in a particular district（选区选民）；a particular group of people in society who are likely to support a person, an idea or a product（（统称）支持者）

constituent.meaning: a person who lives, and can vote in a constituency（（选区的）选民，选举人）；one of the parts of sth that combine to form the whole（成分；构成要素）；(formal) forming or helping to make a whole（组成的；构成的）

constitute.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to be considered to be sth（（被认为或看作）是；被算作）；to be the parts that together form sth（组成；构成）；to form a group legally or officially（（合法或正式地）成立，设立）

constitution.meaning: the system of laws and basic principles that a state, a country or an organization is governed by（宪法；章程）；the condition of a person's body and how healthy it is（身体素质；体质；体格）；(formal) the way sth is formed or organized（构成；构造）；(formal) the act of forming sth（组成；形成）

constitutional.meaning: connected with the constitution of a country or an organization（宪法的；章程的）；allowed or limited by the constitution of a country or an organization（宪法准许的；受宪法限制的；受章程限制的）；related to the body's ability to stay healthy, be strong and fight illness（身体素质的；体质的；体格的）；con·sti·tu·tion·al·ly AW /ˌkɒnstɪˈtjuːʃənəli; NAmEˌkɑːnstəˈtuːʃənəli/ adv. constitutionally guaranteed rights（受到宪法保障的权利）

constitutive.meaning: forming a part, often an essential part, of sth（组成部分的；本质的；基本的）

constrain.meaning: to force sb to do sth or behave in a particular way（强迫；强制；迫使）；to restrict or limit sb/sth（限制；限定；约束）

constraint.meaning: a thing that limits or restricts sth, or your freedom to do sth（限制；限定；约束）；strict control over the way that you behave or are allowed to behave（约束；严管）

constrict.meaning: to become tighter or narrower; to make sth tighter or narrower（（使）紧缩，缩窄）；to limit or restrict what sb is able to do（限制；限定；抑制；约束）；con·strict·ed /; NAmE/ adj. Her throat felt dry and constricted.（她感到喉咙发干发紧。）；con·stric·tion constriction constrictions /kənˈstrɪkʃn; NAmEkənˈstrɪkʃn/ noun [U, C] a feeling of constriction in the chest（胸部的压迫感）

construct.meaning: to build or make sth such as a road, building or machine（建筑；修建；建造）；to form sth by putting different things together（组成；创建）；(geometry 几何) to draw a line or shape according to the rules of mathematics（（按照数学规则）编制，绘制）；an idea or a belief that is based on various pieces of evidence which are not always true（（根据不总是真实的各种证据得出的）构想，观念，概念）

construction.meaning: the process or method of building or making sth, especially roads, buildings, bridges, etc.（建筑；建造；施工）；the way that sth has been built or made（建造（或构造）的方式）；(formal) a thing that has been built or made（建造物；构筑物；制成物）；the way in which words are used together and arranged to form a sentence, phrase, etc.（（句子、短语等的）结构）

constructive.meaning: having a useful and helpful effect rather than being negative or with no purpose（建设性的；有助益的；积极的）

construe.meaning: to understand the meaning of a word, a sentence, or an action in a particular way（理解；领会）

consul.meaning: a government official who is the representative of his or her country in a foreign city（领事）；con·su·lar /ˈkɒnsjələ(r); NAmEˈkɑːnsələr/ adj. consular officials（领事）

consulate.meaning: the building where a consul works（领事馆）

consult.meaning: to go to sb for information or advice（咨询；请教）；to discuss sth with sb to get their permission for sth, or to help you make a decision（（与某人）商议，商量（以得到许可或帮助决策））；to look in or at sth to get information（查阅；查询；参看）

consultant.meaning: a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is employed to give advice about it to other people（顾问）；(BrE) a hospital doctor of the highest rank who is a specialist in a particular area of medicine（高级顾问医师；会诊医师）

consultation.meaning: the act of discussing sth with sb or with a group of people before making a decision about it（咨询；商讨；磋商）；a formal meeting to discuss sth（商讨会；协商会）；a meeting with an expert, especially a doctor, to get advice or treatment（（向专家请教的）咨询会；（尤指）就诊）；the act of looking for information in a book, etc.（查找；查阅；查看）

consultative.meaning: giving advice or making suggestions（咨询的；顾问的）

consume.meaning: to use sth, especially fuel, energy or time（消耗，耗费（尤指燃料、能量或时间））；to eat or drink sth（吃；喝；饮）；to fill sb with a strong feeling（使充满（强烈的感情））；(of fire（火）

consumer.meaning: a person who buys goods or uses services（消费者；顾客；用户）

consumption.meaning: the act of using energy, food or materials; the amount used（（能量、食物或材料的）消耗，消耗量）；the act of buying and using products（消费）；(old-fashioned) a serious infectious disease of the lungs（肺病；肺痨；肺结核）

contact.meaning: the act of communicating with sb, especially regularly（（尤指经常的）联系，联络）；the state of touching sth（触摸；接触）；the state of meeting sb or having to deal with sth（遇见（某人）；碰上（要处理的事））；an occasion on which you meet or communicate with sb; a relationship with sb（会见；交往；人际关系）

contain.meaning: if sth contains sth else, it has that thing inside it or as part of it（包含；含有；容纳）；to keep your feelings under control（控制，克制，抑制（感情））；to prevent sth harmful from spreading or getting worse（防止 … 蔓延（或恶化））

container.meaning: a box, bottle, etc. in which sth can be stored or transported（容器）；a large metal or wooden box of a standard size in which goods are packed so that they can easily be lifted onto a ship, train, etc. to be transported（集装箱；货柜）

containment.meaning: the act of keeping sth under control so that it cannot spread in a harmful way（控制；抑制）；the act of keeping another country's power within limits so that it does not become too powerful（（对另一个国家力量的）遏制）

contaminate.meaning: to make a substance or place dirty or no longer pure by adding a substance that is dangerous or carries disease（污染；弄脏）；(formal) to influence people's ideas or attitudes in a bad way（玷污，毒害，腐蚀（人的思想或品德））；con·tam·in·ation contamination contaminations /kənˌtæmɪˈneɪʃn; NAmEkənˌtæmɪˈneɪʃn/ noun [U] radioactive contamination（放射性污染）

contemplate.meaning: to think about whether you should do sth, or how you should do sth（考虑；思量；思忖）；to think carefully about and accept the possibility of sth happening（考虑接受（发生某事的可能性））；(formal) to think deeply about sth for a long time（深思熟虑；沉思；苦思冥想）；(formal) to look at sb/sth in a careful way for a long time（端详；打量）

contemplation.meaning: the act of thinking deeply about sth（深思；沉思）；the act of looking at sth in a calm and careful way（凝视；默默注视）；(formal) being considered（考虑中）

contemporary.meaning: belonging to the same time（属同时期的；同一时代的）；belonging to the present time（当代的；现代的）；a person who lives or lived at the same time as sb else, especially sb who is about the same age（同代人；同辈人；同龄人）

contempt.meaning: the feeling that sb/sth is without value and deserves no respect at all（蔑视；轻蔑；鄙视）；a lack of worry or fear about rules, danger, etc.（（对规则、危险等的）藐视，不顾）

contemptible.meaning: not deserving any respect at all（可轻蔑的；可鄙的；卑劣的）

contemptuous.meaning: feeling or showing that you have no respect for sb/sth（蔑视的；鄙视的；表示轻蔑的）；con·temp·tu·ous·ly /kənˈtemptʃuəsli; NAmEkənˈtemptʃuəsli/ adv. to laugh contemptuously（轻蔑地大笑）

contend.meaning: (formal) to say that sth is true, especially in an argument（（尤指在争论中）声称，主张，认为）；to compete against sb in order to gain sth（竞争；争夺）；to have to deal with a problem or with a difficult situation or person（（不得不）应付，处理，对付）

contender.meaning: a person who takes part in a competition or tries to win sth（竞争者；角逐者；争夺者）

content.meaning: the things that are contained in sth（所容纳之物；所含之物；内容）；the different sections that are contained in a book（（书的）目录，目次）；the subject matter of a book, speech, programme, etc.（（书、讲话、节目等的）主题，主要内容）；(following a noun（用于名词后）

contented.meaning: showing or feeling happiness or satisfaction, especially because your life is good（（尤指因生活好而）满意的，惬意的，满足的）；con·tent·ed·ly /kənˈtentɪdli; NAmEkənˈtentɪdli/ adv. She smiled contentedly.（她心满意足地笑了。）

contention.meaning: angry disagreement between people（争吵；争执；争论）；a belief or an opinion that you express, especially in an argument（（尤指争论时的）看法，观点）；with a chance of winning sth（有机会赢得）；without a chance of winning sth（没有机会赢得）

contentious.meaning: likely to cause disagreement between people（可能引起争论的）；liking to argue; involving a lot of arguing（爱争论的；好争吵的）

contest.meaning: a competition in which people try to win sth（比赛；竞赛）；a struggle to gain control or power（（控制权或权力的）争夺，竞争）；used to say that one side in a competition is so much stronger or better than the other that it is sure to win easily（（表示竞争中的一方过于强大或出色）完全不是对手，毫无竞争可言）；to take part in a competition, election, etc. and try to win it（争取赢得（比赛、选举等））

contestant.meaning: a person who takes part in a contest（参赛者；竞争者）

context.meaning: the situation in which sth happens and that helps you to understand it（（事情发生的）背景，环境，来龙去脉）；the words that come just before and after a word, phrase or statement and help you to understand its meaning（上下文；语境）

contextual.meaning: connected with a particular context（上下文的；与上下文有关的；与语境相关的）

continent.meaning: one of the large land masses of the earth such as Europe, Asia or Africa（大陆；陆地；洲）；(BrE) the main part of the continent of Europe, not including Britain or Ireland（欧洲大陆（不包括英国和爱尔兰））

continental.meaning: (BrE) of or in the continent of Europe, not including Britain and Ireland（欧洲大陆的（不包括英国和爱尔兰））；(BrE) following the customs of countries in western and southern Europe（随（西、南欧国家）大陆风俗的）；connected with the main part of the N American continent（北美大陆的）；forming part of, or typical of, any of the seven main land masses of the earth（大洲的；大陆的）

contingency.meaning: an event that may or may not happen（可能发生的事；偶发（或不测、意外）事件）

contingent.meaning: a group of people at a meeting or an event who have sth in common, especially the place they come from, that is not shared by other people at the event（（志趣相投、尤指来自同一地方的）一组与会者，代表团）；a group of soldiers that are part of a larger force（（军队的）分遣队，小分队）；(formal) depending on sth that may or may not happen（依情况而定的）；(business 商) a person, or work done by a person, who does not have a permanent contract with a company（临时工；临时工作）

continual.meaning: repeated many times in a way that is annoying（（令人厌烦地）多次重复的，频繁的）；continuing without interruption（接连不断的；连续的；频频的）；con·tinu·al·ly /kənˈtɪnjuəli; NAmEkənˈtɪnjuəli/ adv. They argue continually about money.（他们没完没了地为钱争吵。）

continuance.meaning: (formal) the state of continuing to exist or function（继续；持续）；(NAmE) (law 律) a decision that a court case should be heard later（延期审理）

continuation.meaning: an act or the state of continuing（继续；连续；持续）；something that continues or follows sth else（延续部分；续篇）；something that is joined on to sth else and forms a part of it（附加物；延续物）

continue.meaning: to keep existing or happening without stopping（持续；继续存在；不断发生）；to keep doing sth without stopping（继续做；不停地干）；to go or move further in the same direction（（朝相同方向）走，移动；延伸）；to remain in a particular job or condition（留任；维持原状）

continuity.meaning: the fact of not stopping or not changing（连续性；持续性）；a logical connection between the parts of sth, or between two things（（逻辑上的）连接，联结）；(technical 术语) the organization of a film/movie or television programme, especially making sure that people's clothes, objects, etc. are the same from one scene to the next（（电影或电视节目场景中服装、物体等的）一致性，衔接）

continuous.meaning: happening or existing for a period of time without interruption（不断的；持续的；连续的）；spreading in a line or over an area without any spaces（延伸的；遍布的）；(informal) repeated many times（反复的；频繁的）；con·tinu·ous·ly ★ /kənˈtɪnjuəsli; NAmEkənˈtɪnjuəsli/ adv. He has lived and worked in France almost continuously since 1990.（自从 1990 年以来，他差不多一直在法国居住和工作。）

continuum.meaning: a series of similar items in which each is almost the same as the ones next to it but the last is very different from the first（（相邻两者相似但起首与末尾截然不同的）连续体）

contour.meaning: the outer edges of sth; the outline of its shape or form（外形；轮廓）；a line on a map that joins points that are the same height above sea level（（地图上连接相同海拔各点的）等高线）

contract.meaning: an official written agreement（合同；合约；契约）；(informal) an agreement to kill sb for money（（雇用杀人的）协议，合同）；to become less or smaller; to make sth become less or smaller（（使）收缩，缩小）；(formal or medical 医) to get an illness（感染（疾病）；得（病））

contraction.meaning: the process of becoming smaller（收缩；缩小）；a sudden and painful contracting of muscles, especially of the muscles around a woman's womb, that happens when she is giving birth to a child（（肌肉的）收缩，挛缩；（尤指分娩时的）子宫收缩）；(linguistics 语言) a short form of a word（词的缩约形式）

contractor.meaning: a person or company that has a contract to do work or provide goods or services for another company（承包人；承包商；承包公司）

contractual.meaning: connected with the conditions of a legal written agreement; agreed in a contract（合同的；契约的；按合同（或契约）规定的）

contradict.meaning: to say that sth that sb else has said is wrong, and that the opposite is true（反驳；驳斥；批驳）；(of statements or pieces of evidence（陈述或证据）；to be so different from each other that one of them must be wrong（相抵触；相矛盾；相反）

contradiction.meaning: a lack of agreement between facts, opinions, actions, etc.（（事实、看法、行动等的）不一致，矛盾，对立）；the act of saying that sth that sb else has said is wrong or not true; an example of this（反驳；驳斥）；a statement containing two words that contradict each other's meaning（自相矛盾的说法）

contradictory.meaning: containing or showing a contradiction（相互矛盾的；对立的；不一致的）

contrary.meaning: different from sth; against sth（与之相异的；相对立的；相反的）；completely different in nature or direction（（在性质或方向上）截然不同的，完全相反的）；the opposite fact, event or situation（相反的事实（或事情、情况））；used to introduce a statement that says the opposite of the last one（与此相反；恰恰相反）

contrast.meaning: a difference between two or more people or things that you can see clearly when they are compared or put close together; the fact of comparing two or more things in order to show the differences between them（明显的差异；对比；对照）；a person or thing that is clearly different from sb/sth else（明显不同的人（或事物））；differences in colour or in light and dark, used in photographs and paintings to create a special effect（（摄影或绘画中的）颜色反差，明暗对比）；the amount of difference between light and dark in a photograph or the picture on a television screen（（照片或电视图像的）明暗对比度，反差）

contrasting.meaning: very different in style, colour or attitude（（在式样、颜色或态度上）极不相同的，差异大的）

contribute.meaning: to give sth, especially money or goods, to help sb/sth（捐献，捐赠（尤指金钱或物品）；捐助）；to be one of the causes of sth（是 … 的原因之一）；to increase, improve or add to sth（增加；增进；添加（到某物））；to write things for a newspaper, magazine, or a radio or television programme; to speak during a meeting or conversation, especially to give your opinion（（为报纸、杂志、电台或电视节目）撰稿；（在会议或会谈期间）讲话，（尤指）发表意见）

contribution.meaning: a sum of money that is given to a person or an organization in order to help pay for sth（捐款；捐资）；a sum of money that you pay regularly to your employer or the government in order to pay for benefits such as health insurance, a pension, etc.（（给雇主或政府用作医疗保险、养老金等津贴的）定期缴款）；an action or a service that helps to cause or increase sth（贡献；促成作用）；an item that forms part of a book, magazine, broadcast, discussion, etc.（（书、杂志、广播、讨论等部分内容的）一则，一条，稿件）

contributor.meaning: a person who writes articles for a magazine or a book, or who talks on a radio or television programme or at a meeting（（杂志或书的）撰稿人，投稿人；（电台、电视节目中的）嘉宾；（会议的）发言人）；a person or thing that provides money to help pay for sth, or support sth（捐款者；捐赠者；作出贡献者）；something that helps to cause sth（促成物）

contributory.meaning: helping to cause sth（促成的；促进的；起作用的）；involving payments from the people who will benefit（需要受益人付钱的）

contrive.meaning: to manage to do sth despite difficulties（（不顾困难而）设法做到）；to succeed in making sth happen despite difficulties（（克服困难）促成某事）；to think of or make sth, for example a plan or a machine, in a clever way（巧妙地策划；精巧地制造（如机器））

control.meaning: the power to make decisions about how a country, an area, an organization, etc. is run（（对国家、地区、机构等的）管理权，控制权，支配权）；the ability to make sb/sth do what you want（控制（或操纵）能力）；(often in compounds（常构成复合词）；the act of restricting, limiting or managing sth; a method of doing this（限制；限定；约束；管理；管制）

controllable.meaning: that can be controlled（可控制（或管理、操纵、支配）的）

controlled.meaning: done or arranged in a very careful way（十分小心完成的；精心安排的）；limited, or managed by law or by rules（（受法律或规则）限制的，控制的，管制的）；(in compounds（构成复合词）；managed by a particular group, or in a particular way（（受某团体或用某种方式）管理的，控制的，操纵的）

controversial.meaning: causing a lot of angry public discussion and disagreement（引起争论的；有争议的）

conurbation.meaning: a large area where towns have grown and joined together, often around a city（（有卫星城镇的）大都市，集合城市）

convection.meaning: the process in which heat moves through a gas or a liquid as the hotter part rises and the cooler, heavier part sinks（（热通过气体或液体的）运流，对流）

convene.meaning: to arrange for people to come together for a formal meeting（召集，召开（正式会议））；to come together for a formal meeting（（为正式会议而）聚集，集合）

convenience.meaning: the quality of being useful, easy or suitable for sb（方便；适宜；便利）；something that is useful and can make things easier or quicker to do, or more comfortable（便利的事物（或设施）；方便的用具）；(formal) at a time or a place which is suitable for sb（在（某人）方便时；在（某人）适宜的地点）

convenient.meaning: useful, easy or quick to do; not causing problems（实用的；便利的；方便的；省事的）；near to a particular place; easy to get to（附近的；近便的；容易到达的）；con·veni·ent·ly /kənˈviːniəntli; NAmEkənˈviːniəntli/ adv. The report can be conveniently divided into three main sections.（这份报告不用费事就可划分为三个主要部分。）

convention.meaning: the way in which sth is done that most people in a society expect and consider to be polite or the right way to do it（习俗；常规；惯例）；a large meeting of the members of a profession, a political party, etc.（（某职业、政党等成员的）大会，集会）；an official agreement between countries or leaders（（国家或首脑间的）公约，协定，协议）；a traditional method or style in literature, art or the theatre（（文学、艺术或戏剧的）传统手法，传统风格）

conventional.meaning: (often disapproving) tending to follow what is done or considered acceptable by society in general; normal and ordinary, and perhaps not very interesting（依照惯例的；遵循习俗的；墨守成规的；普通平凡的）；following what is traditional or the way sth has been done for a long time（传统的；习惯的）；(especially of weapons（尤指武器）；not nuclear（非核的；常规的）

conversant.meaning: (formal) knowing about sth; familiar with sth（通晓的；熟悉的）

conversation.meaning: an informal talk involving a small group of people or only two; the activity of talking in this way（（非正式）交谈，谈话）

conversational.meaning: not formal; as used in conversation（非正式的；用于交谈的；口语的）；connected with conversation（交谈的；谈话的；会话的）；con·ver·sa·tion·al·ly /ˌkɒnvəˈseɪʃənli; NAmEˌkɑːnvərˈseɪʃənli/ adv. ‘Have you been here long?’ he asked conversationally.（“你来这里很久了吗？”他攀谈着问道。）

converse.meaning: (formal) to have a conversation with sb（交谈；谈话）；the opposite or reverse of a fact or statement（相反的事物；（事实或陈述的）反面）；con·verse adj. the converse effect（相反的效果）

conversely.meaning: in a way that is the opposite or reverse of sth（相反地；反过来）

conversion.meaning: the act or process of changing sth from one form, use or system to another（转变；转换；转化）；the process or experience of changing your religion or beliefs（（宗教或信仰的）改变；皈依；归附）；(in rugby and American football（橄榄球和美式足球）；a way of scoring extra points after scoring a try or a touchdown（（持球触地或持球越过对方球门线后的）附加得分）

convert.meaning: to change or make sth change from one form, purpose, system, etc. to another（（使）转变，转换，转化）；to be able to be changed from one form, purpose, or system to another（可转变为；可变换成）；to change or make sb change their religion or beliefs（（使）改变（宗教或信仰）；（使）皈依，归附）；to change an opinion, a habit, etc.（改变（观点、习惯等））

converter.meaning: a person or thing that converts sth（使发生转化的人（或物）；转换器）；(physics 物) a device for converting alternating current into direct current or the other way around（整流器；变流器）；(physics 物) a device for converting a radio signal from one frequency to another（（改变无线电信号的）变频器）

convertible.meaning: that can be changed to a different form or use（可改变的；可转换的；可兑换的）；con·vert·ibil·ity /kənˌvɜːtəˈbɪləti; NAmEkənˌvɜːrtəˈbɪləti/ noun [U] noun a car with a roof that can be folded down or taken off（活动顶篷式汽车）

convex.meaning: (of an outline or a surface（外形或表面）；curving out（凸出的；凸面的）

convey.meaning: to make ideas, feelings, etc. known to sb（表达，传递（思想、感情等））；(formal) to take, carry or transport sb/sth from one place to another（传送；运送；输送）

conveyance.meaning: (formal) the process of taking sb/sth from one place to another（传送；运送；输送）；(formal) a vehicle（运载（或交通）工具；车辆）；(law 律) a legal document that moves property from one owner to another（产权转让证书）

conviction.meaning: the act of finding sb guilty of a crime in court; the fact of having been found guilty（判罪；定罪；证明有罪）；a strong opinion or belief（坚定的看法（或信念））；the feeling or appearance of believing sth strongly and of being sure about it（深信；坚信；坚定；肯定）

convincing.meaning: that makes sb believe that sth is true（令人信服的；有说服力的）；con·vin·cing·ly AW /kənˈvɪnsɪŋli; NAmEkənˈvɪnsɪŋli/ adv. Her case was convincingly argued.（她的辩词很有说服力。）

convivial.meaning: cheerful and friendly in atmosphere or character（（气氛或性格）欢快友好的）

cook.meaning: to prepare food by heating it, for example by boiling, baking or frying it（烹饪；烹调）；(of food（食物）；to be prepared by boiling, baking, frying, etc.（煮（或烘烤、煎炸等））；(informal) to be planned secretly（密谋；秘密策划）

cooker.meaning: a large piece of equipment for cooking food, containing an oven and gas or electric rings on top（（带烤箱、燃气炉或电炉的）厨灶，炉具）

cooking.meaning: the process of preparing food（烹饪；烹调）；food that has been prepared in a particular way（（用某种方法烹制的）食物，饭菜）；suitable for cooking rather than eating raw or drinking（适于烹饪的（不宜于生吃或直接饮用的））

cool.meaning: fairly cold; not hot or warm（凉的；凉爽的；凉快的）；making you feel pleasantly cool（使人感到凉爽的；冷色的）；calm; not excited, angry or emotional（冷静的；镇静的；平静的）；not friendly, interested or enthusiastic（不友好的；冷淡的；冷漠的）

cooler.meaning: a container or machine which cools things, especially drinks, or keeps them cold（冷却器；冷藏器）；(NAmE) a drink with ice and usually wine in it（（通常有冰和酒的）清凉饮料）

coolness.meaning: the quality of being cool（凉；凉爽；凉快；冷静；冷漠）

cooper.meaning: a person who makes barrels（制桶工人；箍桶匠）

cooperate.meaning: to work together with sb else in order to achieve sth（合作；协作）；to be helpful by doing what sb asks you to do（协助；配合）

cooperative.meaning: involving doing sth together or working together with others towards a shared aim（合作的；协作的；同心协力的）；helpful by doing what you are asked to do（协助的；配合的）；(business 商) owned and run by the people involved, with the profits shared by them（共同拥有共同经营利益共享的；合作的）；co·opera·tive·ly AW /kəʊˈɒpərətɪvli; NAmEkoʊˈɑːpərətɪvli/ (BrE also co-operatively) adv. noun a cooperative business or other organization（合作企业；合作社组织）

coordinate.meaning: to organize the different parts of an activity and the people involved in it so that it works well（使协调；使相配合）；to make the different parts of your body work well together（使（身体各部位）动作协调；协同动作）；(rather formal) if you coordinate clothes, furniture, etc. or if they coordinate, they look nice together（（使衣服、家具等）搭配，协调）；co·ord·in·ator coordinator coordinators (BrE also co-ordinator) noun The campaign needs an effective coordinator.（这场运动需要一个能干的协调人。）

cop.meaning: (informal) a police officer（警察）；(BrE) (slang) not very good（不太好；不怎么样）；to receive or suffer sth unpleasant（遭受；忍受）；to notice sth（注意到）

copy.meaning: a thing that is made to be the same as sth else, especially a document or a work of art（（尤指文件或艺术品的）复印件，副本，复制品）；a single example of a book, newspaper, etc. of which many have been made（（书、报纸等的）一本，一册，一份）；written material that is to be printed in a newspaper, magazine, etc; news or information that can be used in a newspaper article or advertisement（（报刊等的）稿件；（可用于报纸文章或广告的）消息，信息）；(IndE) a book used by students for writing exercises, etc. in（作业本；练习本）

copyright.meaning: if a person or an organization holds the copyright on a piece of writing, music, etc., they are the only people who have the legal right to publish, broadcast, perform it, etc., and other people must ask their permission to use it or any part of it（版权；著作权）；protected by copyright; not allowed to be copied without permission（受版权保护的；未经准许不得复制的）；to get the copyright for sth（获得 … 的版权）

cord.meaning: strong thick string or thin rope; a piece of this（（结实的）粗线，细绳；一根粗线（或细绳））；a piece of wire that is covered with plastic, used for carrying electricity to a piece of equipment（花线；皮线）；trousers/pants made of corduroy（灯芯绒裤子）

cordial.meaning: (formal) pleasant and friendly（热情友好的；和蔼可亲的）；cor·di·al·ity /ˌkɔːdiˈæləti; NAmEˌkɔːrdʒiləti/ noun [U] I was greeted with a show of cordiality.（我受到了热情友好的接待。）；a sweet drink that does not contain alcohol, made from fruit juice. cordially.meaning: in a pleasant and friendly manner（热情友好地；和蔼可亲地）；(used with verbs showing dislike（与动词连用表示厌恶）；very much（非常；十分；很）

core.meaning: the hard central part of a fruit such as an apple, that contains the seeds（（水果的）果心，核儿）；the central part of an object（（物体的）中心部分）；the most important or central part of sth（最重要的部分；核心；要点；精髓）；a small group of people who take part in a particular activity（（参加某项活动的）一小群人）

coriander.meaning: a plant whose leaves are used in cooking as a herb and whose seeds are used in cooking as a spice（芫荽；香菜）

corn.meaning: any plant that is grown for its grain, such as wheat; the grain of these plants（（小麦等）谷物；谷粒）；a tall plant grown for its large yellow grains that are used for making flour or eaten as a vegetable; the grains of this plant（玉蜀黍；玉米）；the yellow seeds of a type of corn (maize) plant, also called corn, which grow on thick stems and are cooked and eaten as a vegetable（玉米）；a small area of hard skin on the foot, especially the toe, that is sometimes painful（（尤指脚趾上的）钉胼，鸡眼）

cornet.meaning: a brass musical instrument like a small trumpet（短号）

corona.meaning: a ring of light seen around the sun or moon, especially during an eclipse（（尤指在日食或月食期间的）日冕，日华，月华）

corporate.meaning: connected with a corporation（公司的）；(technical 术语) forming a corporation（组成公司（或团体）的；法人的）；involving or shared by all the members of a group（社团的；全体的；共同的）

corporation.meaning: a large business company（（大）公司）；an organization or a group of organizations that is recognized by law as a single unit（法人；法人团体）；(BrE) a group of people elected to govern a large town or city and provide public services（市政委员会）

corpus.meaning: a collection of written or spoken texts（（书面或口语的）文集，文献，汇编；语料库）

correct.meaning: accurate or true, without any mistakes（准确无误的；精确的；正确的）；right and suitable, so that sth is done as it should be done（恰当的；合适的）；taking care to speak or behave in a way that follows the accepted standards or rules（（举止言谈）符合公认准则的，得体的）；cor·rect·ly ★ /kəˈrektli; NAmEkəˈrektli/ adv. Have you spelled it correctly?（你把它拼写对了吗？）

correlate.meaning: if two or more facts, figures, etc. correlate or if a fact, figure, etc. correlates with another, the facts are closely connected and affect or depend on each other（相互关联影响；相互依赖）；to show that there is a close connection between two or more facts, figures, etc.（显示紧密联系）
