correspondent.meaning: a person who reports news from a particular country or on a particular subject for a newspaper or a television or radio station（记者；通讯员）；(used with an adjective（与形容词连用）；a person who writes letters to another person（通信者）

corresponding.meaning: matching or connected with sth that you have just mentioned（符合的；相应的；相关的）；cor·res·pond·ing·ly AW /; NAmE/ adv. a period of high demand and correspondingly high prices（需求大、价格相应较高的时期）

corridor.meaning: a long narrow passage in a building, with doors that open into rooms on either side（（建筑物内的）走廊，过道，通道）；a passage on a train（（火车上的）走道，过道，通道）；a long narrow strip of land belonging to one country that passes through the land of another country; a part of the sky over a country that planes, for example from another country, can fly through（走廊（一国领土通过他国境内的狭长地带）；空中走廊（一国领空中允许他国飞机经过的区域））；a long narrow strip of land that follows the course of an important road or river（（沿着重要道路或河道的）狭长地带）

corrode.meaning: to destroy sth slowly, especially by chemical action; to be destroyed in this way（腐蚀；侵蚀）；cor·ro·sion /kəˈrəʊʒn; NAmEkəˈroʊʒn/ noun [U] Look for signs of corrosion.（寻找腐蚀的痕迹。）

corrosive.meaning: tending to destroy sth slowly by chemical action（腐蚀性的；侵蚀性的）；(formal) tending to damage sth gradually（损害性的；逐渐起破坏作用的）

corrupt.meaning: (of people（人）；willing to use their power to do dishonest or illegal things in return for money or to get an advantage（贪污的；受贿的；腐败的；营私舞弊的）；(of behaviour（行为）；dishonest or immoral（不诚实的；不道德的）

corruption.meaning: dishonest or illegal behaviour, especially of people in authority（腐败；贪污；贿赂；受贿）；the act or effect of making sb change from moral to immoral standards of behaviour（堕落；腐蚀）；the form of a word or phrase that has become changed from its original form in some way（（单词或短语的）变体）

corset.meaning: a piece of women's underwear, fitting the body tightly, worn especially in the past to make the waist look smaller（（尤指旧时妇女束腰的）紧身内衣）

cortex.meaning: the outer layer of an organ in the body, especially the brain（皮层；皮质；（尤指）大脑皮层）

cosmetic.meaning: a substance that you put on your face or body to make it more attractive（化妆品；美容品）；improving only the outside appearance of sth and not its basic character（装门面的；表面的）；connected with medical treatment that is intended to improve a person's appearance（整容的）

cosmic.meaning: connected with the whole universe（宇宙的）；very great and important（巨大且重要的）

cosmopolitan.meaning: containing people of different types or from different countries, and influenced by their culture（世界性的；全球各国的；有各国人的；受各国文化影响的）；having or showing a wide experience of people and things from many different countries（接触过许多国家的人（或事物）的；见过世面的；见识广的）；a person who has experience of many different parts of the world（周游世界的人）

cosmos.meaning: the universe, especially when it is thought of as an ordered system（（尤指被视为有序体系时的）宇宙）

cosset.meaning: (often disapproving) to treat sb with a lot of care and give them a lot of attention, sometimes too much（宠爱；溺爱；娇惯）

cost.meaning: the amount of money that you need in order to buy, make or do sth（费用；花费；价钱）；the total amount of money that needs to be spent by a business（成本）；the effort, loss or damage that is involved in order to do or achieve sth（（为做某事涉及的）努力，代价，损失）；the sum of money that sb is ordered to pay for lawyers, etc. in a legal case（诉讼费用）

costly.meaning: costing a lot of money, especially more than you want to pay（花钱多的；昂贵的；价钱高的）；causing problems or the loss of sth（引起困难的；造成损失的）

costume.meaning: the clothes worn by people from a particular place or during a particular historical period（（某地或某历史时期的）服装，装束）；the clothes worn by actors in a play or film/movie, or worn by sb to make them look like sth else（（戏剧或电影的）戏装，服装）

cosy.meaning: warm, comfortable and safe, especially because of being small or confined（温暖舒适的（尤指细小的室内地方））；friendly and private（亲密无间的；密切的）；(often disapproving) easy and convenient, but not always honest or right（轻易得到的，轻松的（但不一定是诚实或恰当的））；cosi·ly /; NAmE/ (BrE) (NAmE cozi·ly) adv. sitting cosily by the fire（暖融融地坐在炉火旁）

cottage.meaning: a small house, especially in the country（小屋；（尤指）村舍，小别墅）

cotton.meaning: a plant grown in warm countries for the soft white hairs around its seeds that are used to make cloth and thread（棉花植株）；the cloth made from the cotton plant（棉织物；棉布）；(especially BrE) thread that is used for sewing（棉线；棉纱）；a soft mass of white material that is used for cleaning the skin or a wound（药棉；脱脂棉）

cottonwood.meaning: a type of N American poplar tree, with seeds that are covered in hairs that look like white cotton（棉白杨，三角叶杨（产于北美））

couch.meaning: a long comfortable seat for two or more people to sit on（长沙发；长榻）；a long piece of furniture like a bed, especially in a doctor's office（（尤指诊室内的）诊察台）；(formal) to say or write words in a particular style or manner（（用某种文体或方式）表达，措辞）

cough.meaning: to force out air suddenly and noisily through your throat, for example when you have a cold（咳嗽）；to force sth out of your throat or lungs by coughing（（从喉咙或肺中）咳出）；(of an engine（发动机）；to make a sudden unpleasant noise（发出刺耳的声音）

could.meaning: used as the past tense of ‘can’（（用于 can 的过去时））；used to ask if you can do sth（（询问是否可做某事）能，可以）；used to politely ask sb to do sth for you（（礼貌地请求别人做事）能，可以）；used to show that sth is or might be possible（（表示可能）可能）

council.meaning: a group of people who are elected to govern an area such as a city or county（（市、郡等的）政务委员会，地方议会）；(BrE) the organization that provides services in a city or county, for example education, houses, libraries, etc.（市政（或地方管理）服务机构）；a group of people chosen to give advice, make rules, do research, provide money, etc.（（顾问、立法、研究、基金等）委员会）；(formal) (especially in the past) a formal meeting to discuss what action to take in a particular situation（（尤指旧时讨论特定步骤的）协商会议）

councillor.meaning: a member of a council（市议员；政务委员会委员）

counsel.meaning: (formal) advice, especially given by older people or experts; a piece of advice（（尤指年长者或专家的）劝告，忠告，建议）；(law 律) a lawyer or group of lawyers representing sb in court（辩护律师）；(formal) advice not to try to do sth because it is too difficult（知难而退的建议）；(formal) advice that is good but that is difficult or impossible to follow（听上去完美却难以实行的建议）

counsellor.meaning: a person who has been trained to advise people with problems, especially personal problems（（尤指针对私人问题的）顾问；辅导顾问）；(NAmE, IrishE) a lawyer（律师）；(NAmE) a person who is in charge of young people at a summer camp（夏令营负责人）

count.meaning: to say numbers in the correct order（（按顺序）数数）；to calculate the total number of people, things, etc. in a particular group（计算（或清点）总数）；to include sb/sth when you calculate a total（把 … 算入；包括）；(not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）

countable.meaning: a noun that is countable can be used in the plural or with a or an, for example table, cat and idea（（名词）可数的）

countdown.meaning: the action of counting seconds backwards to zero, for example before a spacecraft is launched（倒数读秒，倒计时（如发射宇宙飞船时））；the period of time just before sth important happens（大事临近的时期）

countenance.meaning: (formal or literary) a person's face or their expression（面容；脸色；面部表情）；(formal) to support sth or agree to sth happening（支持；赞成；同意）

counter.meaning: a long flat surface over which goods are sold or business is done in a shop/store, bank, etc.（（商店、银行等的）柜台）；a flat surface in a kitchen for preparing food on（（厨房的）操作台，料理台）；a small disc used for playing or scoring in some board games（（某些棋盘游戏的）筹码）；(especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）

counteract.meaning: to do sth to reduce or prevent the bad or harmful effects of sth（抵制；抵消；抵抗）

counterbalance.meaning: (formal) to have an equal but opposite effect to sth else（抗衡；抵消；对 … 起平衡作用）；a thing that has an equal but opposite effect to sth else and can be used to limit the bad effects of sth（平衡抵消物；平衡重（或块、锤））

counterclockwise.meaning: in the opposite direction to the movement of the hands of a clock（逆时针方向（的））

counterfeit.meaning: (of money and goods for sale（钱币及商品）；made to look exactly like sth in order to trick people into thinking that they are getting the real thing（伪造的；仿造的；假冒的）；coun·ter·feit noun ➔ compare forgery verb counterfeit~ sth (formal) to make an exact copy of sth in order to trick people into thinking that it is the real thing（伪造；仿造；制假）

countermand.meaning: (formal) to cancel an order that has been given, especially by giving a different order（取消，撤销（尤指代以不同的新命令或订单））

countermeasure.meaning: a course of action taken to protect against sth that is considered bad or dangerous（对策；对抗手段；反措施）

counterpart.meaning: a person or thing that has the same position or function as sb/sth else in a different place or situation（职位（或作用）相当的人；对应的事物）

countersign.meaning: (technical 术语) to sign a document that has already been signed by another person, especially in order to show that it is valid（连署，副署，会签（文件））

countless.meaning: very many; too many to be counted or mentioned（无数的；数不胜数的；数不尽的）

country.meaning: an area of land that has or used to have its own government and laws（国；国家）；(often following an adjective（常置于形容词后）；an area of land, especially with particular physical features, suitable for a particular purpose or connected with a particular person or people（（尤指具有某种自然特征、适于某目的或与某种人有关的）地区，区域）；the people of a country; the nation as a whole（全国人民；国民；全民）

countryside.meaning: land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods, etc.（乡村；农村）

county.meaning: an area of Britain, Ireland or the US that has its own government（（英国、爱尔兰的）郡；（美国的）县）；(BrE) (usually disapproving) typical of English upper-class people（典型英国上流社会人物的；世家子弟的）

couple.meaning: two people or things（两人；两件事物）；a small number of people or things（几个人；几件事物）；two people who are seen together, especially if they are married or in a romantic or sexual relationship（（人）一对；（尤指）夫妻，情侣）；a couple ★ /; NAmE/ pron. Do you need any more glasses? I've got a couple I can lend you.（你还需要玻璃杯吗？我有几个可以借给你。）

coupon.meaning: a small piece of printed paper that you can exchange for sth or that gives you the right to buy sth at a cheaper price than normal（配给券；（购物）票证，优惠券）；a printed form, often cut out from a newspaper, that is used to enter a competition, order goods, etc.（（常为剪自报章的）参赛表，订货单）

courage.meaning: the ability to do sth dangerous, or to face pain or opposition, without showing fear（勇气；勇敢；无畏；胆量）；to be/not be brave enough to do what you feel to be right（有/没有勇气做自己认为正确的事）；to begin to feel happier and more confident because of sth（（因某事而）鼓起勇气）；to make yourself do sth that you are afraid of（鼓起勇气（做自己害怕做的事）；敢作敢为）

courier.meaning: a person or company whose job is to take packages or important papers somewhere（（递送包裹或重要文件的）信使，通讯员，专递公司）；(BrE) a person who is employed by a travel company to give advice and help to a group of tourists on holiday（（旅游公司的）导游）；cour·ier verb courier~ sthCourier that letter — it needs to get there today (= send it by courier).（那封信必须今天到达，用专递寄吧。）

course.meaning: a series of lessons or lectures on a particular subject（（有关某学科的系列）课程，讲座）；(especially BrE) a period of study at a college or university that leads to an exam or a qualification（（学院或大学中要进行考试或取得资格的）课程）；a direction or route followed by a ship or an aircraft（（船或飞机的）航向，航线）；the general direction in which sb's ideas or actions are moving（方针；行动方向）

court.meaning: the place where legal trials take place and where crimes, etc. are judged（法院；法庭；审判庭）；the people in a court, especially those who make the decisions, such as the judge and jury（全体出庭人员；（尤指）全体审判人员）；a place where games such as tennis are played（（网球等的）球场）；the official place where kings and queens live（王宫；宫殿；宫廷）

courteous.meaning: polite, especially in a way that shows respect（有礼貌的；客气的；（尤指）恭敬的，谦恭的）

courtesy.meaning: polite behaviour that shows respect for other people（礼貌；谦恭；彬彬有礼）；(formal) a polite thing that you say or do when you meet people in formal situations（（正式场合见面时的）客气话，礼貌）；with the official permission of sb/sth and as a favour（承蒙 … 的允许（或好意））；given as a prize or provided free by a person or an organization（蒙 … 提供；赞助；赠送）

courtship.meaning: (old-fashioned) the time when two people have a romantic relationship before they get married; the process of developing this relationship（求爱期；求爱；追求）；the special way animals behave in order to attract a mate for producing young animals（（动物的）求偶）；(formal) the process or act of attracting a business partner, etc.（招商）

courtyard.meaning: an open space that is partly or completely surrounded by buildings and is usually part of a castle, a large house, etc.（（通常为城堡、大宅第等的）庭院，院子，天井）

cousin.meaning: a child of your aunt or uncle（同辈表亲（或堂亲）；堂兄（或弟、姊、妹）；表兄（或弟、姊、妹））；a person who is in your wider family but who is not closely related to you（远房亲戚；远亲）；a way of describing people from another country who are similar in some way to people in your own country（兄弟的 … 国人民（对与本民族有某些类似的另一国家人民的说法））；a way of describing things that are similar or related in some way（同族；同类）

cover.meaning: to place sth over or in front of sth in order to hide or protect it（掩蔽；遮盖）；to lie or spread over the surface of sth（盖；覆盖）；to put or spread a layer of liquid, dust, etc. on sb/sth（撒上，洒上，溅上（一层液体、尘土等））；to include sth; to deal with sth（包括；包含；涉及；处理）

coverage.meaning: the reporting of news and sport in newspapers and on the radio and television（新闻报道）；the range or quality of information that is included in a book or course of study, on television, etc.（（书、课程学习、电视等的）信息范围，信息质量）；the amount of sth that sth provides; the amount or way that sth covers an area（提供的数量；覆盖范围（或方式））；protection that an insurance company provides by promising to pay you money if a particular event happens（（保险公司的）保险）

covered.meaning: having a layer or amount of sth on it（盖着一层；盖满）；having a roof over it（有顶的）

covering.meaning: a layer of sth that covers sth else（（一层）覆盖层，遮盖物）；a layer of material such as carpet or wallpaper, used to cover, decorate and protect floors, walls, etc.（装饰（或保护）性覆盖物）；a piece of material that covers sth（覆盖某物的一块（或一片）材料）

cow.meaning: a large animal kept on farms to produce milk or beef（母牛；奶牛；菜牛；肉牛）；the female of the elephant, whale and some other large animals（雌象；雌鲸；某些大型雌性动物）；(slang, disapproving) an offensive word for a woman（婆娘；娘儿们）；(AustralE, NZE) an unpleasant person, thing or situation（讨厌的人（或事物、情况））

coward.meaning: a person who is not brave or who does not have the courage to do things that other people do not think are especially difficult（胆小鬼；懦夫；胆怯者）；cow·ard·ly /ˈkaʊədli; NAmEˈkaʊərdli/ adj. a cowardly attack on a defenceless man（欺负一个没有自卫能力的人的不光彩行为）

cowardice.meaning: fear or lack of courage（惧怕；胆小；懦弱）

cowboy.meaning: a man who rides a horse and whose job is to take care of cattle in the western parts of the US（（美国西部的）牛仔，骑马牧人）；a man like this as a character in a film/movie about the American West（（美国西部影片中的）牛仔）；(BrE) (informal, disapproving) a dishonest person in business, especially sb who produces work of bad quality or charges too high a price（（尤指产品质量差或索价太高的）奸商）

cowhand.meaning: a person whose job is taking care of cows（牧牛工；放牛人）

coyote.meaning: a N American wild animal of the dog family（丛林狼，草原狼（犬科动物，分布于北美））

crab.meaning: a sea creature with a hard shell, eight legs and two pincers (= curved and pointed arms for catching and holding things). Crabs move sideways on land.（蟹；螃蟹）；meat from a crab, used for food（蟹肉）；(informal) the condition caused by having lice (called crab lice) in the hair around the genitals（阴虱寄生病）

crack.meaning: to break without dividing into separate parts; to break sth in this way（破裂；裂开；断裂）；to break open or into pieces; to break sth in this way（砸开；破开；砸碎；打碎）；to hit sth/sb with a short hard blow（重击；猛击）；to make a sharp sound; to make sth do this（（使）发出爆裂声，劈啪作响）

cracked.meaning: damaged with lines in its surface but not completely broken（破裂的；有裂纹的）；(of sb's voice（嗓音）；sounding rough with sudden changes in how loud or high it is, because the person is upset（（因心烦意乱而突然）粗声的，沙哑的）；(informal) crazy（疯狂；发疯）

cracker.meaning: a thin dry biscuit that is often salty and usually eaten with cheese（薄脆饼干（多为咸味，常与干酪一起食用））；a tube of coloured paper that makes a loud explosive sound when it is pulled open by two people. Crackers usually contain a paper hat, a small present and a joke, and are used in Britain at Christmas parties and meals.（彩包爆竹，彩色拉炮（在英国用于圣诞聚会和聚餐，通常装有纸帽、小礼品及笑话纸条））；(BrE) (informal) something that you think is very good, funny, etc.（（认为）十分愉快的事，滑稽可笑的事）；(NAmE) (slang) an offensive word for a poor white person with little education from the southern US（（对几乎未受过教育的美国南方贫苦白人的轻蔑语）车把式）

cradle.meaning: a small bed for a baby which can be pushed gently from side to side（摇篮）；the place where sth important began（策源地；发源地；发祥地）；(BrE) a small platform that can be moved up and down the outside of a high building, used by people cleaning windows, etc.（（高楼外供清洁窗户等用的）吊架，托架，吊篮）；the part of a telephone on which the receiver rests（（电话机的）听筒架，叉托支架）

craft.meaning: an activity involving a special skill at making things with your hands（手艺；工艺）；all the skills needed for a particular activity（技巧；技能；技艺）；(formal, disapproving) skill in making people believe what you want them to believe（诡计；手腕；骗术）；(formal) a boat or ship（小船；船）

craftsman.meaning: a skilled person, especially one who makes beautiful things by hand（工匠；手艺人；工艺师）

craftsmanship.meaning: the level of skill shown by sb in making sth beautiful with their hands（手艺；技艺）；the quality of design and work shown by sth that has been made by hand（精工细作）

cram.meaning: to push or force sb/sth into a small space; to move into a small space with the result that it is full（把 … 塞进；挤满；塞满）；(NAmE, informal or rather old-fashioned, BrE) to learn a lot of things in a short time, in preparation for an exam（（为应考）临时死记硬背）

cramp.meaning: a sudden pain that you get when the muscles in a particular part of your body contract, usually caused by cold or too much exercise（痛性痉挛；抽筋）；severe pain in the stomach（（腹部）绞痛）；to prevent the development or progress of sb/sth（阻碍，阻止（发展或进步））；(informal) to stop sb from behaving in the way they want to（束缚 … 的手脚；使不能放开手脚（或施展才能））

crane.meaning: a tall machine with a long arm, used to lift and move building materials and other heavy objects（起重机；吊车）；a large bird with long legs and a long neck（鹤）；to lean or stretch over sth in order to see sth better; to stretch your neck（（为看得更清楚而）探着身子；伸长（脖子））

crash.meaning: an accident in which a vehicle hits sth, for example another vehicle, usually causing damage and often injuring or killing the passengers（撞车；碰撞；相撞）；a sudden loud noise made, for example, by sth falling or breaking（（倒下、破碎等突然的）碰撞声，破裂声，碎裂声）；a sudden serious fall in the price or value of sth; the occasion when a business, etc. fails（暴跌；倒闭；破产；失败）；a sudden failure of a machine or system, especially of a computer or computer system（（机器或系统，尤指计算机或计算机系统的）崩溃）

crate.meaning: a large wooden container for transporting goods（大木箱，板条箱（运货用））；a container made of plastic or metal divided into small sections, for transporting or storing bottles（塑料分格箱，金属分格箱（运送或存放瓶子用））；the amount of sth contained in a crate（一箱（的量））；to pack sth in a crate（把 … 装入大木箱（或板条箱、分格箱））

crater.meaning: a large hole in the top of a volcano（火山口）；a large hole in the ground caused by the explosion of a bomb or by sth large hitting it（（由炸弹爆炸或巨物撞击形成的）坑）

crave.meaning: to have a very strong desire for sth（渴望；热望）；(BrE) (old use) to ask for sth seriously（恳求；请求）

crawl.meaning: to move forward on your hands and knees, with your body close to the ground（爬；爬行；匍匐行进）；when an insect crawls, it moves forward on its legs（（昆虫）爬行）；to move forward very slowly（缓慢行进）；(informal, disapproving) to be too friendly or helpful to sb in authority, in a way that is not sincere, especially in order to get an advantage from them（卑躬屈膝；谄媚；巴结；拍马屁）

crayfish.meaning: an animal like a small lobster, that lives in rivers and lakes and can be eaten, or one like a large lobster, that lives in the sea and can be eaten（淡水螯虾；海水大龙虾）

crayon.meaning: a coloured pencil or stick of soft coloured chalk or wax, used for drawing（彩色铅笔（或粉笔、蜡笔））

craze.meaning: an enthusiastic interest in sth that is shared by many people but that usually does not last very long; a thing that people have a craze for（（通常为一时的）狂热，疯狂；风行一时的东西）

crazy.meaning: (especially NAmE) not sensible; stupid（不理智的；疯狂的；愚蠢的；傻的）；very angry（非常气愤）；(often in compounds（常构成复合词）；very enthusiastic or excited about sth（热衷的；狂热的）

cream.meaning: the thick pale yellowish-white fatty liquid that rises to the top of milk, used in cooking or as a type of sauce to put on fruit, etc.（奶油；乳脂）；(in compounds（构成复合词）；a sweet/candy that has a soft substance like cream inside（奶油夹心糖）；a soft substance or thick liquid used on your skin to protect it or make it feel soft; a similar substance used for cleaning things（护肤霜；洁净剂；清洗液）

creamy.meaning: thick and smooth like cream; containing a lot of cream（像奶油的；光滑细腻的；含乳脂的）；pale yellowish-white in colour（奶油色的；淡黄色的；米色的）

crease.meaning: an untidy line that is made in cloth or paper when it is pressed or crushed（褶痕；皱痕）；a neat line that you make in sth, for example when you fold it（褶缝；褶线）；a line in the skin, especially on the face（（皮肤上，尤指脸上的）皱纹）；(in cricket（板球）

create.meaning: to make sth happen or exist（创造；创作；创建）；to produce a particular feeling or impression（造成，引起，产生（感觉或印象））；to give sb a particular rank or title（授予；册封）

creation.meaning: the act or process of making sth that is new, or of causing sth to exist that did not exist before（创造；创建）；(often humorous) a thing that sb has made, especially sth that shows ability or imagination（作品；创作）；the making of the world, especially by God as described in the Bible（（尤指《圣经》所述由上帝）创造天地）；the world and all the living things in it（世界；天地万物）

creative.meaning: involving the use of skill and the imagination to produce sth new or a work of art（创造（性）的；创作的）；having the skill and ability to produce sth new, especially a work of art; showing this ability（有创造力的；（尤指艺术作品）创作的；表现创造力的）；cre·ative·ly AW /kriˈeɪtɪvli; NAmEkriˈeɪtɪvli/ adv. cre·ativ·ity AW /ˌkriːeɪˈtɪvəti; NAmEˌkriːeɪˈtɪvəti/ noun [U] Creativity and originality are more important than technical skill.（创意和原创性比专门技术更为重要。）；a person who is creative（富于创造力的人；搞创作的人）

creator.meaning: a person who has made or invented a particular thing（创造者；创作者；发明者）；God（造物主；上帝；天主）

creature.meaning: a living thing, real or imaginary, that can move around, such as an animal（生物；动物）；(especially following an adjective（尤置于形容词后）；a person, considered in a particular way（（具有某种特征的）人）；(formal, disapproving) a person or thing that depends completely on sb else and is controlled by them（傀儡）

credence.meaning: a quality that an idea or a story has that makes you believe it is true（可信性；真实性）；belief in sth as true（信任；信念）

credential.meaning: (NAmE) to provide sb with credentials（提供证明书（或证件））

credible.meaning: that can be believed or trusted（可信的；可靠的）；that can be accepted, because it seems possible that it could be successful（（因看似可能成功而）可接受的）；cred·ibly /ˈkredəbli; NAmEˈkredəbli/ adv. We can credibly describe the band's latest album as their best yet.（我们完全可以说，这支乐队的最新专辑是他们迄今的最佳作品。）

credit.meaning: an arrangement that you make, with a shop/store for example, to pay later for sth you buy（赊购；赊欠）；money that you borrow from a bank; a loan（（从银行借的）借款；贷款）；the status of being trusted to pay back money to sb who lends it to you（（借钱偿还的）信誉，信用）；if you or your bank account are in credit, there is money in the account（结余）

creditable.meaning: of a quite good standard and deserving praise or approval（值得赞扬的；应当认可的）；morally good（道德上好的；高尚的）

creditor.meaning: a person, company, etc. that sb owes money to（债权人；债主；贷方）

creditworthy.meaning: able to be trusted to pay back money that is owed; safe to lend money to（可信赖偿还借贷的；信誉好的；信用可靠的；借贷安全的）

creed.meaning: a set of principles or religious beliefs（信念；原则；纲领；宗教信仰）；a statement of Christian belief that is spoken as part of some church services（（基督教）信经）

creek.meaning: a member of a Native American people, many of whom now live in the US state of Oklahoma（克里克人（美洲土著，很多现居于美国俄克拉何马州））

creep.meaning: (of people or animals（人或动物）；to move slowly, quietly and carefully, because you do not want to be seen or heard（悄悄地缓慢行进；蹑手蹑脚地移动）；(NAmE) to move with your body close to the ground; to move slowly on your hands and knees（匍匐行进；爬行）；to move or develop very slowly（非常缓慢地行进；不知不觉产生；渐渐出现）

creeper.meaning: a plant that grows along the ground, up walls, etc., often winding itself around other plants（蔓生植物；攀缘植物）

crescent.meaning: a curved shape that is wide in the middle and pointed at each end（新月形；月牙形）；(often used in street names（常用于街道名称）；a curved street with a row of houses on it（新月形街区（一排房屋））；the curved shape that is used as a symbol of Islam（新月（伊斯兰教的象征））

crest.meaning: the top part of a hill or wave（山顶；顶峰；波峰；浪尖）；a design used as the symbol of a particular family, organization, etc., especially one that has a long history（（尤指象征历史悠久的家族、机构等的）饰章，纹章）；a group of feathers that stand up on top of a bird's head（鸟冠；羽冠）；a situation in which sb is very successful, happy, etc.（顶峰时期；极其成功；春风得意）

cretaceous.meaning: of the period between around 146 to 65 million years ago, when dinosaurs lived (until they died out); of the rocks formed during this time（白垩纪的；白垩（质）的）

crevice.meaning: a narrow crack in a rock or wall（（岩石或墙壁的）裂缝，裂隙，裂口）

crew.meaning: all the people working on a ship, plane, etc.（（轮船、飞机等上面的）全体工作人员）；all the people working on a ship, plane etc. except the officers who are in charge（（轮船、飞机等上面不包括高级职员的）全体船员，全体乘务员）；a group of people with special skills working together（技术人员团队；专业团队）；(usually disapproving) a group of people（一群（或一帮、一伙）人）

cricket.meaning: a game played on grass by two teams of 11 players. Players score points (called runs ) by hitting the ball with a wooden bat and running between two sets of vertical wooden sticks, called stumps.（板球（运动））；a small brown jumping insect that makes a loud high sound by rubbing its wings together（蟋蟀；蛐蛐）；(old-fashioned) (BrE informal) unfair; not honourable（不公正；不光明正大；不光彩；见不得人）

crime.meaning: activities that involve breaking the law（犯罪活动；不法行为）；an illegal act or activity that can be punished by law（罪；罪行）；(informal) an act that you think is immoral or is a big mistake（不道德的行为；罪过）

criminal.meaning: (rather formal or law 律) connected with or involving crime（犯罪的；犯法的；涉及犯罪的）；connected to the laws that deal with crime（刑法的；刑事的）；morally wrong（道德上错误的；不道德的）；a person who commits a crime（罪犯）

crimp.meaning: to make curls in sb's hair by pressing it with a heated tool（烫发；使（头发）拳曲；使（头发）成波形）；to press cloth or paper into small folds（把（织物或纸）压出皱纹；使起皱）；(NAmE) (informal) to restrict the growth or development of sth（阻止，妨碍（某事物的发展））；(NAmE) (informal) to have a bad or negative effect on sth（对 … 造成阻碍；对 … 有负面影响；损害）

crimson.meaning: dark red in colour（深红色的；暗红色的）

cripple.meaning: to damage sb's body so that they are no longer able to walk or move normally（使残废；使跛；使成瘸子）；to seriously damage or harm sb/sth（严重毁坏（或损害））；crip·pling /; NAmE/ adj. a crippling disease（严重损害健康的疾病）；(old-fashioned or offensive) a person who is unable to walk or move normally because of a disease or injury（伤残人；残疾人；跛子；瘸子）

crisis.meaning: a time of great danger, difficulty or confusion when problems must be solved or important decisions must be made（危机；危急关头）；a time when a problem, a bad situation or an illness is at its worst point（危难时刻；病危期）

crisp.meaning: (of food（食物）；pleasantly hard and dry（脆的；酥脆的）；(of fruit and vegetables（水果和蔬菜）；firm and fresh（鲜脆的；脆的）

criterion.meaning: a standard or principle by which sth is judged, or with the help of which a decision is made（（评判或作决定的）标准，准则，原则）

critic.meaning: a person who expresses opinions about the good and bad qualities of books, music, etc.（批评家；评论家；评论员）；a person who expresses disapproval of sb/sth and talks about their bad qualities, especially publicly（批评者；挑剔的人）

critical.meaning: expressing disapproval of sb/sth and saying what you think is bad about them（批评的；批判性的；挑剔的）；extremely important because a future situation will be affected by it（极重要的；关键的；至关紧要的）；serious, uncertain and possibly dangerous（严重的；不稳定的；可能有危险的）；involving making fair, careful judgements about the good and bad qualities of sb/sth（有判断力的；判断公正（或审慎）的）

criticism.meaning: the act of expressing disapproval of sb/sth and opinions about their faults or bad qualities; a statement showing disapproval（批评；批判；责备；指责）；the work or activity of making fair, careful judgements about the good and bad qualities of sb/sth, especially books, music, etc.（（尤指对书、音乐等的）评论文章，评论）

criticize.meaning: to say that you disapprove of sb/sth; to say what you do not like or think is wrong about sb/sth（批评；批判；挑剔；指责）；(BrE) to judge the good and bad qualities of sth（评论；评价）

crocodile.meaning: a large reptile with a long tail, hard skin and very big jaws. Crocodiles live in rivers and lakes in hot countries.（鳄鱼）；crocodile skin made into leather（（做成皮革的）鳄鱼皮）；(BrE) a long line of people, especially children, walking in pairs（成对纵列行进的人（尤指儿童））；if sb sheds (= cries) crocodile tears, they pretend to be sad about sth, but they are not really sad at all（鳄鱼的眼泪；假慈悲）

croissant.meaning: a small sweet roll with a curved shape, eaten especially at breakfast（羊角面包；新月形面包；（台）牛角面包）

crook.meaning: (informal) a dishonest person（骗子）；the place where your arm bends at the elbow（臂弯；肘弯）；a long stick with a hook at one end, used especially in the past by shepherds for catching sheep（（尤指旧时牧羊人捕羊的）曲柄杖）；to bend your finger or arm（使（手指或手臂）弯曲）

crooked.meaning: not in a straight line; bent or twisted（不直的；弯曲的；扭曲的）；dishonest（不诚实的；欺诈的）；(AustralE) (informal) annoyed（生（某人的）气）

crop.meaning: a plant that is grown in large quantities, especially as food（庄稼；作物）；the amount of grain, fruit, etc. that is grown in one season（（谷物、水果等一季的）收成，产量）；a group of people who do sth at the same time; a number of things that happen at the same time（（同时做某事的）一群人，一批人；（同时发生的）一些事情）；a short whip used by horse riders（（骑手的）短马鞭）

cross.meaning: a mark or an object formed by two lines crossing each other (X or +); the mark (X) is often used on paper to show sth（叉字形记号；十字形记号）；a long vertical piece of wood with a shorter piece across it near the top. In the past people were hung on crosses and left to die as a punishment.（（旧时用以处死人的）十字架）；the cross that Jesus Christ died on, used as a symbol of Christianity（（耶稣钉死在上面的）十字架）；an object, a design, a piece of jewellery, etc. in the shape of a cross, used as a symbol of Christianity（十字架物品（或设计、首饰等））

crossing.meaning: a place where you can safely cross a road, a river, etc., or from one country to another（（通过道路、河流等的）安全通行处；人行横道；渡口；（从一国到另一国的）过境处）；a place where two lines, two roads or two tracks cross（（线的）交叉点；（道路的）十字路口；（轨道的）交叉道口）；a journey across a sea or a wide river（（海洋或宽阔江河的）横渡）；an act of going from one side to another（穿越；横越）

crossroads.meaning: a place where two roads meet and cross each other（十字路口）；at an important point in sb's life or development（（人生或发展）处于关键时刻，在紧要关头）

crouch.meaning: to put your body close to the ground by bending your legs under you（蹲；蹲下；蹲伏）；crouched /; NAmE/ adj. She sat crouched in a corner.（她蹲坐在一个角落里。）；to bend over sb/sth so that you are very close to them or it（俯身接近）；a crouching position（蹲着的姿势）

crow.meaning: a member of a Native American people, many of whom live in the US state of Montana（克劳人（美洲土著，很多居于美国蒙大拿州））

crowbar.meaning: a straight iron bar, usually with a curved end, used for forcing open boxes and moving heavy objects（铁撬棍）

crowd.meaning: a large number of people gathered together in a public place, for example in the streets or at a sports game（人群；观众）；(informal, often disapproving) a particular group of people（一伙人；一帮人）；(sometimes disapproving) ordinary people, not special or unusual in any way（群众；民众；老百姓；凡夫俗子）；to fill a place so there is little room to move（挤满；塞满；使 … 拥挤）

crowded.meaning: having a lot of people or too many people（人（太）多的；拥挤的）；full of sth（充满的；挤满的）

crown.meaning: an object in the shape of a circle, usually made of gold and precious stones, that a king or queen wears on his or her head on official occasions（王冠；皇冠；冕）；the government of a country, thought of as being represented by a king or queen（王国政府；王国）；the position or power of a king or queen（王位；王权）；a circle of flowers, leaves, etc. that is worn on sb's head, sometimes as a sign of victory（花冠（戴在头上，有时象征胜利））

crucial.meaning: extremely important, because it will affect other things（至关重要的；关键性的）；cru·cial·ly AW /ˈkruːʃəli; NAmEˈkruːʃəli/ adv. crucially important（极其重要）

crucible.meaning: a pot in which substances are heated to high temperatures, metals are melted, etc.（坩埚；熔炉）；(formal or literary) a place or situation in which people or ideas are tested severely, often creating sth new or exciting in the process（熔炉；严峻的考验；磨练）

crude.meaning: simple and not very accurate but giving a general idea of sth（粗略的；简略的；大概的）；(of objects or works of art（物体或艺术品）；simply made, not showing much skill or attention to detail（粗糙的；粗制的）；(of people or the way they behave（人或行为方式）

cruel.meaning: having a desire to cause pain and suffering（残酷的；冷酷的；残忍的；残暴的）；causing pain or suffering（引起痛苦的）；cruel·ly /ˈkruːəli; NAmEˈkruːəli/ adv. The dog had been cruelly treated.（那条狗受过虐待。）

cruelty.meaning: behaviour that causes pain or suffering to others, especially deliberately（（尤指蓄意的）残酷，残忍，残暴）；a cruel action（残暴的行为）；something that happens that seems unfair（不公；不平）

cruise.meaning: a journey by sea, visiting different places, especially as a holiday/vacation（乘船游览；航行）；to travel in a ship or boat visiting different places, especially as a holiday/vacation（乘船游览）；(of a car, plane, etc.（汽车、飞机等）；to travel at a steady speed（以平稳的速度行驶）

cruiser.meaning: a large fast ship used in war（巡洋舰）；a boat with a motor and room for people to sleep, used for pleasure trips（（可供住宿的）舱式游艇）；(NAmE) a police car（巡逻警车）

crumb.meaning: a very small piece of food, especially of bread or cake, that has fallen off a larger piece（食物碎屑；（尤指）面包屑，糕饼屑）；a small piece or amount（一点；少许；少量）

crumble.meaning: to break or break sth into very small pieces（（使）破碎，成碎屑）；if a building or piece of land is crumbling, parts of it are breaking off（坍塌；损坏；崩裂）；to begin to fail or get weaker or to come to an end（（开始渐渐）衰退，衰弱；崩溃；瓦解；消亡）；a dessert (= a sweet dish) made from fruit that is covered with a rough mixture of flour, butter and sugar, cooked in the oven and usually served hot（酥皮水果甜点）

crumple.meaning: to crush sth into folds; to become crushed into folds（压皱；（使）变皱，起皱）；if your face crumples, you look sad and disappointed, as if you might cry（（脸部）沮丧地皱起，哭丧着）；to fall down in an uncontrolled way because you are injured, unconscious, drunk, etc.（（因受伤、失去知觉、喝醉而）瘫倒）；crump·led /; NAmE/ adj. crumpled clothes/papers（皱巴巴的衣服/纸张）

crunch.meaning: a noise like the sound of sth firm being crushed（压碎声；碎裂声）；(informal) an important and often unpleasant situation or piece of information（紧要关头；困境；症结；令人不快的重要消息）；(especially NAmE) a situation in which there is suddenly not enough of sth, especially money（（突发的）不足，短缺；（尤指）缺钱）；to crush sth noisily between your teeth when you are eating（嘎吱嘎吱地嚼）

crush.meaning: to press or squeeze sth so hard that it is damaged or injured, or loses its shape（压坏；压伤；挤压变形）；to push or press sb/sth into a small space（把 … 挤入，将 … 塞进（狭小的空间内））；to break sth into small pieces or into a powder by pressing hard（压碎；捣碎；碾成粉末）；to become or make sth full of folds or lines（（使）变皱，起皱）

crust.meaning: the hard outer surface of bread（面包皮）；a layer of pastry, especially on top of a pie（糕饼（尤指馅饼）酥皮）；a hard layer or surface, especially above or around sth soft or liquid（（尤指软物或液体上面、周围的）硬层，硬表面）

crustacean.meaning: any creature with a soft body that is divided into sections, and a hard outer shell. Most crustaceans live in water. Crabs, lobsters and shrimps are all crustaceans.（甲壳纲动物（如螃蟹、龙虾和褐虾））

crutch.meaning: one of two long sticks that you put under your arms to help you walk after you have injured your leg or foot（（腿或脚受伤病人用的）腋杖）；(usually disapproving) a person or thing that gives you help or support but often makes you depend on them too much（依靠；依赖）

cry.meaning: to produce tears from your eyes because you are unhappy or hurt（哭；哭泣）；to shout loudly（喊叫；呼喊；呼叫）；(of a bird or an animal（鸟或动物）；to make a loud unpleasant noise（发出刺耳的叫声；嗥叫；吠）

cryptic.meaning: with a meaning that is hidden or not easily understood（含义隐晦的；晦涩难懂的）；cryp·tic·al·ly /ˈkrɪptɪkli; NAmEˈkrɪptɪkli/ adv. ‘Yes and no,’ she replied cryptically.（“又是又不是。”她回答得很隐晦。）

crystal.meaning: a small piece of a substance with many even sides, that is formed naturally when the substance becomes solid（结晶；晶体）；a clear mineral, such as quartz, used in making jewellery and decorative objects（水晶（如石英，用于制作珠宝饰物））；glass of very high quality（水晶玻璃）；(NAmE) a piece of glass or plastic that covers the face of a watch（石英玻璃表护面；塑料表护面；表蒙子）

crystalline.meaning: (technical 术语) made of or similar to crystals（结晶的；水晶制的；晶状的）；(formal) very clear（清澈的；透明的；晶莹的）

cuban.meaning: from or connected with Cuba（古巴的）；a person from Cuba（古巴人）

cube.meaning: a solid or hollow figure with six equal square sides（立方体；立方形）；a piece of sth, especially food, with six sides（立方形的东西（尤指食物））；(mathematics 数) the number that you get when you multiply a number by itself twice（立方；三次幂）；(mathematics 数) to multiply a number by itself twice（求 … 的立方）

cubic.meaning: used to show that a measurement is the volume of sth, that is the height multiplied by the length and the width（立方的）；measured or expressed in cubic units（用立方单位度量（或表示）的）；having the shape of a cube（立方形的）

danger.meaning: the possibility of sth happening that will injure, harm or kill sb, or damage or destroy sth（危险；风险）；the possibility of sth bad or unpleasant happening（（坏事或不快之事发生的）可能性，危险）；a person or thing that may cause damage, or harm sb（危险的人；危险因素；危害；威胁）；(BrE) to be so ill/sick that you may die; to no longer be very ill/sick（病危；病入膏肓；病势危急（或好转）；（病人）转危为安）

dangerous.meaning: likely to injure or harm sb, or to damage or destroy sth（有危险的；引起危险的；不安全的）；dan·ger·ous·ly /ˈdeɪndʒərəsli; NAmEˈdeɪndʒərəsli/ adv. dangle.meaning: to hang or swing freely（悬垂；悬挂；悬荡；悬摆）；to hold sth so that it hangs or swings freely（提着（某物，任其自然下垂或摆动）；来回摆动着）；dan·gly /ˈdæŋɡli; NAmEˈdæŋɡli/ adj. a pair of dangly earrings（一对耳坠）；(informal) to keep sb in an uncertain state by not telling them sth that they want to know（（不对人言明而）使心里没底，使无把握，使拿不准）

danish.meaning: from or connected with Denmark（丹麦的）；the language of Denmark（丹麦语）

dare.meaning: (not usually used in the progressive tenses（通常不用于进行时）；to be brave enough to do sth（敢于；胆敢）；to persuade sb to do sth dangerous, difficult or embarrassing so that they can show that they are not afraid（激（某人做某事）；问（某人）有没有胆量（做某事）；谅（某人）没胆量（做某事））；(informal) used to tell sb strongly not to do sth（（让人绝不要做某事）你敢，谅你不敢）

daring.meaning: brave; willing to do dangerous or unusual things; involving danger or taking risks（勇敢的；敢于冒险的）；dar·ing·ly /ˈdeərɪŋli; NAmEˈderɪŋli/ adv. noun [U] courage and the willingness to take risks（大胆；勇敢；胆量）

dark.meaning: with no or very little light, especially because it is night（黑暗的；昏暗的；阴暗的）；not light; closer in shade to black than to white（深色的；暗色的）；having a colour that is close to black（近乎黑色的）；brown or black in colour（褐色的；黝黑的；乌黑的）

darken.meaning: to become dark; to make sth dark（（使）变暗，变黑）；to become unhappy or angry; to make sb unhappy or angry（（使）忧郁，生气，不快）；(old-fashioned, humorous) used to tell sb never to come to your home again（再不要跨进我的门槛；再不许踏进我的家门）

darkness.meaning: the state of being dark, without any light（黑暗；阴暗；漆黑）；the quality or state of being dark in colour（墨色；暗色；深色）；(literary) evil（邪恶；罪恶）

darling.meaning: (informal) a way of addressing sb that you love（亲爱的；宝贝）；a person who is very friendly and kind（亲切友好的人）；a person who is especially liked and very popular（备受宠爱的人；宠儿）；(informal) much loved; very attractive, special, etc.（备受喜爱的；可爱的；迷人的）

darn.meaning: to repair a hole in a piece of clothing by sewing stitches across the hole（织补；缝补）；(informal) (especially NAmE) used as a mild swear word to show that you are angry or annoyed about sth, to avoid saying ‘damn’（见鬼，真气人，真糟糕（婉辞，与 damn 同义））；(informal) (especially NAmE) used to show that you are surprised about sth（（表示吃惊）真没想到，真叫我吃惊）；a place on a piece of clothing that has been repaired by darning（织补处）

dart.meaning: a small pointed object, sometimes with feathers to help it fly, that is shot as a weapon or thrown in the game of darts（镖；飞镖）；a game in which darts are thrown at a round board marked with numbers for scoring. dash.meaning: an act of going somewhere suddenly and/or quickly（猛冲；突进；急奔）；an act of doing sth quickly because you do not have enough time（匆忙；匆促；仓促）；a small amount of sth that is added to sth else（少量，少许（添加物））；the mark ( — ) used to separate parts of a sentence, often instead of a colon or in pairs instead of brackets/parentheses（破折号）

data.meaning: facts or information, especially when examined and used to find out things or to make decisions（数据；资料；材料）；information that is stored by a computer（（贮存在计算机中的）数据资料）

date.meaning: a particular day of the month, sometimes in a particular year, given in numbers and words（日期；日子）；a time in the past or future that is not a particular day（年代；时期；时候）；(BrE) an arrangement to meet sb at a particular time（会晤时间；约见时间）；a meeting that you have arranged with a boyfriend or girlfriend or with sb who might become a boyfriend or girlfriend（约会；幽会）

datum.meaning: a fact or piece of information（数据；资料）

daughter.meaning: a person's female child（女儿）；(literary) a woman who belongs to a particular place or country, etc.（（某地、某国等的）妇女）

daughter-in-law.meaning: the wife of your son（儿媳妇）

daunt.meaning: to make sb feel nervous and less confident about doing sth（使胆怯；使气馁；使失去信心）；daunt·ing /dɔːntɪŋ; NAmEdɔːntɪŋ/ adj. IDM nothing ˈdaunted (BrE) (formal) confident about sth difficult you have to do（无所畏惧；毫不气馁）

dawn.meaning: the time of day when light first appears（黎明；拂晓；破晓）；the beginning or first signs of sth（开端；曙光；萌芽）；(of a day or a period of time（一天或一个时期）；to begin（开始）

day.meaning: a period of 24 hours（一天；一日）；the time between when it becomes light in the morning and when it becomes dark in the evening（白昼；白天）；the hours of the day when you are awake, working, etc.（工作日；一天的活动时间）；a particular period of time or history（时期；时代）

daybreak.meaning: the time of day when light first appears（黎明；拂晓；破晓；天亮）

daylight.meaning: the light that comes from the sun during the day（日光）；(informal) the fact of sb charging too much money for sth（漫天要价；敲竹杠）

daytime.meaning: the period during the day between the time when it gets light and the time when it gets dark（白天；白昼；日间）

daze.meaning: in a confused state（迷茫；茫然；恍惚）

dazzle.meaning: if a strong light dazzles you, it is so bright that you cannot see for a short time（（强光等）使目眩，使眼花）；to impress sb a lot with your beauty, skill, etc.（（美貌、技能等）使倾倒，使赞叹不已，使眼花缭乱）；daz·zling /; NAmE/ adj. dead.meaning: no longer alive（死的；失去生命的；枯萎的）；no longer believed in or aimed for（不再有人相信（或争取））；belonging to the past; no longer practised or fashionable（过时的；已废弃的；不流行的）；(informal) finished; not able to be used any more（用完了的；不能再用的）

deadly.meaning: causing or likely to cause death（（可能）致命的，致死的）；extreme; complete（极度的；十足的；彻底的）；extremely effective, so that no defence is possible（非常有效的；无法防御的）；(informal) very boring（枯燥的；令人厌烦的）

deaf.meaning: unable to hear anything or unable to hear very well（聋的）；people who cannot hear（耳聋的人；聋子）；not willing to listen or pay attention to sth（不愿听；不去注意）；deaf·ness /defnəs; NAmEdefnəs/ noun [U] IDM (as) ˌdeaf as a ˈpost (informal) very deaf（全聋；聋得什么也听不见）

deafen.meaning: to make sb unable to hear the sounds around them because there is too much noise（使震得耳朵发聋）；to make sb deaf（使聋；使听不见）

deal.meaning: to give cards to each player in a game of cards（发牌）；to buy and sell illegal drugs（非法买卖毒品；贩毒）；to be very shocking or harmful to sb/sth（令 … 震惊；给 … 以打击；使 … 受到伤害）；to hit sb/sth（给 … 一击；打击）

dealer.meaning: a person whose business is buying and selling a particular product（交易商；贸易商）；a person who sells illegal drugs（贩毒者；毒品贩子）；the person who gives out the cards in a card game（（纸牌游戏的）发牌者）

dealing.meaning: business activities; the relations that you have with sb in business（（商业）活动，往来）；a way of doing business with sb（经营作风；经营方式）；buying and selling（买卖；交易）

dean.meaning: (in the Anglican Church（圣公会）；a priest of high rank who is in charge of the other priests in a cathedral（座堂主任牧师）；(BrE) a priest who is in charge of the priests of several churches in an area（（乡间主管若干教堂牧师的）主任牧师）；a person in a university who is in charge of a department of studies（（大学的）学院院长，系主任）

dear.meaning: loved by or important to sb（亲爱的；宝贵的；珍视的）；used at the beginning of a letter before the name or title of the person that you are writing to（（用于信函抬头的名字或头衔前）亲爱的）；(BrE) expensive; costing a lot of money（昂贵；价格高）；(BrE) used to describe sb in a way that shows affection（（表示亲昵喜爱）亲爱的）

dearth.meaning: a lack of sth; the fact of there not being enough of sth（缺乏；不足）

death.meaning: the fact of sb dying or being killed（死；死亡）；the end of life; the state of being dead（生命的终止；死亡状态）；the permanent end or destruction of sth（永久的灭亡；毁灭；破灭）；(literary) the power that destroys life, imagined as human in form（死神）

debatable.meaning: not certain because people can have different ideas and opinions about the thing being discussed（可争辩的；有争议的）

debate.meaning: a formal discussion of an issue at a public meeting or in a parliament. debit.meaning: a written note in a bank account or other financial record of a sum of money owed or spent（借记；借方；收方）；a sum of money taken from a bank account（借项）；when a bank debits an account, it takes money from it（记入（账户）的借方；借记）

debt.meaning: a sum of money that sb owes（借款；欠款；债务）；the situation of owing money, especially when you cannot pay（负债情况）；the fact that you should feel grateful to sb because they have helped you or been kind to you（人情债；情义；恩情）；(formal) to feel grateful to sb for their help, kindness, etc.（欠某人的人情债；受某人的恩惠；感激某人）

debtor.meaning: a person, a country or an organization that owes money（债务人；借方）

debut.meaning: the first public appearance of a performer or sports player（（演员、运动员的）首次亮相；初次登台（或上场））；(of a performer or show（演员或表演等）；to make a first public appearance（首次亮相；初次登台）；(especially NAmE) (business 商) to present a new product or advertising campaign to the market（推出，首发（新产品、广告宣传））

decade.meaning: a period of ten years, especially a continuous period, such as 1910–1919 or 2000–2009（十年，十年期（尤指一个年代））

decease.meaning: the death of a person（死亡；亡故）

deceased.meaning: dead（死去了的；已死的；亡故的）；a person who has died, especially recently（死者；已故者）

deceit.meaning: dishonest behaviour that is intended to make sb believe sth that is not true; an example of this behaviour（欺骗，欺诈（行为）；诡计）

deceive.meaning: to make sb believe sth that is not true（欺骗；蒙骗；诓骗）；to refuse to admit to yourself that sth unpleasant is true（欺骗（自己））；to make sb have a wrong idea about sb/sth（使人误信；误导）

december.meaning: the 12th and last month of the year（十二月）

decent.meaning: of a good enough standard or quality（像样的；相当不错的；尚好的）；(of people or behaviour（人或行为举止）；honest and fair; treating people with respect（正派的；公平的；合乎礼节的）；acceptable to people in a particular situation（得体的；合宜的；适当的）

deception.meaning: the act of deliberately making sb believe sth that is not true (= of deceiving them)（欺骗；蒙骗；诓骗）；a trick intended to make sb believe sth that is not true（诡计；骗术；骗局）

deceptive.meaning: likely to make you believe sth that is not true（欺骗性的；误导的；骗人的）；de·cep·tive·ly /dɪˈseptɪvli; NAmEdɪˈseptɪvli/ adv. a deceptively simple idea（貌似简单的想法）

decide.meaning: to think carefully about the different possibilities that are available and choose one of them（对 … 作出抉择；决定；选定）；(law 律) to make an official or legal judgement（裁决；判决）；to affect the result of sth（影响（或决定）… 的结果）；to be the reason why sb does sth（成为（某人）做某事的原因）

decided.meaning: obvious and definite（明显的；明白无误的；确实无疑的）；(especially BrE) having very strong opinions（坚定的；坚决的；果断的）

decidedly.meaning: (used with an adjective or adverb（与形容词或副词连用）；definitely and in an obvious way（确实；肯定；显然）；(BrE) in a way that shows that you are sure and determined about sth（果断地；坚决地；坚定地）

deciduous.meaning: (of a tree, bush etc.（树、灌木等）；that loses its leaves every year（落叶的）

decimal.meaning: based on or counted in tens or tenths（十进位的；小数的）；a fraction (= a number less than one) that is shown as a dot or point followed by the number of tenths, hundredths, etc.（小数）

decipher.meaning: to succeed in finding the meaning of sth that is difficult to read or understand（破译，辨认（难认、难解的东西））

decision.meaning: a choice or judgement that you make after thinking and talking about what is the best thing to do（（作出的）决定，抉择）；the ability to decide sth clearly and quickly（决断（力）；果断）；the process of deciding sth（作决定；决策）

decision-making.meaning: the process of deciding about sth important, especially in a group of people or in an organization（决策）

deck.meaning: the top outside floor of a ship or boat（甲板；舱面）；one of the floors of a ship or a bus（（船或公共汽车的）一层，层面）；(both especially NAmE) a complete set of 52 playing cards（一副（52 张纸牌））；a wooden floor that is built outside the back of a house where you can sit and relax（（屋后供憩息的）木制平台）

declaration.meaning: an official or formal statement, especially about the plans of a government or an organization; the act of making such a statement（公告；宣告；宣言）；a written or spoken statement, especially about what people feel or believe（声明（书）；宣布；表白；宣称）；an official written statement giving information（申报（单））

declarative.meaning: (of a sentence（句子）；in the form of a simple statement（陈述的）

declare.meaning: to say sth officially or publicly（公布；宣布；宣告）；to state sth firmly and clearly（表明；宣称；断言）；to tell the tax authorities how much money you have earned（申报（收益））；to tell customs officers (= at the border of a country) that you are carrying goods on which you should pay tax（申报（应纳税品））

decline.meaning: a continuous decrease in the number, value, quality, etc. of sth（（数量、价值、质量等的）减少，下降，衰落，衰退）；(rather formal) to become smaller, fewer, weaker, etc.（减少；下降；衰弱；衰退）；(formal) to refuse politely to accept or to do sth（谢绝；婉言拒绝）；(grammar 语法) if a noun, an adjective or a pronoun declines, it has different forms according to whether it is the subject or the object of a verb, whether it is in the singular or plural, etc. When you decline a noun, etc., you list these forms.（（根据名词、形容词或代词在句中的作用）变格，使发生词形变化）

decode.meaning: to find the meaning of sth, especially sth that has been written in code（解（码）；破译（尤指密码））；to receive an electronic signal and change it into pictures that can be shown on a television screen（译解（电子信号））；(linguistics 语言) to understand the meaning of sth in a foreign language（译解，理解（外文））

decor.meaning: the style in which the inside of a building is decorated（（建筑内部的）装饰布局，装饰风格）

decorate.meaning: to make sth look more attractive by putting things on it（装饰；装潢）；(especially BrE) to put paint, wallpaper, etc. on the walls and ceilings of a room or house（粉刷；油漆；糊墙纸）；to be placed on sth in order to make it look more attractive（点缀；装点）；to give sb a medal as a sign of respect for sth they have done（授给（某人）勋章（或奖章））

decoration.meaning: a thing that makes sth look more attractive on special occasions（装饰品）；a pattern, etc. that is added to sth and that stops it from being plain（装饰图案）；the style in which sth is decorated（装饰风格）；(BrE) the act or process of decorating sth such as the inside of a house by painting it, etc.（（房屋内部等的）装饰，装潢）

decorative.meaning: (of an object or a building（物体或建筑）；decorated in a way that makes it attractive; intended to look attractive or pretty（装饰性的；作装饰用的）

decorator.meaning: a person whose job is painting and decorating houses（（房屋的）油漆匠，裱糊匠）

decrease.meaning: (rather formal) to become or make sth become smaller in size, number, etc.（（使大小、数量等）减少，减小，降低）；the process of reducing sth or the amount that sth is reduced by（减少；降低；减少量）

decree.meaning: an official order from a ruler or a government that becomes the law（法令；政令）；a decision that is made in court（（法院的）裁定，判决）；to decide, judge or order sth officially（裁定；判决；颁布）

decrepit.meaning: (of a thing or person（物或人）；very old and not in good condition or health（衰老的；老朽的；破旧的）

democracy.meaning: a system of government in which all the people of a country can vote to elect their representatives（民主；民主政体；民主制度）；a country which has this system of government（民主国家）；fair and equal treatment of everyone in an organization, etc., and their right to take part in making decisions（民主精神；民主权利；民主）

democrat.meaning: a person who believes in or supports democracy（民主主义者）；a member or supporter of the Democratic Party of the US（（美国）民主党党员，民主党人，民主党支持者）

democratic.meaning: (of a country, state, system, etc.（国家、政府、制度等）；controlled by representatives who are elected by the people of a country; connected with this system（民主的；民主政体的；民主制度的）；based on the principle that all members have an equal right to be involved in running an organization, etc.（民主权利的）；connected with the Democratic Party in the US（（美国）民主党的）

demographic.meaning: (statistics 统计) data relating to the population and different groups within it（人口统计数据）；(business 商) a group of customers who are of a similar age, the same sex, etc.（同类客户群体）；relating to the population and different groups within it（人口的；人口学的）

demography.meaning: the changing number of births, deaths, diseases, etc. in a community over a period of time; the scientific study of these changes（人口统计；人口统计学；人口学）

demolish.meaning: to pull or knock down a building（拆毁，拆除（建筑物））；to destroy sth accidentally（（意外）毁坏，破坏）；to show that an idea or theory is completely wrong（推翻，驳倒（观点或理论））；to defeat sb easily and completely（轻易战胜；彻底打败）

demonstrate.meaning: to show sth clearly by giving proof or evidence（证明；证实；论证；说明）；to show by your actions that you have a particular quality, feeling or opinion（表达；表露；表现；显露）；to show and explain how sth works or how to do sth（示范；演示）；to take part in a public meeting or march, usually as a protest or to show support for sth（游行示威）

demonstration.meaning: a public meeting or march at which people show that they are protesting against or supporting sb/sth（游行示威）；an act of showing or explaining how sth works or is done（示范；示范表演；演示）；an act of giving proof or evidence for sth（证明；证实；论证；说明）；an act of showing a feeling or an opinion（表达；表露；表现；显露）

demonstrative.meaning: showing feelings openly, especially feelings of affection（公开表露感情（尤指爱慕之情）的；感情外露的）；(grammar 语法) used to identify the person or thing that is being referred to（指示的）；de·mon·stra·tive·ly AW /; NAmE/ adv. noun (grammar 语法) a demonstrative pronoun or determiner（指示代词；限定词；（台）指示代名词）

den.meaning: the hidden home of some types of wild animal（兽穴；兽窝）；(disapproving) a place where people meet in secret, especially for some illegal or immoral activity（窝点，窝子（尤指非法或邪恶活动秘密聚会处））；(NAmE) a room in a house where people go to relax, watch television, etc.（休息室）；(old-fashioned) (BrE informal) a room in a house where a person can work or study without being disturbed（书斋；书房）

denial.meaning: a statement that says sth is not true or does not exist（否认；否定）；a refusal to allow sb to have sth they have a right to expect（拒绝给予，剥夺（应有的权利））；(psychology 心) a refusal to accept that sth unpleasant or painful is true（拒绝接受，拒不承认（令人不快、痛苦的事））

denominate.meaning: to express an amount of money using a particular unit（以（某种货币）为单位）；(formal) to give sth a particular name or description（将 … 命名为；称 … 为）

denomination.meaning: a branch of the Christian Church（（基督教）教派，宗派）；a unit of value, especially of money（（尤指钱的）面额，面值）

denote.meaning: to be a sign of sth（标志；预示；象征）；to mean sth（表示；意指）

denounce.meaning: to strongly criticize sb/sth that you think is wrong, illegal, etc.（谴责；指责；斥责）；to tell the police, the authorities, etc. about sb's illegal political activities（告发（某人从事非法政治活动））

dense.meaning: containing a lot of people, things, plants, etc. with little space between them（密集的；稠密的）；difficult to see through（浓密的；浓重的）；(informal) stupid（愚笨的；迟钝的；笨拙的）；difficult to understand because it contains a lot of information（（信息量大得）难理解的，难懂的）

density.meaning: the quality of being dense; the degree to which sth is dense（密集；稠密；密度；浓度）；(physics 物) the thickness of a solid, liquid or gas measured by its mass per unit of volume（密度（固体、液体或气体单位体积的质量））；(computing 计) the amount of space available on a disk for recording data（密度（磁盘存贮数据的可用空间））

dent.meaning: to make a hollow place in a hard surface, usually by hitting it（使凹陷；使产生凹痕）；to damage sb's confidence, reputation, etc.（损害，伤害，挫伤（信心、名誉等））；a hollow place in a hard surface, usually caused by sth hitting it（凹痕；凹坑；凹部）；to reduce the amount of sth, especially money（减少，削减（尤指资金））

dental.meaning: connected with teeth（牙齿的；牙科的）；(of a consonant（辅音）；produced with the tongue against the upper front teeth, for example /θ/ and /ð/ in thin and this（齿音的）

dentist.meaning: a person whose job is to take care of people's teeth（牙科医生）；a place where a dentist sees patients（牙科诊所）

deny.meaning: to say that sth is not true（否认；否定）；to refuse to admit or accept sth（拒绝承认；拒绝接受）；(formal) to refuse to allow sb to have sth that they want or ask for（拒绝；拒绝给予）；(formal) to refuse to let yourself have sth that you would like to have, especially for moral or religious reasons（（尤因道德或宗教原因）节制，克制，戒绝）

depart.meaning: to leave a place, especially to start a trip（离开；离去；起程；出发）；(NAmE) to leave your job（离职）；to die. People say ‘depart this life’ to avoid saying ‘die’.（离开人世，去世，亡故（委婉说法，与 die 同义））；to behave in a way that is different from usual（违反，背离（常规））

department.meaning: a section of a large organization such as a government, business, university, etc.（部；司；局；处；系；（医院的）科；部门）；(informal) to be sth that sb is responsible for or knows a lot about（某人的职责范围（或知识范围））

departure.meaning: the act of leaving a place; an example of this（离开；起程；出发）；a plane, train, etc. leaving a place at a particular time（（在特定时间）离开的飞机（或火车等））；an action that is different from what is usual or expected（背离；违反；逾越）

depend.meaning: according to（视乎；决定于）；used to say that you are not certain about sth because other things have to be considered（那得看情况）；to rely on sb/sth and be able to trust them（依靠；信赖）；to be sure or expect that sth will happen（确信；相信；指望）

dependable.meaning: that can be relied on to do what you want or need（可信赖的；可靠的）

dependant.meaning: a person, especially a child, who depends on another person for a home, food, money, etc.（受扶养者（尤指孩子）；靠他人生活者；受扶养的家属）

dependence.meaning: the state of needing the help and support of sb/sth in order to survive or be successful（（生存或成功必需的）依靠，依赖，依存）；the state of being addicted to sth (= unable to stop taking or using it)（瘾）；(technical 术语) the fact of one thing being affected by another（相关（性）；相依（性））

dependent.meaning: needing sb/sth in order to survive or be successful（依靠的；依赖的）；addicted to sth (= unable to stop taking or using it)（有瘾的）；(formal) affected or decided by sth（受 … 的影响；取决于）

depict.meaning: to show an image of sb/sth in a picture（描绘；描画）；to describe sth in words, or give an impression of sth in words or with a picture（描写；描述；刻画）；de·pic·tion depiction depictions /dɪˈpɪkʃn; NAmEdɪˈpɪkʃn/ noun [U, C] They object to the movie's depiction of gay people.（他们反对这部影片对同性恋者的刻画。）

deplete.meaning: (formal) to reduce sth by a large amount so that there is not enough left（大量减少；耗尽；使枯竭）；de·ple·tion depletion depletions /dɪˈpliːʃn; NAmEdɪˈpliːʃn/ noun [U] ozone depletion（臭氧耗损）

deplorable.meaning: very bad and unacceptable, often in a way that shocks people（糟透的；令人震惊的；令人愤慨的）；de·plor·ably /dɪˈplɔːrəbli; NAmEdɪˈplɔːrəbli/ adv. They behaved deplorably.（他们的表现糟透了。）

deplore.meaning: (formal) to strongly disapprove of sth and criticize it, especially publicly（公开谴责；强烈反对）

deposit.meaning: a sum of money that is given as the first part of a larger payment（订金；订钱）；a sum of money that is paid by sb when they rent sth and that is returned to them if they do not lose or damage the thing they are renting（押金）；a sum of money that is paid into a bank account（存款）；(in the British political system) the amount of money that a candidate in an election to Parliament has to pay, and that is returned if he/she gets enough votes（竞选保证金（英国议员候选人预付，获得足够的票数则退还））

deposition.meaning: (technical 术语) the natural process of leaving a layer of a substance on rocks or soil; a substance left in this way（沉积（物）；沉淀（物）；淤积（物））；the act of removing sb, especially a ruler, from power（罢免；废黜）；(law 律) a formal statement, taken from sb and used in court（证词；口供书）

depositor.meaning: a person who puts money in a bank account（储户；存户）

depot.meaning: a place where large amounts of food, goods or equipment are stored（（大量物品的）贮藏处，仓库）；(BrE) a place where buses or other vehicles are kept and repaired（车库；修车厂）；(NAmE) a small station where trains or buses stop（火车小站；公共汽车小站）

deprecate.meaning: (formal) to feel and express strong disapproval of sth（对 … 表示极不赞成；强烈反对）；dep·re·cat·ing (also less frequent dep·re·ca·tory /ˌdeprəˈkeɪtəri; NAmEˈdeprɪkətɔːri/) adj. a deprecating comment（表示反对的评论）

depreciate.meaning: to become less valuable over a period of time（贬值；跌价）；(business 商) to reduce the value, as stated in the company's accounts, of a particular asset over a particular period of time（折旧）；(formal) to make sth seem unimportant or of no value（贬低；轻视）；de·pre·ci·ation depreciation depreciations /dɪˌpriːʃiˈeɪʃn; NAmEdɪˌpriːʃiˈeɪʃn/ noun [U] currency depreciation（通货贬值）

depredation.meaning: acts that cause damage to people's property, lives, etc.（掠夺；劫掠）

depress.meaning: to make sb sad and without enthusiasm or hope（使抑郁；使沮丧；使消沉；使失去信心）；to make trade, business, etc. less active（使萧条；使不景气）；to make the value of prices or wages lower（降低（价格）；减少（工资））；(formal) to press or push sth down, especially part of a machine（按，压，推下（尤指机器部件））

depressed.meaning: very sad and without hope（抑郁的；沮丧的；意志消沉的）；suffering from the medical condition of depression（患抑郁症的）；(of a place or an industry（地方或行业）；without enough economic activity or jobs for people（不景气的；萧条的；经济困难的）

depressing.meaning: making you feel very sad and without enthusiasm（令人抑郁的；令人沮丧的；令人消沉的）；de·press·ing·ly /dɪˈpresɪŋli; NAmEdɪˈpresɪŋli/ adv. a depressingly familiar experience（令人感到腻烦的经历）

depression.meaning: a medical condition in which a person feels very sad and anxious and often has physical symptoms such as being unable to sleep, etc.（抑郁症；精神忧郁）；the state of feeling very sad and without hope（抑郁；沮丧；消沉）；a period when there is little economic activity and many people are poor or without jobs（萧条期；经济衰退；不景气）；(formal) a part of a surface that is lower than the parts around it（洼地；凹地；坑）

deprivation.meaning: the fact of not having sth that you need, like enough food, money or a home; the process that causes this（贫困；丧失；剥夺）

deprive.meaning: to prevent sb from having or doing sth, especially sth important（剥夺；使丧失；使不能享有）

depth.meaning: the distance from the top or surface to the bottom of sth（向下的距离；深（度）；纵深）；the distance from the front to the back of sth（向里的距离；深（度）；宽（度））；the strength and power of feelings（深厚；诚挚；强烈）；(approving) the quality of knowing or understanding a lot of details about sth; the ability to provide and explain these details（渊博；深刻；洞察力）

depute.meaning: (formal) to give sb else the authority to represent you or do sth for you（授（权）；把（权）委托给）

deputy.meaning: a person who is the next most important person below a business manager, a head of a school, a political leader, etc. and who does the person's job when he or she is away（副手；副职；代理）；the name for a member of parliament in some countries（（某些国家的）议员）；(in the US) a police officer who helps the sheriff of an area（（美国协助地方治安官办案的）警官）

derelict.meaning: (especially of land or buildings（尤指土地或建筑物）；not used or cared for and in bad condition（荒废的；被弃置的；破旧的）；(formal) a person without a home, a job or property（无家可归者；乞丐；社会弃儿）

derisive.meaning: unkind and showing that you think sb/sth is ridiculous（嘲笑的；嘲弄的；取笑的）

derivation.meaning: the origin or development of sth, especially a word（（尤指词语的）起源，由来，派生）

derivative.meaning: a word or thing that has been developed or produced from another word or thing（派生词；（台）衍生字）；(usually disapproving) copied from sth else; not having new or original ideas（模仿他人的；缺乏独创性的）

derive.meaning: to come or develop from sth（从 … 衍生出；起源于；来自）；(formal) to get sth from sth（（从 … 中）得到，获得）；(technical 术语) to obtain a substance from sth（（从 … 中）提取）

derrick.meaning: a tall machine used for moving or lifting heavy weights, especially on a ship; a type of crane（转臂起重机；（尤指船上的）吊杆式起重机）；a tall structure over an oil well for holding the drill (= the machine that makes the hole in the ground for getting the oil out)（（油井的）井架，钻塔）

desalination.meaning: the process of removing salt from sea water（（海水的）脱盐）

descend.meaning: (formal) to come or go down from a higher to a lower level（下来；下去；下降）；(of a hill, etc.（山等）；to slope downwards（下斜；下倾）；(of night, darkness, a mood, etc.（夜晚、黑暗、情绪等）

descendant.meaning: a person's descendants are their children, their children's children, and all the people who live after them who are related to them（后裔；后代；子孙）；something that has developed from sth similar in the past（（由过去类似物发展来的）派生物）

descent.meaning: an action of coming or going down（下降；下倾）；a slope going downwards（斜坡；坡道）；a person's family origins（血统；祖籍；祖先；出身）

describe.meaning: to say what sb/sth is like（描述；形容；把 … 称为）；(formal or technical 术语) to make a movement which has a particular shape; to form a particular shape（沿 … 形状移动；画出 … 图形；形成 … 形状）

description.meaning: a piece of writing or speech that says what sb/sth is like; the act of writing or saying in words what sb/sth is like（描写（文字）；形容；说明）；of some, etc. type（类型）；to be like a particular person or thing（与描述的 … 相像）

descriptive.meaning: saying what sb/sth is like; describing sth（描写的；叙述的；说明的）；(linguistics 语言) saying how language is actually used, without giving rules for how it should be used（描写性的（描述语言的实际应用而非使用规则））

desert.meaning: a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand.（沙漠；荒漠；荒原）；to leave sb without help or support（抛弃，离弃，遗弃（某人））；to go away from a place and leave it empty（舍弃，离弃（某地方））；to leave the armed forces without permission（擅离（部队）；逃走；开小差）

deserted.meaning: (of a place（地方）；with no people in it（无人居住的；空寂无人的）；left by a person or people who do not intend to return（被抛弃的；被遗弃的；被舍弃的）

desertification.meaning: the process of becoming or making sth a desert（沙漠化）

deserve.meaning: if sb/sth deserves sth, it is right that they should have it, because of the way they have behaved or because of what they are（值得；应得；应受）；(informal) used to say that you admire sb because they have done sth difficult or unpleasant（（用以夸奖某人完成了艰巨任务）应给某人授勋）；(informal) used to say that you think sb has earned the bad things that happen to them（罪有应得）

desiccation.meaning: the process of becoming completely dry（干涸；枯竭）

design.meaning: the general arrangement of the different parts of sth that is made, such as a building, book, machine, etc.（设计；布局；安排）；the art or process of deciding how sth will look, work, etc. by drawing plans, making models, etc.（设计艺术；构思）；a drawing or plan from which sth may be made（设计图样；设计方案）；an arrangement of lines and shapes as a decoration（装饰图案；花纹）

designate.meaning: to say officially that sb/sth has a particular character or name; to describe sb/sth in a particular way（命名；指定；认定）；to choose or name sb for a particular job or position（选定，指派，委任（某人任某职））；to show sth using a particular mark or sign（标明；标示；指明）；(formal) chosen to do a job but not yet having officially started it（（已受委派）尚未上任；（已当选）尚未就职）

designation.meaning: the action of choosing a person or thing for a particular purpose, or of giving them or it a particular status（选定；指定；委任）；a name, title or description（名称；称号；称呼）

designer.meaning: a person whose job is to decide how things such as clothes, furniture, tools, etc. will look or work by making drawings, plans or patterns（设计者；构思者）；made by a famous designer; expensive and having a famous brand name（由著名设计师设计的；标有设计师姓名的；名牌的）

desirable.meaning: (formal) that you would like to have or do; worth having or doing（想望的；可取的；值得拥有的；值得做的）；(of a person（人）；causing other people to feel sexual desire（引起性欲的；性感的）；de·sir·abil·ity /dɪˌzaɪərəˈbɪləti; NAmEdɪˌzaɪərəˈbɪləti/ noun [U] (formal) No one questions the desirability of cheaper fares.（没有人质疑票价下调是件好事。）

desire.meaning: a strong wish to have or do sth（愿望；欲望；渴望）；a strong wish to have sex with sb（情欲；肉欲；性欲）；a person or thing that is wished for（想望的人；渴望的事物）；(formal) to want sth; to wish for sth（渴望；期望；想望）

desirous.meaning: (formal) having a wish for sth; wanting sth（渴望；想望；希望）

desk.meaning: a piece of furniture like a table, usually with drawers in it, that you sit at to read, write, work, etc.（书桌；写字台；办公桌）；a place where you can get information or be served at an airport, a hotel, etc.（（机场、旅馆等的）问讯台，服务台，工作台）；an office at a newspaper, television company, etc. that deals with a particular subject（（报社、电视台等的）办公处，部，室，组）

desktop.meaning: the top of a desk（桌面）；a screen on a computer which shows the icons of the programs that can be used（桌面（显示使用程序图标的计算机屏幕））

desolate.meaning: (of a place（地方）；empty and without people, making you feel sad or frightened（无人居住的；荒无人烟的；荒凉的）；very lonely and unhappy（孤独凄凉的；不幸的；忧伤的）；(literary) to make sb feel sad and without hope（使感到悲惨；使感到凄凉；使悲伤绝望）

desolation.meaning: the feeling of being very lonely and unhappy（孤寂；悲哀；忧伤）；the state of a place that is ruined or destroyed and offers no joy or hope to people（废墟；荒芜；荒凉）

despair.meaning: the feeling of having lost all hope（绝望）；to make sb worried or unhappy, because they cannot help（令某人担心（或绝望））；to stop having any hope that a situation will change or improve（绝望；失去希望；丧失信心）

desperate.meaning: feeling or showing that you have little hope and are ready to do anything without worrying about danger to yourself or others（（因绝望而）不惜冒险的，不顾一切的，拼命的）；(of an action（行为）；giving little hope of success; tried when everything else has failed（绝望的；孤注一掷的；铤而走险的）；needing or wanting sth very much（非常需要；极想；渴望）

desperation.meaning: the state of being desperate（绝望；拼命；铤而走险）

despise.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to dislike and have no respect for sb/sth（鄙视；蔑视；看不起）

despite.meaning: used to show that sth happened or is true although sth else might have happened to prevent it（即使；尽管）；used to show that sb did not intend to do the thing mentioned（尽管（自己）不愿意）

despondent.meaning: sad, without much hope（苦恼的；沮丧的；泄气的；失望的）；des·pond·ency /dɪˈspɒndənsi; NAmEdɪˈspɑːndənsi/ noun [U] a mood of despondency（沮丧的心情）

dessert.meaning: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal（（饭后）甜点，甜食）

destination.meaning: a place to which sb/sth is going or being sent（目的地；终点）；a hotel, store, etc. that people will make a special trip to visit（预订的旅馆、要去的商店等）

destined.meaning: having a future which has been decided or planned at an earlier time, especially by fate（预定；注定；（尤指）命中注定）；on the way to or intended for a place（开往；运往；前往）
