digital.meaning: using a system of receiving and sending information as a series of the numbers one and zero, showing that an electronic signal is there or is not there（数字信息系统的；数码的；数字式的；（台）数位的）；(of clocks, watches, etc.（钟表等）；showing information by using figures, rather than with hands that point to numbers（数字显示的）；digit·al·ly /ˈdɪdʒɪtəli; NAmEˈdɪdʒɪtəli/ adv. digitally remastered tapes（以数字方式重新灌制的录音带）

dignify.meaning: to make sb/sth seem impressive（使有尊严；使崇高；使显贵；使增辉）；to make sth appear important when it is not really（使显得堂皇；抬高 … 的身价；美化）

dignity.meaning: a calm and serious manner that deserves respect（庄重；庄严；尊严）；the fact of being given honour and respect by people（尊贵；高贵；高尚）；a sense of your own importance and value（自豪；自尊；自重）；below what you see as your own importance or worth（有失尊严；有失身分；有失体面）

dilapidated.meaning: (of furniture and buildings（家具和建筑物）；old and in very bad condition（破旧的；破烂的；年久失修的）；di·lapi·da·tion /dɪˌlæpɪˈdeɪʃn; NAmEdɪˌlæpɪˈdeɪʃn/ noun [U] in a state of dilapidation（处于破旧状态）

dilate.meaning: to become or to make sth larger, wider or more open（扩大；（使）膨胀，扩张）

dilemma.meaning: a situation which makes problems, often one in which you have to make a very difficult choice between things of equal importance（（进退两难的）窘境，困境）

diligence.meaning: careful and thorough work or effort（勤勉；勤奋；用功）

diligent.meaning: showing care and effort in your work or duties（孜孜不倦的；勤勉的；刻苦的）

dilute.meaning: to make a liquid weaker by adding water or another liquid to it（稀释；冲淡）；to make sth weaker or less effective（削弱；降低；使降低效果）；di·lu·tion dilution dilutions /daɪˈluːʃn; daɪˈljuːʃn; NAmEdaɪˈluːʃn/ noun [U] the dilution of sewage（污水的稀释处理）；(of a liquid（液体）

dim.meaning: not bright（暗淡的；昏暗的；微弱的）；where you cannot see well because there is not much light（不明亮的；光线暗淡的；昏暗的）；that you cannot see well because there is not much light（不分明的；不清楚的；朦胧的；隐约的）；not able to see well（看不清的；视力差的；模糊的）

dime.meaning: a coin of the US and Canada worth ten cents（（美国、加拿大的）十分硬币，十分钱）；very common and therefore not valuable（普通得不值钱；（因常见而）价值低）

dimension.meaning: a measurement in space, for example the height, width or length of sth（维（构成空间的因素））；the size and extent of a situation（大小；规模；程度；范围）；an aspect, or way of looking at or thinking about sth（方面；侧面）

diminish.meaning: to become or to make sth become smaller, weaker, etc.（减少；（使）减弱，缩减；降低）；to make sb/sth seem less important than they really are（贬低；贬损；轻视）

dimly.meaning: not very brightly or clearly（暗淡地；昏暗地；模糊地）

din.meaning: a loud, unpleasant noise that lasts for a long time（喧嚣声；嘈杂声；吵闹声）

dine.meaning: to eat dinner（进餐；用饭）；(formal) to have a particular type of food for dinner（正餐吃 … ；以 … 作正餐）；to eat dinner in a restaurant or sb else's home（下馆子；外出进餐）；(informal) to tell other people about sth that has happened to you, in order to make them interested in you（吹嘘自己的经历以引起他人对你的兴趣（或重视））

diner.meaning: a person eating a meal, especially in a restaurant（（尤指餐馆的）就餐者）；(especially NAmE) a small, usually cheap, restaurant（（常指较便宜的）小餐馆，小饭店）

dingy.meaning: dark and dirty（又黑又脏的；昏暗的；肮脏的）

dinner.meaning: the main meal of the day, eaten either in the middle of the day or in the evening（（中午或晚上吃的）正餐，主餐）；a large formal social gathering at which dinner is eaten（宴会）；(AustralE, NZE) (informal) completely defeated（彻底被打败；一败涂地）

dinosaur.meaning: an animal that lived millions of years ago but is now extinct (= it no longer exists). There were many types of dinosaur, some of which were very large.（恐龙）；(disapproving) a person or thing that is old-fashioned and cannot change in the changing conditions of modern life（守旧落伍的人；过时落后的东西）

dioxide.meaning: a substance formed by combining two atoms of oxygen and one atom of another chemical element（二氧化物）

dip.meaning: to put sth quickly into a liquid and take it out again（蘸；浸）；to go downwards or to a lower level; to make sth do this（（使）下降，下沉）；(BrE) if you dip your headlights when driving a car at night, you make the light from them point down so that other drivers do not have the light in their eyes（把（汽车前灯的）远光调为近光）；when farmers dip animals, especially sheep, they put them in a bath of a liquid containing chemicals in order to kill insects, etc.（给（牲畜，尤指绵羊）洗药浴）

diploma.meaning: (BrE) a course of study at a college or university（文凭课程）；a document showing that you have completed a course of study or part of your education（毕业文凭）

diplomacy.meaning: the activity of managing relations between different countries; the skill in doing this（外交；外交技巧；外交手腕）；skill in dealing with people in difficult situations without upsetting or offending them（（处理人际关系的）手腕，手段，策略）

diplomat.meaning: a person whose job is to represent his or her country in a foreign country, for example, in an embassy（外交官）；a person who is skilled at dealing with other people（善于交际的人；通权达变的人；圆通的人；有手腕的人）

diplomatic.meaning: connected with managing relations between countries (= diplomacy)（外交的；从事外交的）；having or showing skill in dealing with people in difficult situations（有手腕的；灵活变通的；策略的；圆通的）；dip·lo·mat·ic·al·ly /ˌdɪpləˈmætɪkli; NAmEˌdɪpləˈmætɪkli/ adv. The country remained diplomatically isolated.（这个国家在外交上仍然受到孤立。）

dire.meaning: (formal) very serious（极其严重的；危急的）；(BrE) (informal) very bad（极糟的；极差的）

direct.meaning: happening or done without involving other people, actions, etc. in between（直接的；亲自的；亲身的）；going in the straightest line between two places without stopping or changing direction（笔直的；径直的；最近的）；with nothing between sth and the source of the heat or light（直射的）；saying exactly what you mean in a way that nobody can pretend not to understand（直爽的；直率的；坦率的）

direction.meaning: the general position a person or thing moves or points towards（方向；方位）；the general way in which a person or thing develops（趋势；动向）；the general position a person or thing comes or develops from（方面）；a purpose; an aim（目的；目标）

directional.meaning: producing or receiving signals, sound, etc. better in one particular direction（（发出或接收信号、声音等）定向的，指向的）；connected with the direction in which sth is moving（方向的）

directive.meaning: an official instruction（指示；命令）；(formal) giving instructions（指示的；指导的）

directly.meaning: in a direct line or manner（直接地；径直地；坦率地）；exactly in a particular position（正；正好地；恰好）；immediately（立即；立刻）；(old-fashioned) (BrE) soon（过一会儿；很快）

director.meaning: one of a group of senior managers who run a company（董事；理事；经理）；a person who is in charge of a particular activity or department in a company, a college, etc.（（某一活动的）负责人；（公司部门的）主任，经理；（学院的）院长）；a person in charge of a film/movie or play who tells the actors and staff what to do（（电影或戏剧的）导演）

directory.meaning: a book containing lists of information, usually in alphabetical order, for example people's telephone numbers or the names and addresses of businesses in a particular area（名录；电话号码簿；公司名录）；a file containing a group of other files or programs in a computer（（计算机文件或程序的）目录）

dirt.meaning: any substance that makes sth dirty, for example dust, soil or mud（污物；尘土；烂泥）；(especially NAmE) loose earth or soil（松土；泥土；散土）；(informal) unpleasant or harmful information about sb that could be used to damage their reputation, career, etc.（丑闻；流言蜚语）

dirty.meaning: not clean（肮脏的；龌龊的；污秽的）；connected with sex in an offensive way（下流的；色情的；黄色的；猥亵的）；(informal) unpleasant or dishonest（令人厌恶的；卑鄙的；不诚实的）；dull（不鲜明的；暗淡的）

disability.meaning: a physical or mental condition that means you cannot use a part of your body completely or easily, or that you cannot learn easily（（某种）缺陷，障碍）；the state of not being able to use a part of your body completely or easily; the state of not being able to learn easily（（指状态、身心、学习等方面的）缺陷，障碍）

disable.meaning: to injure or affect sb permanently so that, for example, they cannot walk or cannot use a part of their body（使丧失能力；使伤残）；to make sth unable to work so that it cannot be used（使无效；使不能运转）

disabled.meaning: unable to use a part of your body completely or easily because of a physical condition, illness, injury, etc; unable to learn easily（丧失能力的；有残疾的；无能力的）；people who are disabled（残疾人；伤残者）

disadvantage.meaning: something that causes problems and tends to stop sb/sth from succeeding or making progress（不利因素；障碍；不便之处）

disadvantageous.meaning: (formal) causing sb to be in a worse situation compared to other people（不利的；不便的）

disagree.meaning: if two people disagree or one person disagrees with another about sth, they have a different opinion about it（不同意；持不同意见；有分歧）；if statements or reports disagree, they give different information（不符；不一致）；if sth, especially food, disagrees with you, it has a bad effect on you and makes you feel ill/sick（（尤指食物）对（某人）不适宜，使不舒服）；to believe that sth is bad or wrong; to disapprove of sth（不赞成；反对）

disagreement.meaning: a situation where people have different opinions about sth and often argue（意见不一；分歧；争论）；a difference between two things that should be the same（不符；不一致）

disallow.meaning: (formal) to officially refuse to accept sth because it is not valid（不准许；不接受；驳回）

disappear.meaning: to become impossible to see（消失；不见）；to stop existing（不复存在；灭绝；消亡）；to be lost or impossible to find（失踪；丢失）；dis·ap·pear·ance disappearance disappearances /ˌdɪsəˈpɪərəns; NAmEˌdɪsəˈpɪrəns/ noun [U, C] the disappearance of many species of plants and animals from our planet（许多动植物物种从我们这颗行星上的消失）

disappoint.meaning: to make sb feel sad because sth that they hope for or expect to happen does not happen or is not as good as they hoped（使失望）；to prevent sth that sb hopes for from becoming a reality（使破灭；使落空）

disappointed.meaning: upset because sth you hoped for has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected（失望的；沮丧的；失意的）

disappointing.meaning: not as good, successful, etc. as you had hoped; making you feel disappointed（令人失望的；令人沮丧的；令人扫兴的）；dis·ap·point·ing·ly /ˌdɪsəˈpɔɪntɪŋli; NAmEˌdɪsəˈpɔɪntɪŋli/ adv. The room was disappointingly small.（房间小得令人失望。）

disappointment.meaning: sadness because sth has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected or hoped（失望；沮丧；扫兴）；a person or thing that is disappointing（使人失望的人（或事物）；令人扫兴的人（或事物））

disapproval.meaning: a feeling that you do not like an idea, an action or sb's behaviour because you think it is bad, not suitable or going to have a bad effect on sb else（不赞成；反对）

disapprove.meaning: to think that sb/sth is not good or suitable; to not approve of sb/sth（不赞成；不同意；反对）

disapproving.meaning: showing that you do not approve of sb/sth（不赞成的；表示反对的；不以为然的）；dis·ap·prov·ing·ly /ˌdɪsəˈpruːvɪŋli; NAmEˌdɪsəˈpruːvɪŋli/ adv. He looked disapprovingly at the row of empty wine bottles.（他不以为然地看了看那排空酒瓶。）

disarm.meaning: to take a weapon or weapons away from sb（缴（某人）的械；解除（某人）的武装）；(of a country or a group of people（国家或集体）；to reduce the size of an army or to give up some or all weapons, especially nuclear weapons（裁军，解除武装，裁减军备（尤指核武器））；to make sb feel less angry or critical（消释（某人）的怒气（或批评））

disarray.meaning: a state of confusion and lack of organization in a situation or a place（混乱；紊乱）

disaster.meaning: an unexpected event, such as a very bad accident, a flood or a fire, that kills a lot of people or causes a lot of damage（灾难；灾祸；灾害）；a very bad situation that causes problems（不幸；祸患）；(informal) a complete failure（彻底失败的人（或事））

disastrous.meaning: very bad, harmful or unsuccessful（极糟糕的；灾难性的；完全失败的）；dis·as·trous·ly /dɪˈzɑːstrəsli; NAmEdɪˈzæstrəsli/ adv. How could everything go so disastrously wrong?（怎么会事事都出这么大的错呢？）

disburse.meaning: (formal) to pay money to sb from a large amount that has been collected for a purpose（（从资金中）支付，支出）；dis·burse·ment disbursement disbursements /dɪsˈbɜːsmənt; NAmEdɪsˈbɜːsmənt/ noun [U, C] the disbursement of funds（拨款）

disc.meaning: a thin flat round object（圆盘；圆片）；(BrE) a disk for a computer（（计算机）磁盘，磁碟）；a structure made of cartilage between the bones of the back（椎间盘）

discard.meaning: (formal) to get rid of sth that you no longer want or need（丢弃；抛弃）；(in card games（纸牌游戏）；to get rid of a card that you do not want（垫（牌）；打出（无用的牌））；a person or thing that is not wanted or thrown away, especially a card in a card game（被抛弃的人（或物）；（尤指纸牌游戏中）垫出的牌）

discern.meaning: to know, recognize or understand sth, especially sth that is not obvious（觉察出；识别；了解）；to see or hear sth, but not very clearly（（依稀）看出，分辨出，听出）；dis·cern·ible /; NAmE/ adj. (formal) SYN perceptible There is often no discernible difference between rival brands.（相互竞争的品牌之间往往看不出明显的区别。）

discharge.meaning: to give sb official permission to leave a place or job; to make sb leave a job（准许（某人）离开；解雇）；to allow sb to leave prison or court（释放）；when a gas or a liquid discharges or is discharged, or sb discharges it, it flows somewhere（排出；放出；流出）；(technical 术语) to release force or power（发（力）；放（电））

disciple.meaning: a person who believes in and follows the teachings of a religious or political leader（信徒；门徒；追随者）；(according to the Bible) one of the people who followed Jesus Christ and his teachings when he was living on earth, especially one of the twelve Apostles（（《圣经》中耶稣的）门徒，十二宗徒之一）

disciplinary.meaning: connected with the punishment of people who break rules（有关纪律的；执行纪律的；惩戒性的）

discipline.meaning: the practice of training people to obey rules and orders and punishing them if they do not; the controlled behaviour or situation that results from this training（训练；训导；纪律；风纪）；a method of training your mind or body or of controlling your behaviour; an area of activity where this is necessary（训练方法；行为准则；符合准则的行为）；the ability to control your behaviour or the way you live, work, etc.（自制力；遵守纪律）；(formal) an area of knowledge; a subject that people study or are taught, especially in a university（知识领域；（尤指大学的）学科，科目）

disclaim.meaning: to state publicly that you have no knowledge of sth, or that you are not responsible for sth（否认；拒绝承认）；to give up your right to sth, such as property or a title（放弃（财产、头衔等的）权利）

disclaimer.meaning: (formal) a statement in which sb says that they are not connected with or responsible for sth, or that they do not have any knowledge of it（免责声明）；(law 律) a statement in which a person says officially that they do not claim the right to do sth（弃权声明（书））

disclose.meaning: to give sb information about sth, especially sth that was previously secret（揭露；透露；泄露）；to allow sth that was hidden to be seen（使显露；使暴露）

disco.meaning: a club or party where people dance to recorded pop music（迪斯科舞厅（或舞会））；the lights and sound equipment for such an event（迪斯科舞会的灯光及音响设备）

discoloration.meaning: the process of becoming discoloured（变色；褪色）；a place where sth has become discoloured（变色处；褪色处）

discomfort.meaning: a feeling of slight pain or of being physically uncomfortable（轻微的病痛；不舒服；不适）；a feeling of worry or embarrassment（不安；不自在；尴尬）；something that makes you feel uncomfortable or causes you a slight feeling of pain（使人不舒服的事物；苦事；痛苦）；(formal) to make sb feel anxious or embarrassed（使不舒服；使不安；使尴尬）

discontent.meaning: a feeling of being unhappy because you are not satisfied with a particular situation; sth that makes you have this feeling（不满；感到不满的事情）

discontinue.meaning: to stop doing, using or providing sth, especially sth that you have been doing, using or providing regularly（停止；终止；中断）；to stop making a product（停止，终止（生产））

discontinuity.meaning: the state of not being continuous（不连贯；不连续）；a break or change in a continuous process（中断；间断；停顿）

discord.meaning: (formal) disagreement; arguing（不一致；不和；纷争）；(music 音) a combination of musical notes that do not sound pleasant together（不协和和弦）

discount.meaning: an amount of money that is taken off the usual cost of sth（折扣）；(formal) to think or say that sth is not important or not true（认为 … 不重要；对 … 不全信；低估）；to take an amount of money off the usual cost of sth; to sell sth at a discount（打折扣；打折出售）

discourage.meaning: to try to prevent sth or to prevent sb from doing sth, especially by making it difficult to do or by showing that you do not approve of it（阻拦；阻止；劝阻）；to make sb feel less confident or enthusiastic about doing sth（使灰心；使泄气；使丧失信心）；dis·cour·aged /; NAmE/ adj. [not usually before noun] SYN disheartened Learners can feel very discouraged if an exercise is too difficult.（如果练习太难，学习者就可能感到没信心。）；dis·cour·aging /dɪsˈkʌrɪdʒɪŋ; NAmEdɪsˈkɜːrɪdʒɪŋ/ adj. a discouraging experience/response/result（令人泄气的经历/回答/结果）

discourse.meaning: (formal) a long and serious treatment or discussion of a subject in speech or writing（论文；演讲）；(linguistics 语言) the use of language in speech and writing in order to produce meaning; language that is studied, usually in order to see how the different parts of a text are connected（话语；语篇）；(formal) to talk or give a long speech about sth that you know a lot about（讲述；论述）

discover.meaning: to be the first person to become aware that a particular place or thing exists（（第一个）发现）；to find sb/sth that was hidden or that you did not expect to find（（出乎意料地）发现，找到，发觉）；to find out about sth; to find some information about sth（了解到；认识到；查明）；to be the first person to realize that sb is very good at singing, acting, etc. and help them to become successful and famous（发现，发掘（人才））

discovery.meaning: an act or the process of finding sb/sth, or learning about sth that was not known about before（发现；发觉）；a thing, fact or person that is found or learned about for the first time（被发现的事物（或真相、人））

discredit.meaning: to make people stop respecting sb/sth（败坏 … 的名声；使丧失信誉；使丢脸）；to make people stop believing that sth is true; to make sth appear unlikely to be true（使不相信；使怀疑；使不可置信）；(formal) damage to sb's reputation; loss of respect（名誉丧失；信誉丧失；丢脸）

discreet.meaning: careful in what you say or do, in order to keep sth secret or to avoid causing embarrassment or difficulty for sb（（言行）谨慎的，慎重的，考虑周到的）；dis·creet·ly /dɪˈskriːtli; NAmEdɪˈskriːtli/ adv. She coughed discreetly to announce her presence.（她审慎地咳了一声以让人注意自己在场。）

discrepancy.meaning: a difference between two or more things that should be the same（差异；不符合；不一致）

discrete.meaning: independent of other things of the same type（分离的；互不相连的；各别的）

discretion.meaning: the freedom or power to decide what should be done in a particular situation（自行决定的自由；自行决定权）；care in what you say or do, in order to keep sth secret or to avoid causing embarrassment to or difficulty for sb; the quality of being discreet（谨慎；慎重；审慎）；according to what sb decides or wishes to do（由某人斟酌决定；按照某人的意愿）；(saying) you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks（谨慎即大勇；慎重为勇敢之本）

discriminate.meaning: to recognize that there is a difference between people or things; to show a difference between people or things（区别；辨别；区分）；to treat one person or group worse/better than another in an unfair way（区别对待；歧视；偏袒）

discrimination.meaning: the practice of treating sb or a particular group in society less fairly than others（区别对待；歧视；偏袒）；(approving) the ability to judge what is good, true, etc.（识别力；辨别力；鉴赏力）；the ability to recognize a difference between one thing and another; a difference that is recognized（区别；识别；辨别）

discriminatory.meaning: unfair; treating sb or one group of people worse than others（区别对待的；不公正的；歧视的）

discuss.meaning: to talk about sth with sb, especially in order to decide sth（讨论；谈论；商量）；to write or talk about sth in detail, showing the different ideas and opinions about it（详述；论述）

discussion.meaning: the process of discussing sb/sth; a conversation about sb/sth（讨论；商讨）；a speech or a piece of writing that discusses many different aspects of a subject（详述；论述）

disdain.meaning: the feeling that sb/sth is not good enough to deserve your respect or attention（鄙视；蔑视；鄙弃）；to think that sb/sth is not good enough to deserve your respect（鄙视；蔑视；鄙弃）；to refuse to do sth because you think that you are too important to do it（不屑（做某事））

disease.meaning: an illness affecting humans, animals or plants, often caused by infection（病；疾病）；(formal) something that is very wrong with people's attitudes, way of life or with society（弊端；恶疾；痼疾）

disentangle.meaning: to separate different arguments, ideas, etc. that have become confused（理顺，分清，清理出（混乱的论据、想法等））；to free sb/sth from sth that has become wrapped or twisted around it or them（使解脱；使脱出；使摆脱）；to get rid of the twists and knots in sth（解开 … 的结；理顺）

disgrace.meaning: the loss of other people's respect and approval because of the bad way sb has behaved（丢脸；耻辱；不光彩）；a person or thing that is so bad that people connected with them or it feel or should feel ashamed（令人感到羞耻的人（或事））；to behave badly in a way that makes you or other people feel ashamed（使丢脸；使蒙受耻辱）；to lose the respect of people, usually so that you lose a position of power（使名誉扫地；使失势；使失去地位）

disgraceful.meaning: very bad or unacceptable; that people should feel ashamed about（不光彩的；可耻的；丢脸的）

disguise.meaning: to change your appearance so that people cannot recognize you（假扮；装扮；伪装）；to hide sth or change it, so that it cannot be recognized（掩蔽；掩饰）；a thing that you wear or use to change your appearance so that people do not recognize you（伪装物；化装用具）；the art of changing your appearance so that people do not recognize you（假扮；装扮；伪装）

disgust.meaning: a strong feeling of dislike or disapproval for sb/sth that you feel is unacceptable, or for sth that looks, smells, etc. unpleasant（厌恶；憎恶；反感）；if sth disgusts you, it makes you feel shocked and almost ill/sick because it is so unpleasant（使作呕；使厌恶；使反感）

disgusted.meaning: feeling or showing disgust（厌恶的；憎恶的；反感的）；dis·gust·ed·ly /dɪsˈɡʌstɪdli; NAmEdɪsˈɡʌstɪdli/ adv. ‘This champagne is warm!’, he said disgustedly.（“这香槟酒是温的！”他气愤地说。）

disgusting.meaning: extremely unpleasant（极糟的；令人不快的）；unacceptable and shocking（令人厌恶的；令人气愤的）

dish.meaning: a flat shallow container for cooking food in or serving it from（碟；盘）；the plates, bowls, cups, etc. that have been used for a meal and need to be washed（（待清洗的）餐具）；food prepared in a particular way as part of a meal（一道菜；菜肴）；any object that is shaped like a dish or bowl（盘状物；碟状物）

dishonest.meaning: not honest; intending to trick people（不诚实的；骗人的；欺骗性的）

dishonour.meaning: (formal) a loss of honour or respect because you have done sth immoral or unacceptable（不名誉；耻辱；丢脸）；to make sb/sth lose the respect of other people（使丧失名誉；使蒙受耻辱；使丢脸）；to refuse to keep an agreement or promise（违背，违反（协议或诺言））

disillusion.meaning: to destroy sb's belief in or good opinion of sb/sth（使醒悟；使不再抱幻想；使幻想破灭）

disinclined.meaning: (formal) not willing（不情愿；不乐意；无意于）

disinfectant.meaning: a substance that disinfects（消毒剂；杀菌剂）

disintegrate.meaning: to break into small parts or pieces and be destroyed（碎裂；解体；分裂）；to become much less strong or united and be gradually destroyed（衰微；瓦解；崩溃）；dis·in·te·gra·tion /dɪsˌɪntɪˈɡreɪʃn; NAmEdɪsˌɪntɪˈɡreɪʃn/ noun [U] the gradual disintegration of traditional values（传统价值观念的逐渐淡薄）

disinterest.meaning: lack of interest（无兴趣；不关心；冷漠）；the fact of not being involved in sth（客观；公正）

disk.meaning: (computing 计) a device for storing information on a computer, with a magnetic surface that records information received in electronic form（磁盘；磁碟）

dislike.meaning: (rather formal) to not like sb/sth（不喜爱；厌恶）；a feeling of not liking sb/sth（不喜爱；厌恶；反感）；a thing that you do not like（不喜欢的事物；讨厌的事物）

dislodge.meaning: to force or knock sth out of its position（（把某物）强行去除，取出，移动）；to force sb to leave a place, position or job（（把某人）逐出，赶出，驱逐出）

disloyal.meaning: not loyal or faithful to your friends, family, country, etc.（（对国家、家庭等）不忠实的，不忠诚的；（对朋友等）不守信义的）

dismal.meaning: causing or showing sadness（忧郁的；凄凉的；惨淡的；阴沉的）；(informal) not skilful or successful; of very low quality（不熟练的；差劲的；不怎么样的）；dis·mal·ly /ˈdɪzməli; NAmEˈdɪzməli/ adv. I tried not to laugh but failed dismally (= was completely unsuccessful).（我想尽量忍着不笑，但根本忍不住。）

dismantle.meaning: to take apart a machine or structure so that it is in separate pieces（拆开，拆卸（机器或结构））；to end an organization or system gradually in an organized way（（逐渐）废除，取消）

dismay.meaning: a worried, sad feeling after you have received an unpleasant surprise（诧异；惊愕；灰心；丧气）；to make sb feel shocked and disappointed（使诧异；使惊愕；使失望）；dis·mayed /; NAmE/ adj. dismayed~ (at/by sth) He was dismayed at the change in his old friend.（他对老朋友变化之大感到震惊。）

dismember.meaning: to cut or tear the dead body of a person or an animal into pieces（分割 … 的躯体；肢解）；(formal) to divide a country, an organization, etc. into smaller parts（分割；瓜分）

dismiss.meaning: to decide that sb/sth is not important and not worth thinking or talking about（不予考虑；摒弃；对 … 不屑一提）；to put thoughts or feelings out of your mind（去除，消除，摒除（思想、感情等））；to officially remove sb from their job（解雇；免职；开除）；to send sb away or allow them to leave（让（某人）离开；把（某人）打发走；解散）

dismissal.meaning: the act of dismissing sb from their job; an example of this（解雇；开除；撤职）；the failure to consider sth as important（不予考虑；不予理会；摒弃）；(law 律) the act of not allowing a trial or legal case to continue, usually because there is not enough evidence（驳回（诉讼）；不予受理）；the act of sending sb away or allowing them to leave（解散；打发走）

disobey.meaning: to refuse to do what a person, law, order, etc. tells you to do; to refuse to obey（不服从；不顺从；违抗）

disorder.meaning: (formal) an untidy state; a lack of order or organization（杂乱；混乱；凌乱）；(formal) violent behaviour of large groups of people（骚乱；动乱）；(medical 医) an illness that causes a part of the body to stop functioning correctly（失调；紊乱；不适；疾病）

disparity.meaning: a difference, especially one connected with unfair treatment（（尤指因不公正对待引起的）不同，不等，差异，悬殊）

dispatch.meaning: (formal) to send sb/sth somewhere, especially for a special purpose（派遣；调遣；派出）；(formal) to send a letter, package or message somewhere（发出，发送（邮件、包裹、信息））；(formal) to deal or finish with sb/sth quickly and completely（迅速处理；迅速办妥；迅速完成）；(old-fashioned) to kill a person or an animal（杀死；处决）

dispel.meaning: to make sth, especially a feeling or belief, go away or disappear（驱散，消除（尤指感觉或信仰））

dispense.meaning: (formal) to give out sth to people（分配；分发）；(formal) to provide sth, especially a service, for people（施与，提供（尤指服务））；to prepare medicine and give it to people, as a job（配（药）；发（药））；to stop using sb/sth because you no longer need them or it（摒弃；不再需要；不再用）

dispersal.meaning: the process of sending sb/sth in different directions; the process of spreading sth over a wide area（分散；疏散；散布）

disperse.meaning: to move apart and go away in different directions; to make sb/sth do this（（使）分散，散开；疏散；驱散）；to spread or to make sth spread over a wide area（散布；散发；传播）

displace.meaning: to take the place of sb/sth（取代；替代；置换）；to force people to move away from their home to another place（迫使（某人）离开家园）；to move sth from its usual position（移动；挪开；转移）；(especially NAmE) to remove sb from a job or position（撤职；免职；使失业）

displacement.meaning: (formal) the act of displacing sb/sth; the process of being displaced（取代；替代；移位；免职）；(physics 物) the amount of a liquid moved out of place by sth floating or put in it, especially a ship floating in water（排水量）

display.meaning: to put sth in a place where people can see it easily; to show sth to people（陈列；展出；展示）；to show signs of sth, especially a quality or feeling（显示，显露，表现（尤指特性或情感））；(of a computer, etc.（计算机等）；to show information（显示）

displease.meaning: (formal) to make sb feel upset, annoyed or not satisfied（使恼怒；使生气；使不悦）；dis·pleased /; NAmE/ adj. displeased~ (with sb/sth) Are you displeased with my work?（你对我的工作不满意吗？）；dis·pleas·ing /dɪsˈpliːzɪŋ; NAmEdɪsˈpliːzɪŋ/ adj. displeasing~ (to sb/sth) His remarks were clearly not displeasing to her.（他的话显然并没使她不快。）

displeasure.meaning: (formal) the feeling of being upset and annoyed（烦恼；生气；不悦）

disposable.meaning: made to be thrown away after use（用后即丢弃的；一次性的）；(finance 财) available for use（可动用的；可自由支配的）

disposal.meaning: the act of getting rid of sth（去掉；清除；处理）；(business 商) the sale of part of a business, property, etc.（（企业、财产等的）变卖，让与）；available for use as you prefer/sb prefers（任某人处理；供某人任意使用；由某人自行支配）

dispose.meaning: to arrange things or people in a particular way or position（排列；布置；安排）；to make sb behave in a particular way（使倾向于；使有意于；使易于）；to get rid of sb/sth that you do not want or cannot keep（去掉；清除；销毁）；to deal with a problem, question or threat successfully（应付；解决；处理）

disposed.meaning: willing or prepared to do sth（倾向于；有意于；乐意）；having a good/bad opinion of a person or thing（对 … 有好感（或恶感））

disposition.meaning: (formal) the natural qualities of a person's character（性格；性情）；(formal) a tendency to behave in a particular way（倾向；意向）；(formal) the way sth is placed or arranged（排列；布置；安排）；(law 律) a formal act of giving property or money to sb（（财产、金钱的）处置，让与）

disproportionate.meaning: too large or too small when compared with sth else（不成比例的；不相称的；太大（或太小）的）；dis·pro·por·tion·ately AW /ˌdɪsprəˈpɔːʃənətli; NAmEˌdɪsprəˈpɔːrʃənətli/ adv. The lower-paid spend a disproportionately large amount of their earnings on food.（低工资者将收入花在食物上的比例很大。）

disprove.meaning: to show that sth is wrong or false（证明 … 是错误（或虚假）的）

disputable.meaning: that can or should be questioned or argued about（可质疑的；有争辩余地的；可商榷的）

dispute.meaning: an argument or a disagreement between two people, groups or countries; discussion about a subject where there is disagreement（争论；辩论；争端；纠纷）；to question whether sth is true and valid（对 … 提出质询；对 … 表示异议（或怀疑））；to argue or disagree strongly with sb about sth, especially about who owns sth（争论；辩论；争执）；to fight to get control of sth or to win sth（争夺；竞争）

disregard.meaning: (formal) to not consider sth; to treat sth as unimportant（不理会；不顾；漠视）；(formal) the act of treating sb/sth as unimportant and not caring about them/it（漠视；忽视）

disreputable.meaning: that people consider to be dishonest and bad（名声不好的；不名誉的；不光彩的）

disrepute.meaning: the fact that sb/sth loses the respect of other people（丧失名誉；坏名声）

disrupt.meaning: to make it difficult for sth to continue in the normal way（扰乱；使中断；打乱）；dis·rup·tion disruption disruptions /dɪsˈrʌpʃn; NAmEdɪsˈrʌpʃn/ noun [U, C] We aim to help you move house with minimum disruption to yourself.（我们的宗旨是帮您搬家的时候，尽量减少给您带来的不便。）

disruptive.meaning: causing problems, noise, etc. so that sth cannot continue normally（引起混乱的；扰乱性的；破坏性的）

dissatisfaction.meaning: a feeling that you are not pleased and satisfied（不快；不悦；不满意）

disseminate.meaning: (formal) to spread information, knowledge, etc. so that it reaches many people（散布，传播（信息、知识等））

dissension.meaning: disagreement between people or within a group（意见分歧；（派性）纷争；不和）

dissenter.meaning: a person who does not agree with opinions that are officially or generally accepted（（对官方或普遍认可的意见）持异议者，持不同意见者）

dissertation.meaning: a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree（专题论文；（尤指）学位论文）

dissimilar.meaning: (formal) not the same（不一样的；不同的；不相似的）

dissipate.meaning: to gradually become or make sth become weaker until it disappears（（使）消散，消失；驱散）；to waste sth, such as time or money, especially by not planning the best way of using it（挥霍，浪费，消磨（时间、金钱等））

dissolution.meaning: the act of officially ending a marriage, a business agreement or a parliament（（婚姻关系的）解除；（商业协议的）终止；（议会的）解散）；the process in which sth gradually disappears（消失；消亡）；the act of breaking up an organization, etc.（解体；瓦解；分裂）

dissolve.meaning: (of a solid（固体）；to mix with a liquid and become part of it（溶解）；to make a solid become part of a liquid（使（固体）溶解）；to officially end a marriage, business agreement or parliament（解除（婚姻关系）；终止（商业协议）；解散（议会））

distance.meaning: the amount of space between two places or things（距离；间距）；being far away in space or in time（（空间的）遥远；（时间的）久远，间隔）；a point that is a particular amount of space away from sth else（远方；远处）；a difference or lack of a connection between two things（（两事物之间的）差异，无关）

distant.meaning: far away in space or time（遥远的；远处的；久远的）；not like sth else（不相似的；不同的）；(of a person（人）；related to you but not closely（远亲的；远房的）

distasteful.meaning: unpleasant or offensive（使人不愉快的；令人反感的；讨厌的）

distend.meaning: (formal or medical 医) to swell or make sth swell because of pressure from inside（（使）膨胀，肿胀）；dis·ten·sion distension distensions /dɪˈstenʃn; NAmEdɪˈstenʃn/ noun [U] distension of the stomach（胃胀）

distil.meaning: to make a liquid pure by heating it until it becomes a gas, then cooling it and collecting the drops of liquid that form（蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取）；to make sth such as a strong alcoholic drink in this way（用蒸馏法制造（酒等））；(formal) to get the essential meaning or ideas from thoughts, information, experiences, etc.（吸取 … 的精华；提炼；浓缩）；dis·til·la·tion distillation distillations /ˌdɪstɪˈleɪʃn; NAmEˌdɪstɪˈleɪʃn/ noun [C, U] the distillation process（蒸馏过程）

distinct.meaning: easily or clearly heard, seen, felt, etc.（清晰的；清楚的；明白的；明显的）；clearly different or of a different kind（截然不同的；有区别的；不同种类的）；used to emphasize that you think an idea or situation definitely exists and is important（确定无疑的；确实的；确切的）；dis·tinct·ly AW /dɪˈstɪŋktli; NAmEdɪˈstɪŋktli/ adv. I distinctly heard someone calling me.（我清楚地听到有人在叫我。）

distinction.meaning: a clear difference or contrast especially between people or things that are similar or related（差别；区别；对比）；the quality of being excellent or important（优秀；杰出；卓越）；the quality of being sth that is special（特质；特点；不同凡响）；the separation of people or things into different groups（区分；分清；辨别）

distinctive.meaning: having a quality or characteristic that makes sth different and easily noticed（独特的；特别的；有特色的）；dis·tinct·ive·ly AW /dɪˈstɪŋktɪvli; NAmEdɪˈstɪŋktɪvli/ adv. a distinctively nutty flavour（特别的坚果味道）

distinguish.meaning: to recognize the difference between two people or things（区分；辨别；分清）；to be a characteristic that makes two people, animals or things different（成为 … 的特征；使具有 … 的特色；使有别于）；to be able to see or hear sth（看清；认出；听出）；to do sth so well that people notice and admire you（使出众；使著名；使受人青睐）

distinguished.meaning: very successful and admired by other people（卓越的；杰出的；著名的）；having an appearance that makes sb look important or that makes people admire or respect them（显得重要的；高贵的；有尊严的）

distort.meaning: to change the shape, appearance or sound of sth so that it is strange or not clear（使变形；扭曲；使失真）；to twist or change facts, ideas, etc. so that they are no longer correct or true（歪曲；曲解）；dis·tort·ion AW distortion distortions /dɪˈstɔːʃn; NAmEdɪˈstɔːrʃn/ noun [C, U] modern alloys that are resistant to wear and distortion（耐磨、防变形的新型合金）

distract.meaning: to take sb's attention away from what they are trying to do（转移（注意力）；分散（思想）；使分心）；dis·tract·ing /dɪˈstræktɪŋ; NAmEdɪˈstræktɪŋ/ adj. distracting thoughts（令人分心的想法）

distraction.meaning: a thing that takes your attention away from what you are doing or thinking about（分散注意力的事；使人分心的事）；an activity that amuses or entertains you（娱乐；消遣）；so that you become upset, excited or angry, and not able to think clearly（到心烦意乱（或激动、气愤）的地步）

distress.meaning: a feeling of great worry or unhappiness; great suffering（忧虑；悲伤；痛苦）；suffering and problems caused by not having enough money, food, etc.（贫困；窘迫；困苦）；a situation in which a ship, plane, etc. is in danger or difficulty and needs help（（船、飞机等）遇难，遇险）；to make sb feel very worried or unhappy（使忧虑；使悲伤；使苦恼）

distribute.meaning: to give things to a large number of people; to share sth between a number of people（分发；分配）；to send goods to shops/stores and businesses so that they can be sold（分销）；to spread sth, or different parts of sth, over an area（使散开；使分布；分散）

distribution.meaning: the way that sth is shared or exists over a particular area or among a particular group of people（分配；分布）；the act of giving or delivering sth to a number of people（分发；分送）；(business 商) the system of transporting and delivering goods（（商品）运销，经销，分销）

distributive.meaning: connected with distribution of goods（经销的；分销的）

distributor.meaning: a person or company that supplies goods to shops/stores, etc.（经销商；分销商）；a device in an engine that sends electric current to the spark plugs（（发动机的）配电器，配电盘）

district.meaning: an area of a country or town, especially one that has particular features（地区；区域）；one of the areas which a country, town or state is divided into for purposes of organization, with official boundaries (= borders)（区；管区；行政区）

distrust.meaning: a feeling of not being able to trust sb/sth（不信任；怀疑）；dis·trust·ful /dɪsˈtrʌstfl; NAmEdɪsˈtrʌstfl/ adj. distrustful of authority（不相信权威）；to feel that you cannot trust or believe sb/sth（不信任；怀疑）

disturb.meaning: to interrupt sb when they are trying to work, sleep, etc.（打扰；干扰；妨碍）；to move sth or change its position（搅乱；弄乱；搞乱）；to make sb worry（使焦虑；使不安；使烦恼）

disturbance.meaning: actions that make you stop what you are doing, or that upset the normal state that sth is in; the act of disturbing sb/sth or the fact of being disturbed（（受）打扰，干扰，妨碍）；a situation in which people behave violently in a public place（骚乱；骚动；动乱）；a state in which sb's mind or a function of the body is upset and not working normally（障碍；失调；紊乱）

disturbing.meaning: making you feel anxious and upset or shocked（引起烦恼的；令人不安的；引起恐慌的）

disunite.meaning: (formal) to make a group of people unable to agree with each other or work together（使不统一；使不和；使纷争）

disuse.meaning: a situation in which sth is no longer being used（不用；废弃）

ditch.meaning: a long channel dug at the side of a field or road, to hold or take away water（沟；渠）；(informal) to get rid of sth/sb because you no longer want or need it/them（摆脱；抛弃；丢弃）；if a pilot ditches an aircraft, or if it ditches, it lands in the sea in an emergency（使（飞机）在海上紧急降落；（在海上）迫降）；(NAmE) (informal) to stay away from school without permission（逃学；旷课）

ditto.meaning: used, especially in a list, underneath a particular word or phrase, to show that it is repeated and to avoid having to write it again（（尤用于表格中）同上，同前）；(informal) used instead of a particular word or phrase, to avoid repeating it（（代替某一词语以免重复）同样，也一样）

diva.meaning: a famous woman singer, especially an opera singer（著名女歌唱家（尤指歌剧女主角））

dive.meaning: to jump into water with your head and arms going in first（跳水（头和双臂先入水））；to swim underwater wearing breathing equipment, collecting or looking at things（（戴呼吸装备）潜水）；to go to a deeper level underwater（下潜；潜到更深的水下）；to go steeply down through the air（俯冲）

diver.meaning: a person who works underwater, usually with special equipment（（通常有专用装备的）潜水员）；a person who jumps into the water with their head first and their arms in front of them（跳水者；跳水运动员）

diverge.meaning: to separate and go in different directions（分叉；岔开）；(of opinions, views, etc.（意见、观点等）；to be different（分歧；相异）；to be or become different from what is expected, planned, etc.（偏离；背离；违背）

diverse.meaning: very different from each other and of various kinds（不同的；相异的；多种多样的；形形色色的）

diversify.meaning: (especially of a business or company（尤指企业或公司）；to develop a wider range of products, interests, skills, etc. in order to be more successful or reduce risk（增加 … 的品种；从事多种经营；扩大业务范围）；to change or to make sth change so that there is greater variety（（使）多样化，变化，不同）

diversion.meaning: the act of changing the direction that sb/sth is following, or what sth is used for（转向；转移；偏离）；something that takes your attention away from sb/sth while sth else is happening（转移视线（或注意力）的事物）；a road or route that is used when the usual one is closed（临时绕行路；临时支路）；(formal) an activity that is done for pleasure, especially because it takes your attention away from sth else（消遣；娱乐）

diversity.meaning: a range of many people or things that are very different from each other（差异（性）；不同（点））；the quality or fact of including a range of many people or things（多样性；多样化）

divert.meaning: to make sb/sth change direction（使转向；使绕道；转移）；to use money, materials, etc. for a different purpose from their original purpose（改变（资金、材料等）的用途）；to take sb's thoughts or attention away from sth（转移（某人）的注意力；使分心）；(formal) to entertain people（娱乐；供消遣）

divide.meaning: to separate or make sth separate into parts（（使）分开，分散，分割，分成 …）；to separate sth into parts and give a share to each of a number of different people, etc.（分配；分享；分担）；to use different parts of your time, energy, etc. for different activities, etc.（把（时间、精力等）分别用于）；(formal) to separate two people or things（使分离；使分开）

dividend.meaning: an amount of the profits that a company pays to people who own shares in the company（红利；股息；股利）；(BrE) a money prize that is given to winners in the football pools（（足球彩票的）彩金）

divine.meaning: coming from or connected with God or a god（天赐的；上帝的；神的）；(old-fashioned) wonderful; beautiful（绝妙的；非凡的；极美的）；div·ine·ly /dɪˈvaɪnli; NAmEdɪˈvaɪnli/ adv. verb 1. [T] divine~ what, whether, etc. … | divine~ sth (formal) to find out sth by guessing（猜到；领悟）；to search for underground water using a stick in the shape of a Y, called a divining rod（（用丫形杖）探测（地下水））

division.meaning: the process or result of dividing into separate parts; the process or result of dividing sth or sharing it out（分开；分隔；分配；（分出来的）部分）；the process of dividing one number by another（除（法））；a disagreement or difference in opinion, way of life, etc., especially between members of a society or an organization（分歧；不和；差异）；a large and important unit or section of an organization（（机构的）部门）

divisive.meaning: causing people to be split into groups that disagree with or oppose each other（造成不和的；引起分歧的；制造分裂的）

divorce.meaning: the legal ending of a marriage（离婚）；a separation; the ending of a relationship between two things（分离；脱离）；to end your marriage to sb legally（与（某人）离婚；判（某人）离婚）；(formal) to separate a person, an idea, a subject, etc. from sth; to keep two things separate（使分离；使脱离）

divorced.meaning: no longer married（离婚的；离异的）；(formal) appearing not to be affected by sth; separate from sth（表现得不受影响的；脱离 … 的）

dizzy.meaning: feeling as if everything is spinning around you and that you are not able to balance（头晕目眩的；眩晕的）；making you feel dizzy; making you feel that a situation is changing very fast（使人眩晕的；使人头昏眼花的；使人感到变化太快的）；(informal) (especially NAmE) silly or stupid（愚蠢的；笨的）；diz·zily /; NAmE/ adv. diz·zi·ness /ˈdɪzinəs; NAmEˈdɪzinəs/ noun [U] IDM the dizzy ˈheights (of sth) (informal) an important or impressive position（重要的职位；显赫的地位）

dna.meaning: deoxyribonucleic acid (the chemical in the cells of animals and plants that carries genetic information and is a type of nucleic acid)（脱氧核糖核酸（动植物的细胞中带有基因信息的化学物质））

do.meaning: used to refer to actions that you do not mention by name or do not know about（做，干，办（某事））；to act or behave in the way mentioned（（以某种方式）做，行动，表现）；used to ask or talk about the success or progress of sb/sth（（问询或谈论时用）进展，进行）；to work at or perform an activity or a task（从事（工作）；进行（活动）；执行（任务））

dock.meaning: a part of a port where ships are repaired, or where goods are put onto or taken off them（船坞；船埠；码头）；a group of docks in a port and the buildings around them that are used for repairing ships, storing goods, etc.（港区）；(NAmE) a raised platform for loading vehicles or trains（（供运货汽车或铁路货车装卸货物的）月台）；the part of a court where the person who has been accused of a crime stands or sits during a trial（（法庭的）被告席）

doctor.meaning: a person who has been trained in medical science, whose job is to treat people who are ill/sick or injured（医生；大夫）；a place where a doctor sees patients（诊所）；a person who has received the highest university degree（博士）；(especially NAmE) used as a title or form of address for a dentist（（用作头衔或称呼）牙医）

doctoral.meaning: connected with a doctorate（博士的；博士学位的）

doctorate.meaning: the highest university degree（博士学位）

doctrine.meaning: a belief or set of beliefs held and taught by a Church, a political party, etc.（教义；主义；学说；信条）；(US) a statement of government policy（（政府政策的）正式声明）

document.meaning: an official paper or book that gives information about sth, or that can be used as evidence or proof of sth（文件；公文；文献；证件）；a computer file that contains text that has a name that identifies it（（计算机）文档，文件）；to record the details of sth（记录，记载（详情））；to prove or support sth with documents（用文件证明（或证实））

documentary.meaning: a film or a radio or television programme giving facts about sth（纪录片；纪实广播（或电视）节目）；consisting of documents（文件的；文献的；由文件（或文献）组成的）；giving a record of or report on the facts about sth, especially by using pictures, recordings, etc. of people involved（纪录的；纪实的）

documentation.meaning: the documents that are required for sth, or that give evidence or proof of sth（必备资料；证明文件）；the act of recording sth in a document; the state of being recorded in a document（文件记载；文献记录；归档）

dodge.meaning: to move quickly and suddenly to one side in order to avoid sb/sth（闪开；躲开；避开）；(rather informal) to avoid doing sth, especially in a dishonest way（（尤指不诚实地）逃避）；(informal) a clever and dishonest trick, played in order to avoid sth（推脱的计策；逃避的诡计；骗人的伎俩）

dog.meaning: an animal with four legs and a tail, often kept as a pet or trained for work, for example hunting or guarding buildings. There are many types of dog, some of which are wild.（狗；犬）；a male dog, fox or wolf（公狗；公狐；公狼）；(BrE) (informal) greyhound racing（赛狗；灵 赛）；(informal) (especially NAmE) a thing of low quality; a failure（蹩脚货；失败）

dogged.meaning: showing determination; not giving up easily（顽强的；坚持不懈的）

dogma.meaning: a belief or set of beliefs held by a group or organization, which others are expected to accept without argument（教义；教理；信条；教条）

dogwood.meaning: a bush or small tree with red or pink berries and red stems, that grows in northern regions; the hard wood of this tree（梾木；梾木的木材）

dole.meaning: (BrE) (informal) money paid by the state to unemployed people（失业救济金）；(informal) to give out an amount of food, money, etc. to a number of people in a group（发放，发给（食物、钱等）；施舍）

doll.meaning: a child's toy in the shape of a person, especially a baby or a child（玩偶；玩具娃娃）；(old-fashioned, informal) (especially NAmE) a word used to describe a pretty or attractive woman, now often considered offensive（俊妞，甜姐儿，美人儿（现多认为意含冒犯））；(informal) to make sb/yourself look attractive for a party, etc., with fashionable clothes（（把 … ）打扮得花枝招展，装扮得漂漂亮亮）

dollar.meaning: the unit of money in the US, Canada, Australia and several other countries（元（美国、加拿大、澳大利亚等国的货币单位））；a banknote or coin worth one dollar（一元（纸币或硬币））；(finance 财) the value of the US dollar compared with the value of the money of other countries（美元（币值））

dolphin.meaning: a sea animal (a mammal) that looks like a large fish with a pointed mouth. Dolphins are very intelligent and often friendly towards humans. There are several types of dolphin.（海豚）

domain.meaning: an area of knowledge or activity; especially one that sb is responsible for（（知识、活动的）领域，范围，范畴）；lands owned or ruled by a particular person, government, etc., especially in the past（（尤指旧时个人、国家等所拥有或统治的）领土，领地，势力范围）；(computing 计) a set of websites on the Internet which end with the same group of letters, for example ‘.com’, ‘.org’（域；定义域）；(mathematics 数) the range of possible values of a particular variable（区域；定义域）

dome.meaning: a round roof with a circular base（穹顶；圆屋顶）；a thing or a building shaped like a dome（圆顶状物；穹状建筑物）；(NAmE) (in names（用于名称）；a sports stadium whose roof is shaped like a dome（圆顶体育场）

domestic.meaning: of or inside a particular country; not foreign or international（本国的；国内的）；used in the home; connected with the home or family（家用的；家庭的；家务的）；liking home life; enjoying or good at cooking, cleaning the house, etc.（喜爱家庭生活的；享受家庭乐趣的；乐于操持家务的）；(of animals（动物）

domesticate.meaning: to make a wild animal used to living with or working for humans（驯养，驯化（动物））；to grow plants or crops for human use（栽培，培育（植物或农作物））；(often humorous) to make sb good at cooking, caring for a house, etc; to make sb enjoy home life（使精于家务；使喜家居）；do·mes·ti·cated AW /; NAmE/ adj. domesticated animals（驯养的动物）

dominant.meaning: more important, powerful or noticeable than other things（首要的；占支配地位的；占优势的；显著的）；(biology 生) a dominant gene causes a person to have a particular physical characteristic, for example brown eyes, even if only one of their parents has passed on this gene（（基因）显性的，优势的）；dom·in·ance AW /ˈdɒmɪnəns; NAmEˈdɑːmɪnəns/ noun [U] to achieve/assert dominance over sb（取得对某人的支配地位）

dominate.meaning: to control or have a lot of influence over sb/sth, especially in an unpleasant way（支配；控制；左右；影响）；to be the most important or noticeable feature of sth（在 … 中具有最重要（或明显）的特色）；to be the largest, highest or most obvious thing in a place（在 … 中最显眼的位置；俯视；高耸于）；(sport 体) to play much better than your opponent in a game（（在比赛中）占有优势，占据主动，控制战局）

don.meaning: (BrE) a teacher at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge（（尤指牛津大学和剑桥大学的）大学教师）；(informal) the leader of a group of criminals involved with the Mafia（黑手党头目）；(formal) to put clothes, etc. on（披上；穿上；戴上）

donate.meaning: to give money, food, clothes, etc. to sb/sth, especially a charity（（尤指向慈善机构）捐赠，赠送）；to allow doctors to remove blood or a body organ in order to help sb who needs it（献（血）；（台）捐（血））

donation.meaning: something that is given to a person or an organization such as a charity, in order to help them; the act of giving sth in this way（捐赠物；捐赠；赠送）

donkey.meaning: an animal of the horse family, with short legs and long ears. People ride donkeys or use them to carry heavy loads.（驴）；(BrE) (informal) a very long time（很长时间）

donor.meaning: a person or an organization that makes a gift of money, clothes, food, etc. to a charity, etc.（捐赠者；捐赠机构）；a person who gives blood or a part of his or her body to be used by doctors in medical treatment（献血者；器官捐献者）

doom.meaning: death or destruction; any terrible event that you cannot avoid（死亡；毁灭；厄运；劫数）；a general feeling of having lost all hope, and of pessimism (= expecting things to go badly)（悲观失望；无望；前景暗淡）；a person who predicts that things will go very badly（末日预言者）；to make sb/sth certain to fail, suffer, die, etc.（使 … 注定失败（或遭殃、死亡等））

door.meaning: a piece of wood, glass, etc. that is opened and closed so that people can get in and out of a room, building, car, etc; a similar thing in a cupboard/closet（门）；the space when a door is open（出入口；门口）；the area close to the entrance of a building（门边；门旁）；a house, room, etc. that is a particular number of houses, rooms, etc. away from another（栋；住户；人家）

doorknob.meaning: a type of round handle for a door, that you turn in order to open the door（球形门拉手）

doorway.meaning: an opening into a building or a room, where the door is（出入口；门口；门道）

dormant.meaning: not active or growing now but able to become active or to grow in the future（休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的）

dormitory.meaning: a room for several people to sleep in, especially in a school or other institution（宿舍；学生宿舍）；a building for university or college students to live in（（大学）学生宿舍）

dorsal.meaning: on or connected with the back of a fish or an animal（（鱼或动物）背部的，背上的，背侧的）

dosage.meaning: an amount of sth, usually a medicine or a drug, that is taken regularly over a particular period of time（（通常指药的）剂量）

dose.meaning: an amount of a medicine or a drug that is taken once, or regularly over a period of time（（药的）一剂，一服）；(informal) an amount of sth（一份；一次；一点）；(old-fashioned) (BrE informal) very fast and easily（迅速轻易地；一下子）；to give sb/yourself a medicine or drug（给（某人）服药）

dot.meaning: a small round mark, especially one that is printed（点；小点；小圆点）；(computing 计) a symbol like a full stop/period used to separate parts of a domain name, a URL or an email address（点（用以分隔域名、统一资源地址、电子邮件地址的组成部分））；(informal) exactly on time or at the exact time mentioned（准时；在指定时刻）；to put a dot above or next to a letter or word（打点于；在（字母上方、字母或单词旁边）加点）

double.meaning: twice as much or as many as usual（两倍的；加倍的）；having or made of two things or parts that are equal or similar（双的；成双的；成对的）；made for two people or things（供两者用的；双人的）；combining two things or qualities（双重的）

doubt.meaning: a feeling of being uncertain about sth or not believing sth（疑惑；疑问；不确定；不相信）；in a way that shows that sth is completely certain（无疑；确实）；to be uncertain（不肯定；不确定；拿不准）；to have reasons why you are not certain about whether sth is good or whether sth good will happen（（有理由）不相信；对（某事）持怀疑态度）

doubtful.meaning: (of a person（人）；not sure; uncertain and feeling doubt（拿不定主意；不确定；怀疑）；unlikely; not probable（未必；难说；不大可能）；(of a thing（事情）

dough.meaning: a mixture of flour, water, etc. that is made into bread and pastry（（用于制面包和糕点的）生面团）；(old-fashioned, slang) money（钱）

douse.meaning: to stop a fire from burning by pouring water over it; to put out a light（浇灭（火）；熄（灯））；to pour a lot of liquid over sb/sth; to soak sb/sth in liquid（往 … 上泼水；把 … 浸在液体里）

dove.meaning: a bird of the pigeon family. The white dove is often used as a symbol of peace.（鸽子（白鸽常作为和平的象征））；a person, especially a politician, who prefers peace and discussion to war（鸽派人物，温和派人物（尤指愿意和平与谈判而不愿战争的从政者））

down.meaning: to or at a lower place or position（向下；朝下；在下面）；from a standing or vertical position to a sitting or horizontal one（（坐、倒、躺）下）；at a lower level or rate（在较低水平；下降；下跌）；used to show that the amount or strength of sth is lower, or that there is less activity（（数量、力量、活动等）减少，减弱，降低）

downfall.meaning: the loss of a person's money, power, social position, etc; the thing that causes this（衰落；衰败；垮台；衰落（或衰败、垮台）的原因）

downhill.meaning: towards the bottom of a hill; in a direction that goes down（向山下；向下）；to get worse in quality, health, etc.（（质量、健康等）每况愈下，走下坡路，恶化）；going or sloping towards the bottom of a hill（下山的；下坡的；下斜的）；to be easy compared to what came before（（与前面的相比较）容易）

download.meaning: (computing 计) to move data to a smaller computer system from a larger one（下载；下装）；(computing 计) data which is downloaded from another computer system（已下载的数据资料）

downpour.meaning: a heavy fall of rain that often starts suddenly（倾盆大雨；暴雨；骤雨）

downstairs.meaning: down the stairs; on or to a floor or a house or building lower than the one you are on, especially the one at ground level（顺楼梯而下；在楼下；往楼下）；down·stairs adj. [only before noun] a downstairs bathroom（楼下的盥洗室）；the lower floor of a house or building, especially the one at ground level（楼下（尤指地面的一层））

downtown.meaning: in or towards the centre of a city, especially its main business area（在市中心，往市中心（尤指商业中心区））；ˈdown·town downtown downtowns /ˌdaʊnˈtaʊn; NAmEˌdaʊnˈtaʊn/ adj. a downtown store（闹市区的商店）；ˈdown·town downtown downtowns /; NAmE/ noun [U] a hotel in the heart of downtown（市区中心的旅馆）

downward.meaning: moving or pointing towards a lower level（下降的；向下的）

downwards.meaning: towards the ground or towards a lower level（向下）

doze.meaning: to sleep lightly for a short time（打瞌睡；打盹儿；小睡）；to go to sleep, especially during the day（（尤指在日间）打瞌睡，打盹儿）；a short period of sleep, usually during the day（（通常在日间的）瞌睡，小睡）

dozen.meaning: a group of twelve of the same thing（（一）打；十二个）；a group of approximately twelve people or things（十来个；十几个；十多个）；(informal) a lot of people or things（许多；很多）

drab.meaning: without interest or colour; dull and boring（单调乏味的；无光彩的；无生气的）

draft.meaning: a rough written version of sth that is not yet in its final form（草稿；草案；草图）；(finance 财) a written order to a bank to pay money to sb（汇票）；(NAmE) a system in which professional teams in some sports choose players each year from among college students（运动员选拔制（某些职业运动队每年在大学生中选拔新队员））；to write the first rough version of sth such as a letter, speech or book（起草；草拟）

drag.meaning: to pull sb/sth along with effort and difficulty（（使劲而吃力地）拖，拉，拽，扯）；to move yourself slowly and with effort（缓慢而费力地移动（或行进））；to persuade sb to come or go somewhere they do not really want to come or go to（生拉硬拽；劝人勉强来（或去））；(of time or an event（时间或活动）

dragon.meaning: (in stories) a large aggressive animal with wings and a long tail, that can breathe out fire（（传说中的）龙）；(disapproving) (especially BrE) a woman who behaves in an aggressive and frightening way（悍妇；母夜叉）

drain.meaning: to make sth empty or dry by removing all the liquid from it; to become empty or dry in this way（排空；（使）流光；放干）；to make liquid flow away from sth; to flow away（（使）流走，流出）；to empty a cup or glass by drinking everything in it（喝光；喝干）；to make sb/sth weaker, poorer, etc. by using up their/its strength, money, etc.（使（精力、金钱等）耗尽）

drainage.meaning: the process by which water or liquid waste is drained from an area（排水；放水）；a system of drains（排水系统）

drainpipe.meaning: a pipe that carries rainwater from the roof of a building to a drain（（把雨水从屋顶输送到下水道的）雨水管，排水管）；a pipe that carries dirty water or other liquid waste away from a building（（排放建筑物内污水的）排水管，泄水管）

dram.meaning: a small amount of an alcoholic drink, especially whisky（少量的酒（尤指威士忌））
