employ.meaning: to give sb a job to do for payment（雇用）；(formal) to use sth such as a skill, method, etc. for a particular purpose（应用；运用；使用）；if a person or their time is employed in doing sth, the person spends time doing that thing（从事于，忙于（做某事））；(formal) working for sb; employed by sb（替某人工作；为某人所雇用）

employee.meaning: a person who is paid to work for sb（受雇者；雇工；雇员）

employer.meaning: a person or company that pays people to work for them（雇用者；雇主；老板）

employment.meaning: work, especially when it is done to earn money; the state of being employed（工作；职业；受雇）；the situation in which people have work（就业）；the act of employing sb（雇用）；(formal) the use of sth（使用；利用）

empower.meaning: (formal) to give sb the power or authority to do sth（授权；给（某人）… 的权力）；to give sb more control over their own life or the situation they are in（增加（某人的）自主权；使控制局势）；em·power·ment /; NAmE/ noun [U] the empowerment of the individual（让个人掌握自己的命运）

empress.meaning: a woman who is the ruler of an empire（女皇）；the wife of an emperor（皇后）

emptiness.meaning: a feeling of being sad because nothing seems to have any value（空虚）；the fact that there is nothing or nobody in a place（空无；空旷）；(formal) a place that is empty（空地）

empty.meaning: with no people or things inside（空的）；(of sth that sb says or does（言语或行动）；with no meaning; not meaning what is said（空洞的；说话不算数的；无诚意的）；(of a person, or a person's life（人或其生活）

emulsion.meaning: any mixture of liquids that do not normally mix together, such as oil and water（乳状液；乳浊液；乳剂）；(BrE) a type of paint used on walls and ceilings that dries without leaving a shiny surface（乳胶漆（干后无光泽））；(technical 术语) a substance on the surface of photographic film that makes it sensitive to light（感光乳剂）

enable.meaning: to make it possible for sb to do sth（使能够；使有机会）；to make it possible for sth to happen or exist by creating the necessary conditions（使成为可能；使可行；使实现）

enact.meaning: (law 律) to pass a law（通过（法律））；(formal) to perform a play or act a part in a play（扮演；担任 … 角色；演出）；(formal) to take place（发生；进行；举行）

enactment.meaning: the process of a law becoming official; a law which has been made official（（法律、法案、法令的）制订，通过，颁布；法律；法规）

enamel.meaning: a substance that is melted onto metal, pots, etc. and forms a hard shiny surface to protect or decorate them; an object made from enamel（搪瓷；珐琅；搪瓷制品）；the hard white outer layer of a tooth（（牙齿的）珐琅质，釉质）；a type of paint that dries to leave a hard shiny surface（瓷漆；瓷釉）

encapsulate.meaning: (formal) to express the most important parts of sth in a few words, a small space or a single object（简述；概括；压缩）

encase.meaning: (formal) to surround or cover sth completely, especially to protect it（把 … 装箱（或围住、包起））

enchant.meaning: (formal) to attract sb strongly and make them feel very interested, excited, etc.（使着迷；使陶醉）；to place sb/sth under a magic spell (= magic words that have special powers)（使着魔；对 … 用魔法（或念咒语））

encircle.meaning: (formal) to surround sb/sth completely in a circle（环绕；围绕；包围）

enclose.meaning: to build a wall, fence, etc. around sth（（用墙、篱笆等）把 … 围起来）；(especially of a wall, fence, etc.（尤指墙、篱笆等）；to surround sth（围住）；to put sth in the same envelope, package, etc. as sth else（附入；随函（或包裹等）附上）

enclosure.meaning: a piece of land that is surrounded by a fence or wall and is used for a particular purpose（圈占地；圈用地；围场）；the act of placing a fence or wall around a piece of land（圈地）；something that is placed in an envelope with a letter（（信中）附件）

encode.meaning: to change ordinary language into letters, symbols, etc. in order to send secret messages（把 … 译成电码（或密码））；(computing 计) to change information into a form that can be processed by a computer（把 … 编码）；(linguistics 语言) to express the meaning of sth in a foreign language（把 … 译成外语）

encompass.meaning: to include a large number or range of things（包含，包括，涉及（大量事物））；to surround or cover sth completely（包围；围绕；围住）

encounter.meaning: to experience sth, especially sth unpleasant or difficult, while you are trying to do sth else（遭遇，遇到（尤指令人不快或困难的事））；(formal) to meet sb, or discover or experience sth, especially sb/sth new, unusual or unexpected（偶然碰到；意外地遇见；与 … 邂逅）；a meeting, especially one that is sudden, unexpected or violent（（尤指突然、意外或暴力的）相遇，邂逅，遭遇，冲突）；a sports match against a particular player or team（（体育）比赛，交锋）

encourage.meaning: to give sb support, courage or hope（支持；鼓励；激励）；to persuade sb to do sth by making it easier for them and making them believe it is a good thing to do（鼓动；劝告；怂恿）；to make sth more likely to happen or develop（促进；助长；刺激）；en·cour·aging /ɪnˈkʌrɪdʒɪŋ; NAmEɪnˈkɜːrɪdʒɪŋ/ adj. [not usually before noun] This month's unemployment figures are not very encouraging.（这个月的失业统计数字不太乐观。）

encouragement.meaning: the act of encouraging sb to do sth; something that encourages sb（鼓舞；鼓励；起激励作用的事物）

encroach.meaning: (disapproving) to begin to affect or use up too much of sb's time, rights, personal life, etc.（侵占（某人的时间）；侵犯（某人的权利）；扰乱（某人的生活））；to slowly begin to cover more and more of an area（侵蚀，蚕食（地区））；en·croach·ment encroachment encroachments /ɪnˈkrəʊtʃmənt; NAmEɪnˈkroʊtʃmənt/ noun [U, C] encroachment~ (on/upon sth) the regime's many encroachments on human rights（这个政权种种侵犯人权的行为）

encyclopedia.meaning: a book or set of books giving information about all areas of knowledge or about different areas of one particular subject, usually arranged in alphabetical order; a similar collection of information on a website or CD-ROM（（纸质、网络或光盘版）百科全书；（某一学科的）专科全书）

end.meaning: the final part of a period of time, an event, an activity or a story（（时间、事件、活动或故事的）终止，终结，结局，结尾）；the part of an object or a place that is the furthest away from its centre（末端；尽头；末梢）；a situation in which sth does not exist any more（结束；破灭）；an aim or a purpose（目的；目标）

endanger.meaning: to put sb/sth in a situation in which they could be harmed or damaged（使遭危险；危及；危害）

endear.meaning: to make sb/yourself popular（使受欢迎（或喜爱、爱慕））

endeavour.meaning: (formal) an attempt to do sth, especially sth new or difficult（（尤指新的或艰苦的）努力，尝试）；(formal) to try very hard to do sth（努力；尽力；竭力）

ending.meaning: the last part of a story, film/movie, etc.（（故事、电影等的）结尾，结局）；the act of finishing sth; the last part of sth（结束；终结；最后部分）；the last part of a word, that is added to a main part（词尾；（台）字尾）

endless.meaning: very large in size or amount and seeming to have no end（无止境的；无垠的；无穷无尽的；不计其数的）；continuing for a long time and seeming to have no end（永久的；不断的；无休止的）；(of a loop, etc.（环状物）；having the ends joined together so it forms one piece（两端连接的；环状的）

endocrine.meaning: connected with glands that put hormones and other products directly into the blood（内分泌腺的；内分泌的）

endocrinology.meaning: the part of medicine concerning the endocrine system and hormones（内分泌学）

endogenous.meaning: (of a disease or symptom（疾病或症状）；having no obvious cause（内源性的；内生的）

endorse.meaning: to say publicly that you support a person, statement or course of action（（公开）赞同，支持，认可）；to say in an advertisement that you use and like a particular product so that other people will want to buy it（（在广告中）宣传，代言（某一产品））；to write your name on the back of a cheque so that it can be paid into a bank account（（在支票背面）签名，背书）；(BrE) to write details of a driving offence on sb's driving licence（（在驾驶执照上）记录违章事项）

endorsement.meaning: a public statement or action showing that you support sb/sth（（公开的）赞同，支持，认可）；a statement made in an advertisement, usually by sb famous or important, saying that they use and like a particular product（（通常由名人或要人在广告中为某一产品的）宣传，代言）；(BrE) details of a driving offence written on sb's driving licence（（驾驶执照上的）违章记录）

endow.meaning: to give a large sum of money to a school, a college or another institution to provide it with an income（（向学校等机构）捐钱，捐赠，资助）；(formal) to naturally have a particular feature, quality, etc.（天生赋有，生来具有（某种特性、品质等））；to believe or imagine that sb/sth has a particular quality（认为 … 具有某种品质）；to give sth to sb/sth（给予；赋予）

endowment.meaning: money that is given to a school, a college or another institution to provide it with an income; the act of giving this money（捐款；捐赠；资助）；a quality or an ability that you are born with（天赋；天资；才能）

endurance.meaning: the ability to continue doing sth painful or difficult for a long period of time without complaining（忍耐力；耐久力）

endure.meaning: to experience and deal with sth that is painful or unpleasant, especially without complaining（忍耐；忍受）；to continue to exist for a long time（持续；持久）；en·dur·able /ɪnˈdjʊərəbl; NAmEɪnˈdʊrəbl/ adj. I felt that life was no longer endurable.（我感到生活再也无法忍受。）

enemy.meaning: a person who hates sb or who acts or speaks against sb/sth（敌人；仇人；反对者）；a country that you are fighting a war against; the soldiers, etc. of this country（敌国；敌军；敌兵）；(formal) anything that harms sth or prevents it from being successful（危害物；大敌）

energetic.meaning: having or needing a lot of energy and enthusiasm（精力充沛的；充满活力的；需要能量的；积极的）

energy.meaning: the ability to put effort and enthusiasm into an activity, work, etc.（精力；活力；干劲）；the physical and mental effort that you use to do sth（精力；力量）；a source of power, such as fuel, used for driving machines, providing heat, etc.（能源）；(physics 物) the ability of matter or radiation to work because of its mass, movement, electric charge, etc.（能；能量）

enforce.meaning: to make sure that people obey a particular law or rule（强制执行，强行实施（法律或规定））；to make sth happen or force sb to do sth（强迫；迫使）；en·force·able /ɪnˈfɔːsəbl; NAmEɪnˈfɔːrsəbl/ adj. A gambling debt is not legally enforceable.（赌债不能通过法律手段强制偿还。）；en·force·ment AW /ɪnˈfɔːsmənt; NAmEɪnˈfɔːrsmənt/ noun [U] strict enforcement of regulations（规章的严格执行）

enforcer.meaning: a person whose responsibility is to make sure that other people perform the actions they are supposed to, especially in a government（实施者；强制执行者）

engage.meaning: (formal) to succeed in attracting and keeping sb's attention and interest（吸引住（注意力、兴趣））；(formal) to employ sb to do a particular job（雇用；聘用）；to become involved with and try to understand sth/sb（与 … 建立密切关系；尽力理解）；(formal) to begin fighting with sb（与（某人）交战；与（某人）开战）

engaged.meaning: (formal) busy doing sth（忙于；从事于）；having agreed to marry sb（已订婚）；(of a telephone line（电话线）；being used（被占用的；使用中的）

engagement.meaning: an agreement to marry sb; the period during which two people are engaged（订婚；订婚期间）；an arrangement to do sth at a particular time, especially sth official or sth connected with your job（（尤指正式的或与工作有关的）约定，约会，预约）；(technical 术语) fighting between two armies, etc.（战斗；交战）；(formal) being involved with sb/sth in an attempt to understand them/it（（与 … 的）密切关系；（对 … 的）了解）

engender.meaning: (formal) to make a feeling or situation exist（产生，引起（某种感觉或情况））

engine.meaning: the part of a vehicle that produces power to make the vehicle move（发动机；引擎）；a vehicle that pulls a train（火车头；机车）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；having the type or number of engines mentioned（有 … 型发动机的；有 … 个引擎的）

engineer.meaning: a person whose job involves designing and building engines, machines, roads, bridges, etc.（工程师；设计师）；a person who is trained to repair machines and electrical equipment（机修工；技师；技工）；a person whose job is to control and repair engines, especially on a ship or an aircraft（（船上的）轮机手；（飞机上的）机械师）；a person whose job is driving a railway/railroad engine（火车司机；机车司机）

engineering.meaning: the activity of applying scientific knowledge to the design, building and control of machines, roads, bridges, electrical equipment, etc.（工程）；the study of engineering as a subject（工程学）

english.meaning: the language, originally of England, now spoken in many other countries and used as a language of international communication throughout the world（英语；英文）；English language or literature as a subject of study（（作为一门学科的）英语语言文学；英语学科）；the people of England (sometimes wrongly used to mean the British, including the Scots, the Welsh and the Northern Irish)（英格兰人（有时误用以指包括苏格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰人在内的英国人））；connected with England, its people or its language（英格兰的；英格兰人的；英语的）

englishman.meaning: a man from England（英格兰（男）人；英国（男）人）；(saying) a person's home is a place where they can be private and safe and do as they like（英国人的家就是他的城堡）

engrave.meaning: to cut words or designs on wood, stone, metal, etc.（在 … 上雕刻（字或图案））；to be sth that you will never forget because it affected you so strongly（牢记，铭记，深深印入（心中、记忆中、头脑中等））

engraving.meaning: a picture made by cutting a design on a piece of metal and then printing the design on paper（版画；雕版印刷品）；the art or process of cutting designs on wood, stone, metal, etc.（雕刻（术）；镌版术）

engross.meaning: if sth engrosses you, it is so interesting that you give it all your attention and time（使全神贯注；占去（某人的）全部注意力和时间）；en·gross·ing /ɪnˈɡrəʊsɪŋ; NAmEɪnˈɡroʊsɪŋ/ adj. an engrossing problem（引人关注的问题）

engulf.meaning: to surround or to cover sb/sth completely（包围；吞没；淹没）；to affect sb/sth very strongly（严重影响）

enhance.meaning: to increase or further improve the good quality, value or status of sb/sth（提高；增强；增进）；en·hanced AW /; NAmE/ adj. enhanced efficiency（提高了的效率）；en·hance·ment AW enhancement enhancements /ɪnˈhɑːnsmənt; NAmEɪnˈhænsmənt/ noun [U, C] equipment for the enhancement of sound quality（音质提升设备）

enigma.meaning: a person, thing or situation that is mysterious and difficult to understand（神秘的人；费解的事物；令人困惑的处境）

enigmatic.meaning: mysterious and difficult to understand（神秘的；费解的；令人困惑的）；en·ig·mat·ic·al·ly /ˌenɪɡˈmætɪkli; NAmEˌenɪɡˈmætɪkli/ adv. ‘I might,’ he said enigmatically.（“我也许会的。”他神秘地说道。）

enjoy.meaning: to get pleasure from sth（享受 … 的乐趣；欣赏；喜爱）；to be happy and get pleasure from what you are doing（过得快活；玩得痛快；得到乐趣）；(formal) to have sth good that is an advantage to you（享有；享受）；(informal) used to say that you hope sb gets pleasure from sth that you are giving them or recommending to them（（祝愿时说）玩痛快些，过愉快些，好好欣赏）

enjoyable.meaning: giving pleasure（有乐趣的；使人快乐的；令人愉快的）；en·joy·ably /ɪnˈdʒɔɪəbli; NAmEɪnˈdʒɔɪəbli/ adv. The evening passed enjoyably.（这个晚上过得很愉快。）

enjoyment.meaning: the pleasure that you get from sth（愉快；快乐；乐趣）；something that gives you pleasure（乐事；令人愉快的事）；(formal) the fact of having and using sth（享有；享受）

enlarge.meaning: to make sth bigger; to become bigger（扩大；扩充；扩展；增大）；to make a bigger copy of a photograph or document（放大（照片或文件））；en·larged /; NAmE/ adj. an enlarged heart（肥大的心脏）；(formal) to say or write more about sth that has been mentioned（详述；细说）

enlargement.meaning: the process or result of sth becoming or being made larger（扩大；扩充；扩展；增大）；something that has been made larger, especially a photograph（扩大物，放大物（尤指照片））

enlighten.meaning: (formal) to give sb information so that they understand sth better（启发；开导；阐明）；en·light·en·ing /ɪnˈlaɪtnɪŋ; NAmEɪnˈlaɪtnɪŋ/ adj. It was a very enlightening interview.（那次面谈让人很受启发。）

enlightenment.meaning: knowledge about and understanding of sth; the process of understanding sth or making sb understand it（启迪；启发；开导；开明）；the period in the 18th century when many writers and scientists began to argue that science and reason were more important than religion and tradition（（18 世纪欧洲的）启蒙运动）

enormous.meaning: extremely large（巨大的；庞大的；极大的）

enough.meaning: used before plural or uncountable nouns to mean ‘as many or as much as sb needs or wants’（（用于复数或不可数名词前）足够的，充足的，充分的）；Although enough after a noun now sounds old-fashioned, time enough is still fairly common.（尽管 enough 置于名词后似乎有点过时，但 time enough 仍然相当常用）；as many or as much as sb needs or wants（足够；充分；充足）；(informal) (especially NAmE) used to say that sth is annoying or boring and that you want it to stop（行了；早已够了）

enquire.meaning: [I, T] (rather formal) to ask sb for some information（询问；打听）；In British English people sometimes distinguish between enquire and inquire, using enquire for the general meaning of ‘ask for information’ and inquire for the more particular meaning of ‘officially investigate’.（在英式英语中，人们有时会区分 enquire 和 inquire 的用法，用 enquire 表示一般意义上的询问、打听，用 inquire 表示特别意义上的探究、查询、调查）；However, you can use either spelling in either meaning. In American English inquire is usually used in both meanings.（不过两种拼写用于两个意思均可。在美式英语中，通常两种意思均用 inquire。）；(formal) to ask for information about sb, especially about their health or about what they are doing（向某人问好（或问候））

enquiry.meaning: an official process to find out the cause of sth or to find out information about sth（调查；查究；查问）；a request for information about sb/sth; a question about sb/sth（询问；打听）；the act of asking questions or collecting information about sb/sth（查询；探究；探索）；(BrE) a place where you can get information（问讯处）

enrich.meaning: to improve the quality of sth, often by adding sth to it（充实；使丰富；使饱含（某物））；to make sb/sth rich or richer（使富有；使富裕）

enrol.meaning: to arrange for yourself or for sb else to officially join a course, school, etc.（（使）加入；注册；登记）

enrolment.meaning: the act of officially joining a course, school, etc; the number of people who do this（入学，注册，登记（人数））

ensemble.meaning: a small group of musicians, dancers or actors who perform together（乐团，剧团，舞剧团（全体成员））；(formal) a number of things considered as a group（全体；整体）；a set of clothes that are worn together（全套服装）

ensue.meaning: to happen after or as a result of another event（接着发生；因而产生）；en·su·ing /ɪnˈsjuːɪŋ; NAmEɪnˈsuːɪŋ/ adj. He had become separated from his parents in the ensuing panic.（在随后的慌乱中他便与父母分散了。）

ensure.meaning: to make sure that sth happens or is definite（保证；担保；确保）

entail.meaning: to involve sth that cannot be avoided（牵涉；需要；使必要）

entangle.meaning: to make sb/sth become caught or twisted in sth（使纠缠；缠住；套住）；to involve sb in a difficult or complicated situation（使卷入；使陷入）

entanglement.meaning: a difficult or complicated relationship with another person or country（瓜葛；牵连）；the act of becoming entangled in sth; the state of being entangled（纠缠；缠住）；(technical 术语) barriers made of barbed wire, used to stop an enemy from getting close（铁丝网（用以阻止敌人靠近））

enter.meaning: (not usually used in the passive（通常不用于被动语态）；to come or go into sth（进来；进去；进入）；(formal) to become a member of an institution; to start working in an organization or a profession（成为 … 的一员；加入；开始从事）；to begin or become involved in an activity, a situation, etc.（开始参加；开始进入；着手进行）

enterprise.meaning: a company or business（公司；企业单位；事业单位）；a large project, especially one that is difficult（（尤指艰巨而重大的）规划，事业）；the development of businesses by the people of a country rather than by the government（企业发展；企业经营；企业活动）；(approving) the ability to think of new projects and make them successful（事业心；进取心；创业精神）

enterprising.meaning: having or showing the ability to think of new projects or new ways of doing things and make them successful（有事业心的；有进取心的；有创业精神的）

entertain.meaning: to invite people to eat or drink with you as your guests, especially in your home（（尤指在自己家中）招待，款待）；to interest and amuse sb in order to please them（使有兴趣；使快乐；娱乐）；(formal) to consider or allow yourself to think about an idea, a hope, a feeling, etc.（心存，怀有（想法、希望、感觉等））

entertainer.meaning: a person whose job is amusing or interesting people, for example, by singing, telling jokes or dancing（（歌唱、说笑话、舞蹈等的）演员，表演者，艺人）

entertaining.meaning: interesting and amusing（有趣的；娱乐的；使人愉快的）

entertainment.meaning: films/movies, music, etc. used to entertain people; an example of this（娱乐片；文娱节目；表演会；娱乐活动）；the act of entertaining sb（招待；款待；娱乐）

enthusiasm.meaning: a strong feeling of excitement and interest in sth and a desire to become involved in it（热情；热心；热忱）；(formal) something that you are very interested in and spend a lot of time doing（热衷的事物；激发热情的事物）

enthusiast.meaning: a person who is very interested in sth and spends a lot of time doing it（热衷于 … 的人；热心者；爱好者）；a person who approves of sth and shows enthusiasm for it（热烈支持者；热情赞成者）

enthusiastic.meaning: feeling or showing a lot of excitement and interest about sb/sth（热情的；热心的；热烈的；满腔热忱的）

entice.meaning: to persuade sb/sth to go somewhere or to do sth, usually by offering them sth（诱使；引诱）；en·tice·ment enticement enticements /ɪnˈtaɪsmənt; NAmEɪnˈtaɪsmənt/ noun [C, U] The party is offering low taxation as its main enticement.（这个党正提出低税收，以此作为其主要的诱人举措。）

entire.meaning: (used when you are emphasizing that the whole of sth is involved（用以强调涉及全部）；including everything, everyone or every part（全部的；整个的；完全的）

entirely.meaning: in every way possible; completely（全部地；完整地；完全地）

entirety.meaning: the whole of sth（全部；全体；整体）；as a whole, rather than in parts（作为整体；整个地；全面地）

entitle.meaning: to give sb the right to have or to do sth（使享有权利；使符合资格）；to give a title to a book, play, etc.（给 … 命名（或题名））

entity.meaning: something that exists separately from other things and has its own identity（独立存在物；实体）

entomb.meaning: to bury or completely cover sb/sth so that they cannot get out, be seen, etc.（掩埋；埋葬）；to put a dead body in a tomb（把（尸体）葬入坟墓）

entrance.meaning: a door, gate, passage, etc. used for entering a room, building or place（大门（口）；入口（处）；通道）；the act of entering a room, building or place, especially in a way that attracts the attention of other people（进入；出场；登场）；the right or opportunity to enter a building or place（进入权；进入机会）；the act of becoming involved in sth（卷入；参与）

entrant.meaning: a person who has recently joined a profession, university, etc.（新职员；新生；新会员；新成员）；a person or an animal that enters a race or a competition; a person that enters an exam（参赛者（或动物）；考生）

entreat.meaning: to ask sb to do sth in a serious and often emotional way（恳求；乞求）

entrench.meaning: (sometimes disapproving) to establish sth very firmly so that it is very difficult to change（使处于牢固地位；牢固确立）

entrepreneur.meaning: a person who makes money by starting or running businesses, especially when this involves taking financial risks（创业者，企业家（尤指涉及财务风险的））；en·tre·pre·neur·ial /ˌɒntrəprəˈnɜːriəl; NAmEˌɑːntrəprəˈnɜːriəl/ adj. entrepreneurial skills（办企业的能力）

entrust.meaning: to make sb responsible for doing sth or taking care of sb（委托；交托；托付）

entry.meaning: an act of going into or getting into a place（进入（指行动））；the right or opportunity to enter a place（进入（指权利、机会））；the right or opportunity to take part in sth or become a member of a group（参与，加入（指权利、机会））；something that you do, write or make to take part in a competition, for example answering a set of questions（参赛作品；竞赛答题）

entwine.meaning: to twist or wind sth around sth else（盘绕；缠绕）；to be very closely involved or connected with sth（与 … 密切相关（或紧密相联））

enumerate.meaning: (formal) to name things on a list one by one（列举；枚举）

envelop.meaning: (formal) to wrap sb/sth up or cover them or it completely（包住；裹住；盖住）

envelope.meaning: a flat paper container used for sending letters in（信封）；a flat container made of plastic for keeping papers in（塑料封套；塑料封皮；（台）塑胶封套）

envious.meaning: wanting to be in the same situation as sb else; wanting sth that sb else has（羡慕的；忌妒的）；en·vi·ous·ly /ˈenviəsli; NAmEˈenviəsli/ adv. They look enviously at the success of their European counterparts.（他们看着欧洲同行的成功，羡慕不已。）

environment.meaning: the conditions that affect the behaviour and development of sb/sth; the physical conditions that sb/sth exists in（（影响个体行为或事物发展的）环境；客观环境）；the natural world in which people, animals and plants live（自然环境；生态环境）；(computing 计) the complete structure within which a user, computer or program operates（（运行）环境；工作平台；软件包）

environmental.meaning: connected with the natural conditions in which people, animals and plants live; connected with the environment（自然环境的；生态环境的；有关环境的）；connected with the conditions that affect the behaviour and development of sb/sth（（有关影响个体或事物行为或发展）环境的）；en·vir·on·men·tal·ly AW /ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentəli; NAmEɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentəli/ adv. an environmentally sensitive area (= one that is easily damaged or that contains rare animals, plants, etc.)（生态环境脆弱的地区）

environmentalist.meaning: a person who is concerned about the natural environment and wants to improve and protect it（环境保护论者）

envisage.meaning: to imagine what will happen in the future（想像；设想；展望）

envision.meaning: (formal) to imagine what a situation will be like in the future, especially a situation you intend to work towards（展望；想像）

envy.meaning: the feeling of wanting to be in the same situation as sb else; the feeling of wanting sth that sb else has（羡慕；忌妒）；to be a person or thing that other people admire and that causes feelings of envy（成为羡慕（或忌妒）的对象；成为羡慕（或忌妒）的东西）；to wish you had the same qualities, possessions, opportunities, etc. as sb else（羡慕；忌妒）；to be glad that you do not have to do what sb else has to do（庆幸（不必做别人非做不可的事））

enzyme.meaning: a substance, produced by all living things, which helps a chemical change happen or happen more quickly, without being changed itself（酶）

eon.meaning: (formal) an extremely long period of time; thousands of years（极漫长的时间；千万年）；(geology 地) a major division of time, divided into eras（宙（地质学上的年代分期，下分代））

ephemeral.meaning: lasting or used for only a short period of time（短暂的；瞬息的）

epic.meaning: a long poem about the actions of great men and women or about a nation's history; this style of poetry（叙事诗；史诗）；a long film/movie or book that contains a lot of action, usually about a historical subject（史诗般的电影（或书））；(sometimes humorous) a long and difficult job or activity that you think people should admire（壮举；惊人之举）；having the features of an epic（具有史诗性质的；史诗般的）

epidemic.meaning: a large number of cases of a particular disease happening at the same time in a particular community（流行病）；a sudden rapid increase in how often sth bad happens（（坏事迅速的）泛滥，蔓延）；epi·dem·ic adj. Car theft is now reaching epidemic proportions.（汽车偷盗现已近泛滥成灾。）

epidermis.meaning: the outer layer of the skin（表皮）

episode.meaning: an event, a situation, or a period of time in sb's life, a novel, etc. that is important or interesting in some way（（人生的）一段经历；（小说的）片段，插曲）；one part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio in several parts（（电视连续剧或广播剧的）一集）

episodic.meaning: happening occasionally and not at regular intervals（偶尔发生的；不定期的）；(of a story, etc.（故事等）；containing or consisting of many separate and different events（由松散片段组成的；有许多片段的）

epistle.meaning: any of the letters in the New Testament of the Bible, written by the first people who followed Christ（使徒书信，宗徒书信（《〈圣经〉新约》书卷））；(formal or humorous) a long, serious letter on an important subject（（文体郑重、内容重要、篇幅较长的）书信）

epithet.meaning: an adjective or phrase that is used to describe sb/sth's character or most important quality, especially in order to give praise or criticism（（尤用于褒贬人或事物特征或性质的）表述形容词，修饰语）；(especially NAmE) an offensive word or phrase that is used about a person or group of people（别称；绰号；诨名）

epitome.meaning: (formal) a perfect example of sth（典型；典范）

epoch.meaning: a period of time in history, especially one during which important events or changes happen（时代；纪元；时期）；(geology 地) a length of time which is a division of a period（世（地质年代，纪下分世））

epoch-making.meaning: having a very important effect on people's lives and on history（划时代的；开创新纪元的；意义重大的）

equal.meaning: the same in size, quantity, value, etc. as sth else（（大小、数量、价值等）相同的，同样的；相等的）；having the same rights or being treated the same as other people, without differences such as race, religion or sex being considered（平等的；同等的）；(formal) having the necessary strength, courage and ability to deal with sth successfully（（力气、勇气、能力）相当的；能胜任的；能应付的）；having the same advantages and disadvantages as sb else（（与某人）处于平等的地位）

equality.meaning: the fact of being equal in rights, status, advantages, etc.（平等；均等；相等）

equally.meaning: to the same degree; in the same or in a similar way（平等地；同样地）；in equal parts, amounts, etc.（平均地；相等地；均等地）；used to introduce another phrase or idea that adds to and is as important as what you have just said（（引出同样重要的内容）同样，此外，也）

equation.meaning: (mathematics 数) a statement showing that two amounts or values are equal, for example 2x + y = 54（方程；方程式；等式）；the act of making sth equal or considering sth as equal (= of equating them)（相等；等同看待）；a problem or situation in which several things must be considered and dealt with（（多种因素的）平衡，综合体）

equator.meaning: an imaginary line around the earth at an equal distance from the North and South Poles（赤道）

equatorial.meaning: near the equator or typical of a country that is near the equator（赤道的；赤道附近的；赤道地区特有的）

equestrian.meaning: connected with riding horses, especially as a sport（骑术的）

equilibrium.meaning: a state of balance, especially between opposing forces or influences（平衡；均衡；均势）；a calm state of mind and a balance of emotions（（心情、情绪）平静，安宁；心理平衡）

equip.meaning: to provide yourself/sb/sth with the things that are needed for a particular purpose or activity（配备；装备）；to prepare sb for an activity or task, especially by teaching them what they need to know（使有所准备；使有能力）

equipment.meaning: the things that are needed for a particular purpose or activity（设备；器材）；the process of providing a place or person with necessary things（配备；装备）

equitable.meaning: fair and reasonable; treating everyone in an equal way（公平合理的；公正的）

equity.meaning: the trade/labor union for actors in the UK, the US and some other countries（（英、美等国的）演员工会）

equivalent.meaning: equal in value, amount, meaning, importance, etc.（（价值、数量、意义、重要性等）相等的，相同的）；equiva·lence AW equivalence equivalences /ɪˈkwɪvələns; NAmEɪˈkwɪvələns/ noun [U] (formal) There is no straightforward equivalence between economic progress and social well-being.（经济进步与社会福利之间绝非轻易等同。）；a thing, amount, word, etc. that is equivalent to sth else（相等的东西；等量；对应词）

equivocal.meaning: (of words or statements（言语或陈述）；not having one clear or definite meaning or intention; able to be understood in more than one way（模棱两可的；意义双关的；含糊其词的）；(of actions or behaviour（行动或行为）；difficult to understand or explain clearly or easily（难以理解的；难以解释清楚的）

era.meaning: a period of time, usually in history, that is different from other periods because of particular characteristics or events（时代；年代；纪元）；(geology 地) a length of time which is a division of an aeon（代（地质年代，宙下分代））

eradicate.meaning: to destroy or get rid of sth completely, especially sth bad（根除；消灭；杜绝）

erase.meaning: to remove sth completely（清除；消除；消灭）；to make a mark or sth you have written disappear, for example by rubbing it, especially in order to correct it（擦掉，抹掉（笔迹等））；to remove a recording from a tape or information from a computer's memory（抹去，清洗（磁带上的录音或存贮器中的信息））

eraser.meaning: a small piece of rubber or a similar substance, used for removing pencil marks from paper; a piece of soft material used for removing chalk marks from a blackboard（橡皮擦；黑板擦）

erasure.meaning: the act of removing or destroying sth（擦掉；抹掉；消除；消灭；删除）

erect.meaning: (formal) in a vertical position（垂直的；竖直的；直立的）；(of the penis or nipples（阴茎或乳头）；larger than usual, stiff and standing up because of sexual excitement（（因性兴奋）勃起的，坚挺的）；to build sth（建立；建造）

erection.meaning: if a man has an erection, his penis is hard and stands up because he is sexually excited（（阴茎）勃起）；(formal) the act of building sth or putting it in a vertical position（建造；竖立）；(formal) a structure or building, especially a large one（（尤指大型）结构，建筑物）

erode.meaning: to gradually destroy the surface of sth through the action of wind, rain, etc; to be gradually destroyed in this way（侵蚀；腐蚀；风化）；to gradually destroy sth or make it weaker over a period of time; to be destroyed or made weaker in this way（逐渐毁坏；削弱；损害）；ero·sion AW erosion erosions /ɪˈrəʊʒn; NAmEɪˈroʊʒn/ noun [U] the erosion of the coastline by the sea（海水对海岸线的侵蚀）

err.meaning: to make a mistake（犯错误；做错事；出差错）；to show too much of a good quality（过于；失之）

errand.meaning: a job that you do for sb that involves going somewhere to take a message, to buy sth, deliver goods, etc.（差使；差事）

erratic.meaning: (often disapproving) not happening at regular times; not following any plan or regular pattern; that you cannot rely on（不规则的；不确定的；不稳定的；不可靠的）；er·rat·ic·al·ly /ɪˈrætɪkli; NAmEɪˈrætɪkli/ adv. He was obviously upset and was driving erratically.（他显然心烦意乱，开起车来摇晃不定。）；(geology 地) a large rock that is different from the rock around and was left behind when a large mass of ice melted（漂砾；漂石）

erroneous.meaning: not correct; based on wrong information（错误的）

error.meaning: a mistake, especially one that causes problems or affects the result of sth（错误；差错；谬误）；(formal or humorous) to realize or admit that you have done sth wrong and decide to change your behaviour（知过即改；承认自己的做法不对并决心改正）

erupt.meaning: when a volcano erupts or burning rocks, smoke, etc. erupt or are erupted, the burning rocks, etc. are thrown out from the volcano（（火山）爆发；（岩浆、烟等）喷出）；to start happening, suddenly and violently（突然发生；爆发）；to suddenly express your feelings very strongly, especially by shouting loudly（突然发出（尤指叫喊））；(of spots, etc.（斑点等）

escalate.meaning: to become or make sth greater, worse, more serious, etc.（（使）逐步扩大，不断恶化，加剧）；es·cal·ation escalation escalations /ˌeskəˈleɪʃn; NAmEˌeskəˈleɪʃn/ noun [C, U] an escalation in food prices（食品价格的不断上涨）

escalator.meaning: moving stairs that carry people between different floors of a large building（自动扶梯；电扶梯；滚梯）

escape.meaning: to get away from a place where you have been kept as a prisoner or not allowed to leave（（从监禁或管制中）逃跑，逃走，逃出）；to get away from an unpleasant or dangerous situation（（从不愉快或危险处境中）逃脱，摆脱，逃避）；to avoid sth unpleasant or dangerous（避开，避免（不愉快或危险的事物））；to suffer no harm or less harm than you would expect（（没有受伤或只受了一点伤害而）逃脱，幸免于难）

escort.meaning: a person or group of people or vehicles that travels with sb/sth in order to protect or guard them（护送者；护卫队；护卫舰（或车队、飞机））；(formal or old-fashioned) a person, especially a man, who takes sb to a particular social event（陪同某人参加社交活动的人（尤指男人））；a person, especially a woman, who is paid to go out socially with sb（受雇陪同某人外出社交的人（尤指女人））；to go with sb to protect or guard them or to show them the way（护卫；护送）

escutcheon.meaning: a flat piece of metal around a keyhole, door handle, or light switch（孔罩；锁眼盖；门把手盖板；电灯开关板）；a shield that has a coat of arms on it（盾形饰牌）

esoteric.meaning: likely to be understood or enjoyed by only a few people with a special knowledge or interest（只有内行才懂的；难领略的）

esp..meaning: (in writing) especially（（书写形式）尤其，特别）

especial.meaning: greater or better than usual; special in some way or for a particular group（格外的；特别的；特殊的）

especially.meaning: more with one person, thing, etc. than with others, or more in particular circumstances than in others（尤其；特别；格外）；for a particular purpose, person, etc.（专门；特地）；very much; to a particular degree（十分；非常）

essay.meaning: a short piece of writing by a student as part of a course of study（（作为课程作业，学生写的）文章，短文）；a short piece of writing on a particular subject, written in order to be published（（用来刊登的）论说文，小品文）；(formal) an attempt to do sth（企图；尝试）；(literary) to try to do sth（企图；试图）

essayist.meaning: a person who writes essays to be published（论说文（或小品文）作者）

essence.meaning: the most important quality or feature of sth, that makes it what it is（本质；实质；精髓）；a liquid taken from a plant, etc. that contains its smell and taste in a very strong form（香精；精油）；necessary and very important（必不可少；非常重要）

essential.meaning: completely necessary; extremely important in a particular situation or for a particular activity（完全必要的；必不可少的；极其重要的）；connected with the most important aspect or basic nature of sb/sth（本质的；基本的；根本的）；something that is needed in a particular situation or in order to do a particular thing（必不可少的东西；必需品）；an important basic fact or piece of knowledge about a subject（要点；要素；实质）

essentially.meaning: when you think about the true, important or basic nature of sb/sth（本质上；根本上；基本上）

establish.meaning: to start or create an organization, a system, etc. that is meant to last for a long time（建立；创立；设立）；to start having a relationship, especially a formal one, with another person, group or country（建立（尤指正式关系））；to hold a position for long enough or succeed in sth well enough to make people accept and respect you（确立；使立足；使稳固）；to make people accept a belief, claim, custom etc.（使 … 获得接受；使 … 得到认可）

established.meaning: respected or given official status because it has existed or been used for a long time（已确立的；已获确认的；确定的）；(of a person（人）；well known and respected in a job, etc. that they have been doing for a long time（著名的；成名的；公认的）；(of a Church or a religion（教会或宗教）

establishment.meaning: (formal) an organization, a large institution or a hotel（机构；大型机关；企业；旅馆）；(often disapproving) the people in a society or a profession who have influence and power and who usually do not support change（（通常反对变革的）当权派，权势集团；（统称）权威人士）；the act of starting or creating sth that is meant to last for a long time（建立；创立；确立）

estate.meaning: a large area of land, usually in the country, that is owned by one person or family（（通常指农村的）大片私有土地，庄园）；(BrE) an area of land with a lot of houses or factories of the same type on it（住宅区；工业区；工厂区）；all the money and property that a person owns, especially everything that is left when they die（个人财产；（尤指）遗产）

esteem.meaning: (formal) great respect and admiration; a good opinion of sb（尊重；敬重；好评）；to respect and admire sb/sth very much（尊重；敬重）；(old-fashioned, formal) to think of sb/sth in a particular way（把 … 看作；认为）

estimate.meaning: a judgement that you make without having the exact details or figures about the size, amount, cost, etc. of sth（（对大小、数量、成本等的）估计；估价）；a statement of how much a piece of work will probably cost（估计的成本；估价）；to form an idea of the cost, size, value etc. of sth, but without calculating it exactly（估计；估价；估算）

estimation.meaning: a judgement or opinion about the value or quality of sb/sth（判断；评价；看法）；a judgement about the levels or quantity of sth（（对水平、数量的）估计）

estuary.meaning: the wide part of a river where it flows into the sea（（江河入海的）河口，河口湾）

etc..meaning: used after a list to show that there are other things that you could have mentioned (the abbreviation for ‘et cetera’)（以及诸如此类；以及其他；等等）

eternity.meaning: (formal) time without end, especially life continuing without end after death（永恒；永生；不朽）；(informal) a period of time that seems to be very long or to never end（（似乎）无穷无尽的一段时间）

fabulous.meaning: (informal) extremely good（极好的；绝妙的）；(formal) very great（很大的；巨大的）；(literary) appearing in fables（寓言中的；神话似的）

flake.meaning: a small, very thin layer or piece of sth, especially one that has broken off from sth larger（小薄片；（尤指）碎片）；(NAmE) (informal) a person who is strange or unusual or who forgets things easily（古怪的人；奇特的人；健忘的人）；to fall off in small thin pieces（（成小薄片）脱落，剥落）；to break sth, especially fish or other food into small thin pieces; to fall into small thin pieces（把（鱼、食物等）切成薄片）

flamboyant.meaning: (of people or their behaviour（人或行为）；different, confident and exciting in a way that attracts attention（炫耀的；卖弄的）；brightly coloured and noticeable（艳丽的；绚丽夺目的）

flame.meaning: a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from sth that is on fire（火焰；火舌）；a bright red or orange colour（鲜红色；橘红色；橙黄色）；(literary) a very strong feeling（强烈的感情；激情）；(informal) an angry or insulting message sent to sb by email or on the Internet（火药味电邮（或互联网信息））

flaming.meaning: full of anger（满腔怒火的；激动的）；burning and covered in flames（燃烧的；冒火焰的）；(BrE) (informal) used to emphasize that you are annoyed（（强调恼怒）可恶的，讨厌的）；bright red or orange in colour（鲜红色的；橙黄色的；橘红色的）

flank.meaning: the side of sth such as a building or mountain（（建筑物、山等的）侧面）；the left or right side of an army during a battle, or a sports team during a game（（军队或运动队的）翼侧，侧面，侧翼）；the side of an animal between the ribs and the hip（（动物的）胁腹）；to have sb/sth on one or both sides（侧面（或两侧）有）

flannel.meaning: a type of soft light cloth, containing cotton or wool, used for making clothes（法兰绒）；a small piece of cloth used for washing yourself（（洗擦身体用的）毛巾）；trousers/pants made of flannel（法兰绒男裤）；(BrE) (informal) words that do not have much meaning and that avoid telling sb what they want to know（兜圈子的话语；应付性言语）

flap.meaning: a flat piece of paper, cloth, metal, etc. that is attached to sth along one side and that hangs down or covers an opening（（附于某物的）片状下垂物，封盖，口盖，袋盖）；a quick often noisy movement of sth up and down or from side to side（（上下或左右）拍打，振（翅），拍击）；(informal) (especially BrE) a state of worry, confusion and excitement（忧虑；困惑；激动）；(NAmE) public disagreement, anger or criticism caused by sth a public figure has said or done（公众不同意；群众愤怒；大众批评）

flare.meaning: to burn brightly, but usually for only a short time or not steadily（（短暂）烧旺；（摇曳着）燃烧；（火光）闪耀）；(especially of anger and violence（尤指愤怒和暴力）；to suddenly start or become much stronger（突发；加剧）；to say sth in an angry and aggressive way（发怒地说；粗暴地说）

flash.meaning: to shine very brightly for a short time; to make sth shine in this way（（使）闪耀，闪光）；to use a light to give sb a signal（用光发出信号）；to show sth to sb quickly（（快速地）出示，显示）；to move or pass very quickly（飞速运动；掠过）

flashbulb.meaning: a small electric bulb that can be attached to a camera to take photographs indoors or when it is dark（（照相机的）闪光灯泡）

flashy.meaning: (of things（物品）；attracting attention by being bright, expensive, large, etc.（俗艳的；（因昂贵、巨大等）显眼的）；(of people（人）；attracting attention by wearing expensive clothes, etc.（穿着奢华的）

flask.meaning: a bottle with a narrow top, used in scientific work for mixing or storing chemicals（烧瓶）；a small flat bottle made of metal or glass and often covered with leather, used for carrying alcohol（小扁酒瓶（用金属或玻璃制成，常带皮套，随身携带））

flat.meaning: having a level surface, not curved or sloping（水平的；平坦的）；(of land（土地）；without any slopes or hills（平坦的）；(of surfaces（表面）

flatfish.meaning: any sea fish with a flat body, for example a plaice（比目鱼（扁平海鱼，如鲽））

flatten.meaning: to become or make sth become flat or flatter（（使）变平；把 … 弄平）；to destroy or knock down a building, tree, etc.（摧毁，推倒，弄倒（建筑物、树木等））；(informal) to defeat sb easily in a competition, an argument, etc.（轻易击败对手）；(informal) to hit sb very hard so that they fall down（击倒；打倒）

flatter.meaning: to say nice things about sb, often in a way that is not sincere, because you want them to do sth for you or you want to please them（奉承；讨好；向 … 谄媚）；to choose to believe sth good about yourself and your abilities, especially when other people do not share this opinion（自命不凡）；to make sb seem more attractive or better than they really are（使显得更漂亮（或更好））；flat·ter·er flatterer flatterers /ˈflætərə(r); NAmEˈflætərər/ noun IDM be/feel ˈflattered to be pleased because sb has made you feel important or special（被奉承得高兴；感到荣幸）

flaunt.meaning: to show sth you are proud of to other people, in order to impress them（炫耀；夸示；夸耀；卖弄）；to behave in a confident and sexual way to attract attention（（性感地）招摇过市）；(humorous, saying) used to tell sb that they should not be afraid of allowing other people to see their qualities and abilities（有什么能耐施出来瞧瞧）

flavour.meaning: how food or drink tastes（（食物或饮料的）味道）；a particular type of taste（（某种）味道）；a particular quality or atmosphere（特点；特色；气氛）；an idea of what sth is like（像 … 的想法）

flaw.meaning: a mistake in sth that means that it is not correct or does not work correctly（错误；缺点）；a crack or fault in sth that makes it less attractive or valuable（裂痕；裂隙；瑕疵）；a weakness in sb's character（（性格上的）弱点，缺点）

flawless.meaning: without flaws and therefore perfect（完美的；无瑕的）

flax.meaning: a plant with blue flowers, grown for its stem that is used to make thread and its seeds that are used to make linseed oil（亚麻）；threads from the stem of the flax plant, used to make linen（亚麻纤维）

flee.meaning: to leave a person or place very quickly, especially because you are afraid of possible danger（迅速离开；（尤指害怕有危险而）逃避，逃跑）

fleece.meaning: the wool coat of a sheep; this coat when it has been removed from a sheep (by shearing)（羊毛；（一只羊一次剪下的）毛）；a type of soft warm cloth that feels like sheep's wool; a jacket or sweatshirt that is made from this cloth（羊毛状织物；绒头织物短上衣；绒头织物运动衫）；(informal) to take a lot of money from sb by charging them too much（敲诈；敲竹杠）

fleet.meaning: a group of military ships commanded by the same person（舰队）；a group of ships fishing together（捕鱼船队）；all the military ships of a particular country（（一国的）全部军舰，海军）；a group of planes, buses, taxis, etc. travelling together or owned by the same organization（（同一机构或统一调度的）机群，车队）

fleeting.meaning: lasting only a short time（短暂的；闪现的）

flesh.meaning: the soft substance between the skin and bones of animal or human bodies（（动物或人的）肉）；the skin of the human body（（人体的）皮肤）；the soft part of fruit and vegetables, especially when it is eaten（蔬菜的可食部分；果肉）；(literary) the human body when considering its physical and sexual needs, rather than the mind or soul（肉体；肉欲；情欲）

fleshy.meaning: (of parts of the body or people（人体部位或人）；having a lot of flesh（多肉的；肥胖的）；(of plants or fruit（植物或水果）；thick and soft（肉质的）

flexible.meaning: (approving) able to change to suit new conditions or situations（能适应新情况的；灵活的；可变动的）；able to bend easily without breaking（柔韧的；可弯曲的；有弹性的）；flexi·bil·ity AW /ˌfleksəˈbɪləti; NAmEˌfleksəˈbɪləti/ noun [U] Computers offer a much greater degree of flexibility in the way work is organized.（利用计算机，工作安排可以灵活得多。）

flick.meaning: to hit sth with a sudden quick movement, especially using your finger and thumb together, or your hand（（尤指用手指或手快速地）轻击，轻拍，轻拂，轻弹）；to move or make sth move with sudden quick movements（（使）突然快速移动）；to smile or look at sb suddenly and quickly（向 … 笑了一下（或瞥了一眼等））；to press a button or switch quickly in order to turn a machine, etc. on or off（（快速地）按开关，按键）

flicker.meaning: (of a light or a flame（灯光或火焰）；to keep going on and off as it shines or burns（闪烁；闪现；忽隐忽现；摇曳）；(of an emotion, a thought, etc.（情绪、思想等）；to be expressed or appear somewhere for a short time（闪现；一闪而过）

flight.meaning: a journey made by air, especially in a plane（（尤指乘飞机的）空中航行，航程）；a plane making a particular journey（航班飞机；班机）；the act of flying（飞行；飞翔）；the movement or direction of an object as it travels through the air（（物体的）飞行，飞行方向）

flimsy.meaning: badly made and not strong enough for the purpose for which it is used（劣质的；不结实的）；(of material（材料）；thin and easily torn（薄而易损坏的）；difficult to believe（不足信的）

fling.meaning: to throw sb/sth somewhere with force, especially because you are angry（（尤指生气地）扔，掷，抛，丢）；to move yourself or part of your body suddenly and with a lot of force（猛动（身体或身体部位））；to say sth to sb in an aggressive way（粗暴地（向某人）说；气势汹汹地（对某人）说）；(informal, disapproving) to make it too obvious to sb that you want to have a sexual relationship with them（（太露骨地）向某人求爱；向（异性）献殷勤）

flint.meaning: a type of very hard grey stone that can produce a spark when it is hit against steel（燧石；火石）；a piece of flint or hard metal that is used to produce a spark（打火石）

flip.meaning: to turn over into a different position with a sudden quick movement; to make sth do this（（使）快速翻转，迅速翻动）；to press a button or switch in order to turn a machine, etc. on or off（按（开关）；按（按钮）；开（或关）（机器等））；to throw sth somewhere using your thumb and/or fingers（（用手指）轻抛，轻掷）；(informal) to become very angry, excited or unable to think clearly（十分气愤；异常激动；神志不清）

flipper.meaning: a flat part of the body of some sea animals such as seals and turtles, used for swimming（（海豹、海龟等的）鳍肢，鳍足）；a long flat piece of rubber or plastic that you wear on your foot to help you swim more quickly, especially below the surface of the water（（潜水、游泳用的）脚蹼，蛙鞋，鸭脚板，橡皮脚掌）

flirt.meaning: to behave towards sb as if you find them sexually attractive, without seriously wanting to have a relationship with them（调情）；to think about or be interested in sth for a short time but not very seriously（玩儿似地想做某事）；to take risks or not worry about a dangerous situation that may happen（冒险；不顾危险后果）；a person who flirts with a lot of people（与多人调情的人）

float.meaning: to move slowly on water or in the air（浮动；漂流；飘动；飘移）；to stay on or near the surface of a liquid and not sink（浮；漂浮）；to make sth move on or near the surface of a liquid（使浮动；使漂流）；(literary) to walk or move in a smooth and easy way（轻盈走动；飘然移动）

flock.meaning: a group of sheep, goats or birds of the same type（（羊或鸟）群）；a large group of people, especially of the same type（（尤指同类人的）一大群）；(literary) the group of people who regularly attend the church of a particular priest, etc.（（常跟随某圣职人员等学习的）信众）；small pieces of soft material used for filling cushions, chairs, etc.（（填充垫子、椅子等的）小块软填料）

flood.meaning: a large amount of water covering an area that is usually dry（洪水；水灾）；a very large number of things or people that appear at the same time（大批，大量（的人或事物））；if a place floods or sth floods it, it becomes filled or covered with water（（使）灌满水；淹没）；to become so full that it spreads out onto the land around it（泛滥；淹没）

floodplain.meaning: an area of flat land beside a river that regularly becomes flooded when there is too much water in the river（洪泛区；泛滥平原）

floor.meaning: the surface of a room that you walk on（地板；地面）；the bottom surface of a vehicle（（车厢内的）底板）；all the rooms that are on the same level of a building（楼层）；the ground at the bottom of the sea, a forest, etc.（（海等的）底；（森林等的）地面）

flop.meaning: to sit or lie down in a heavy and sudden way because you are very tired（（因疲惫而）猛然坐下，沉重地躺下）；to fall, move or hang in a heavy or awkward way, without control（（沉重、笨拙或不自主地）落下，移动，悬挂）；(informal) to be a complete failure（砸锅；完全失败）；(informal) a film/movie, play, party, etc. that is not successful（（电影、戏剧、聚会等）失败，不成功）

flora.meaning: the plants of a particular area, type of environment or period of time（（某地区、环境或时期的）植物群）

floral.meaning: consisting of pictures of flowers; decorated with pictures of flowers（绘有花的；饰以花的）；made of flowers（花的）

florist.meaning: a person who owns or works in a shop/store that sells flowers and plants（花商）；a shop/store that sells flowers and plants（花店）

flotation.meaning: (business 商) the process of selling shares in a company to the public for the first time in order to raise money（（公司的）发行股份）；the act of floating on or in water（浮；漂浮）

flour.meaning: a fine white or brown powder made from grain, especially wheat, and used in cooking for making bread, cakes, etc.（（尤指小麦的）面粉；（谷物磨成的）粉）；to cover sth with a layer of flour（在 … 上撒（或覆以）面粉）

flourish.meaning: to develop quickly and be successful or common（繁荣；昌盛；兴旺）；to grow well; to be healthy and happy（茁壮成长；健康幸福）；to wave sth around in a way that makes people look at it（（为引起注意）挥舞）；an exaggerated movement that you make when you want sb to notice you（（为引起注意的）夸张动作）

flout.meaning: to show that you have no respect for a law, etc. by openly not obeying it（公然藐视，无视（法律等））

flow.meaning: the steady and continuous movement of sth/sb in one direction（流；流动）；the continuous production or supply of sth（持续生产；不断供应）；continuous talk by sb（滔滔不绝）；the way that words and ideas are linked together in speech or writing（连贯；流畅）

flower.meaning: the coloured part of a plant from which the seed or fruit develops. Flowers usually grow at the end of a stem and last only a short time.（花；花朵）；a plant grown for the beauty of its flowers（开花植物）；a flower with its stem that has been picked as a decoration（（已摘）带梗的花）；(literary) the finest or best part of sth（（某事物的）最佳部分，精华；精英）

flowerpot.meaning: a container made of plastic or clay for growing plants in（花盆）

flu.meaning: an infectious disease like a very bad cold, that causes fever, pains and weakness（流行性感冒；流感）

fluctuate.meaning: to change frequently in size, amount, quality, etc., especially from one extreme to another（（大小、数量、质量等）波动；（在 … 之间）起伏不定）；fluc·tu·ation AW fluctuation fluctuations /ˌflʌktʃuˈeɪʃn; NAmEˌflʌktʃuˈeɪʃn/ noun [C, U] fluctuation~ (in/of sth) wild fluctuations in interest rates（利率的疯狂波动）

flue.meaning: a pipe or tube that takes smoke, gas or hot air away from a fire, a heater or an oven（烟道）

fluency.meaning: the quality of being able to speak or write a language, especially a foreign language, easily and well（（尤指外语）流利，流畅）；the quality of doing sth in a smooth and skilful way（熟练自如；流畅）

fluent.meaning: able to speak, read or write a language, especially a foreign language, easily and well（（尤指外语）流利，文字流畅）；(of a language, especially a foreign language（语言，尤指外语）；expressed easily and well（流利的；通畅的）；(of an action（动作）

fluff.meaning: small pieces of wool, cotton, etc. that gather on clothes and other surfaces（（衣服等上的）绒毛，蓬松毛团，尘团）；soft animal fur or bird feathers, that is found especially on young animals or birds（（禽兽，尤指幼者的）绒毛）；(informal) (especially NAmE) entertainment that is not serious and is not considered to have great value（没多大意义的娱乐）；(informal) to do sth badly or to fail at sth（搞糟；弄砸）

fluffy.meaning: like fluff; covered in fluff（绒毛般的；覆有绒毛的）；(of food（食物）；soft, light and containing air（松软的）；looking as if it is soft and light（轻软状的）

fluid.meaning: (formal or technical 术语) a liquid; a substance that can flow（液体；流体；液）；(of movements, designs, music, etc.（动作、设计、音乐等）；smooth and elegant（流畅优美的）；(of a situation（形势）

fluidity.meaning: (formal) the quality of being smooth and elegant（流畅优美）；(formal) the quality of being likely to change（易变（性）；不稳定（性））；(technical 术语) the quality of being able to flow freely, as gases and liquids do（流动（性））

fluke.meaning: a lucky or unusual thing that happens by accident, not because of planning or skill（侥幸；偶然；意外）

fluorescent.meaning: (of substances（物质）；producing bright light by using some forms of radiation（发荧光的）；(of a colour, material, etc.（颜色、材料等）；appearing very bright when light shines on it; that can be seen in the dark（强烈反光的；发亮的）

flush.meaning: (of a person or their face（人或脸）；to become red, especially because you are embarrassed, angry or hot（发红；脸红）；when a toilet flushes or you flush it, water passes through it to clean it, after a handle, etc. has been pressed（冲洗（抽水马桶））；to clean sth by causing water to pass through it（（用水）冲洗净，冲洗）

flute.meaning: a musical instrument of the woodwind group, shaped like a thin pipe. The player holds it sideways and blows across a hole at one end.（长笛）；a tall narrow glass used for drinking champagne（细长香槟杯（形似长笛））

flutter.meaning: to move lightly and quickly; to make sth move in this way（（使）飘动，挥动，颤动）；when a bird or an insect flutters its wings, or its wings flutter, the wings move lightly and quickly up and down（（鸟或昆虫）拍（翅），振（翅），鼓（翼））；(of a bird or an insect（鸟或昆虫）；to fly somewhere moving the wings quickly and lightly（飞来飞去；翩翩飞舞）

flux.meaning: continuous movement and change（不断的变动；不停的变化）；(technical 术语) a flow; an act of flowing（通量；流动）

fly.meaning: to move through the air, using wings（飞；飞翔）；(of an aircraft or a spacecraft（航空器或航天器）；to move through air or space（（在空中或宇宙）飞行，航行）；to travel in an aircraft or a spacecraft（（乘飞行器或航天器）航行，飞行）

flying.meaning: able to fly（能飞的）；very well; with a very high mark/grade（很好；成绩优异）；travelling in an aircraft（乘飞机）；operating the controls of an aircraft（飞行；飞行器驾驶）

flyover.meaning: a bridge that carries one road over another one（跨线桥；立交桥；（台）立体交叉道）

foam.meaning: a soft light rubber material, full of small holes, that is used for seats, mattresses, etc.（泡沫橡胶；海绵橡胶）；a mass of very small air bubbles on the surface of a liquid（泡沫）；a chemical substance that forms or produces a soft mass of very small bubbles, used for washing, shaving, or putting out fires, for example（泡沫剂（用于洗涤、剃须、灭火等））；(of a liquid（液体）

fob.meaning: the abbreviation for ‘fresh off the boat’ (a person who has recently come to a country as an immigrant and does not speak or behave like people who have lived there a long time)（新移民（全写为 fresh off the boat，指其不谙当地语言以及尚未融入当地社会））

focus.meaning: to give attention, effort, etc. to one particular subject, situation or person rather than another（集中（注意力、精力等）于）；(of your eyes, a camera, etc.（眼睛、摄影机等）；to adapt or be adjusted so that things can be seen clearly; to adjust sth so that you can see things clearly（（使）调节焦距）；(technical 术语) to aim light onto a particular point using a lens（集中光束（于）；聚焦（于））

fodder.meaning: food for horses and farm animals（（马等家畜的）饲料，秣）；(disapproving) (often after a noun（常置于名词后）；people or things that are considered to have only one use（（人或东西）只能是 … 的料）

fog.meaning: a thick cloud of very small drops of water in the air close to the land or sea, that is very difficult to see through（雾）；a state of confusion, in which things are not clear（迷惘；困惑）；if a glass surface fogs or is fogged up, it becomes covered in steam or small drops of water so that you cannot see through（（使）雾气笼罩）；to make sb/sth confused or less clear（使迷惘；使困惑）

foggy.meaning: not clear because of fog（有雾的；雾茫茫的）；(informal) to not know anything at all about sth（完全不知道；一无所知；茫无头绪）

foghorn.meaning: an instrument that makes a loud noise to warn ships of danger in fog（雾角，雾喇叭（向雾中的船只发警告））

foible.meaning: a silly habit or a strange or weak aspect of a person's character, that is considered harmless by other people（（性格上无伤大雅的）怪癖，弱点，小缺点）

foil.meaning: metal made into very thin sheets that is used for covering or wrapping things, especially food（（尤指包装食物等用的）箔）；paper that is covered in very thin sheets of metal（箔纸（覆有箔的纸））；a person or thing that contrasts with, and therefore emphasizes, the qualities of another person or thing（陪衬者；陪衬物）；a long thin light sword used in the sport of fencing（（击剑运动用的）花剑，（台）钝剑）

fool.meaning: a person who you think behaves or speaks in a way that lacks intelligence or good judgement（蠢人；傻瓜）；(in the past) a man employed by a king or queen to entertain people by telling jokes, singing songs, etc.（（旧时国王或王后豢养供人娱乐的）小丑，弄臣）；(BrE) (usually in compounds（通常构成复合词）；a cold light dessert (= a sweet dish) made from fruit that is cooked and crushed and mixed with cream or custard（奶油果泥，蛋奶果泥（甜食））

fruitful.meaning: producing many useful results（成果丰硕的；富有成效的）；(of land or trees（土地或树木）；producing a lot of crops（富饶的；丰产的）

fruitless.meaning: producing no useful results（没有成果的；无成效的；徒然的）

frustrate.meaning: to make sb feel annoyed or impatient because they cannot do or achieve what they want（使懊丧；使懊恼；使沮丧）；to prevent sb from doing sth; to prevent sth from happening or succeeding（阻止；防止；挫败）

frustrating.meaning: causing you to feel annoyed and impatient because you cannot do or achieve what you want（令人懊恼的；令人沮丧的）；frus·trat·ing·ly /frʌˈstreɪtɪŋli; NAmEˈfrʌstreɪtɪŋli/ adv. Progress was frustratingly slow.（进展慢得使人沮丧。）

frustration.meaning: the feeling of being frustrated（懊丧；懊恼；沮丧）；something that causes you to feel frustrated（令人懊丧（或懊恼、沮丧）的事物）；(formal) the fact that sth is preventing sth/sb from succeeding（受阻；受挫；阻止；挫败）

fry.meaning: to cook sth in hot fat or oil; to be cooked in hot fat or oil（油炸；油煎；油炒）；(informal) to be burnt by the sun（（被阳光）灼伤，晒伤）；very small young fish（鱼苗；鱼秧子）

fuck.meaning: to have sex with sb（与 … 性交；肏）；a swear word that many people find offensive that is used to express anger, disgust or surprise（（表示气愤、厌恶、惊奇的粗话）他妈的，见他妈的鬼，滚他妈的蛋）；used to express surprise（（表示惊奇）我他妈的见鬼了）；to waste time by behaving in a silly way（闲混；瞎混）

fuel.meaning: any material that produces heat or power, usually when it is burnt（燃料）；a thing that is said or done that makes sth, especially an argument, continue or get worse（（尤指使争论等继续或更加激烈的）刺激性言行）；to supply sth with material that can be burnt to produce heat or power（给 … 提供燃料）；to put petrol/gas into a vehicle（给（交通工具）加油）

fulfil.meaning: to do or achieve what was hoped for or expected（实现）；(formal) to do or have what is required or necessary（履行；执行；符合；具备）；to have a particular role or purpose（起 … 作用；目的是）；to make sb feel happy and satisfied with what they are doing or have done（使高兴；使满意）

full.meaning: containing or holding as much or as many as possible; having no empty space（满的；充满的；满是 … 的）；having or containing a large number or amount of sth（（有）大量的；（有）许多的；丰富的）；(of a person（人）；thinking or talking a lot about a particular thing（（关于某事物）想得很多，谈得很多）

fullness.meaning: (of the body or part of the body（身体或身体部分）；the quality of being large and round（丰满）；(of colours, sounds and flavours（颜色、声音和味道）；the quality of being deep and rich（（颜色）深浓；（声音）圆浑，圆润；（味道）浓郁）

fully.meaning: completely（完全地；全部地；充分地）；(formal) (used to emphasize an amount（强调数量）；the whole of; as much as（整整；足足）

fumble.meaning: to use your hands in an awkward way when you are doing sth or looking for sth（笨手笨脚地做（某事）；笨拙地摸找（某物））；to have difficulty speaking clearly or finding the right words to say（笨嘴拙舌地说话；支支吾吾地说）；(especially in sport（尤用于体育运动）；to drop a ball or to fail to stop or kick it（失球；接球失误；漏接）

fume.meaning: to be very angry about sth（（对 … ）大为生气，十分恼火）；to produce smoke or fumes（冒烟；冒气）

fumigate.meaning: to use special chemicals, smoke or gas to destroy the harmful insects or bacteria in a place（烟熏，熏蒸（以灭虫或消毒））

fun.meaning: enjoyment; pleasure; a thing that gives enjoyment or pleasure and makes you feel happy（享乐；乐趣；快乐；享乐的事）；behaviour or activities that are not serious but come from a sense of enjoyment（嬉戏；逗乐；玩笑）；(informal) activities that are not serious and that other people may disapprove of（嬉戏；欢闹；寻欢作乐）；to laugh at sb/sth or make other people laugh at them, usually in an unkind way（嘲弄；取笑；拿 … 开玩笑）

function.meaning: a special activity or purpose of a person or thing（作用；功能；职能；机能）；a social event or official ceremony（社交聚会；典礼；宴会）；(mathematics 数) a quantity whose value depends on the varying values of others. In the statement 2x=y, y is a function of x.（函数）；(computing 计) a part of a program, etc. that performs a basic operation（子程序；例程）

functional.meaning: practical and useful; with little or no decoration（实用的）；having a special purpose; making it possible for sb to do sth or for sth to happen（作用的；功能的；机能的；职能的）；(especially of a machine, an organization or a system（尤指机器、组织、机构或体系）；working; able to work（（能）起作用的，工作的，运转的）

functionalism.meaning: the idea or belief that the most important thing about the style or design of a building or object is how it is going to be used, not how it will look（功能主义，实用建筑主义（主张建筑或物品设计首要的是用途而不是外观））

fund.meaning: an amount of money that has been saved or has been made available for a particular purpose（基金；专款）；money that is available to be spent（资金；现款）；an amount or a supply of sth（（相当）数量；储备）；to provide money for sth, usually sth official（提供资金；拨款）

fundamental.meaning: serious and very important; affecting the most central and important parts of sth（十分重大的；根本的）；central; forming the necessary basis of sth（基础的；基本的）；(physics 物) forming the source or base from which everything else is made; not able to be divided any further（基本的；不能再分的）；a basic rule or principle; an essential part（基本规律；根本法则；基本原理；基础）

fundamentally.meaning: in every way that is important; completely（根本上；完全地）；used when you are introducing a topic and stating sth important about it（（引入话题时说）从根本上说，基本上）；used when you are saying what is the most important thing about sb/sth（（表示最重要的方面）根本上，基本上）

funding.meaning: money for a particular purpose; the act of providing money for such a purpose（基金；资金；提供基金；提供资金）

funeral.meaning: a ceremony, usually a religious one, for burying or cremating (= burning) a dead person（葬礼；丧礼；出殡）；(informal) used to tell sb that they, and nobody else, will have to deal with the unpleasant results of their own actions（这是你自作自受）

fungal.meaning: of or caused by fungus（真菌的；真菌引起的）

fungicide.meaning: a substance that kills fungus（杀真菌剂）

fungus.meaning: any plant without leaves, flowers or green colouring, usually growing on other plants or on decaying matter. Mushrooms and mildew are both fungi.（真菌（如蘑菇和霉））；a covering of mould or a similar fungus, for example on a plant or wall（霉；霉菌）

funnel.meaning: a device that is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom, used for pouring liquids or powders into a small opening（漏斗）；a metal chimney, for example on a ship or an engine, through which smoke comes out（（蒸汽机车或轮船上的）烟囱）；to move or make sth move through a narrow space, or as if through a funnel（（使）流经狭窄空间，经过漏斗形口子）

funny.meaning: making you laugh; amusing（滑稽的；好笑的）；Note that funny does not mean ‘enjoyable’.（注意 funny 不表示 enjoyable 的意思）；difficult to explain or understand（奇怪的；难以解释的；难理解的）；(informal) suspicious and probably illegal or dishonest（可疑的；非法的；不诚实的）

fur.meaning: the soft thick mass of hair that grows on the body of some animals（（动物浓厚的）软毛）；the skin of an animal with the fur still on it, used especially for making clothes（（动物的）毛皮）；an artificial material that looks and feels like fur（人造毛皮）；a piece of clothing, especially a coat or jacket, made of real or artificial fur（毛皮衣服，裘皮衣服（尤指大衣或短上衣））

furious.meaning: very angry（狂怒的；暴怒的）；with great energy, speed or anger（激烈的；猛烈的；高速的；盛怒的）；furi·ous·ly /ˈfjʊəriəsli; NAmEˈfjʊriəsli/ adv. furiously angry（大发雷霆）

furnace.meaning: a space surrounded on all sides by walls and a roof for heating metal or glass to very high temperatures（熔炉）

furnish.meaning: to put furniture in a house, room, etc.（布置家具）；(formal) to supply or provide sb/sth with sth; to supply sth to sb（向（某人或某事物）供应，提供）

furniture.meaning: objects that can be moved, such as tables, chairs and beds, that are put into a house or an office to make it suitable for living or working in（（可移动的）家具）

furrow.meaning: a long narrow cut in the ground, especially one made by a plough for planting seeds in（犁沟；沟；车辙）；a deep line in the skin of the face（（脸上的）皱纹）；to make a furrow in the earth（犁）；(formal) if your brows or eyebrows furrow or are furrowed, you pull them together, usually because you are worried, and so produce lines on your face（（使）皱（眉），蹙（额））

further.meaning: (comparative of far（*）；at or to a greater distance（（空间距离）较远，更远）；a longer way in the past or the future（（过去或未来）较远，更久远）；to a greater degree or extent（进一步；在更大程度上；在更大范围内）

furthermore.meaning: in addition to what has just been stated. Furthermore is used especially to add a point to an argument.（此外；而且；再者）

fury.meaning: extreme anger that often includes violent behaviour（狂怒；暴怒；狂暴；大发雷霆）；a state of being extremely angry about sth（狂怒；暴怒）；(in ancient Greek stories) three goddesses who punish people for their crimes（（古希腊神话）复仇三女神）；(informal) with great effort, power, speed, etc.（拼命；猛烈；迅猛）

fuse.meaning: a small wire or device inside a piece of electrical equipment that breaks and stops the current if the flow of electricity is too strong（保险丝；熔丝）；a long piece of string or paper which is lit to make a bomb or a firework explode（导火线；导火索）；a device that makes a bomb explode when it hits sth or at a particular time（引信；信管；雷管）；(formal or technical 术语) when one thing fuses with another, or two things fuse or are fused, they are joined together to form a single thing（（使）融合，熔接，结合）

fusion.meaning: the process or result of joining two or more things together to form one（融合；熔接；结合）；(physics 物) the act or process of combining the nuclei (= central parts) of atoms to form a heavier nucleus, with energy being released（核聚变；热核反应）；music that is a mixture of different styles, especially jazz and rock（合成音乐，混合音乐（尤指爵士乐和摇滚乐））；cooking that is a mixture of different styles（（各种方式的）混合烹调）

fuss.meaning: unnecessary excitement, worry or activity（无谓的激动（或忧虑、活动）；大惊小怪）；anger or complaints about sth, especially sth that is not important（（为小事）大吵大闹，大发牢骚）；to pay a lot of attention to sb, usually to show how much you like them（关爱备至；过分爱护）；to do things, or pay too much attention to things, that are not important or necessary（瞎忙一气；过分关心（枝节小事））

fussy.meaning: too concerned or worried about details or standards, especially unimportant ones（无谓忧虑（或担心）的；大惊小怪的；挑剔的）；doing sth with small, quick, nervous movements（紧张不安的）；having too much detail or decoration（过分琐碎的；装饰太多的）

futile.meaning: having no purpose because there is no chance of success（徒然的；徒劳的；无效的）；fu·tile·ly /ˈfjuːtaɪli; NAmEˈfjuːtli/ adv. fu·til·ity /fjuːˈtɪləti; NAmEfjuːˈtɪləti/ noun [U] a sense of futility（徒劳感）

future.meaning: the time that will come after the present or the events that will happen then（将来；未来）；what will happen to sb/sth at a later time（未来的事；将来发生的事；前景）；the possibility of being successful or surviving at a later time（前途；前程）；(finance 财) goods or shares that are bought at agreed prices but that will be delivered and paid for at a later time（期货）

gadget.meaning: a small tool or device that does sth useful（小器具；小装置）

gadgetry.meaning: a collection of modern tools and devices（（统称）小器具，小装置）

gaily.meaning: in a bright and attractive way（花哨地；艳丽地；华丽地）；in a cheerful way（快乐地；欢乐地；喜气洋洋地）；without thinking or caring about the effect of your actions on other people（欠思索地；毫无顾忌地；轻率地）

gain.meaning: to obtain or win sth, especially sth that you need or want（获得；赢得；博得；取得）；to obtain an advantage or benefit from sth or from doing sth（（从 … 中）受益，获益；得到（好处））；to gradually get more of sth（增加；增添；增进；增长）；to go too fast（走得太快；快）

galaxy.meaning: any of the large systems of stars, etc. in outer space（星系）；the system of stars that contains our sun and its planets, seen as a bright band in the night sky（银河；银河系）；(informal) a group of famous people, or people with a particular skill（群英；人才荟萃）

gale.meaning: an extremely strong wind（大风；飓风）；the sound of people laughing very loudly（一阵大笑声）

gallery.meaning: a room or building for showing works of art, especially to the public（（艺术作品的）陈列室，展览馆；画廊）；a small private shop/store where you can see and buy works of art（私家画店）；an upstairs area at the back or sides of a large hall where people can sit（（大厅的）楼座，楼上旁听席）；the highest level in a theatre where the cheapest seats are（（剧场中票价最低的）顶层楼座）

gallium.meaning: a chemical element. Gallium is a soft silver-white metal.（镓）

gallon.meaning: a unit for measuring liquid. In the UK, Canada and other countries it is equal to about 4.5 litres; in the US it is equal to about 3.8 litres. There are four quarts in a gallon.（加仑（液量单位，在英国、加拿大及其他一些国家约等于 4.5 升，在美国约等于 3.8 升，一加仑为四夸脱））

gallop.meaning: when a horse or similar animal gallops, it moves very fast and each stride includes a stage when all four feet are off the ground together（（马等）飞奔，奔驰，疾驰）；to ride a horse very fast, usually at a gallop（骑马奔驰；使（马）飞奔）；(of a person（人）；to run very quickly（飞跑；奔跑）

galvanize.meaning: to make sb take action by shocking them or by making them excited（使震惊；使振奋；激励；刺激）；(technical 术语) to cover metal with zinc in order to protect it from rust（电镀；给（金属）镀锌）

gamble.meaning: to risk money on a card game, horse race, etc.（（牌戏、赛马等中）赌博，打赌）；to risk losing sth in the hope of being successful（冒风险；碰运气；以 … 为赌注）；gam·bler gambler gamblers /ˈɡæmblə(r); NAmEˈɡæmblər/ noun He was a compulsive gambler (= found it difficult to stop).（他嗜赌成癖。）；to lose sth such as money, possessions, etc. by gambling（赌掉；赌光）

gambling.meaning: the activity of playing games of chance for money and of betting on horses, etc.（赌博；打赌；赌钱）

game.meaning: an activity or a sport with rules in which people or teams compete against each other（（有规则的）游戏，运动，比赛项目）；an occasion of playing a game（（一项）游戏，运动，比赛）；the way in which sb plays a game（比赛时用的手法；比赛技巧）；a large organized sports event（运动会）

gamma.meaning: the third letter of the Greek alphabet (Γ, γ)（希腊字母表的第 3 个字母）

gang.meaning: an organized group of criminals（一帮，一伙（罪犯））；a group of young people who spend a lot of time together and often cause trouble or fight against other groups（一帮，一群，一伙（闹事、斗殴的年轻人））；(informal) a group of friends who meet regularly（一伙（经常聚在一起的朋友））；an organized group of workers or prisoners doing work together（一队，一组（一起干活的工人或囚犯））

gangster.meaning: a member of a group of violent criminals（匪徒；歹徒；土匪）

gannet.meaning: a large bird that lives near the sea which catches fish by diving（塘鹅（潜水捕鱼的大海鸟））；(BrE) (informal) a person who eats a lot（大胃王；吃得多的人）

gap.meaning: a space between two things or in the middle of sth, especially because there is a part missing（开口；豁口；缺口；裂口）；a period of time when sth stops, or between two events（间断；间隔；间隙）；a difference that separates people, or their opinions, situation, etc.（分歧；隔阂；差距）；a space where sth is missing（缺口；空白；漏洞）

gape.meaning: to stare at sb/sth with your mouth open because you are shocked or surprised（张口结舌地看；目瞪口呆地凝视）；to be or become wide open（张开；裂开；豁开）

garage.meaning: a building for keeping one or more cars or other vehicles in（停车房；车库）；a place where vehicles are repaired and where you can buy a car or buy petrol/gas and oil（（兼营汽车销售、修理及加油的）汽车修理厂）；a type of house music（车库音乐，加拉奇音乐（货仓音乐的一种））；to put or keep a vehicle in a garage（把 … 送入车库（或修车厂））

garb.meaning: clothes, especially unusual clothes or those worn by a particular type of person（（尤指某类人穿的特定）服装，衣服；制服）

garbage.meaning: (especially NAmE) waste food, paper, etc. that you throw away（（生活）垃圾；废物）；(especially NAmE) a place or container where waste food, paper, etc. can be placed（垃圾场；垃圾箱；垃圾桶）；(informal) something stupid or not true（废话；无聊的东西）；used to express the idea that if wrong or poor quality data is put into a computer, wrong or poor quality data will come out of it（（用于计算机）废料输入废料输出，无用输入无用输出）

garden.meaning: a piece of land next to or around your house where you can grow flowers, fruit, vegetables, etc., usually with a lawn (= an area of grass)（（住宅旁或周围的）庭园，花园，果园，菜园）；(NAmE) an area in a yard where you grow flowers or plants（庭园；园子）；a public park（公园）；(BrE) used in the name of streets（（用于街名）园，街，广场）

garland.meaning: a circle of flowers and leaves that is worn on the head or around the neck or is hung in a room as decoration（花环；花冠；环状花饰）；(literary) to decorate sb/sth with a garland or garlands（用花环装饰；给 … 饰以花环（或戴上花冠））

garlic.meaning: a vegetable of the onion family with a very strong taste and smell, used in cooking to give flavour to food（蒜；大蒜）；gar·licky /; NAmE/ adj. garlicky breath/food（带大蒜味的气息；加有大蒜的食物）

garment.meaning: a piece of clothing（（一件）衣服）

garrison.meaning: a group of soldiers living in a town or fort to defend it; the buildings these soldiers live in（卫戍部队；守备部队；卫戍区；驻防地）；to put soldiers in a place in order to defend it from attack（驻防；派（兵）驻守）

gas.meaning: any substance like air that is neither a solid nor a liquid, for example hydrogen and oxygen are both gases（气体）；a particular type of gas or mixture of gases used as fuel for heating and cooking（气体燃料；煤气；天然气）；a particular type of gas used during a medical operation, to make the patient sleep or to make the pain less（（外科手术用）麻醉气）；a particular type of gas used in war to kill or injure people, or used by the police to control people（（战争用）毒气；（警察用）瓦斯）

gaseous.meaning: like or containing gas（似气体的；含气体的）

gasp.meaning: to take a quick deep breath with your mouth open, especially because you are surprised or in pain（（尤指由于惊讶或疼痛而）喘气，喘息，倒抽气）；to have difficulty breathing or speaking（透不过气；气喘吁吁地说）；(BrE) (informal) to want or need sth very badly, especially a drink or a cigarette（渴望，很想要（尤指饮料或香烟））；a quick deep breath, usually caused by a strong emotion（（常指由强烈情感引起的）深吸气，喘息，倒抽气）

gate.meaning: a barrier like a door that is used to close an opening in a fence or a wall outside a building（大门；栅栏门；围墙门）；an opening that can be closed by a gate or gates（大门口）；a barrier that is used to control the flow of water on a river or canal（闸门；阀门）；a way out of an airport through which passengers go to get on their plane（登机门；登机口）

gateway.meaning: an opening in a wall or fence that can be closed by a gate（大门口；门道；出入口）；a place through which you can go to reach another larger place（（通往其他地区的）门户）；a means of getting or achieving sth（途径；方法；手段）；(computing 计) a device that connects two computer networks that cannot be connected in any other way（网关；网间连接器）

gather.meaning: to come together, or bring people together, in one place to form a group（聚集；集合；召集）；to bring things together that have been spread around（收拢，归拢（分散的东西））；to collect information from different sources（搜集，收集（情报））；to collect plants, fruit, etc. from a wide area（采集（植物、水果等））

gatherer.meaning: a person who collects sth（收集者；采集者）

gathering.meaning: a meeting of people for a particular purpose（聚集；聚会；集会）；the process of collecting sth（收集；采集；搜集）

gaudy.meaning: too brightly coloured in a way that lacks taste（俗艳的；花哨的）；gaud·ily /ˈɡɔːdɪli; NAmEˈɡɔːdɪli/ adv. gaudily dressed/painted（穿着/涂饰得太俗艳）

gauge.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；an instrument for measuring the amount or level of sth（测量仪器（或仪表）；计量器）；a measurement of the width or thickness of sth（宽度；厚度）；a measurement of the width of the barrel of a gun（（枪管的）口径，码）

generation.meaning: all the people who were born at about the same time（（统称）一代人，同代人，同辈人）；the average time in which children grow up, become adults and have children of their own, (usually considered to be about 30 years)（代，一代，一辈（通常认为大约 30 年））；a single stage in the history of a family（（家史中的）一代，一辈）；a group of people of similar age involved in a particular activity（一批，一届（从事特定活动的同龄人））

genuine.meaning: real; exactly what it appears to be; not artificial（真的；名副其实的）；sincere and honest; that can be trusted（真诚的；诚实的；可信赖的）；genu·ine·ly ★ /ˈdʒenjuɪnli; NAmEˈdʒenjuɪnli/ adv. genuinely sorry（真遗憾）

glad.meaning: pleased; happy（高兴；愉快）；grateful for sth（感激；感谢）；very willing to do sth（乐意；情愿；愿意）；(old-fashioned) bringing joy; full of joy（令人愉快的；使人高兴的；充满欢乐的）
