glimpse.meaning: a look at sb/sth for a very short time, when you do not see the person or thing completely（一瞥；一看）；a short experience of sth that helps you to understand it（短暂的感受（或体验、领会））；to see sb/sth for a moment, but not very clearly（瞥见；看一眼）；to start to understand sth（开始领悟；开始认识到）

glisten.meaning: (of sth wet（湿物）；to shine（闪光；闪亮）

glitter.meaning: to shine brightly with little flashes of light, like a diamond（闪亮；闪耀；光彩夺目）；(of the eyes（眼睛）；to shine brightly with a particular emotion, usually a strong one（闪现（某种强烈情感））；bright light consisting of many little flashes（灿烂的光辉；闪烁；闪耀）

global.meaning: covering or affecting the whole world（全球的；全世界的）；considering or including all parts of sth（整体的；全面的；总括的）；glob·al·ly AW /ˈɡləʊbəli; NAmEˈɡloʊbəli/ adv. We need to start thinking globally.（我们需着手全面考虑。）

globalization.meaning: the fact that different cultures and economic systems around the world are becoming connected and similar to each other because of the influence of large multinational companies and of improved communication（全球化，全世界化（世界各地的文化和经济体系日益关联））

globalize.meaning: (economics 经) if sth, for example a business company, globalizes or is globalized, it operates all around the world（（使）全球化，全世界化）

globe.meaning: an object shaped like a ball with a map of the world on its surface, usually on a stand so that it can be turned（地球仪）；the world (used especially to emphasize its size)（地球，世界（尤用以强调其大））；a thing shaped like a ball（球体；球状物）

gloom.meaning: a feeling of being sad and without hope（忧郁；愁闷；无望）；(literary) almost total darkness（幽暗；黑暗；昏暗）

gloomy.meaning: nearly dark, or badly lit in a way that makes you feel sad（黑暗的；阴暗的；幽暗的）；sad and without hope（忧郁的；沮丧的；无望的）；without much hope of success or happiness in the future（前景黯淡的；悲观的）；gloom·ily /ˈɡluːmɪli; NAmEˈɡluːmɪli/ adv. He stared gloomily at the phone.（他满脸愁容地盯着电话。）

glorify.meaning: (often disapproving) to make sth seem better or more important than it really is（吹捧；吹嘘；美化）；(formal) to praise and worship God（颂扬，赞美，崇拜（上帝））；glori·fi·ca·tion /ˌɡlɔːrɪfɪˈkeɪʃn; NAmEˌɡlɔːrɪfɪˈkeɪʃn/ noun [U] the glorification of war（对战争的颂扬）

glorious.meaning: (formal) deserving or bringing great fame and success（值得称道的；光荣的；荣耀的）；(formal) very beautiful and impressive（壮丽的；辉煌的；光辉灿烂的）；extremely enjoyable（极其令人愉快的；极为宜人的）；(of weather（天气）

glory.meaning: fame, praise or honour that is given to sb because they have achieved sth important（荣誉；光荣；桂冠）；praise and worship of God（（对上帝的）赞颂，赞美，崇拜）；great beauty（壮丽；辉煌；灿烂）；a special cause for pride, respect or pleasure（产生骄傲（或崇敬、愉快）的理由）

gloss.meaning: a shine on a smooth surface（（平滑表面上的）光泽，光亮）；(often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a substance designed to make sth shiny（用以产生光泽的物质）；paint which, when dry, has a hard shiny surface（光泽涂料；亮光漆）

glossary.meaning: a list of technical or special words, especially those in a particular text, explaining their meanings（术语汇编；词汇表）

glossy.meaning: smooth and shiny（光滑的；光彩夺目的；有光泽的）；giving an appearance of being important and expensive（浮华的；虚有其表的；虚饰的）；(BrE) (informal) an expensive magazine printed on glossy paper, with a lot of colour photographs, etc.（用亮光纸印刷的杂志）

glove.meaning: a covering for the hand, made of wool, leather, etc. with separate parts for each finger and the thumb（（分手指的）手套）；used to say that sb is ready for a fight or an argument（准备动手打架；做好战斗（或辩论）准备）

glow.meaning: (especially of sth hot or warm（尤指热或微温的物体）；to produce a dull, steady light（发出微弱而稳定的光；发出暗淡的光）；(of a person's body or face（人体或脸）；to look or feel warm or pink, especially after exercise or because of excitement, embarrassment, etc.（（尤指运动后或因情绪激动、尴尬等而）发红，发热，显得红，感觉热）

glue.meaning: a sticky substance that is used for joining things together（胶；胶水）；to join two things together using glue（（用胶水）粘合，粘牢，粘贴）；(informal) to give all your attention to sth; to stay very close to sth（全神贯注看着某物；离某物很近）；not able to move, for example because you are frightened or surprised（动弹不得；吓呆了；惊呆了）

glut.meaning: a situation in which there is more of sth than is needed or can be used（供应过剩；供过于求）；to supply or provide sth with too much of sth（超量供应；充斥）

gnaw.meaning: to keep biting sth or chewing it hard, so that it gradually disappears（咬；啃；啮）；to make sb feel anxious, frightened or uncomfortable over a long period of time（（长时间）折磨某人）

gnp.meaning: the abbreviation for ‘gross national product’ (the total value of all the goods and services produced by a country in one year, including the total income from foreign countries)（国民生产总值，（台）国民生产毛额）

go.meaning: to move or travel from one place to another（去；走）；In spoken English go can be used with and plus another verb to show purpose or to tell sb what to do.（英语口语中，go 可与 and 连用加上另一动词，表示目的或让某人做某事）；The and is sometimes left out, especially in NAmE.（*）；to move or travel, especially with sb else, to a particular place or in order to be present at an event（（尤指与某人）去（某处或出席某项活动））

goad.meaning: to keep irritating or annoying sb/sth until they react（（不断地）招惹，激怒，刺激）；to drive or encourage sb to do sth（驱使（或怂恿、激励）某人）；a pointed stick used for making cows, etc. move forwards（（赶牛等牲畜用的）尖头棒）；something that makes sb do sth, usually by annoying them（刺激；激励）

goal.meaning: (in sports（体育运动）；a frame with a net into which players must kick or hit the ball in order to score a point（球门）；the act of kicking or hitting the ball into the goal; a point that is scored for this（射门；进球得分）；something that you hope to achieve（目标；目的）

goat.meaning: an animal with horns and a coat of hair, that lives wild in mountain areas or is kept on farms for its milk or meat（山羊）；(informal) an unpleasant old man who is annoying in a sexual way（老色鬼；色狼；好色之徒）；(informal) to annoy sb very much（使某人恼怒）

god.meaning: (in Christianity, Islam and Judaism（基督教、伊斯兰教和犹太教）；the being or spirit that is worshipped and is believed to have created the universe（上帝；天主；真主）；(in some religions) a being or spirit who is believed to have power over a particular part of nature or who is believed to represent a particular quality（（某些宗教中主宰某个领域的）神）；a person who is loved or admired very much by other people（极受崇拜的人；被崇拜的偶像）

goddess.meaning: a female god（女神）；a woman who is loved or admired very much by other people（极受崇拜（或敬慕）的女人）

gold.meaning: a chemical element. Gold is a yellow precious metal used for making coins, jewellery, decorative objects, etc.（金）；money, jewellery, etc. that is made of gold（金币；金饰品；黄金制品）；the colour of gold（金色；金黄色）；(saying) not everything that seems good, attractive, etc. is actually good, etc.（闪闪发光的未必都是金子；中看未必中用）

golden.meaning: (especially literary) made of gold（金质的；金的）；bright yellow in colour like gold（金色的；金黄色的）；special; wonderful（特别的；美好的）；(NAmE) (informal) in a situation where you are successful or do not have any problems（大功告成；大获成功；一帆风顺）

goldfish.meaning: a small orange or red fish. Goldfish are kept as pets in bowls or ponds.（金鱼）

goldsmith.meaning: a person who makes, repairs or sells articles made of gold（金匠；金器商）

golf.meaning: a game played over a large area of ground using specially shaped sticks to hit a small hard ball (a golf ball) into a series of 9 or 18 holes, using as few strokes as possible（高尔夫球运动）

good.meaning: of high quality or an acceptable standard（好的；优质的；符合标准的；可接受的）；pleasant; that you enjoy or want（令人愉快的；令人满意的）；sensible, logical or strongly supporting what is being discussed（合情理的；有说服力的；有充分根据的）；showing or getting approval or respect（赞同的；赢得赞许的；令人尊敬的）

goodbye.meaning: used when you are leaving sb or when sb else is leaving（再见；再会）

good-looking.meaning: (especially of people（尤指人）；physically attractive（漂亮的；好看的）

goodness.meaning: the quality of being good（善良；优良；美德）；the part of sth that has a useful effect on sb/sth, especially sb's health（（尤指有益健康的）精华，营养，养分）；(informal) used to express surprise（（表示惊讶）天哪，啊呀）；from feelings of kindness, without thinking about what advantage there will be for you（出于好心（不从中捞取好处））

goods.meaning: things that are produced to be sold（商品；货品）；possessions that can be moved（动产；私人财产）；(BrE) things (not people) that are transported by rail or road（（铁路或公路）运载的货物）；(BrE) (informal) to be very good or impressive（非常好；给人以深刻印象）

goodwill.meaning: friendly or helpful feelings towards other people or countries（友善；友好；善意；亲善）；the good relationship between a business and its customers that is calculated as part of its value when it is sold（信誉；商誉）

goose.meaning: a bird like a large duck with a long neck. Geese either live wild or are kept on farms.（鹅）；meat from a goose（鹅肉）；a female goose（雌鹅）；(old-fashioned, informal) a silly person（傻瓜；笨蛋）

gorge.meaning: a deep narrow valley with steep sides（峡；峡谷）；(formal) somebody feels so angry about sth that they feel physically sick（感到烦心（或厌恶）；作呕）；(sometimes disapproving) to eat a lot of sth, until you are too full to eat any more（贪婪地吃；狼吞虎咽）

gorgeous.meaning: (informal) very beautiful and attractive; giving pleasure and enjoyment（非常漂亮的；美丽动人的；令人愉快的）；(of colours, clothes, etc.（颜色、衣服等）；with very deep colours; impressive（绚丽的；灿烂的；华丽的）

gorilla.meaning: a very large powerful African ape (= an animal like a large monkey without a tail) covered with black or brown hair（大猩猩（产于非洲））；(informal) a large aggressive man（高大凶恶的人）

gosling.meaning: a young goose (= a bird like a large duck)（小鹅；幼鹅）

gospel.meaning: one of the four books in the Bible about the life and teaching of Jesus（福音（《圣经》中关于耶稣生平和教诲的四福音书之一））；the life and teaching of Jesus as explained in the Bible（福音（耶稣的事迹和教诲））；a set of ideas that sb believes in and tries to persuade others to accept（（个人的）信念，信仰）；(informal) the complete truth（绝对真理）

gossamer.meaning: the very fine thread made by spiders（蛛丝）；(literary) any very light delicate material（薄纱；精细织物）

gossip.meaning: (disapproving) informal talk or stories about other people's private lives, that may be unkind or not true（流言蜚语；闲言碎语）；a conversation about other people and their private lives（张家长，李家短；闲聊）；(disapproving) a person who enjoys talking about other people's private lives（喜欢传播流言蜚语的人；爱说长道短（或说三道四）的人）；gos·sipy /ˈɡɒsɪpi; NAmEˈɡɑːsɪpi/ adj. a gossipy letter/neighbour（闲聊式的信；爱说三道四的邻居）

gothic.meaning: connected with the Goths (= a Germanic people who fought against the Roman Empire)（哥特人的，哥特族的，哥特语的（指反对罗马帝国的一支日耳曼民族））；(architecture 建) built in the style that was popular in western Europe from the 12th to the 16th centuries, and which has pointed arches and windows and tall thin pillars（哥特式的，哥特风格的（12 至 16 世纪流行于西欧的建筑风格，以尖拱、尖窗和细长柱为特色））；(of a novel, etc.（小说等）；written in the style popular in the 18th and 19th centuries, which described romantic adventures in mysterious or frightening surroundings（哥特派的，哥特风格的（流行于 18 至 19 世纪，描述神秘或恐怖气氛中的爱情故事））

gouache.meaning: a method of painting using colours that are mixed with water and made thick with a type of glue; the paints used in this method（广告色画法；广告色画颜料）；a picture painted using this method（广告色画）

gourd.meaning: a type of large fruit with hard skin and soft flesh. Gourds are often dried and used as containers.（葫芦科植物，葫芦（晾干后常作容器））

gourmet.meaning: a person who knows a lot about good food and wines and who enjoys choosing, eating and drinking them（美食家；讲究饮食的人；美酒美食品尝家）；gour·met adj. [only before noun] gourmet food (= of high quality and often expensive)（美味佳肴）

govern.meaning: to legally control a country or its people and be responsible for introducing new laws, organizing public services, etc.（统治；控制；管理；治理）；to control or influence sb/sth or how sth happens, functions, etc.（控制；影响；支配）；(grammar 语法) if a word governs another word or phrase, it affects how that word or phrase is formed or used（支配（词或短语的形式或用法））

governance.meaning: the activity of governing a country or controlling a company or an organization; the way in which a country is governed or a company or institution is controlled（统治；管理；治理；统治方式；管理方法）

governess.meaning: (especially in the past), a woman employed to teach the children of a rich family in their home and to live with them（（尤指旧时的）家庭女教师）

government.meaning: the group of people who are responsible for controlling a country or a state（政府；内阁）；a particular system or method of controlling a country（政体；国家体制）；the activity or the manner of controlling a country（（一国的）统治，治理，统治方式，管理方法）

governmental.meaning: connected with government; of a government（统治的；政体的；政府的）

governor.meaning: a person who is the official head of a country or region that is governed by another country（统治者；管辖者；总督）；a person who is chosen to be in charge of the government of a state in the US（（美国的）州长）；(especially BrE) a member of a group of people who are responsible for controlling an institution such as a school, a college or a hospital（（学校、学院、医院等机构的）董事，理事）；(BrE) a person who is in charge of an institution（主管；机构负责人；总裁）

gown.meaning: a woman's dress, especially a long one for special occasions（（尤指特别场合穿的）女裙，女长服，女礼服）；a long loose piece of clothing that is worn over other clothes by judges and (in Britain) by other lawyers, and by members of universities (at special ceremonies)（（法官、英国律师、大学学生在特别仪式上穿的）长袍，长外衣）；a piece of clothing that is worn over other clothes to protect them, especially in a hospital（（尤指在医院穿的）罩衣，外罩）

grab.meaning: to take or hold sb/sth with your hand suddenly, firmly or roughly（抓住；攫取）；to try to take hold of sth（（试图）抓住，夺得）；to take advantage of an opportunity to do or have sth（利用，抓住（机会））；to have or take sth quickly, especially because you are in a hurry（（尤指匆忙地）取，拿，吃，喝）

grace.meaning: an attractive quality of movement that is smooth, elegant and controlled（优美；优雅）；a quality of behaviour that is polite and pleasant and deserves respect（文雅；高雅）；(especially BrE) ways of behaving that people think are polite and acceptable（风度；体面）；extra time that is given to sb to enable them to pay a bill, finish a piece of work, etc.（宽限期；延缓期）

graceful.meaning: moving in a controlled, attractive way or having a smooth, attractive form（优美的；优雅的；雅致的）；polite and kind in your behaviour, especially in a difficult situation（（尤指在困境中）得体的，有风度的）；grace·ful·ly /ˈɡreɪsfəli; NAmEˈɡreɪsfəli/ adv. The cathedral's white towers climb gracefully into the sky.（大教堂白色的塔楼优雅庄重地耸入云霄。）

gracious.meaning: (of people or behaviour（人或行为）；kind, polite and generous, especially to sb of a lower social position（（尤指对社会地位较低者）和蔼的，慈祥的，有礼貌的，宽厚的）；showing the comfort and easy way of life that wealth can bring（富贵安逸的）；(BrE) (formal) used as a very polite word for royal people or their actions（（对王族及其行为的敬语）仁慈的，宽厚的）

grade.meaning: the quality of a particular product or material（（产品、材料的）等级，品级）；a level of ability or rank that sb has in an organization（（官衔的）级别；职别）；a mark given in an exam or for a piece of school work（成绩等级；评分等级）；(in the US school system) one of the levels in a school with children of similar age（（美国学制）年级）

gradient.meaning: the degree to which the ground slopes, especially on a road or railway（（尤指公路或铁路的）坡度，斜率，倾斜度）；(technical 术语) the rate at which temperature, pressure, etc. changes, or increases and decreases, between one region and another（（温度、压力等的）变化率，梯度变化曲线）

gradual.meaning: happening slowly over a long period; not sudden（逐渐的；逐步的；渐进的）；(of a slope（斜坡）；not steep（平缓的；不陡的）

gradually.meaning: slowly, over a long period of time（逐渐地；逐步地；渐进地）

graduate.meaning: a person who has a university degree（大学毕业生；学士学位获得者）；(NAmE) a person who has completed their school studies（毕业生）；to get a degree, especially your first degree, from a university or college（获得学位（尤指学士）；大学毕业）；(NAmE) to complete a course in education, especially at high school（毕业（尤指中学））

graduation.meaning: the act of successfully completing a university degree, or studies at an American high school（（大学或美国高中的）毕业）；a ceremony at which degrees, etc. are officially given out（毕业典礼）

grain.meaning: the small hard seeds of food plants such as wheat, rice, etc; a single seed of such a plant（谷物；谷粒）；a small hard piece of particular substances（颗粒；细粒）；(used especially in negative sentences（尤用于否定句）；a very small amount（少量；微量；一点儿）

grainy.meaning: (especially of photographs（尤指照片）；not having completely clear images because they look as if they are made of a lot of small dots and marks（有颗粒的；粒状的；有纹的）；having a rough surface or containing small bits, seeds, etc.（表面粗糙的；粒面的）

gram.meaning: a unit for measuring weight. There are 1 000 grams in one kilogram.（克（重量单位，1 公斤为 1 000 克））；a thing that is written or drawn（写（或画）的东西）

grammar.meaning: the rules in a language for changing the form of words and joining them into sentences（语法；文法）；a person's knowledge and use of a language（（人的）语言知识及运用能力）；a book containing a description of the rules of a language（语法书）

grammatical.meaning: connected with the rules of grammar（语法的；文法的）；correctly following the rules of grammar（符合语法规则的；合乎文法的）；gram·mat·ical·ly /ɡrəˈmætɪkli; NAmEɡrəˈmætɪkli/ adv. a grammatically correct sentence（语法上正确的句子）

granary.meaning: (of bread（面包）；containing whole grains of wheat（谷仓牌的（全麦的））

grand.meaning: impressive and large or important（壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的）；used in the names of impressive or very large buildings, etc.（（用于大建筑物等的名称）大）；needing a lot of effort, money or time to succeed but intended to achieve impressive results（宏大的；宏伟的；有气派的）；(of people（人）

grandchild.meaning: a child of your son or daughter（（外）孙子；（外）孙女）

granddaughter.meaning: a daughter of your son or daughter（（外）孙女）

grandeur.meaning: the quality of being great and impressive in appearance（宏伟；壮丽；堂皇）；the importance or social status sb has or thinks they have（高贵；显赫；伟大）

grandfather.meaning: the father of your father or mother（（外）祖父；爷爷；外公）

grandiose.meaning: seeming very impressive but too large, complicated, expensive, etc. to be practical or possible（华而不实的；浮夸的；不切实际的）

grandmother.meaning: the mother of your father or mother（（外）祖母；奶奶；外婆）

grandparent.meaning: the father or mother of your father or mother（祖父；祖母；外祖父；外祖母）

grandson.meaning: a son of your son or daughter（孙子；外孙）

granite.meaning: a type of hard grey stone, often used in building（花岗岩；花岗石）

grant.meaning: to agree to give sb what they ask for, especially formal or legal permission to do sth（（尤指正式地或法律上）同意，准予，允许）；to admit that sth is true, although you may not like or agree with it（（勉强）承认，同意）；to believe sth is true without first making sure that it is（认为 … 是理所当然）；to be so used to sb/sth that you do not recognize their true value any more and do not show that you are grateful（（因习以为常）对 … 不予重视；（因视为当然而）不把 … 当回事）

granted.meaning: used to show that you accept that sth is true, often before you make another statement about it（（表示肯定属实，然后再作另一番表述）不错，的确）；because of the fact that（因为）

granular.meaning: consisting of small granules; looking or feeling like a collection of granules（由颗粒构成的；含颗粒的；似颗粒状的）

granule.meaning: a small, hard piece of sth; a small grain（颗粒状物；微粒；细粒）

grape.meaning: a small green or purple fruit that grows in bunches on a climbing plant (called a vine ). Wine is made from grapes.（葡萄）

graph.meaning: a planned drawing, consisting of a line or lines, showing how two or more sets of numbers are related to each other（图；图表；曲线图）

grave.meaning: a place in the ground where a dead person is buried（坟墓；墓穴；坟头）；(usually literary) death; a person's death（死亡；去世；逝世）；(of a person who is dead（亡者）；likely to be very shocked or angry（九泉之下不得安宁）

grown.meaning: (of a person（人）；mentally and physically an adult（成熟的；成年的；长大的）

guilt.meaning: the unhappy feelings caused by knowing or thinking that you have done sth wrong（内疚；悔恨）；the fact that sb has done sth illegal（犯罪；罪行；有罪）；blame or responsibility for doing sth wrong or for sth bad that has happened（罪责；责任；罪过）；guilt·less /; NAmE/ adj. IDM a ˈguilt trip (informal) things you say to sb in order to make them feel guilty about sth（使人内疚的责备）

guilty.meaning: feeling ashamed because you have done sth that you know is wrong or have not done sth that you should have done（感到内疚的；感到惭愧的）；having done sth illegal; being responsible for sth bad that has happened（犯了罪；有过失的；有罪责的）；guilt·ily /ˈɡɪltɪli; NAmEˈɡɪltɪli/ adv. IDM a guilty ˈsecret a secret that sb feels ashamed about（见不得人的秘密）

guinea.meaning: an old British gold coin or unit of money worth 21 shillings (= now £1.05). Prices are sometimes still given in guineas, for example when buying or selling horses.（几尼（英国旧时金币或货币单位，价值 21 先令，现值 1.05 英镑。现时有些价格仍用几尼计算，如马匹买卖））

guitar.meaning: a musical instrument that usually has six strings, that you play with your fingers or with a plectrum（吉他）

guitarist.meaning: a person who plays the guitar（吉他弹奏者；吉他手）

gulf.meaning: a large area of sea that is partly surrounded by land（海湾）；the Persian Gulf, the area of sea between the Arabian peninsula and Iran（波斯湾）；a large difference between two people or groups in the way that they think, live or feel（分歧；鸿沟；隔阂）；a wide deep crack in the ground（（地面的）裂口，深坑，沟壑）

gull.meaning: a bird with long wings and usually white and grey or black feathers that lives near the sea. There are several types of gull.（海鸥）

gullible.meaning: too willing to believe or accept what other people tell you and therefore easily tricked（轻信的；易受骗的；易上当的）

gully.meaning: a small, narrow channel, usually formed by a stream or by rain（溪谷；冲沟）；a deep ditch（深沟；沟壑）

gulp.meaning: to swallow large amounts of food or drink quickly（狼吞虎咽；大口吞咽；匆匆吞下）；to swallow, but without eating or drinking anything, especially because of a strong emotion such as fear or surprise（（尤因害怕或惊讶而）倒吸气）；to breathe quickly and deeply, because you need more air（深呼吸；喘大气；大口大口地吸气）；to stop yourself showing your emotions by swallowing hard（咽下 …（以防止感情的流露））

gum.meaning: either of the firm areas of flesh in the mouth to which the teeth are attached（牙龈；齿龈；牙床）；a sticky substance produced by some types of tree（树胶；树脂）；a type of glue used for sticking light things together, such as paper（黏胶，胶质物（用以粘轻东西，如纸等））；a firm transparent fruit-flavoured sweet/candy that you chew（透明果味糖）

gun.meaning: a weapon that is used for firing bullets or shells（枪；炮）；a tool that uses pressure to send out a substance or an object（喷射器；喷枪）；the signal to begin a race, that is made by firing a special gun, called a starting pistol, into the air（起跑信号；发令枪声）；(informal) (especially NAmE) a person who is paid to shoot sb（受雇杀人的枪手）

gunfire.meaning: the repeated firing of guns; the sound of guns firing（（接连不断的）炮火，炮火声）

gunpowder.meaning: explosive powder used especially in bombs or fireworks（火药）

gush.meaning: to flow or pour suddenly and quickly out of a hole in large amounts（（从 … 中）喷出，涌出，冒出）；(of a container/vehicle etc.（容器、车辆等）；to suddenly let out large amounts of a liquid（大量涌出，大量泄出（液体））；(disapproving) to express so much praise or emotion about sb/sth that it does not seem sincere（过分称赞；夸张地表现对 … 的感情；装腔作势）

gust.meaning: a sudden strong increase in the amount and speed of wind that is blowing（一阵强风；一阵狂风）；a sudden strong expression of emotion（（感情的）迸发，爆发，发作）；(of the wind（风）；to suddenly blow very hard（猛刮；劲吹）

gut.meaning: the tube in the body through which food passes when it leaves the stomach（消化道；肠道）；the organs in and around the stomach, especially in an animal（（尤指动物的）内脏）；(informal) a person's stomach, especially when it is large（（尤指大的）胃，肚子）；(informal) the courage and determination that it takes to do sth difficult or unpleasant（勇气；胆量；决心；毅力）

gutter.meaning: a long curved channel made of metal or plastic that is fixed under the edge of a roof to carry away the water when it rains（檐沟；天沟）；a channel at the edge of a road where water collects and is carried away to drains（路旁排水沟；阴沟）；the bad social conditions or low moral standards sometimes connected with the lowest level of society（恶劣的社会环境；（社会最低阶层的）道德沦落）；(of a flame or candle（火焰或蜡烛）

guy.meaning: (informal) a man（男人；小伙子；家伙）；(informal) (especially NAmE) a group of people of either sex（一群男人（或女人）；伙计们；兄弟（或姐妹）们）；(in Britain) a model of a man dressed in old clothes that is burned on a bonfire on 5 November during the celebrations for Bonfire Night（盖伊模拟像（英国每年 11 月 5 日庆祝篝火之夜焚烧的身着古装的人体模型））；a rope used to keep a pole or tent in a vertical position（（立竿子或架帐篷用的）支索，牵索，拉索）

gym.meaning: a room or hall with equipment for doing physical exercise, for example in a school（健身房；体育馆）；physical exercises done in a gym, especially at school（（尤指学校的）体育活动，健身）

gymnast.meaning: a person who performs gymnastics, especially in a competition（体操运动员）

gymnastics.meaning: physical exercises that develop and show the body's strength and ability to move and bend easily, often done as a sport in competitions（体操；体操训练）

gypsum.meaning: a soft white mineral like chalk that is found naturally and is used in making plaster of Paris（石膏）

gypsy.meaning: a member of a race of people, originally from Asia, who traditionally travel around and live in caravans. Many people prefer to use the name Roma or Romani.（吉卜赛人（许多人更喜欢用 Roma 或 Romani））

habit.meaning: a thing that you do often and almost without thinking, especially sth that is hard to stop doing（习惯）；usual behaviour（惯常行为；习性）；(informal) a strong need to keep using drugs, alcohol or cigarettes regularly（（吸毒、喝酒、抽烟的）瘾）；a long piece of clothing worn by a monk or nun（（修道士或修女穿的）长袍；道袍；道服）

habitable.meaning: suitable for people to live in（适合居住的）

habitat.meaning: the place where a particular type of animal or plant is normally found（（动植物的）生活环境，栖息地）

habitual.meaning: usual or typical of sb/sth（惯常的；典型的）；(of an action（行为）；done, often in a way that is annoying or difficult to stop（讨厌的；上瘾的）；(of a person（人）

hacienda.meaning: a large farm in a Spanish-speaking country（（讲西班牙语国家的）大庄园，大农场）

hack.meaning: to cut sb/sth with rough, heavy blows（砍；劈）；to kick sth roughly or without control（猛踢）；to secretly find a way of looking at and/or changing information on sb else's computer system without permission（非法侵入（他人的计算机系统））；(informal) to be able/not able to manage in a particular situation（能/不能应付（某情形））

hacker.meaning: a person who secretly finds a way of looking at and/or changing information on sb else's computer system without permission（黑客，骇客（秘密窥视或改变他人计算机系统信息））

haggard.meaning: looking very tired because of illness, worry or lack of sleep（（由于生病、焦虑或睡眠不足）憔悴的，疲惫的）

haggle.meaning: to argue with sb in order to reach an agreement, especially about the price of sth（争论；（尤指）讲价）

hail.meaning: to describe sb/sth as being very good or special, especially in newspapers, etc.（赞扬（或称颂）… 为（尤用于报章等））；to signal to a taxi or a bus, in order to get the driver to stop（招手（请出租车或公共汽车停下））；(literary) to call to sb in order to say hello to them or attract their attention（跟 … 打招呼；向 … 喊）；when it hails, small balls of ice fall like rain from the sky（下雹）

hair.meaning: the substance that looks like a mass of fine threads growing especially on the head; one of these threads growing on the body of people and some animals（毛发；（尤指）头发）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；having the type of hair mentioned（有 … 毛发（或头发）的）；a thing that looks like a fine thread growing on the leaves and stems of some plants（（植物叶茎上的）茸毛）

haircut.meaning: the act of sb cutting your hair（理发）；the style in which sb's hair is cut（发型；发式）

hairdo.meaning: the style in which a woman's hair is arranged（（女子）发式，发型）

hairdresser.meaning: a person whose job is to cut, wash and shape hair（理发师；美发师；发型师）；a place where you can get your hair cut, washed and shaped（理发店；美发店）

hairpin.meaning: a small thin piece of wire that is folded in the middle, used by women for holding their hair in place（发夹）

hairy.meaning: covered with a lot of hair（多毛的）；(informal) dangerous or frightening but often exciting（惊险的；可怕（但刺激）的）

hale.meaning: (especially of an old person（尤指老年人）；strong and healthy（健壮的；硬朗的）

half.meaning: either of two equal parts into which sth is or can be divided（一半；半）；either of two periods of time into which a sports game, concert, etc. is divided（（比赛、音乐会等的）半场，半局）；(BrE) (informal) half a pint of beer or a similar drink（（啤酒等饮料的）半品脱）；(informal) bigger, better, more important, etc. than usual（更大（或好、重要等）的；非同寻常的；出色的）

halfway.meaning: at an equal distance between two points; in the middle of a period of time（在 … 的中间；在中途；到一半）；part of the way towards doing or achieving sth（部分地做（或达到）…）；(informal) fairly, but not very, good（还不错的；过得去的）；half·way adj. the halfway point/stage（中间点/阶段）

halibut.meaning: a large flat sea fish that is used for food（圣日比目鱼，大比目鱼（可食用））

hall.meaning: a space or passage inside the entrance or front door of a building（门厅；正门过道）；a passage in a building with rooms down either side（（大楼内的）走廊）；a building or large room for public meetings, meals, concerts, etc.（礼堂；大厅）；(BrE) (often as part of a name（常作名称的一部分）

hallmark.meaning: a feature or quality that is typical of sb/sth（特征；特点）；a mark put on gold, silver and platinum objects that shows the quality of the metal and gives information about when and where the object was made（金银纯度印记（打在金、银、铂制品上，表示纯度、生产日期及产地））；to put a hallmark on metal goods（给 … 打金银纯度印记）

halt.meaning: to stop; to make sb/sth stop（（使）停止，停下）；an act of stopping the movement or progress of sb/sth（停止；阻止；暂停）；(BrE) a small train station in the country that has a platform but no buildings（乡间小火车站（只有站台））

halve.meaning: to reduce by a half; to make sth reduce by a half（（使）减半）；to divide sth into two equal parts（把 … 对半分）

ham.meaning: the top part of a pig's leg that has been cured (= preserved using salt or smoke) and is eaten as food; the meat from this（火腿；火腿肉）；a person who sends and receives radio messages as a hobby rather than as a job（无线电通讯爱好者）；(informal) (often used as an adjective（常用作形容词）；an actor who performs badly, especially by exaggerating emotions（拙劣演员（尤指表演过火者））

hamburger.meaning: finely chopped beef made into a flat round shape that is then fried, often served in a bread roll（汉堡包；汉堡牛肉饼）；beef that has been finely chopped in a special machine（绞碎的牛肉；牛肉末）

hammer.meaning: a tool with a handle and a heavy metal head, used for breaking things or hitting nails（锤子；榔头:）；a tool with a handle and a wooden head, used by a person in charge of an auction (= a sale at which things are sold to the person who offers the most money) in order to get people's attention when sth is just being sold（（拍卖用的）木槌）；a small wooden part inside a piano, that hits the strings to produce a sound（音槌）；a part inside a gun that makes the gun fire（击铁）

hammerhead.meaning: a shark with flat parts sticking out from either side of its head with eyes at the ends（锤头鲨；双髻鲨）

hamper.meaning: to prevent sb from easily doing or achieving sth（妨碍；阻止；阻碍）；a large basket with a lid, especially one used to carry food in（（尤指用于盛食物的）带盖大篮子）；(especially BrE) a box or package containing food, sent as a gift（（作为礼品的）盒装食物，袋装食物）；(NAmE) a large basket that you keep your dirty clothes in until they are washed（盛脏衣服的大篮子）

hand.meaning: the part of the body at the end of the arm, including the fingers and thumb（手）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；using the hand or number of hands mentioned（用 … 手的；用 … 只手的）；(informal) help in doing sth（帮助；协助）

handbag.meaning: a small bag for money, keys, etc., carried especially by women（小手提包；（尤指）坤包）

handbook.meaning: a book giving instructions on how to use sth or information about a particular subject（手册；指南）

handcuff.meaning: to put handcuffs on sb or to fasten sb to sth/sb with handcuffs（用手铐铐住（某人）；把（某人）铐在（某物、某人）上）

handful.meaning: the amount of sth that can be held in one hand（一把（的量）；用手抓起的数量）；a small number of people or things（少数人（或物））；(informal) a person or an animal that is difficult to control（难以控制的人（或动物））

handicap.meaning: (becoming old-fashioned, sometimes offensive) a permanent physical or mental condition that makes it difficult or impossible to use a particular part of your body or mind（生理缺陷；弱智；残疾）；something that makes it difficult for sb to do sth（障碍；阻碍）；(sport 体) a race or competition in which the most skilful must run further, carry extra weight, etc. in order to give all those taking part an equal chance of winning; the disadvantage that is given to sb you are competing against in such a race or competition（让步赛（使参赛者中的优势方跑得较远、增加负重等）；（让步赛中给优势方施加的）障碍，不利条件）；(in golf（高尔夫球）

handicapped.meaning: suffering from a mental or physical handicap（有生理缺陷的；残疾的；弱智的）；people who are handicapped（残疾人；弱智者）

handicraft.meaning: activities such as sewing and making cloth that use skill with your hands and artistic ability to make things（手工艺）；things made in this way（手工艺品）

handkerchief.meaning: a small piece of material or paper that you use for blowing your nose, etc.（手帕；纸巾）

handle.meaning: to deal with a situation, a person, an area of work or a strong emotion（处理，应付（局势、人、工作或感情））；to touch, hold or move sth with your hands（（用手）触，拿，搬动）；to control a vehicle, an animal, a tool, etc.（控制，操纵（车辆、动物、工具等））；to be easy/difficult to drive or control（（容易/难以）驾驶，操纵）

handling.meaning: the way that sb deals with or treats a situation, a person, an animal, etc.（（对形势、人、动物等的）处理，对付，对待）；the action of organizing or controlling sth（组织；控制；管理）；the action of touching, feeling or holding sth with your hands（（手的）触摸，触摸感觉，握，拿）；the cost of dealing with an order, delivering goods, booking tickets, etc.（（订货、送货、订票等的）费用，手续费）

handmade.meaning: made by a person using their hands rather than by machines（手工制作的）

handout.meaning: (sometimes disapproving) food, money or clothes that are given to a person who is poor（捐赠品；救济品）；(often disapproving) money that is given to a person or an organization by the government, etc., for example to encourage commercial activity（政府拨款（为促进商业活动））；a free document that gives information about an event or a matter of public interest, or that states the views of a political party, etc.（传单）；a document that is given to students in class or people attending a talk, etc. and that contains a summary of the lesson/talk, a set of exercises, etc.（（发给学生或参与讨论者等的）讲义，文字材料）

handsome.meaning: (of men（男子）；attractive（英俊的；漂亮的；有魅力的）；(of women（女子）；attractive, with large strong features rather than small delicate ones（健美的）

handwriting.meaning: writing that is done with a pen or pencil, not printed or typed（手写；书写）；a person's particular style of writing in this way（笔迹）

handy.meaning: easy to use or to do（易使用的；容易做的；便利的）；located near to sb/sth; located or stored in a convenient place（近便的；便利的）；skilful in using your hands or tools to make or repair things（手巧；有手艺）；handi·ness /ˈhændinəs; NAmEˈhændinəs/ noun [U] IDM ˌcome in ˈhandy (informal) to be useful（有用处）

hang.meaning: to attach sth, or to be attached, at the top so that the lower part is free or loose（悬挂；吊）；when sth hangs in a particular way, it falls in that way（垂下；垂落）；to bend or let sth bend downwards（（使）低垂，下垂）；to kill sb, usually as a punishment, by tying a rope around their neck and allowing them to drop; to be killed in this way（（被）绞死，施以绞刑）

hanger.meaning: a curved piece of wood, plastic or wire, with a hook at the top, that you use to hang clothes up on（衣架）

hanker.meaning: to have a strong desire for sth（渴望，渴求（某事物））

haphazard.meaning: with no particular order or plan; not organized well（无秩序的；无计划的；组织混乱的）

happen.meaning: to take place, especially without being planned（（尤指偶然）发生，出现）；to take place as the result of sth（（作为结果）出现，发生）；to do or be sth by chance（碰巧；恰好）；used to tell sb sth, especially when you are disagreeing with them or annoyed by what they have said（（向对方表示异议或不悦等））

happening.meaning: an event; something that happens, often sth unusual（事件；发生的事情（常指不寻常的））；an artistic performance or event that is not planned（即兴艺术表演）；(informal) where there is a lot of exciting activity; fashionable（热闹的；时髦的）

happily.meaning: in a cheerful way; with feelings of pleasure or satisfaction（快乐地；高兴地；满足地）；by good luck（幸运地）；willingly（欣然；情愿地）；(formal) in a way that is suitable or appropriate（合适地；恰当地）

happy.meaning: feeling or showing pleasure; pleased（感到（或显得）快乐的；高兴的）；giving or causing pleasure（给予（或带来）快乐的；使人高兴的；幸福的）；if you wish sb a Happy Birthday, Happy New Year, etc. you mean that you hope they have a pleasant celebration（（表示祝愿，如 Happy Birthday 生日快乐、Happy New Year 新年好等））；satisfied that sth is good or right; not anxious（（对事物）满意的，放心的）

harangue.meaning: to speak loudly and angrily in a way that criticizes sb/sth or tries to persuade people to do sth（呵斥；大声谴责；慷慨激昂地劝说）；a long loud angry speech that criticizes sb/sth or tries to persuade people to do sth（义愤填膺的谴责；慷慨激昂的劝说）

harass.meaning: to annoy or worry sb by putting pressure on them or saying or doing unpleasant things to them（侵扰；骚扰）；to make repeated attacks on an enemy（不断攻击（敌人））；har·ass·ment harassment harassments /; NAmE/ noun [U] racial/sexual harassment（种族侵扰；性骚扰）

harbour.meaning: an area of water on the coast, protected from the open sea by strong walls, where ships can shelter（（海）港；港口；港湾）；to hide and protect sb who is hiding from the police（窝藏，庇护（罪犯等））；to keep feelings or thoughts, especially negative ones, in your mind for a long time（怀有，心怀（尤指反面感情或想法））；to contain sth and allow it to develop（包含；藏有）

hard.meaning: solid, firm or stiff and difficult to bend or break（坚固的；坚硬的；结实的）；difficult to do, understand or answer（难做的；难懂的；难以回答的）；full of difficulty and problems, especially because of a lack of money（困苦的；艰苦的；艰难的）；needing or using a lot of physical strength or mental effort（耗费体力（或脑力）的；辛苦的）

harden.meaning: to become or make sth become firm, stiff or solid（（使）变硬，硬化）；if your voice, face, etc. hardens, or you harden it, it becomes more serious or severe（（使声音、面孔等）更严肃，更严厉）；if sb's feelings or attitudes harden or sb/sth hardens them, they become more fixed and determined（（使）更坚定，更强硬）；to make sb less kind or less affected by extreme situations（使变得无情；使不被打动）

hardly.meaning: almost no; almost not; almost none（几乎不；几乎没有）；used especially after ‘can’ or ‘could’ and before the main verb, to emphasize that it is difficult to do sth（（尤用于 can 或 could 之后，主要动词之前，强调做某事很难））；used to say that sth has just begun, happened, etc.（刚刚；才）；used to suggest that sth is unlikely or unreasonable or that sb is silly for saying or doing sth（（表示不大可能、不合理或愚蠢））

hardship.meaning: a situation that is difficult and unpleasant because you do not have enough money, food, clothes, etc.（艰难；困苦；拮据）

hardware.meaning: (computing 计) the machinery and electronic parts of a computer system（硬件；（台）硬体）；tools and equipment that are used in the house and garden/yard（（家庭及园艺用）工具，设备，五金制品）；the equipment, machinery and vehicles used to do sth（硬件设备；机器；车辆）

hardwood.meaning: hard heavy wood from a broadleaved tree（硬材（硬木阔叶树种的木材））

hard-working.meaning: putting a lot of effort into a job and doing it well（工作努力的；辛勤的）

hardy.meaning: strong and able to survive difficult conditions and bad weather（能吃苦耐劳的；适应力强的）；(of a plant（植物）；that can live outside through the winter（耐寒的；能越冬的）

hare.meaning: an animal like a large rabbit with very strong back legs, that can run very fast（野兔）；(BrE) to run or go somewhere very fast（飞跑；疾走）

harem.meaning: the women or wives belonging to a rich man, especially in some Muslim societies in the past（哈来姆（尤指旧时某些穆斯林社会中富人的女眷））；the separate part of a traditional Muslim house where the women live（（穆斯林传统住宅中的）闺阁，闺房）；(technical 术语) a group of female animals that share the same male for reproducing（繁殖群（和同一雄性动物交配的一群雌性动物））

hen.meaning: a female chicken, often kept for its eggs or meat（母鸡）；(especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）；any female bird（雌禽）

henceforth.meaning: starting from a particular time and at all times in the future（此后；从此以后）

hepatitis.meaning: a serious disease of the liver. There are three main forms: hepatitis A (the least serious, caused by infected food), hepatitis B and hepatitis C (both very serious and caused by infected blood).（肝炎）

her.meaning: used as the object of a verb, after the verb be or after a preposition to refer to a woman or girl who has already been mentioned or is easily identified（（用作动词或介词的宾语，或作表语）她）；(the possessive form of she（*）；of or belonging to a woman or girl who has already been mentioned or is easily identified（她的）

herald.meaning: to be a sign that sth is going to happen（是（某事）的前兆；预示）；to say in public that sb/sth is good or important（宣称（ … 是好的或重要的））；something that shows that sth else is going to happen soon（预兆）；(in the past) a person who carried messages from a ruler（（旧时的）信使，传令官，使者）

herb.meaning: a plant whose leaves, flowers or seeds are used to flavour food, in medicines or for their pleasant smell. Parsley, mint and oregano are all herbs.（药草；香草）；(technical 术语) a plant with a soft stem that dies down after flowering（草本植物）

herbaceous.meaning: connected with plants that have soft stems（草本的）

herbal.meaning: connected with or made from herbs（药草的；香草的）；a book about herbs, especially those used in medicines（草本植物志；（尤指）草药志）

herbalist.meaning: a person who grows, sells or uses herbs for medical purposes（药草栽培者；药草商；草药医生）

herbicide.meaning: a chemical that is poisonous to plants, used to kill plants that are growing where they are not wanted（除莠剂；除草剂）

herbivore.meaning: any animal that eats only plants（食草动物；草食动物）；herb·iv·or·ous /hɜːˈbɪvərəs; NAmEɜːrˈbɪvərəs; hɜːrˈbɪvərəs/ adj. herbivorous dinosaurs（食草恐龙）

herculean.meaning: needing a lot of strength, determination or effort（费力的；需要决心的；艰巨的）

herd.meaning: a group of animals of the same type that live and feed together（兽群；牧群）；(usually disapproving) a large group of people of the same type（人群；芸芸众生）；to move or make sb/sth move in a particular direction（（使）向 … 移动）；to make animals move together as a group（牧放（牲畜、兽群））

here.meaning: used after a verb or preposition to mean ‘in, at or to this position or place’（（用于动词或介词之后）在这里，向这里）；now; at this point（现在；在这一点上）；used when you are giving or showing sth to sb（（给某人东西或指出某物时说））；used to show your role in a situation（（表示某人的作用））

hereafter.meaning: (in legal documents, etc.（用于法律文件等）；in the rest of this document（在本文件其余部分；以下）；(formal) from this time; in future（此后；今后；将来）；(formal) after death（死后）

hereby.meaning: (in legal documents, etc.（用于法律文件等）；as a result of this statement, and in a way that makes sth legal（特此；以此）

hereditary.meaning: (especially of illnesses（尤指疾病）；given to a child by its parents before it is born（遗传的；遗传性的）；that is legally given to sb's child, when that person dies（世袭的）；holding a rank or title that is hereditary（有世袭身分（或头衔）的）

heredity.meaning: the process by which mental and physical characteristics are passed by parents to their children; these characteristics in a particular person（遗传（过程）；遗传特征）

herein.meaning: in this place, document, statement or fact（在此处；于此文件（或声明、事实）中）

hereof.meaning: of this（关于这个；在本文件中）

heretic.meaning: a person who is guilty of heresy（犯异端罪者；离经叛道者）；her·et·ical /həˈretɪkl; NAmEhəˈretɪkl/ adj. heretical beliefs（异端信仰）

hereto.meaning: to this（到此为止；至此；于此）

herewith.meaning: with this letter, book or document（随同此信（或书、文件））

heritage.meaning: the history, traditions and qualities that a country or society has had for many years and that are considered an important part of its character（遗产（指国家或社会长期形成的历史、传统和特色））

hermetic.meaning: (technical 术语) tightly closed so that no air can escape or enter（密封的；不透气的）；(formal, disapproving) closed and difficult to become a part of（封闭的；不受外界影响的）；her·met·ic·al·ly /hɜːˈmetɪkli; NAmEhɜːrˈmetɪkli/ adv. a hermetically sealed container（密封的容器）

hermit.meaning: a person who, usually for religious reasons, lives a very simple life alone and does not meet or talk to other people（隐士；隐修者；遁世者）

hero.meaning: a person, especially a man, who is admired by many people for doing sth brave or good（英雄，豪杰（尤指男性））；the main male character in a story, novel, film/movie, etc.（（故事、小说、电影等的）男主人公，男主角）；a person, especially a man, that you admire because of a particular quality or skill that they have（崇拜的对象，偶像（尤指男性））

heroic.meaning: showing extreme courage and admired by many people（英勇的；英雄的）；showing great determination to succeed or to achieve sth, especially sth difficult（有必胜决心的；不畏艰难的）；that is about or involves a hero（（关于）英雄的）；very large or great（非常大的；巨大的）

heroin.meaning: a powerful illegal drug made from morphine, that some people take for pleasure and can become addicted to（海洛因）

heroine.meaning: a girl or woman who is admired by many for doing sth brave or good（女英雄；女豪杰）；the main female character in a story, novel, film/movie, etc.（（故事、小说、电影等中的）女主人公，女主角）；a woman that you admire because of a particular quality or skill that she has（崇拜的女人；女偶像）

heroism.meaning: very great courage（英勇表现；英雄精神）

herring.meaning: a N Atlantic fish that swims in very large groups and is used for food（鲱（产于北大西洋，成大群游动，可食））

hers.meaning: of or belonging to her（她的；属于她的）

herself.meaning: (the reflexive form of she（*）；used to emphasize the female subject or object of a sentence（（强调句中的女性主语或宾语））；(of a woman or girl（女性）；to be in a normal state of health or happiness; not influenced by other people（身体或心情状况正常；如平时一样；没有受他人影响）

hesitant.meaning: slow to speak or act because you feel uncertain, embarrassed or unwilling（犹豫的；踌躇的；不情愿的）

hesitate.meaning: to be slow to speak or act because you feel uncertain or nervous（（对某事）犹豫，迟疑不决）；to be worried about doing sth, especially because you are not sure that it is right or appropriate（顾虑；疑虑）；hesi·ta·tion hesitation hesitations /ˌhezɪˈteɪʃn; NAmEˌhezɪˈteɪʃn/ noun [U, C] She agreed without the slightest hesitation.（她毫不犹豫地同意了。）；(saying) if you delay in doing sth you may lose a good opportunity（当断不断（，反受其乱）；优柔寡断者坐失良机）

heterogeneous.meaning: consisting of many different kinds of people or things（由很多种类组成的；各种各样的）

hexagon.meaning: a flat shape with six straight sides and six angles（六边形；六角形）

hey.meaning: used to attract sb's attention or to express interest, surprise or anger（（用以引起注意或表示兴趣、惊讶或生气）嘿，喂）；used to show that you do not really care about sth or that you think it is not important（（表示不真正在意或认为不重要）嘿）；(SAfrE) used at the end of a statement, to show that you have finished speaking, or to form a question or invite sb to reply（（用于陈述末尾，表示话已说完，或构成问题或请求回答）就这样，怎么样，你说呢）；(NAmE) (informal) used to say that sth does not matter or that you do not care about it（那有什么要紧；没什么；管它呢）

heyday.meaning: the time when sb/sth had most power or success, or was most popular（最为强大（或成功、繁荣）的时期）

hi.meaning: used to say hello（（用于打招呼）喂，嗨）

hibernate.meaning: (of animals（动物）；to spend the winter in a state like deep sleep（冬眠；蛰伏）

hiccup.meaning: a sharp, usually repeated, sound made in the throat, that is caused by a sudden movement of the diaphragm and that you cannot control（嗝；呃逆）；a series of hiccups（一连串的打嗝）；(informal) a small problem or temporary delay（小问题；暂时性耽搁）；to have hiccups or a single hiccup（打嗝；打呃）

hide.meaning: to put or keep sb/sth in a place where they/it cannot be seen or found（藏；隐蔽）；to go somewhere where you hope you will not be seen or found（躲避；隐匿）；to cover sth so that it cannot be seen（遮住；遮挡）；to keep sth secret, especially your feelings（掩盖，隐瞒（尤指感情））

hideous.meaning: very ugly or unpleasant（十分丑陋的；令人厌恶的）；hid·eous·ly /ˈhɪdiəsli; NAmEˈhɪdiəsli/ adv. His face was hideously deformed.（他的脸严重变形。）

hiding.meaning: the state of being hidden（隐藏；躲藏）；(informal) (especially BrE) a physical punishment, usually involving being hit hard many times（体罚；痛打）；(BrE) (informal) having no chance of success, or not getting much advantage even if you do succeed（毫无成功机会；（即使成功了）也得不到多大好处）

hierarchy.meaning: a system, especially in a society or an organization, in which people are organized into different levels of importance from highest to lowest（等级制度（尤指社会或组织））；the group of people in control of a large organization or institution（统治集团）；(formal) a system that ideas or beliefs can be arranged into（层次体系）

high.meaning: measuring a long distance from the bottom to the top（高的）；used to talk about the distance that sth measures from the bottom to the top（有某高度的）；at a level which is a long way above the ground or above the level of the sea（（离地面）很高的；海拔很高的）；greater or better than normal in quantity or quality, size or degree（（数量、质量、体积或程度）高的，超乎寻常的）

highland.meaning: connected with an area of land that has hills or mountains（高地的；高原的；山区的）；connected with the Highlands of Scotland（苏格兰高地的）；an area of land with hills or mountains（高地；高原）；the high mountain region of Scotland（苏格兰高地）

highlight.meaning: to emphasize sth, especially so that people give it more attention（突出；强调）；to mark part of a text with a special coloured pen, or to mark an area on a computer screen, to emphasize it or make it easier to see（将（文本的某部分）用彩笔做标记；将（计算机屏幕的某区域）增强亮度；使醒目）；to make some parts of your hair a lighter colour than the rest by using a chemical substance on them（挑染（将部分头发染成浅色））；the best, most interesting or most exciting part of sth（最好（或最精彩、最激动人心）的部分）

high-powered.meaning: (of people（人）；having a lot of power and influence; full of energy（有权势的；精力旺盛的）；(of activities（活动）；important; with a lot of responsibility（重要的；责任重大的）

high-pressure.meaning: that involves aggressive ways of persuading sb to do sth or to buy sth（强力劝说的）；that involves a lot of worry and anxiety（令人焦虑的；非常紧张的；压力大的）；using or containing a great force of a gas or a liquid（（气体或液体产生的）高压）

high-resolution.meaning: (of a photograph or an image on a computer or television screen（照片、计算机或电视屏幕的图像）；showing a lot of clear sharp detail（高清晰度的；高分辨率的）

high-speed.meaning: that travels, works or happens very fast（高速的；高效率的；迅速的）

high-tech.meaning: using the most modern methods and machines, especially electronic ones（高技术的，高科技的（尤指电子方面））；(of designs, objects, etc.（图案、物体等）；very modern in appearance; using modern materials（样式新颖的；用高新技术材料的）

highway.meaning: (especially NAmE) a main road for travelling long distances, especially one connecting and going through cities and towns（（尤指城镇间的）公路，干道，交通要道）；(BrE) (formal) a public road（公用通道）

hijacker.meaning: a person who hijacks a plane or other vehicle（劫机者；劫持交通工具者；劫持者）

hike.meaning: a long walk in the country（远足；徒步旅行）；(informal) a large or sudden increase in prices, costs, etc.（（价格、花费等的）大幅度提高，猛增）；(NAmE) (informal) a rude way of telling sb to go away（滚开；走开）；to go for a long walk in the country, especially for pleasure（去 … 远足；做徒步旅行）

hilarious.meaning: extremely funny（极其滑稽的）；hil·ari·ous·ly /hɪˈleəriəsli; NAmEhɪˈleriəsli/ adv. hilariously funny（滑稽可笑）

hill.meaning: an area of land that is higher than the land around it, but not as high as a mountain（山丘；小山）；a slope on a road（（道路的）斜坡）；(old-fashioned) (NAmE informal) something that is not worth much（没有多大价值的东西）；(of a person（人）

hillbilly.meaning: (NAmE) (disapproving) a person who lives in the mountains and is thought to be stupid by people who live in the towns（山区乡巴佬）

hillside.meaning: the side of a hill（小山坡）

hilly.meaning: having a lot of hills（多小山的；多丘陵的）

him.meaning: used as the object of a verb, after the verb be or after a preposition to refer to a male person or animal that has already been mentioned or is easily identified（他，它（用作动词或介词的宾语，或作表语））；used when referring to God（祂（指上帝））

himself.meaning: (the reflexive form of he（*）；used to emphasize the male subject or object of a sentence（（强调句中的男性主语或宾语））；(of a man or boy（男性）；to be in a normal state of health or happiness; not influenced by other people（一切正常；如平时一般；未受他人影响）

hind.meaning: the hind legs or feet of an animal with four legs are those at the back（（四足动物的腿、蹄）后面的）；a female deer, especially a red deer; a doe（雌鹿（尤指雌赤鹿））

hinder.meaning: to make it difficult for sb to do sth or for sth to happen（阻碍；妨碍；阻挡）

hindrance.meaning: a person or thing that makes it more difficult for sb to do sth or for sth to happen（造成妨碍的人（或事物））；(formal) the act of making it more difficult for sb to do sth or for sth to happen（妨碍；阻挠）

hinge.meaning: a piece of metal, plastic, etc. on which a door, lid or gate moves freely as it opens or closes（铰链；合叶）；to attach sth with a hinge（给（某物）装铰链）；hinged /; NAmE/ adj. a hinged door/lid（铰接的门/盖）；(of an action, a result, etc.（行动、结果等）

hint.meaning: something that you say or do in an indirect way in order to show sb what you are thinking（暗示；提示；示意）；something that suggests what will happen in the future（征兆；迹象）；a small amount of sth（少许；少量）；a small piece of practical information or advice（秘诀；窍门）

hinterland.meaning: the areas of a country that are away from the coast, from the banks of a large river or from the main cities（内陆；腹地；内地）

hip.meaning: the area at either side of the body between the top of the leg and the waist; the joint at the top of the leg（臀部；髋）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；having hips of the size or shape mentioned（臀部 … 的）；the red fruit that grows on some types of wild rose bush（野蔷薇果）

hippopotamus.meaning: a large heavy African animal with thick dark skin and short legs, that lives in rivers and lakes（河马）

hire.meaning: (especially BrE) to pay money to borrow sth for a short time（租用；租借）；(especially NAmE) to give sb a job（聘用；录用；雇用）；to employ sb for a short time to do a particular job（临时雇用）；to let sb use sth for a short time, in return for payment（出租某物）

his.meaning: of or belonging to a man or boy who has already been mentioned or is easily identified（他的）；of or belonging to God（上帝的；属于上帝的）；of or belonging to him（他的；属于他的）

hispanic.meaning: of or connected with Spain or Spanish-speaking countries, especially those of Latin America（西班牙的；西班牙语国家（尤指拉丁美洲）的）；a person whose first language is Spanish, especially one from a Latin American country living in the US or Canada（母语为西班牙语的人（尤指住在美国或加拿大的拉丁美洲人））

hiss.meaning: to make a sound like a long ‘s’（发嘶嘶声）；to make a sound like a long ‘s’ to show disapproval of sb/sth, especially an actor or a speaker（发嘘声（表示不满，尤指对演员或演讲人））；to say sth in a quiet angry voice（带怒气地低声说出（某事））；a sound like a long ‘s’; this sound used to show disapproval of sb（嘶嘶声；嘘声）

historian.meaning: a person who studies or writes about history; an expert in history（史学工作者；历史学家）

historic.meaning: important in history; likely to be thought of as important at some time in the future（历史上著名（或重要）的；可名垂青史的）；of a period during which history was recorded（有史时期的）

historical.meaning: connected with the past（（有关）历史的）；connected with the study of history（有关历史研究的；历史学的）；(of a book, film/movie, etc.（书、电影等）；about people and events in the past（历史题材的）

history.meaning: all the events that happened in the past（历史（指过去发生的所有事情））；the past events concerned in the development of a particular place, subject, etc.（（有关某个地方、主题等的）发展史，历史）；the study of past events as a subject at school or university（历史课；历史学）；a written or spoken account of past events（历史（指历史记载或历史传说））

hit.meaning: to bring your hand, or an object you are holding, against sb/sth quickly and with force（（用手或器具）击，打）；to come against sth/sb with force, especially causing damage or injury（碰撞；撞击（造成损伤））；to knock a part of your body against sth（使（身体部位）碰上（某物））；(of a bullet, bomb, etc. or a person using them（子弹、炸弹或射击者、抛掷者）

hitherto.meaning: until now; until the particular time you are talking about（迄今；直到某时）

hive.meaning: a structure made for bees to live in（蜂房；蜂箱）；the bees living in a hive（一箱蜜蜂；蜂群）；a place full of people who are busy（忙碌的场所；繁忙的地方）；(especially BrE) to separate one part of a group from the rest; to sell part of a business（把一部分分拆出来；卖掉公司的一部分）

hoarse.meaning: (of a person or voice（人或嗓音）；sounding rough and unpleasant, especially because of a sore throat（嘶哑的；沙哑的）

hobby.meaning: an activity that you do for pleasure when you are not working（业余爱好）

hoe.meaning: a garden tool with a long handle and a blade, used for breaking up soil and removing weeds (= plants growing where they are not wanted)（锄头）；to break up soil, remove plants, etc. with a hoe（用锄头锄地（或除草））；(AustralE, NZE) (informal) to eat with enthusiasm（痛快地吃）

hoist.meaning: to raise or pull sth up to a higher position, often using ropes or special equipment（吊起；提升；拉高）；to be hurt or to have problems as a result of your own plans to hurt or trick others（害人反害己；自食其果）；a piece of equipment used for lifting heavy things, or for lifting people who cannot stand or walk（起重机；吊车；（残疾人用）升降机）

hold.meaning: to carry sth; to have sb/sth in your hand, arms, etc.（拿着；抓住；抱住；托住；夹着）；to put your hand on part of your body, usually because it hurts（抱住，捂住，按住（受伤的身体部位等））；to keep sb/sth in a particular position（使保持（在某位置））；to support the weight of sb/sth（支撑 … 的重量）

holder.meaning: a person who has or owns the thing mentioned（持有者；拥有者）；a thing that holds the object mentioned（支托（或握持）… 之物）

holding.meaning: a number of shares that sb has in a company（股份）；an amount of property that is owned by a person, museum, library, etc.（私有财产；（博物馆、图书馆等的）馆藏）；a piece of land that is rented by sb and used for farming（租种的土地）

huge.meaning: extremely large in size or amount; great in degree（巨大的；极多的；程度高的）；(informal) very successful（非常成功的；走红的）

hull.meaning: the main, bottom part of a ship, that goes in the water（船身；船体）；to remove the outer covering of peas, beans, etc. or the ring of leaves attached to strawberries（剥去（豌豆、大豆等的）外壳；摘掉（草莓的）花萼）

hum.meaning: to sing a tune with your lips closed（哼（曲子））；to make a low continuous sound（发嗡嗡声）；to be full of activity（活跃；繁忙）；(informal) to take a long time to make a decision or before you say sth（犹豫不决；支支吾吾；嗯嗯呃呃）

human.meaning: of or connected with people rather than animals, machines or gods（人的）；showing the weaknesses that are typical of people, which means that other people should not criticize the person too much（显示人类特有弱点的；人本性的）；having the same feelings and emotions as most ordinary people（有人情味的；通人情的）；a person who is involved in a subject, issue, etc. and makes it easier for ordinary people to understand and have sympathy with it（（某主题、话题等的）标志性人物）

humane.meaning: showing kindness towards people and animals by making sure that they do not suffer more than is necessary（善良的；仁慈的；人道的）；hu·mane·ly /hjuːˈmeɪnli; NAmEhjuːˈmeɪnli/ adv. to treat sb humanely（仁慈地对待某人）

humanism.meaning: a system of thought that considers that solving human problems with the help of reason is more important than religious beliefs. It emphasizes the fact that the basic nature of humans is good.（人文主义）；hu·man·is·tic /ˌhjuːməˈnɪstɪk; NAmEˌhjuːməˈnɪstɪk/ adj. humanistic ideals（人文主义理想）

humanist.meaning: a person who believes in humanism（人文主义者）

humanitarian.meaning: concerned with reducing suffering and improving the conditions that people live in（人道主义的（主张减轻人类苦难、改善人类生活）；慈善的）

humanity.meaning: people in general（（统称）人；人类）；the state of being a person rather than a god, an animal or a machine（人性）；the quality of being kind to people and animals by making sure that they do not suffer more than is necessary; the quality of being humane（人道；仁慈）；the subjects of study that are concerned with the way people think and behave, for example literature, language, history and philosophy（人文学科）

humble.meaning: showing you do not think that you are as important as other people（谦逊的；虚心的）；(ironic or humorous) used to suggest that you are not as important as other people, but in a way that is not sincere or not very serious（（表示谦逊，但不够诚挚或认真））；having a low rank or social position（（级别或地位）低下的，卑微的）；(of a thing（事物）

humdrum.meaning: boring and always the same（乏味的；单调的）

humid.meaning: (of the air or climate（空气或气候）；warm and damp（温暖潮湿的；湿热的）

humidity.meaning: the amount of water in the air（（空气中的）湿度）；conditions in which the air is very warm and damp（湿热；高温潮湿）

humiliate.meaning: to make sb feel ashamed or stupid and lose the respect of other people（羞辱；使丧失尊严）；hu·mili·at·ing /hjuːˈmɪlieɪtɪŋ; NAmEhjuːˈmɪlieɪtɪŋ/ adj. a humiliating defeat（耻辱的失败）；hu·mili·ation humiliation humiliations /hjuːˌmɪliˈeɪʃn; NAmEhjuːˌmɪliˈeɪʃn/ noun [U, C] She suffered the humiliation of being criticized in public.（她当众受到指责，丢了面子。）

humility.meaning: the quality of not thinking that you are better than other people; the quality of being humble（谦逊；谦虚）

hummingbird.meaning: a small brightly coloured bird that lives in warm countries and that can stay in one place in the air by beating its wings very fast, making a continuous low sound (= a humming sound)（蜂鸟（快速扇动翅膀发出声音，能原位停留））

humorous.meaning: funny and entertaining; showing a sense of humour（滑稽有趣的；有幽默感的）；hu·mor·ous·ly /ˈhjuːmərəsli; NAmEˈhjuːmərəsli/ adv. The poem humorously describes local characters and traditions.（那首诗幽默地描述了当地的人物和传统。）

humour.meaning: the quality in sth that makes it funny or amusing; the ability to laugh at things that are amusing（幽默；幽默感）；(formal) the state of your feelings or mind at a particular time（感觉；心情；精神状态）；(old use) one of the four liquids that were thought in the past to be in a person's body and to influence health and character（体液（旧时认为存在人体内，有四种，可影响健康和性格））；to agree with sb's wishes, even if they seem unreasonable, in order to keep the person happy（迁就；顺应）

hump.meaning: a large lump that sticks out above the surface of sth, especially the ground（（平面上的）大隆起物；（尤指）土墩，丘，冈）；a large lump on the back of some animals, especially camels（（某些动物的）峰；（尤指）驼峰）；a large lump on the back of a person, caused by an unusual curve in the spine (= the row of bones in the middle of the back)（（人的）驼背）；to have done the most difficult part of sth（完成最困难的部分；渡过最困难阶段）

hundred.meaning: You say a, one, two, several, etc. hundred without a final ‘s’ on ‘hundred’. Hundreds (of … ) can be used if there is no number or quantity before it. Always use a plural verb with hundred or hundreds, except when an amount of money is mentioned.（说 a, one, two, several, etc. hundred 时，hundred 后面不加 s。若前面没有数目或数量，可用 hundreds (of ... )。除指金额外，hundred 和 hundreds 均用复数动词）；(usually informal) a large amount（许多；数量大）；the numbers from 100 to 999（*）；the years of a particular century（某个世纪的年代）

hundredth.meaning: th（第一百）；each of one hundred equal parts of sth（百分之一）

hunger.meaning: the state of not having enough food to eat, especially when this causes illness or death（饥饿；饥荒）；the feeling caused by a need to eat（饥饿感；食欲；胃口）；(formal) a strong desire for sth（（对某事物的）渴望，渴求）；(literary) to have a strong desire or need for sth/sb（渴望得到；渴求）

hungry.meaning: feeling that you want to eat sth（感到饿的）；not having enough food to eat（饥饿的；挨饿的）；people who do not have enough food to eat（（统称）饿民）；causing you to feel that you want to eat sth（使人饥饿的；引起食欲的）

hunt.meaning: to chase wild animals or birds in order to catch or kill them for food, sport or to make money（打猎；猎取；猎杀）；to look for sth that is difficult to find（搜寻；搜索）；to look for sb in order to catch them or harm them（追踪；追捕）；(in Britain) to chase and kill foxes as a sport, riding horses and using dogs. Fox-hunting with dogs has been illegal in the UK since 2005.（（英国）猎狐（作为运动，自 2005 年起用狗猎狐是违法的））

hunter.meaning: a person who hunts wild animals for food or sport; an animal that hunts its food（猎人；狩猎者；（猎食其他动物的）猎兽）；(usually in compounds（通常构成复合词）；a person who looks for and collects a particular kind of thing（搜集某种东西的人）；(BrE) a fast strong horse used in hunting foxes（猎狐马）

hunter-gatherer.meaning: a member of a group of people who do not live in one place but move around and live by hunting, fishing and gathering plants（游猎采集部族成员）

hunting.meaning: chasing and killing wild animals and birds as a sport or for food（狩猎运动；打猎）；(in compounds（构成复合词）；the process of looking for sth（找；寻找）

hurdle.meaning: each of a series of vertical frames that a person or horse jumps over in a race（（供人或马在赛跑中跨越的）栏架，跨栏）；a race in which runners or horses have to jump over hurdles（跨栏赛）；a problem or difficulty that must be solved or dealt with before you can achieve sth（难关；障碍）；to jump over sth while you are running（（奔跑中）跳越（某物））

hurl.meaning: to throw sth/sb violently in a particular direction（猛扔；猛投；猛摔）；to shout insults, etc. at sb（大声说出（辱骂或斥责等））；(NAmE) (slang) to vomit（呕吐）

hurricane.meaning: a violent storm with very strong winds, especially in the western Atlantic Ocean（（尤指西大西洋的）飓风）

hurry.meaning: to do sth more quickly than usual because there is not much time（赶快，匆忙，急忙（做某事））；In spoken English hurry can be used with and plus another verb, instead of with to and the infinitive, especially to tell somebody to do something quickly.（英语口语中 hurry 可与 and 及所连接的另一个动词连用，而不和 to 所引导的不定式连用，尤用于告诉某人快点干某事）；to move quickly in a particular direction（（朝某方向）迅速移动）；to make sb do sth more quickly（催促（某人））

hurt.meaning: to cause physical pain to sb/yourself; to injure sb/yourself（（使）疼痛，受伤）；to feel painful（感到疼痛）；to make sb unhappy or upset（使不快；使烦恼）；(informal) to feel unhappy or upset（感到不高兴（或烦恼））

hurtful.meaning: (of comments（评论）；making you feel upset and offended（伤感情的；伤害自尊的）；hurt·ful·ly /ˈhɜːtfəli; NAmEˈhɜːrtfəli/ adv. He said, rather hurtfully, that he had better things to do than come and see me.（他相当刻薄地说来看我还不如去干别的事。）

hurtle.meaning: to move very fast in a particular direction（（向某个方向）飞驰，猛冲）

husband.meaning: the man that a woman is married to; a married man（丈夫）；a man and woman who are married to each other（夫妇）；(formal) to use sth very carefully and make sure that you do not waste it（节俭使用）

husbandry.meaning: farming, especially when done carefully and well（（尤指精心经营的）农牧业）；(old-fashioned) the careful use of food, money and supplies（节俭使用；精打细算）

hush.meaning: (used especially in orders（尤用于命令）；to be quiet; to stop talking or crying（安静；别说话；别叫喊）；to make sb/sth become quieter; to make sb stop talking, crying, etc.（使安静下来；使停止说话（或叫喊等））；to hide information about a situation because you do not want people to know about it（掩盖，蒙蔽（事实））

husk.meaning: the dry outer covering of nuts, fruits and seeds, especially of grain（（尤指谷类、果实和种子的）外壳，外皮）；to remove the husks from grain, seeds, nuts, etc.（去皮；去壳；去荚）

husky.meaning: (of a person or their voice（人或嗓音）；sounding deep, quiet and rough, sometimes in an attractive way（深沉沙哑的）；(of a man（男子）；big, strong and sexually attractive（粗壮有魅力的；高大威猛的）

hustle.meaning: to make sb move quickly by pushing them in a rough aggressive way（推搡；猛推）；to force sb to make a decision before they are ready or sure（催促（某人作决定））；(informal) (especially NAmE) to sell or obtain sth, often illegally（（常指非法地）兜售，取得）；(NAmE) (informal) to act in an aggressive way or with a lot of energy（强行；强迫；硬干）

hut.meaning: a small, simply built house or shelter（简陋的小房子（或棚、舍））

hydra.meaning: (in ancient Greek stories（古希腊故事）；a snake with several heads. As one head was cut off, another one grew. In the end it was killed by Hercules.（许德拉，多头蛇（砍去一个头即长出新头，后为大力神赫拉克勒斯所杀））；(formal) a thing that is very difficult to deal with, because it continues for a long time or because it has many different aspects（棘手的复杂事物；难以根绝的祸患）；(biology 生) an extremely small water creature with a tube-shaped body and tentacles around its mouth（水螅）

hydraulic.meaning: (of water, oil, etc.（水、油等）；moved through pipes, etc. under pressure（（通过水管等）液压的，水力的）；(of a piece of machinery（机器）；operated by liquid moving under pressure（液压驱动的）

hydroelectric.meaning: using the power of water to produce electricity; produced by the power of water（使用水力发电的；水力产生的）

hydrogen.meaning: a chemical element. Hydrogen is a gas that is the lightest of all the elements. It combines with oxygen to form water.（氢；氢气）

hygiene.meaning: the practice of keeping yourself and your living and working areas clean in order to prevent illness and disease（卫生）

hymn.meaning: a song of praise, especially one praising God and sung by Christians（赞美诗，圣歌（尤指基督徒唱的颂扬上帝的歌））；if a film/movie, book, etc. is a hymn to sth, it praises it very strongly（歌颂某事物的电影（或书等））

hyper.meaning: excited and nervous; having too much nervous energy（既兴奋又紧张的；精力过旺的）

hypersensitive.meaning: very easily offended（非常敏感的；很容易生气的）；extremely physically sensitive to particular substances, medicines, light, etc.（（对某些物质、药物、光等）过敏的）

hyphen.meaning: the mark ( ‐ ) used to join two words together to make a new one, as in back-up, or to show that a word has been divided between the end of one line and the beginning of the next（连字符）

hypnosis.meaning: an unconscious state in which sb can still see and hear and can be influenced to follow commands or answer questions（催眠状态）

hypocrisy.meaning: behaviour in which sb pretends to have moral standards or opinions that they do not actually have（伪善；虚伪）

hypothalamus.meaning: an area in the central lower part of the brain that controls body temperature, hunger, and the release of hormones（下丘脑（有调节体温、摄食、内分泌等的功能））

hypothesis.meaning: an idea or explanation of sth that is based on a few known facts but that has not yet been proved to be true or correct（（有少量事实依据但未被证实的）假说，假设）；guesses and ideas that are not based on certain knowledge（（凭空的）猜想，猜测）

hypothesize.meaning: (formal) to suggest a way of explaining sth when you do not definitely know about it; to form a hypothesis（假设；假定）

hypothetical.meaning: based on situations or ideas which are possible and imagined rather than real and true（假设的；假定的）

hysteria.meaning: a state of extreme excitement, fear or anger in which a person, or a group of people, loses control of their emotions and starts to cry, laugh, etc.（歇斯底里；情绪失控）；(disapproving) an extremely excited and exaggerated way of behaving or reacting to an event（大肆鼓吹；狂热夸张；大惊小怪）；(medical 医) a condition in which sb experiences violent or extreme emotions that they cannot control, especially as a result of shock（癔病；歇斯底里）

hysterical.meaning: in a state of extreme excitement, and crying, laughing, etc. in an uncontrolled way（歇斯底里的；情绪狂暴不可抑止的）；(informal) extremely funny（极其可笑的）；hys·ter·ic·al·ly /hɪˈsterɪkli; NAmEhɪˈsterɪkli/ adv. to laugh/cry/scream/sob hysterically（歇斯底里地大笑/大哭/尖叫/哭泣）

i.meaning: the 9th letter of the English alphabet（英语字母表的第 9 个字母）；used as the subject of a verb when the speaker or writer is referring to himself/herself（（指称自己，作动词的主语）我）；the number 1 in Roman numerals（（罗马数字）1）；(especially on maps) Island(s); Isle(s)（（尤用于地图）岛，群岛）

ibex.meaning: a mountain goat with long curved horns（北山羊，羱羊（角长而弯曲））

ice.meaning: water that has frozen and become solid（冰）；a frozen surface that people skate on（冰场；溜冰场）；a piece of ice used to keep food and drinks cold（冰块）；(old-fashioned) (especially BrE) an ice cream（一份冰淇淋）

iceberg.meaning: an extremely large mass of ice floating in the sea（冰山（浮在海上的巨大冰块））

ice-bound.meaning: surrounded by or covered in ice（被冰围封的；冰封的）

icicle.meaning: a pointed piece of ice that is formed when water freezes as it falls down from sth such as a roof（（屋檐等处滴水形成的）冰锥，冰柱）

icon.meaning: (computing 计) a small symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file（图标；图符；（台）图示）；a famous person or thing that people admire and see as a symbol of a particular idea, way of life, etc.（崇拜对象；偶像）；(in the Orthodox Church（东正教）；a painting or statue of a holy person that is also thought of as a holy object（圣像）

iconography.meaning: the use or study of images or symbols in art（图示法；象征手法；图像学）

icy.meaning: very cold（冰冷的；冰冻的）；covered with ice（覆盖着冰的；结满冰的）；(of a person's voice, manner, etc.（嗓音、态度等）；not friendly or kind; showing feelings of dislike or anger（冷冰冰的；冷峻的）

id.meaning: the abbreviation for ‘identity’ or ‘identification’ (an official way of showing who you are, for example a document with your name, date of birth and often a photograph on it)（身分证明（全写为 identity 或 identification)）

idea.meaning: a plan, thought or suggestion, especially about what to do in a particular situation（想法；构思；主意）；a picture or an impression in your mind of what sb/sth is like（印象；概念）；an opinion or a belief about sth（意见；看法；信念）；a feeling that sth is possible（（认为某事可能发生的）感觉）

ideal.meaning: perfect; most suitable（完美的；理想的；最合适的）；existing only in your imagination or as an idea; not likely to be real（想像的；不切实际的）；ideal·ly /aɪˈdiːəli; NAmEaɪˈdiːəli/ adv. She's ideally suited for this job.（她最适合这项工作。）；an idea or standard that seems perfect, and worth trying to achieve or obtain（理想；看似完美的思想（或标准））

idealism.meaning: the belief that a perfect life, situation, etc. can be achieved, even when this is not very likely（理想主义）；(philosophy 哲) the belief that our ideas are the only things that are real and that we can know about（唯心主义；唯心论；观念论；理念论）；ideal·ist /aɪˈdiːəlɪst; NAmEaɪˈdiːəlɪst/ noun He's too much of an idealist for this government.（在现政府的眼中，他是一个过度的理想主义者。）

idealistic.meaning: having a strong belief in perfect standards and trying to achieve them, even when this is not realistic（理想主义的；空想的）

idealize.meaning: to consider or represent sb/sth as being perfect or better than they really are（将 … 视为理想；将 … 理想化）

identical.meaning: similar in every detail（完全同样的；相同的）；the same（同一的）；iden·ti·cal·ly AW /aɪˈdentɪkli; NAmEaɪˈdentɪkli/ adv. The children were dressed identically.（孩子们的穿着完全一样。）

identifiable.meaning: that can be recognized（可识别的；可辨认的）

identification.meaning: the process of showing, proving or recognizing who or what sb/sth is（鉴定；辨认）；the process of recognizing that sth exists, or is important（确认；确定）；official papers or a document that can prove who you are（身分证明）；a strong feeling of sympathy, understanding or support for sb/sth（强烈的同情感（或谅解、支持））

identify.meaning: to recognize sb/sth and be able to say who or what they are（确认；认出；鉴定）；to find or discover sb/sth（找到；发现）；to make it possible to recognize who or what sb/sth is（显示；说明身分）；to feel that you can understand and share the feelings of sb else（与某人产生共鸣；谅解；同情）

identity.meaning: who or what sb/sth is（身分；本身；本体）；the characteristics, feelings or beliefs that distinguish people from others（特征；特有的感觉（或信仰））；the state or feeling of being very similar to and able to understand sb/sth（同一性；相同；一致）

ideology.meaning: a set of ideas that an economic or political system is based on（思想（体系）；思想意识）；a set of beliefs, especially one held by a particular group, that influences the way people behave（意识形态；观念形态）；ideo·logic·al AW /ˌaɪdiəˈlɒdʒɪkl; NAmEˌaɪdiəˈlɑːdʒɪkl/ adj. ideological differences（意识形态上的差别）；ideo·logic·al·ly AW /ˌaɪdiəˈlɒdʒɪkli; NAmEˌaɪdiəˈlɑːdʒɪkli/ adv. ideologically correct（意识上正确）

idiom.meaning: a group of words whose meaning is different from the meanings of the individual words（习语；成语；惯用语）；(formal) the kind of language and grammar used by particular people at a particular time or place（（某时期或某地区的人的）语言和语法）；(formal) the style of writing, music, art, etc. that is typical of a particular person, group, period or place（（写作、音乐、艺术等的）典型风格）

idiomatic.meaning: containing expressions that are natural to a native speaker of a language（表达方式地道的；符合（某一）语言习惯的）；containing an idiom（包含习语的）

idiosyncrasy.meaning: a person's particular way of behaving, thinking, etc., especially when it is unusual; an unusual feature（（个人特有的）习性；特征；癖好）；idio·syn·crat·ic /ˌɪdiəsɪŋˈkrætɪk; NAmEˌɪdiəsɪŋˈkrætɪk/ adj. His teaching methods are idiosyncratic but successful.（他的教学方法很奇特，但很成功。）

idiot.meaning: (informal) a very stupid person（蠢人；笨蛋）；(old-fashioned, offensive) a person with very low intelligence who cannot think or behave normally（白痴）

idle.meaning: (of people（人）；not working hard（懈怠的；懒惰的）；(of machines, factories, etc.（机器、工厂等）；not in use（闲置的）

idly.meaning: without any particular reason, purpose or effort; doing nothing（毫无目的地；漫不经心地；闲散地）

idol.meaning: a person or thing that is loved and admired very much（受到热爱和崇拜的人（或物）；偶像）；a statue that is worshipped as a god（神像）

idyll.meaning: (literary) a happy and peaceful place, event or experience, especially one connected with the countryside（（尤指乡下的）愉快恬静的地方（或事情、经历））；a short poem or other piece of writing that describes a peaceful and happy scene（描述恬静愉快情景的短诗（或短文）；田园诗）

idyllic.meaning: peaceful and beautiful; perfect, without problems（平和美丽的；完美无瑕的）；idyl·lic·al·ly /ɪˈdɪlɪkli; NAmEaɪˈdɪlɪkli/ adv. a house idyllically set in wooded grounds（诗情画意般的林荫中的房子）

i.e..meaning: used to explain exactly what the previous thing that you have mentioned means (from Latin ‘id est’)（也就是，亦即（源自拉丁文 id est））

invasion.meaning: the act of an army entering another country by force in order to take control of it（武装入侵；侵略；侵犯）；the fact of a large number of people or things arriving somewhere, especially people or things that are disturbing or unpleasant（（尤指烦扰的）涌入）；an act or a process that affects sb/sth in a way that is not welcome（侵犯；干预）

keen.meaning: (especially BrE) wanting to do sth or wanting sth to happen very much（渴望；热切；热衷于）；(especially BrE) enthusiastic about an activity or idea, etc.（热情的；热心的）；(BrE) (informal) liking sb/sth very much; very interested in sb/sth（喜爱；（对 … ）着迷，有兴趣）；quick to understand（思维敏捷的；机灵的；机智的）

keeper.meaning: (especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）；a person whose job is to take care of a building, its contents or sth valuable（看守人；保管人）；a person whose job is to take care of animals, especially in a zoo（（尤指动物园的）饲养员）

keeping.meaning: being taken care of by sb（由某人照料（或供养、饲养））；appropriate or expected in a particular situation; in agreement with sth（（与 … ）协调，一致）；not appropriate or expected in a particular situation; not in agreement with sth（（与 … ）不协调，不一致）

kennel.meaning: a small shelter for a dog to sleep in（狗窝；犬舍）；a place where people can leave their dogs to be taken care of when they go on holiday/vacation; a place where dogs are bred（（寄养狗的）养狗场；狗繁殖场）

kernel.meaning: the inner part of a nut or seed（（坚果或籽粒的）仁，核）；the central, most important part of an idea or a subject（（思想或主题的）核心，中心，要点）

kerosene.meaning: a type of fuel oil that is made from petroleum and that is used in the engines of planes and for heat and light. In British English it is usually called paraffin when it is used for heat and light.（煤油）

kestrel.meaning: a small bird of prey (= a bird that kills other creatures for food) of the falcon family（红隼（小猛禽））

ketchup.meaning: a thick cold sauce made from tomatoes, usually sold in bottles（番茄酱）

kettle.meaning: a container with a lid, handle and a spout, used for boiling water（（烧水用的）壶，水壶）

key.meaning: a specially shaped piece of metal used for locking a door, starting a car, etc.（钥匙）；a thing that makes you able to understand or achieve sth（关键；要诀）；any of the buttons that you press to operate a computer or typewriter（（计算机或打字机的）键）；any of the wooden or metal parts that you press to play a piano and some other musical instruments（（钢琴或其他乐器的）键）

keyboard.meaning: the set of keys for operating a computer or typewriter（（计算机或打字机的）键盘）；the set of black and white keys on a piano or other musical instrument（（钢琴或其他乐器的）琴键，键盘）；an electronic musical instrument that has keys like a piano and can be made to play in different styles or to sound like different instruments（键盘式电子乐器）；to type information into a computer（用键盘输入；将（信息）键入计算机）

keyhole.meaning: the hole in a lock that you put a key in（锁眼；钥匙孔）

kick.meaning: to hit sb/sth with your foot（踢；踹）；to move your legs as if you were kicking sth（踢蹬；踢（腿））；(informal) to be annoyed with yourself because you have done sth stupid, missed an opportunity, etc.（（因干了蠢事、失去良机等）对（自己）生气）；(in sports such as football (soccer) and rugby（体育运动，如足球和橄榄球）

kid.meaning: (informal) a child or young person（小孩；年轻人）；a young goat（小山羊）；soft leather made from the skin of a young goat（小山羊皮革）；to deal with sb in a very careful way so that you do not offend or upset them（小心应付某人）

kidney.meaning: either of the two organs in the body that remove waste products from the blood and produce urine（肾；肾脏）；the kidneys of some animals that are cooked and eaten（（食用的）动物腰子）

kill.meaning: to make sb/sth die（杀死；弄死；导致死亡）；to destroy or spoil sth or make it stop（毁灭；破坏；扼杀；使停止）；(informal) (usually used in the progressive tenses and not used in the passive（通常用于进行时，不用于被动语态）；to cause sb pain or suffering（使痛苦；使疼痛；使受折磨）

killer.meaning: a person, an animal or a thing that kills（杀人者；杀手；导致死亡的人（或动物、事物））；(informal) something that is very difficult, very exciting or very skilful（棘手的事；令人激动的事物；精彩的事物）

killing.meaning: an act of killing sb deliberately（故意杀人；谋杀）；(informal) to make a lot of money quickly（发大财；获取暴利；财运亨通）；making you very tired（使人筋疲力尽的）

kiln.meaning: a large oven for baking clay and bricks, drying wood and grain, etc.（窰）

kilogram.meaning: a unit for measuring weight; 1 000 grams（千克；公斤）

kilometre.meaning: a unit for measuring distance; 1 000 metres（千米；公里）

kilowatt.meaning: a unit for measuring electrical power; 1 000 watts（千瓦（电的功率计量单位，等于 1 000 瓦特））

kin.meaning: your family or your relatives（（统称）家属，亲属，亲戚）

kind.meaning: a group of people or things that are the same in some way; a particular variety or type（同类的人（或事物）；种类）；(of a payment（支付）；consisting of goods or services, not money（以实物支付；以货代款；以服务偿付）；(formal) with the same thing（以同样的方法（或手段））

kindergarten.meaning: (especially NAmE) a school or class to prepare children aged five for school（学前班）

kindle.meaning: to start burning; to make a fire start burning（开始燃烧；点燃）；to make sth such as an interest, emotion, etc. start to grow in sb; to start to be felt by sb（激起（兴趣、感情等）；发展起来；被感受到）
