kindness.meaning: the quality of being kind（仁慈；善良；体贴；宽容）；a kind act（友好（或仁慈、体贴）的举动）

kinetic.meaning: of or produced by movement（运动的；运动引起的）

king.meaning: the male ruler of an independent state that has a royal family（君主；国王）；a person, an animal or a thing that is thought to be the best or most important of a particular type（（人、动物、事物中的）首屈一指者，最重要者，大王）；used in compounds with the names of animals or plants to describe a very large type of the thing mentioned（（与动植物名称连用构成复合词，表示巨型）… 之最， … 之王，巨型 …）；the most important piece used in the game of chess, that can move one square in any direction（（国际象棋中的）王）

kingdom.meaning: a country ruled by a king or queen（王国）；an area controlled by a particular person or where a particular thing or idea is important（管辖范围；领域）；one of the three traditional divisions of the natural world（自然三界之一）；(biology 生) one of the five major groups into which all living things are organized（界（生物的五大类别之一））

kink.meaning: a bend or twist in sth that is usually straight（（直线物体上的）弯，结）；(informal, disapproving) an unusual feature in a person's character or mind, especially one that does not seem normal（怪癖；怪念头；奇想）；to develop or make sth develop a bend or twist（（使）弯曲，扭结，绞缠）

kinship.meaning: the fact of being related in a family（亲属关系）；a feeling of being close to sb because you have similar origins or attitudes（（因出身或态度相似而产生的）亲切感）

kiosk.meaning: a small shop/store, open at the front, where newspapers, drinks, etc. are sold. In some countries kiosks also sell food and things used in the home.（（出售报纸、饮料等的）小亭；售货亭；报刊亭）；(old-fashioned) (BrE) a public telephone box（公用电话亭）

kit.meaning: a set of parts ready to be made into sth（配套元件）；a set of tools or equipment that you use for a particular purpose（成套工具；成套设备）；(BrE) a set of clothes and equipment that you use for a particular activity（全套衣服及装备）；(BrE) (slang) to take your clothes off（把你的衣服都脱掉）

kitchen.meaning: a room in which meals are cooked or prepared（厨房）；(informal, humorous) a very large number of things, probably more than is necessary（过多的东西；大量的东西）

kitchenware.meaning: used in shops/stores to describe objects that you use in a kitchen, such as pans, bowls, etc.（（商店用语）厨房用具）

kite.meaning: a toy made of a light frame covered with paper, cloth, etc., that you fly in the air at the end of one or more long strings（风筝）；a bird of prey (= a bird that kills other creatures for food) of the hawk family（鸢（猛禽））；(NAmE) (informal) to use an illegal cheque to obtain money or to dishonestly change the amount written on a cheque（使用（非法支票）骗钱；涂改（支票））

knead.meaning: to press and stretch dough, wet clay, etc. with your hands to make it ready to use（揉，捏（面团、湿黏土等））；to rub and squeeze muscles, etc. especially to relax them or to make them less painful（揉捏，按摩，推拿（肌肉等））

knee.meaning: the joint between the top and bottom parts of the leg where it bends in the middle（膝；膝盖；膝关节）；the part of a piece of clothing that covers the knee（（裤子的）膝部）；the top surface of the upper part of the legs when you are sitting down（（坐下时）大腿朝上的面）；to defeat sb, especially in a war（（尤指战争中）打败某人，使某人屈膝投降）

kneel.meaning: to be in or move into a position where your body is supported on your knee or knees（跪；跪着；跪下）

knife.meaning: a sharp blade with a handle, used for cutting or as a weapon（刀）；the situation has become so bad that people are preparing to make one person take the blame, for example by taking away their job（（对某人）磨刀霍霍，兴师问罪）；(informal) easily; without meeting any difficulty（轻而易举；毫无困难）；(informal) to be very unfriendly to sb and try to harm them（对某人怀恨在心；加害于某人）

knight.meaning: (in the Middle Ages) a man of high social rank who had a duty to fight for his king. Knights are often shown in pictures riding horses and wearing armour.（（中世纪的）骑士）；(in Britain) a man who has been given a special honour by the king or queen and has the title Sir before his name（（英国）爵士（其名前冠以 Sir））；a piece used in the game of chess that is shaped like a horse's head（（国际象棋中的）马）；(usually humorous) a man who saves sb, especially a woman, from a dangerous situation（救人（尤指女子）于危难之中的男子；（拯救美人的）英雄）

knit.meaning: to make clothes, etc. from wool or cotton thread using two long thin knitting needles or a machine（编织；针织；机织）；to use a basic stitch in knitting（织平针）；to join people or things closely together or to be joined closely together（（使）紧密结合，严密，紧凑）；(of broken bones（断骨）

knitted.meaning: made by knitting wool or thread（编织的；针织的）

knitting.meaning: an item that is being knitted（编织物；针织品）；the activity of knitting（编织；针织）

knob.meaning: a round switch on a machine such as a television that you use to turn it on and off, etc.（（用以开关电视机等的）旋钮）；a round handle on a door or a drawer（（门或抽屉的）球形把手）；a round lump on the surface or end of sth（疙瘩；节）；(especially BrE) a small lump of sth such as butter（小块（黄油等））

knock.meaning: to hit a door, etc. firmly in order to attract attention（敲；击）；to hit sth, often by accident, with a short, hard blow（（常为无意地）碰，撞）；to put sb/sth into a particular state by hitting them/it（把 … 撞击成（某种状态））；to hit sth so that it moves or breaks（打掉；敲动；打破）

knot.meaning: a join made by tying together two pieces or ends of string, rope, etc.（（用绳索等打的）结）；a way of twisting hair into a small round shape at the back of the head（发髻）；a hard round spot in a piece of wood where there was once a branch（节子；节疤）；a small group of people standing close together（一小群人）

knotty.meaning: complicated and difficult to solve（复杂的；难以解决的；棘手的）；having parts that are hard and twisted together（有节的；缠绕在一起的）

know.meaning: to have information in your mind as a result of experience or because you have learned or been told it（知道；知悉；了解）；to realize, understand or be aware of sth（认识到；懂得；意识到）；to feel certain about sth（确信；确知；肯定）；to be familiar with a person, place, thing, etc.（熟悉；认识；了解）

knowledge.meaning: the information, understanding and skills that you gain through education or experience（知识；学问；学识）；the state of knowing about a particular fact or situation（知晓；知悉；了解）；working with information rather than producing goods（信息，知识（与产品制造相对））；to be sth that everyone knows, especially in a particular community or group（常识；众所周知）

knuckle.meaning: any of the joints in the fingers, especially those connecting the fingers to the rest of the hand（指节；指关节）；a piece of meat from the lower part of an animal's leg, especially a pig（（猪等动物的）肘，蹄）；(of a remark, joke, etc.（言语、玩笑等）；concerned with sex in a way that is likely to offend people or make them feel embarrassed（近乎下流；近乎猥亵）

krill.meaning: very small shellfish that live in the sea around the Antarctic and are eaten by whales（南极磷虾；磷虾）

label.meaning: a piece of paper, etc. that is attached to sth and that gives information about it（标签；签条；标记）；(disapproving) a word or phrase that is used to describe sb/sth in a way that seems too general, unfair or not correct（（不恰当的）称谓，绰号，叫法）；a company that produces and sells music, CDs, etc.（唱片公司）；to fix a label on sth or write information on sth（贴标签于；用标签标明）

labour.meaning: work, especially physical work（劳动；（尤指）体力劳动）；(formal) a task or period of work（任务；（一段时间的）工作）；the people who work or are available for work in a country or company（（统称）劳工，工人；劳动力）；the period of time or the process of giving birth to a baby（分娩期；分娩；生产）

labyrinth.meaning: a complicated series of paths, which it is difficult to find your way through（迷宫；曲径）；laby·rin·thine /ˌlæbəˈrɪnθaɪn; NAmEˌlæbəˈrɪnθaɪn; ˌlæbəˈrɪnθɪn/ adj. (formal) labyrinthine corridors（迷宫式的走廊）

lad.meaning: (old-fashioned or informal, BrE) a boy or young man（男孩儿；少年；男青年；小伙子）；(BrE) (informal) a group of friends that a man works with or spends free time with（伙伴；哥们儿）；(BrE) (informal) a lively young man, especially one who is very interested in women and having sex, drinks a lot of alcohol and enjoys sport（（精力旺盛的）放荡小伙子）；(BrE) a person who works in a stable（马夫；马倌）

ladder.meaning: a piece of equipment for climbing up and down a wall, the side of a building, etc., consisting of two lengths of wood or metal that are joined together by steps or rungs（梯子）；a series of stages by which you can make progress in your life or career（（生活上进步或事业上晋升的）阶梯，途径）；a long thin hole in tights or stockings where some threads have broken（（紧身裤袜或长筒袜的）滑丝，抽丝）；a competition in a particular sport or game in which teams or players are arranged in a list and they can move up the list by defeating one of the teams or players above（开级比赛，开级游戏（将参赛者排名，胜者名次前提））

laden.meaning: heavily loaded with sth（载满的；装满的）；(literary) full of sth, especially sth unpleasant（充满的（尤指充满令人不快的东西））；used to form adjectives showing that sth is full of, or loaded with, the thing mentioned（（用于构成形容词）充满 … 的，装载 … 的）

lag.meaning: to move or develop slowly or more slowly than other people, organizations, etc.（缓慢移动；发展缓慢；滞后；落后于）；(BrE) to cover pipes, etc. with a special material to stop the water in them from freezing, or to save heat（给（管道等）加防冻保暖层）

lake.meaning: a large area of water that is surrounded by land（湖；湖泊）

mad.meaning: (especially BrE) having a mind that does not work normally; mentally ill（疯的；神经错乱的；有精神病的）；(informal) (especially BrE) very stupid; not at all sensible（极愚蠢的；很不明智的）；(informal) (especially NAmE) very angry（很生气；气愤）；(BrE) (informal) liking sth/sb very much; very interested in sth（特别喜欢；痴迷；迷恋）

madam.meaning: (formal) used when speaking or writing to a woman in a formal or business situation（夫人；女士）；(informal, disapproving) (especially BrE) a girl or young woman who expects other people to do what she wants（喜欢支使别人的年轻女子；任性妄为的年轻女子）；a woman who is in charge of the prostitutes in a brothel（老鸨；鸨母；妓院女老板）

madden.meaning: to make a person or an animal very angry or crazy（使非常生气；使发疯）；mad·den·ing /ˈmædnɪŋ; NAmEˈmædnɪŋ/ adj. maddening delays（令人非常气恼的延误）；mad·den·ing·ly /ˈmædnɪŋli; NAmEˈmædnɪŋli/ adv. Progress is maddeningly slow.（进展慢得令人心烦。）

madman.meaning: a man who has a serious mental illness（疯子；精神病患者）

madness.meaning: (old-fashioned) the state of having a serious mental illness（精神失常；疯狂）；crazy or stupid behaviour that could be dangerous（（会带来危险的）癫狂，疯狂，愚蠢行为）

magazine.meaning: a type of large thin book with a paper cover that you can buy every week or month, containing articles, photographs, etc., often on a particular topic（杂志；期刊）；a radio or television programme that is about a particular topic（（电视、广播）专题节目）；the part of a gun that holds the bullets before they are fired（弹仓；弹盒；弹盘）；a room or building where weapons, explosives and bullets are stored（弹药库；军火库；军械库）

magenta.meaning: reddish-purple in colour（紫红色的；洋红色的）

magic.meaning: the secret power of appearing to make impossible things happen by saying special words or doing special things（魔法；法术；巫术）；the art of doing tricks that seem impossible in order to entertain people（戏法；魔术）；a special quality or ability that sb/sth has, that seems too wonderful to be real（魔力；魅力；神奇）；having or using special powers to make impossible things happen or seem to happen（有魔力的；（施）巫术的；有神奇力量的）

magical.meaning: containing magic; used in magic（有魔力的；用于巫术的）；(informal) wonderful; very enjoyable（奇妙的；令人愉快的）

magician.meaning: a person who can do magic tricks（魔术师；变戏法的人）；(in stories（故事中）；a person who has magic powers（巫师；术士；施妖术的人）

magistrate.meaning: an official who acts as a judge in the lowest courts of law（地方执法官）

magma.meaning: very hot liquid rock found below the earth's surface（岩浆；熔岩）

magnanimous.meaning: kind, generous and forgiving, especially towards an enemy or a rival（宽宏的，大度的（尤指对敌人或对手））；mag·na·nim·ity /ˌmæɡnəˈnɪməti; NAmEˌmæɡnəˈnɪməti/ noun [U] She accepted the criticism with magnanimity.（她很大度地接受了批评。）

magnate.meaning: a person who is rich, powerful and successful, especially in business（权贵；要人；富豪；（尤指）产业大亨）

magnesium.meaning: a chemical element. Magnesium is a light, silver-white metal that burns with a bright white flame.（镁）

magnet.meaning: a piece of iron that attracts objects made of iron towards it, either naturally or because of an electric current that is passed through it（磁铁；磁石；吸铁石）；a person, place or thing that sb/sth is attracted to（有吸引力的人（或地方、事物））；an object with a magnetic surface that you can stick onto a metal surface（磁体；磁性物体）

magnetic.meaning: behaving like a magnet (1)（像磁铁的；有磁性的）；connected with or produced by magnetism（磁的；磁性的）；that people find very powerful and attractive（富有吸引力的；有魅力的）

magnetism.meaning: a physical property (= characteristic) of some metals such as iron, produced by electric currents, that causes forces between objects, either pulling them towards each other or pushing them apart（磁性；磁力）；the qualities of sth, especially a person's character, that people find powerful and attractive（吸引力；魅力）

magnetize.meaning: (technical 术语) to make sth metal behave like a magnet（磁化；使有磁性）；to strongly attract sb（吸引；迷住）

magnification.meaning: the act of making sth look larger（放大）；the degree to which sth is made to look larger; the degree to which sth is able to make things look larger（放大率；放大倍数）

magnificent.meaning: extremely attractive and impressive; deserving praise（壮丽的；宏伟的；值得赞扬的）；mag·nifi·cence /mæɡˈnɪfɪsns; NAmEmæɡˈnɪfɪsns/ noun [U] the magnificence of the scenery（景色壮观）；mag·nifi·cent·ly /mæɡˈnɪfɪsntli; NAmEmæɡˈnɪfɪsntli/ adv. The public have responded magnificently to our appeal.（对于我们的呼吁，公众的反响极为热烈。）

magnify.meaning: to make sth look bigger than it really is, for example by using a lens or microscope（放大）；to make sth bigger, louder or stronger（扩大；增强）；to make sth seem more important or serious than it really is（夸大（重要性或严重性）；夸张）

magnitude.meaning: (formal) the great size or importance of sth; the degree to which sth is large or important（巨大；重大；重要性）；(astronomy 天) the degree to which a star is bright（星等；星的亮度）；(geology 地) the size of an earthquake（震级）

maid.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a female servant in a house or hotel（女仆；侍女；（旅馆的）女服务员）；(old use) a young woman who is not married（少女；年轻姑娘；未婚年轻女子）

maiden.meaning: (literary) a young girl or woman who is not married（少女；处女；未婚女子）；(in cricket（板球）；an over in which no points are scored（未得分的一轮投球）；being the first of its kind（首次的；初次的）

mail.meaning: the official system used for sending and delivering letters, packages, etc.（邮政；邮递系统）；letters, packages, etc. that are sent and delivered（邮件；信件；邮包）；messages that are sent or received on a computer（电子邮件；电邮）；used in the title of some newspapers（（用作报纸名称）邮报）

mailbox.meaning: a small box near the main door of a building or by the road, which mail is delivered to（（建筑物大门口或路旁的）信箱）；a public box, for example in the street, that you put letters into when you send them（邮筒；邮箱）；the area of a computer's memory where email messages are stored（电子邮箱，信箱区（计算机的电邮存贮区））

maim.meaning: to injure sb seriously, causing permanent damage to their body（使残废；使受重伤）

main.meaning: being the largest or most important of its kind（主要的；最重要的）；a large pipe that carries water or gas to a building; a large cable that carries electricity to a building（（通往建筑物的）主管道，总管，输电干线）；a large pipe that carries waste/water and sewage (= human waste, etc.) away from a building（（建筑物的）污水总管道）；(BrE) the place where the supply of water, gas or electricity to a building or an area starts; the system of providing gas, water and electricity to a building or of carrying it away from a building（水源；煤气源；电源；（水、煤气、电等的）供应系统；下水道系统）

mainland.meaning: the main area of land of a country, not including any islands near to it（大陆；（不包括附近岛屿的）国土的主体）；main·land adj. [only before noun] mainland Greece（希腊大陆）

mainly.meaning: more than anything else; also used to talk about the most important reason for sth（主要地；首要地）；in most cases; used to talk about the largest part of a group of people or things（大部分；大多）

mainstay.meaning: a person or thing that is the most important part of sth and enables it to exist or be successful（支柱；中流砥柱）

mainstream.meaning: the ideas and opinions that are thought to be normal because they are shared by most people; the people whose ideas and opinions are most accepted（主流思想；主流群体）；main·stream adj. [usually before noun] mainstream education（主流教育）；to make a particular idea or opinion accepted by most people（使为大多数人所接受）；(especially NAmE) to include children with mental or physical problems in ordinary school classes（让（身心有缺陷的儿童）融入主流教育）

maintain.meaning: to make sth continue at the same level, standard, etc.（维持；保持）；to keep a building, a machine, etc. in good condition by checking or repairing it regularly（维修；保养）；to keep stating that sth is true, even though other people do not agree or do not believe it（坚持意见；固执己见）；to support sb/sth over a long period of time by giving money, paying for food, etc.（供养；扶养）

maintenance.meaning: the act of keeping sth in good condition by checking or repairing it regularly（维护；保养）；the act of making a state or situation continue（维持；保持）；(BrE) money that sb must pay regularly to their former wife, husband or partner, especially when they have had children together（（依法应负担的）生活费；抚养费）

maize.meaning: a tall plant grown for its large yellow grains that are used for making flour or eaten as a vegetable; the grains of this plant（玉蜀黍；玉米）

majestic.meaning: impressive because of size or beauty（雄伟的；威严的；壮观的）

majesty.meaning: the impressive and attractive quality that sth has（雄伟壮观；庄严；威严）；a title of respect used when speaking about or to a king or queen（（对国王或女王的尊称）陛下）；royal power（王权）

major.meaning: very large or important（主要的；重要的；大的）；(NAmE) serious（严重）；(music 音) based on a scale (= a series of eight notes) in which the third note is two whole tones/steps higher than the first note（大调的）；(NAmE) related to sb's main subject of study in college（（课程）主修的）

majority.meaning: the largest part of a group of people or things（大部分；大多数）；(BrE) the number of votes by which one political party wins an election; the number of votes by which one side in a discussion, etc. wins（（获胜的）票数；多数票）；(NAmE) the difference between the number of votes given to the candidate who wins the election and the total number of votes of all the other candidates（超出其余各方票数总和的票数）；(law 律) the age at which you are legally considered to be an adult（成年的法定年龄）

make.meaning: to create or prepare sth by combining materials or putting parts together（制造；做；组装）；to write, create or prepare sth（写；出产；制订）；to arrange a bed so that it is neat and ready for use（铺床）；to cause sth to appear as a result of breaking, tearing, hitting or removing material（造成（破坏、破损等））

maker.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a person, company, or piece of equipment that makes or produces sth（生产者；制造者；制订者）；God（上帝）

makeshift.meaning: used temporarily for a particular purpose because the real thing is not available（临时替代的；权宜的）

make-up.meaning: substances used especially by women to make their faces look more attractive, or used by actors to change their appearance（化妆品）；the different qualities that combine to form sb's character or being（性格；气质）；the different things, people, etc. that combine to form sth; the way in which they combine（组成成分；构成方式）；(NAmE) a special exam taken by students who missed or failed an earlier one（补考）

making.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；the act or process of making or producing sth（生产；制造）；to make sb become a better or more successful person（使成为更好（或更有作为）的人）；to have the qualities that are necessary to become sth（具备了成为 … 的必要条件）

malady.meaning: (formal) a serious problem（严重问题；痼疾）；(old use) an illness（疾病）

malaise.meaning: the problems affecting a particular situation or group of people that are difficult to explain or identify（（影响某个情况或某群人的）难以捉摸的问题，无法描述的问题）；a general feeling of being ill/sick, unhappy or not satisfied, without signs of any particular problem（莫名的不适（或不快、不满等））

malaria.meaning: a disease that causes fever and shivering (= shaking of the body) caused by the bite of some types of mosquito（疟疾）；mal·ar·ial /məˈleəriəl; NAmEməˈleriəl/ adj. malarial insects/patients/regions（传播疟疾的昆虫；疟疾病人/流行区域）

male.meaning: belonging to the sex that does not give birth to babies; connected with this sex（男性的；雄性的；男的）；(of most plants（大多数植物）；producing pollen（雄性的）；(of electrical plugs, parts of tools, etc.（电器插头、工具部件等）

malfunction.meaning: (of a machine, etc.（机器等）；to fail to work correctly（运转失常；失灵；出现故障）

malice.meaning: a feeling of hatred for sb that causes a desire to harm them（恶意；怨恨）；(law 律) with the deliberate intention of committing a crime or harming sb（（犯罪或伤人）有恶意预谋的）

malicious.meaning: having or showing hatred and a desire to harm sb or hurt their feelings（怀有恶意的；恶毒的）

malignant.meaning: (of a tumour or disease（肿瘤或疾病）；that cannot be controlled and is likely to cause death（恶性的）；(formal) having or showing a strong desire to harm sb（恶意的；恶毒的）

mall.meaning: (both especially NAmE) a large building or covered area that has many shops/stores, restaurants, etc. inside it（购物商场；购物广场）

malleable.meaning: (of metal, etc.（金属等）；that can be hit or pressed into different shapes easily without breaking or cracking（可锻造的；可轧压的；易成型的）；(of people, ideas, etc.（人、思想等）；easily influenced or changed（可塑的；易受影响（或改变）的）

mallet.meaning: a hammer with a large wooden head（木槌）；a hammer with a long handle and a wooden head, used for hitting the ball in the games of croquet and polo（（槌球和马球运动的）球棍，球棒）

malnutrition.meaning: a poor condition of health caused by a lack of food or a lack of the right type of food（营养不良）

malpractice.meaning: careless, wrong or illegal behaviour while in a professional job（渎职；玩忽职守）

maltreat.meaning: to be very cruel to a person or an animal（虐待）

mammal.meaning: any animal that gives birth to live babies, not eggs, and feeds its young on milk. Cows, humans and whales are all mammals.（哺乳动物）

mammoth.meaning: an animal like a large elephant covered with hair, that lived thousands of years ago and is now extinct（猛犸（象）；毛象）；extremely large（极其巨大的；庞大的）

man.meaning: an adult male human（成年男子；男人）；humans as a group or from a particular period of history（人类；（特定历史时期的）人）；(literary or old-fashioned) a person, either male or female（（不论性别的）人）；(in compounds（构成复合词）

manacle.meaning: one of two metal bands joined by a chain, used for fastening a prisoner's ankles or wrists together（手铐；脚镣；镣铐）；to put manacles on sb's wrists or ankles, to stop them from escaping（给 … 戴上镣铐）

manage.meaning: to succeed in doing sth, especially sth difficult（完成（困难的事）；勉力完成）；to be able to solve your problems, deal with a difficult situation, etc.（能解决（问题）；应付（困难局面等））；to be able to live without having much money（凑合着活下去；支撑）；to use money, time, information, etc. in a sensible way（明智地使用（金钱、时间、信息等））

manageable.meaning: possible to deal with or control（可操纵的；可处理的）

management.meaning: the act of running and controlling a business or similar organization（经营；管理）；the people who run and control a business or similar organization（经营者；管理部门；资方）；the act or skill of dealing with people or situations in a successful way（（成功的）处理手段；（有效的）处理能力）

manager.meaning: a person who is in charge of running a business, a shop/store or a similar organization or part of one（（企业、店铺等的）经理，经营者，老板）；a person who deals with the business affairs of an actor, a musician, etc.（（演员、音乐家等的）经理人，个人经理）；a person who trains and organizes a sports team（（运动队的）经理）

managerial.meaning: connected with the work of a manager（经理的；管理的）

mandarin.meaning: a powerful official of high rank, especially in the civil service（政界要员；（尤指）内务官员）；a government official of high rank in China in the past（（旧时）中国政府高级官吏）；the standard form of Chinese, which is the official language of China（普通话）；a type of small orange with loose skin that comes off easily（柑橘）

mandate.meaning: the authority to do sth, given to a government or other organization by the people who vote for it in an election（（政府或组织等经选举而获得的）授权）；the period of time for which a government is given power（（政府的）任期）；(formal) an official order given to sb to perform a particular task（委托书；授权令）；the power given to a country to govern another country or region, especially in the past（（尤指旧时授予某国对别国或地区的）委任统治权）

mandatory.meaning: required by law（强制的；法定的；义务的）

mandible.meaning: the jawbone（下颌骨；颌）；the upper or lower part of a bird's beak（鸟喙的上部（或下部））；either of the two parts that are at the front and on either side of an insect's mouth, used especially for biting and crushing food（（昆虫的）上颚）

manganese.meaning: a chemical element. Manganese is a grey-white metal that breaks easily, used in making glass and steel.（锰）

mangrove.meaning: a tropical tree that grows in mud or at the edge of rivers and has roots that are above ground（红树林植物（生长在淤泥或河边的热带树木，有支柱根暴露在空气中））

manhattan.meaning: an alcoholic drink made by mixing whisky or another strong alcoholic drink with vermouth（曼哈顿鸡尾酒（用威士忌或其他烈酒与苦艾酒调制而成））

manhole.meaning: a hole in the street that is covered with a lid, used when sb needs to go down to examine the pipes or sewers below the street（（检查地下管道用的）人孔，检查井）

manhood.meaning: the state or time of being an adult man rather than a boy（成年；成年时期）；the qualities that a man is supposed to have, for example courage, strength and sexual power（男儿气质）；(literary or humorous) a man's penis. People use ‘manhood’ to avoid saying ‘penis’.（（与 penis 同义，即阴茎））；(literary) all the men of a country（一国的男子）

mania.meaning: an extremely strong desire or enthusiasm for sth, often shared by a lot of people at the same time（（通常指许多人共有的）强烈的欲望，狂热，极大的热情）；(psychology 心) a mental illness in which sb has an obsession about sth that makes them extremely anxious, violent or confused（躁狂症）

maniac.meaning: (informal) a person who behaves in an extremely dangerous, wild or stupid way（行为极其危险（或狂暴、愚蠢）的人；疯子；狂人）；a person who has an extremely strong desire or enthusiasm for sth, to an extent that other people think is not normal（狂热分子；过激分子）；(psychology 心) a person suffering from mania（躁狂症患者；疯子）；ma·niac adj. [only before noun] a maniac driver/fan/killer（发了疯的司机；狂热的爱好者；疯狂杀手）

manifest.meaning: to show sth clearly, especially a feeling, an attitude or a quality（表明，清楚显示（尤指情感、态度或品质））；to appear or become noticeable（显现；使人注意到）；(formal) easy to see or understand（明显的；显而易见的）；mani·fest·ly /ˈmænɪfestli; NAmEˈmænɪfestli/ adv. manifestly unfair（明显不公平）

manifestation.meaning: an event, action or thing that is a sign that sth exists or is happening; the act of appearing as a sign that sth exists or is happening（显示；表明；表示）；an appearance of a ghost or spirit（（幽灵的）显现，显灵）

manifesto.meaning: a written statement in which a group of people, especially a political party, explain their beliefs and say what they will do if they win an election（宣言）

manifold.meaning: (formal) many; of many different types（多的；多种多样的；许多种类的）；(technical 术语) a pipe or chamber with several openings for taking gases in and out of a car engine（歧管（汽车引擎用以进气和排气））

manila.meaning: strong brown paper, used especially for making envelopes（马尼拉纸）

manipulate.meaning: (disapproving) to control or influence sb/sth, often in a dishonest way so that they do not realize it（（暗中）控制，操纵，影响）；(formal) to control or use sth in a skilful way（（熟练地）操作，使用）；(technical 术语) to move a person's bones or joints into the correct position（正骨；治疗脱臼）；ma·nipu·la·tion AW manipulation manipulations /məˌnɪpjuˈleɪʃn; NAmEməˌnɪpjuˈleɪʃn/ noun [U, C] Advertising like this is a cynical manipulation of the elderly.（作这样的广告宣传就是耍弄老年人。）

manipulative.meaning: (disapproving) skilful at influencing sb or forcing sb to do what you want, often in an unfair way（善于操纵的；会控制的；会摆布人的）；(formal) connected with the ability to handle objects skilfully（熟练操作的；有操作能力的）

mankind.meaning: all humans, thought about as one large group; the human race（人类）

manly.meaning: having the qualities or physical features that are admired or expected in a man（有男子汉气概的；强壮的）

manner.meaning: (formal) the way that sth is done or happens（方式；方法）；the way that sb behaves towards other people（举止；行为方式）；behaviour that is considered to be polite in a particular society or culture（礼貌；礼仪）；(formal) the habits and customs of a particular group of people（规矩；习俗）

maw.meaning: (literary) something that seems like a big mouth that swallows things up completely（无底洞；吞噬一切的深渊）；(old-fashioned) an animal's stomach or throat（（动物的）胃，咽喉）

maximal.meaning: as great or as large as possible（最大的；最高的）

maximize.meaning: to increase sth as much as possible（使增加到最大限度）；to make the best use of sth（充分利用；最大限度地利用）

maximum.meaning: as large, fast, etc. as is possible, or the most that is possible or allowed（最高的；最多的；最大极限的）；the greatest amount, size, speed, etc. that is possible, recorded or allowed（最大量；最大限度；最高限度）

may.meaning: the fifth month of the year, between April and June（五月）

maybe.meaning: used when you are not certain that sth will happen or that sth is true or is a correct number（（不确定）大概，或许，可能）；used when making a suggestion（（提出建议）或许，也许）；used to agree with sb, and to add more information that should be thought about（（赞同并补充信息）或许，也许，可能）；used when replying to a question or an idea, when you are not sure whether to agree or disagree（（不置可否）也许，或许）

mayor.meaning: (in England, Wales and Northern Ireland) the head of a town, borough or county council, chosen by other members of the council to represent them at official ceremonies, etc.（（英格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰由议员选举产生的）镇长，市长，郡长）；the head of the government of a town or city, etc., elected by the public（（民选的）市长，镇长）；may·oral /ˈmeərəl; NAmEˈmeɪərəl/ adj. [only before noun] mayoral robes/duties（市长的礼袍/职责）

me.meaning: the abbreviation for ‘myalgic encephalomyelitis’ (an illness that makes people feel extremely weak and tired and that can last a long time)（肌痛性脑脊髓炎（全写为 myalgic encephalomyelitis））

meadow.meaning: a field covered in grass, used especially for hay（草地；牧场）

meagre.meaning: small in quantity and poor in quality（少量且劣质的）

meal.meaning: an occasion when people sit down to eat food, especially breakfast, lunch or dinner（早（或午、晚）餐；一顿饭）；the food that is eaten at a meal（一餐所吃的食物）；(often in compounds（常构成复合词）；grain that has been crushed to produce a powder, used as food for animals and for making flour（谷物粗粉（用作饲料或加工面粉））

mean.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to have sth as a meaning（表示 … 的意思）；to intend to say sth on a particular occasion（意思是；本意是）；to have sth as a purpose or intention（打算；意欲；有 … 的目的）

meander.meaning: (of a river, road, etc.（河流、道路等）；to curve a lot rather than being in a straight line（蜿蜒而行；迂回曲折）；to walk slowly and change direction often, especially without a particular aim（漫步；闲逛）；(of a conversation, discussion, etc.（谈话、讨论等）

meaning.meaning: the thing or idea that a sound, word, sign, etc. represents（（声音、文字、信号等传递的）意义，意思）；the things or ideas that sb wishes to communicate to you by what they say or do（（想要表达的）意义，意思）；the real importance of a feeling or experience（真正重要性；价值）；the ideas that a writer, artist, etc. wishes to communicate through a book, painting, etc.（（作家或艺术家要表达的）意义，含义，思想）

meaningful.meaning: serious and important（严肃的；重要的；重大的）；intended to communicate or express sth to sb, without any words being spoken（意味深长的；意在言外的）；having a meaning that is easy to understand（意义明显的；易于理解的）

meaningless.meaning: without any purpose or reason and therefore not worth doing or having（毫无意义的；毫无目的的；无价值的）；not considered important（不重要的；无所谓的）；not having a meaning that is easy to understand（意思不明确的；晦涩的）

means.meaning: an action, an object or a system by which a result is achieved; a way of achieving or doing sth（方式；方法；途径）；the money that a person has（财富；钱财）；used to say that you are very willing for sb to have sth or do sth（可以；当然行；没问题）；(formal) with the help of sth（借助 … 手段；依靠 … 方法）

meantime.meaning: (BrE) for a short period of time but not permanently（眼下；暂时）；in the period of time between two times or two events（其间；同时）

meanwhile.meaning: while sth else is happening（同时；与此同时）；in the period of time between two times or two events（其间）；used to compare two aspects of a situation（（比较两方面）对比之下）；(BrE) for a short period of time but not permanently（一会儿；暂时）

measurable.meaning: that can be measured（可测量的；可度量的）；large enough to be noticed or to have a clear and noticeable effect（显著的；有明显影响的）；meas·ur·ably /ˈmeʒərəbli; NAmEˈmeʒərəbli/ adv. Working conditions have changed measurably in the last ten years.（十年来，工作环境有了明显的改变。）

measure.meaning: to find the size, quantity, etc. of sth in standard units（测量；度量）；to be a particular size, length, amount, etc.（（指尺寸、长短、数量等）量度为）；to judge the importance, value or effect of sth（估量，判定（重要性、价值或影响等））；to compare sb/sth with sb/sth（使相比较）

measurement.meaning: the act or the process of finding the size, quantity or degree of sth（测量；度量）；the size, length or amount of sth（（某物的）尺寸，长度，数量）

meat.meaning: the flesh of an animal or a bird eaten as food; a particular type of this（肉类；（某种）食用肉）；the important or interesting part of sth（重要的部分；有趣的部分）；something that sb enjoys very much（让某人非常开心的事）

meaty.meaning: containing a lot of meat（含肉多的）；smelling, or tasting like meat（气味（或味道）像肉的）；(approving) containing a lot of important or interesting ideas（富含重要（或有趣）的观点的）；(informal) large and fat; with a lot of flesh（肥硕的；多肉的）

mechanic.meaning: a person whose job is repairing machines, especially the engines of vehicles（机械师；机械修理工；技工）；the science of movement and force（力学）；the practical study of machinery（机械学）；the way sth works or is done（方法；手段）

mechanical.meaning: operated by power from an engine（机动的；机械驱动的；机械的）；connected with machines and engines（机器的；机械的；发动机的）；(of people's behaviour and actions（人的行为或行动）；done without thinking, like a machine（机械般的；呆头呆脑的；无思想的）

mechanism.meaning: a set of moving parts in a machine that performs a task（机械装置；机件）；a method or a system for achieving sth（方法；机制）；a system of parts in a living thing that together perform a particular function（（生物体内的）机制，构造）

mechanization.meaning: isa·tion /ˌmekənaɪˈzeɪʃn; NAmEˌmekənəˈzeɪʃn/ noun [U] the increasing mechanization of farm work（农活机械化的程度越来越高）

mechanize.meaning: to change a process, so that the work is done by machines rather than people（机械化；使机械化）；mech·an·iza·tion, -isa·tion /ˌmekənaɪˈzeɪʃn; NAmEˌmekənəˈzeɪʃn/ noun [U] the increasing mechanization of farm work（农活机械化的程度越来越高）

medal.meaning: a flat piece of metal, usually shaped like a coin, that is given to the winner of a competition or to sb who has been brave, for example in war（奖章；勋章）；to win a medal in a competition（（在比赛中）获得奖牌（或奖章））

meddle.meaning: to become involved in sth that does not concern you（管闲事；干涉；干预）；to touch sth in a careless way, especially when it is not yours or when you do not know how to use it correctly（瞎搞，乱弄（尤指不应管或不懂的事物））

media.meaning: the main ways that large numbers of people receive information and entertainment, that is television, radio, newspapers and the Internet（大众传播媒介，大众传播工具（指电视、广播、报纸、互联网））

mediate.meaning: to try to end a disagreement between two or more people or groups by talking to them and trying to find things that everyone can agree on（调停；调解；斡旋）；to succeed in finding a solution to a disagreement between people or groups（找到（解决分歧的）方法；促成 … 的解决）；(formal or technical 术语) to influence sth and/or make it possible for it to happen（影响 … 的发生；使 … 可能发生）

medical.meaning: connected with illness and injury and their treatment（伤病的；疾病的；医疗的）；connected with ways of treating illness that do not involve cutting the body（内科的）；med·ic·al·ly AW /ˈmedɪkli; NAmEˈmedɪkli/ adv. medically fit/unfit（体格健康/不佳）；a thorough examination of your body that a doctor does, for example, before you start a particular job（体格检查）

medicare.meaning: (in the US) the federal insurance system that provides medical care for people over 65（医疗保障制度，老年保健医疗制度（美国政府向 65 岁以上的人提供医疗保险））；(in Australia and Canada) the national medical care system for all people that is paid for by taxes (spelt ‘medicare’ in Canada)（医疗保健制度（澳大利亚和加拿大政府为所有国民而设，资源来自税收；加拿大拼写为 medicare））

medication.meaning: a drug or another form of medicine that you take to prevent or to treat an illness（药；药物）

medicinal.meaning: helpful in the process of healing illness or infection（有疗效的；药用的；药的）

medicine.meaning: the study and treatment of diseases and injuries（医学）；a substance, especially a liquid that you drink or swallow in order to cure an illness（药；（尤指）药水）；the best way of improving a situation, especially of making you feel happier（（改进状况的）最佳方法；（尤指）除去心病的良方）；the same bad treatment that you have given to others（自己曾给别人的苦头）

medieval.meaning: connected with the Middle Ages (about AD 1000 to AD 1450)（中世纪的（约公元 1000 到 1450 年））

mediocre.meaning: not very good; of only average standard（平庸的；普通的；平常的）

meditate.meaning: to think deeply, usually in silence, especially for religious reasons or in order to make your mind calm（冥想；沉思）；(formal) to plan sth in your mind; to consider doing sth（暗自策划；考虑；谋划）

meditation.meaning: the practice of thinking deeply in silence, especially for religious reasons or in order to make your mind calm（冥想；沉思；深思）；(formal) serious thoughts on a particular subject that sb writes down or speaks（沉思录）

mediterranean.meaning: connected with the Mediterranean Sea or the countries and regions that surround it; typical of this area（地中海的）

medium.meaning: in the middle between two sizes, amounts, lengths, temperatures, etc.（中等的；中号的）；a way of communicating information, etc. to people（（传播信息的）媒介，手段，方法）；something that is used for a particular purpose（手段；工具；方法）；the material or the form that an artist, a writer or a musician uses（（文艺创作中使用的）材料，形式）

meek.meaning: quiet, gentle, and always ready to do what other people want without expressing your own opinion（温顺的；谦恭的；驯服的）；people who are meek（温顺的人；谦恭的人）；meek·ly /miːkli; NAmEmiːkli/ adv. He meekly did as he was told.（他温顺地听从吩咐。）

meet.meaning: to be in the same place as sb by chance and talk to them（相遇；相逢；遇见）；to come together formally in order to discuss sth（开会；会晤）；to come together socially after you have arranged it（（与 … ）会面；集合）；to go to a place and wait there for a particular person to arrive（迎接）

meeting.meaning: an occasion when people come together to discuss or decide sth（会议；集会）；the people at a meeting（（统称）与会者）；a situation in which two or more people meet together, because they have arranged it or by chance（会面；集会；集合）；(BrE) a sports event or set of races, especially for horses（运动会；（尤指）赛马）

megalopolis.meaning: a very large city or group of cities where a great number of people live（大都会（区））

megawatt.meaning: a unit for measuring electrical power; one million watts（兆瓦，百万瓦特（电能计量单位））

melancholy.meaning: (formal) a deep feeling of sadness that lasts for a long time and often cannot be explained（忧郁；伤悲）；very sad or making you feel sadness（（令人）悲哀的；（令人）沮丧的）

melange.meaning: a mixture or variety of different things（混合物；大杂烩）

melodic.meaning: connected with the main tune in a piece of music（主旋律的；旋律的）

melodious.meaning: pleasant to listen to, like music（悦耳的；优美动听的；像音乐的）

melodrama.meaning: a story, play or novel that is full of exciting events and in which the characters and emotions seem too exaggerated to be real（情节剧；通俗剧；情节剧式故事（或小说））；events, behaviour, etc. which are exaggerated or extreme（戏剧性的事件（或行为等）；过于夸大的事件（或行为等））

melody.meaning: a tune, especially the main tune in a piece of music written for several instruments or voices（旋律；曲调；（尤指）主旋律）；a piece of music or a song with a clear or simple tune（（旋律简洁的）乐曲，歌曲）；the arrangement of musical notes in a tune（乐曲的音符编排）

melon.meaning: a large fruit with hard green, yellow or orange skin, sweet flesh and juice and a lot of seeds（甜瓜；瓜）

melt.meaning: to become or make sth become liquid as a result of heating（（使）熔化，融化）；to become or to make a feeling, an emotion, etc. become gentler and less strong（（使）软化，变得温柔）；(of food（食物）；to be soft and very good to eat（爽滑可口；柔嫩好吃）

meltdown.meaning: a serious accident in which the central part of a nuclear reactor melts, causing harmful radiation to escape（核反应堆核心熔毁（导致核辐射泄漏））；(economics 经) a situation where sth fails or becomes weaker in a sudden or dramatic way（崩溃；垮台）

member.meaning: a person, an animal or a plant that belongs to a particular group（成员；分子）；a person, a country or an organization that has joined a particular group, club or team（成员；会员）；(old use or literary) a part of the body, especially an arm or a leg（身体部位（尤指胳膊或腿））；a penis. People say ‘member’ to avoid saying ‘penis’.（（委婉说法，与 penis 同义，即阴茎））

membership.meaning: the state of being a member of a group, a club, an organization, etc.（会员资格；成员资格）；the members, or the number of members, of a group, a club, an organization, etc.（（统称）会员，成员；会员人数；成员数）

membrane.meaning: a thin layer of skin or tissue that connects or covers parts inside the body（（身体内的）膜）；a very thin layer found in the structure of cells in plants（（植物的）细胞膜）；a thin layer of material used to prevent air, liquid, etc. from entering a particular part of sth（（可起防水、防风等作用的）膜状物）

memento.meaning: a thing that you keep or give to sb to remind you or them of a person or place（纪念品）

memo.meaning: an official note from one person to another in the same organization（备忘录）

memoir.meaning: an account written by sb, especially sb famous, about their life and experiences（（尤指名人的）回忆录；自传）；(formal) a written account of sb's life, a place, or an event, written by sb who knows it well（传说；地方志；大事记）

memorable.meaning: special, good or unusual and therefore worth remembering or easy to remember（值得纪念的；难忘的）

memorandum.meaning: (law 律) a record of a legal agreement which has not yet been formally prepared and signed（协议备忘录）；a proposal or report on a particular subject for a person, an organization, a committee, etc.（建议书；报告）

memorial.meaning: a statue, stone, etc. that is built in order to remind people of an important past event or of a famous person who has died（纪念碑（或像等））；a thing that will continue to remind people of sb/sth（纪念物；纪念品）；created or done in order to remember sb who has died（纪念的；悼念的）

memorize.meaning: to learn sth carefully so that you can remember it exactly（记忆；记住）

memory.meaning: your ability to remember things（记忆力；记性）；the period of time that sb is able to remember events（记忆所及的时期；回忆所及的范围）；a thought of sth that you remember from the past（回忆；记忆）；(formal) what is remembered about sb after they have died（对死者的记忆）

menace.meaning: a person or thing that causes, or may cause, serious damage, harm or danger（威胁；危险的人（或物））；an atmosphere that makes you feel threatened or frightened（令人恐怖的氛围；危险气氛）；(informal) a person or thing that is annoying or causes trouble（烦人的人（或事物）；引起麻烦的人（或事物））；(BrE) threats that sb will cause harm if they do not get what they are asking for（恐吓；威胁）

mend.meaning: (BrE) to repair sth that has been damaged or broken so that it can be used again（修理；修补）；to repair a hole in a piece of clothing, etc.（缝补；织补）；to find a solution to a problem or disagreement（弥合（分歧）；解决（争端））；(of a person（人）

mennonite.meaning: a member of a Protestant religious group that lives in the US and Canada. Mennonites live a simple life and do not work as public officials or soldiers.（门诺派教徒（美国和加拿大一个新教教派的成员，生活简朴，不当公务员或服兵役））

mental.meaning: connected with or happening in the mind; involving the process of thinking（思想的；精神的；思考的；智力的）；connected with the state of health of the mind or with the treatment of illnesses of the mind（精神病治疗的；精神健康的）；(BrE) (slang) crazy（疯狂；发疯）

mentality.meaning: the particular attitude or way of thinking of a person or group（心态；思想状况；思想方法）

mentally.meaning: connected with or happening in the mind（精神上；智力上；思想上）

mention.meaning: to write or speak about sth/sb, especially without giving much information（提到；写到；说到）；(informal) used as a polite answer when sb has thanked you for sth（（别人道谢时回答）不客气）；used to introduce extra information and emphasize what you are saying（更不用说；且不说）；an act of referring to sb/sth in speech or writing（提及；说起；写上一笔）

menu.meaning: a list of the food that is available at a restaurant or to be served at a meal（菜单）；(computing 计) a list of possible choices that are shown on a computer screen（功能选择单；选单）

mercantile.meaning: connected with trade and commercial affairs（商业的；贸易的）

mercenary.meaning: a soldier who will fight for any country or group that offers payment（雇佣兵）；(disapproving) only interested in making or getting money（只为金钱的）

merchandise.meaning: (formal) goods that are bought or sold; goods that are for sale in a shop/store（商品；货品）；things you can buy that are connected with or that advertise a particular event or organization（相关商品；指定商品）；to sell sth using advertising, etc.（推销；（运用广告等进行）销售）

merchant.meaning: a person who buys and sells goods in large quantities, especially one who imports and exports goods（商人；批发商；（尤指）进出口批发商）；(BrE) (informal, disapproving) a person who likes a particular activity（（某活动的）爱好者；热衷于 … 的人）；connected with the transport of goods by sea（海上货运的）

merciful.meaning: ready to forgive people and show them kindness（宽大的；仁慈的；慈悲的）；(of an event（事件）；seeming to be lucky, especially because it brings an end to sb's problems or suffering（还算幸运的，不幸而可取的（因能解决问题或能除痛苦））

merciless.meaning: showing no kindness or pity（毫不怜悯的；无情的；残忍的）

mercurial.meaning: (literary) often changing or reacting in a way that is unexpected（多变的；变幻莫测的）；(literary) lively and quick（活泼的；机智的）；(technical 术语) containing mercury（含水银的；水银的）

mercury.meaning: the smallest planet in the solar system, nearest to the sun（水星）

mercy.meaning: a kind or forgiving attitude towards sb that you have the power to harm or right to punish（仁慈；宽恕）；(informal) an event or a situation to be grateful for, usually because it stops sth unpleasant（幸运；恩惠）；not able to stop sb/sth harming you because they have power or control over you（任 … 处置；对 … 无能为力；任由 … 摆布）；to leave sb/sth in a situation that may cause them to suffer or to be treated badly（听任某人可能受苦或受到虐待（而无能为力））

mere.meaning: used when you want to emphasize how small, unimportant, etc. sb/sth is（仅仅的；只不过）；used when you are saying that the fact that a particular thing is present in a situation is enough to have an influence on that situation（只凭 … 就足以）；(BrE, literary) (also used in names（也用于名称）；a small lake（小湖；池塘）

merely.meaning: used meaning ‘only’ or ‘simply’ to emphasize a fact or sth that you are saying（仅仅；只不过）

merge.meaning: to combine or make two or more things combine to form a single thing（（使）合并，结合，并入）；if two things merge, or if one thing merges into another, the differences between them gradually disappear so that it is impossible to separate them（相融；融入；渐渐消失在某物中）；(of a person（人）；to behave quietly when you are with a group of people so that they do not notice you（悄悄融入整体；不求闻达）

meringue.meaning: a sweet white mixture made from egg whites and sugar, usually baked until crisp and used to make cakes; a small cake made from this mixture（蛋白酥；蛋糖脆皮）

merit.meaning: (formal) the quality of being good and of deserving praise, reward or admiration（优点；美德；价值）；a good feature that deserves praise, reward or admiration（值得赞扬（或奖励、钦佩）的特点；功绩；长处）；(BrE) a mark/grade in an exam or for a piece of work at school or university which is excellent（（学校或大学考试或作业的）良好）；(BrE) a mark/grade given as a reward for good behaviour at school（（在校操行好而获得的）良好）

mermaid.meaning: (in stories) a creature with a woman's head and body, and a fish's tail instead of legs（（传说中的）美人鱼）

merriment.meaning: happy talk, enjoyment and the sound of people laughing（欢乐；嬉戏；欢笑）

merry.meaning: happy and cheerful（愉快的；高兴的）；used at Christmas to say that you hope that sb has an enjoyable holiday（（圣诞节祝贺语）圣诞快乐）；(informal) (especially BrE) slightly drunk（微醺）；(old-fashioned) to enjoy yourself by singing, laughing, drinking, etc.（行乐；宴乐）

minstrel.meaning: a musician or singer in the Middle Ages（（中世纪的）游方艺人）

minus.meaning: used when you subtract (= take away) one number or thing from another one（减；减去）；used to express temperature below zero degrees（零下）；(informal) without sth that was there before（无，欠缺（曾经有过的东西））；The symbol (−), used in mathematics（减号；负号）

minute.meaning: each of the 60 parts of an hour, that are equal to 60 seconds（分钟；分）；(informal) a very short time（一会儿；一会儿的工夫）；an exact moment in time（时刻）；each of the 60 equal parts of a degree, used in measuring angles（分（角度单位，六十分之一度））

miracle.meaning: an act or event that does not follow the laws of nature and is believed to be caused by God（圣迹；神迹）；(informal) a lucky thing that happens that you did not expect or think was possible（奇迹；不平凡的事）；a very good example or product of sth（极好的例子；精品）；to achieve very good results（创造奇迹；有奇效）

miraculous.meaning: like a miracle; completely unexpected and very lucky（奇迹般的；不可思议的；不平凡的）；mi·racu·lous·ly /mɪˈrækjələsli; NAmEmɪˈrækjələsli/ adv. They miraculously survived the plane crash.（在空难中，他们奇迹般地幸免于难。）

mirage.meaning: an effect caused by hot air in deserts or on roads, that makes you think you can see sth, such as water, which is not there（幻景；海市蜃楼）；a hope or wish that you cannot make happen because it is not realistic（幻想；妄想）

mire.meaning: an area of deep mud（泥潭；泥沼）

mirror.meaning: a piece of special flat glass that reflects images, so that you can see yourself when you look in it（镜子）；something that shows what sth else is like（写照；反映某种情况的事物）；to have features that are similar to sth else and which show what it is like（反映）；to show the image of sb/sth on the surface of water, glass, etc.（映照；反射）

misappropriate.meaning: (formal) to take sb else's money or property for yourself, especially when they have trusted you to take care of it（私吞；挪用）

miscarriage.meaning: the process of giving birth to a baby before it is fully developed and able to survive; an occasion when this happens（流产）

miscarry.meaning: to give birth to a baby before it is fully developed and able to live（流产）；(of a plan（计划）；to fail（失败）

miscellaneous.meaning: consisting of many different kinds of things that are not connected and do not easily form a group（混杂的；各种各样的）

mischief.meaning: bad behaviour (especially of children) that is annoying but does not cause any serious damage or harm（淘气；恶作剧；顽皮）；the wish or tendency to behave or play in a way that causes trouble（恶意；使坏的念头）；(formal) harm or injury that is done to sb or to their reputation（伤害；毁损）；(BrE) (informal) to hurt yourself physically（伤害自己的身体）

misconceive.meaning: (formal) to understand sth in the wrong way（误解；误会）

misconception.meaning: a belief or an idea that is not based on correct information, or that is not understood by people（错误认识；误解）

misdeed.meaning: a bad or evil act（恶行；不义之举）

miser.meaning: a person who loves money and hates spending it（吝啬鬼；守财奴）

miserable.meaning: very unhappy or uncomfortable（痛苦的；非常难受的；可怜的）；making you feel very unhappy or uncomfortable（使难受的；使不舒服的；令人不快的）；(of a person（人）；always unhappy, bad-tempered and unfriendly（乖戾的；脾气坏的）

misery.meaning: great suffering of the mind or body（痛苦；悲惨）；very poor living conditions（穷困；悲惨的生活）；something that causes great suffering of mind or body（不幸的事；痛苦的事）；(BrE) (informal) a person who is always unhappy and complaining（老发牢骚的人；不痛快的人）

misfortune.meaning: bad luck（厄运；不幸）；an unfortunate accident, condition or event（不幸的事故（或情况、事件））

misgiving.meaning: feelings of doubt or anxiety about what might happen, or about whether or not sth is the right thing to do（疑虑；顾虑）

misguided.meaning: wrong because you have understood or judged a situation badly（（因理解或判断失误）搞错的）

mishandle.meaning: to deal badly with a problem or situation（处理不当）；to touch or treat sb/sth in a rough and careless way（粗暴对待；胡乱操作）；mis·hand·ling /; NAmE/ noun [U] the government's mishandling of the economy（政府对经济问题处理不当）

mishap.meaning: a small accident or piece of bad luck that does not have serious results（小事故；晦气）

misinterpret.meaning: to understand sth/sb wrongly（误解；误释）；mis·in·ter·pret·ation AW misinterpretation misinterpretations /ˌmɪsɪntɜːprɪˈteɪʃn; NAmEˌmɪsɪntɜːrprɪˈteɪʃn/ noun [U, C] A number of these statements could be open to misinterpretation (= could be understood wrongly).（这些话有许多可能被误解。）

mislead.meaning: to give sb the wrong idea or impression and make them believe sth that is not true（误导；引入歧途；使误信）

misleading.meaning: giving the wrong idea or impression and making you believe sth that is not true（误导的；引入歧途的）；mis·lead·ing·ly /ˌmɪsˈliːdɪŋli; NAmEˌmɪsˈliːdɪŋli/ adv. These bats are sometimes misleadingly referred to as ‘flying foxes’.（这些蝙蝠有时被误称为“飞狐”。）

mismatch.meaning: a combination of things or people that do not go together well or are not suitable for each other（误配；错配；搭配不当）；mis·match /ˌmɪsˈmætʃ; NAmEˌmɪsˈmætʃ/ verb [often passive] mismatch~ sb/sthThey made a mismatched couple.（他们夫妻俩不般配。）

misrepresent.meaning: to give information about sb/sth that is not true or complete so that other people have the wrong impression about them/it（误传；不实报道；歪曲）；mis·rep·re·sen·ta·tion misrepresentation misrepresentations /ˌmɪsˌreprɪzenˈteɪʃn; NAmEˌmɪsˌreprɪzenˈteɪʃn/ noun [C, U] a deliberate misrepresentation of the facts（故意歪曲事实）

miss.meaning: to fail to hit, catch, reach, etc. sth（未击中；未得到；未达到；错过）；to fail to hear, see or notice sth（未见到；未听到；未觉察）；to fail to understand sth（不理解；不懂）；to fail to be or go somewhere（不在；不去；错过）

missile.meaning: a weapon that is sent through the air and that explodes when it hits the thing that it is aimed at（导弹）；an object that is thrown at sb to hurt them（发射物；投掷物）

missing.meaning: that cannot be found or that is not in its usual place, or at home（找不到的；不在的；丢失的）；that has been removed, lost or destroyed and has not been replaced（被去除的；丢失的；被损毁的；缺少的）；(of a person（人）；not present after an accident, battle, etc. but not known to have been killed（失踪的）

mission.meaning: an important official job that a person or group of people is given to do, especially when they are sent to another country（官方使命；使团的使命）；a group of people doing such a job; the place where they work（使团；代表团；执行任务的地点）；the work of teaching people about Christianity, especially in a foreign country; a group of people doing such work（（尤指在海外的）传教，布道；布道团）；a building or group of buildings used by a Christian mission（布道所；传教区）

missionary.meaning: a person who is sent to a foreign country to teach people about Christianity（传教士）

mist.meaning: a cloud of very small drops of water in the air just above the ground, that make it difficult to see（薄雾；水汽）；a fine spray of liquid, for example, from an aerosol can（液体喷雾）；when sth such as glass mists or is misted, it becomes covered with very small drops of water, so that it is impossible to see through it（使结满雾气（模糊不清））；if your eyes mist or sth mists them, they fill with tears（（眼）含泪水；被泪水模糊）

mistake.meaning: an action or an opinion that is not correct, or that produces a result that you did not want（（言语或行为上的）错误，失误）；a word, figure, etc. that is not said or written down correctly（（用词或数字上的）错误，口误，笔误）；(old-fashioned) (especially BrE) used to show that you are sure about the truth of what you have just said（准确无误；毫无疑问）；by accident; without intending to（错误地；无意中）

mistaken.meaning: wrong in your opinion or judgement（错误；不正确）；based on a wrong opinion or bad judgement（判断错误的；被误解的）；mis·taken·ly /mɪˈsteɪkənli; NAmEmɪˈsteɪkənli/ adv. He mistakenly believed that his family would stand by him.（他误以为他的家人会支持他。）

mister.meaning: the full form, not often used in writing, of the abbreviation Mr（先生（Mr 的全写，书写时不常用））；(informal) used, especially by children, to address a man whose name they do not know（（儿童常用，称呼不知姓名的男子）先生）

mistress.meaning: a man's (usually a married man's) mistress is a woman that he is having a regular sexual relationship with and who is not his wife（情妇）；(BrE) (old-fashioned) a female teacher in a school, especially a private school（（尤指私立学校的）女教师）；(in the past) the female head of a house, especially one who employed servants（（尤指旧时雇用仆人的）女主人，主妇）；the female owner of a dog or other animal（（狗或其他动物的）女主人）

mistrust.meaning: to have no confidence in sb/sth because you think they may be harmful; to not trust sb/sth（猜疑；不信任）；a feeling that you cannot trust sb/sth（猜疑；疑虑；不信任）；mis·trust·ful /ˌmɪsˈtrʌstfl; NAmEˌmɪsˈtrʌstfl/ adj. mistrustful~ (of sb/sth) Some people are very mistrustful of computers.（有些人对电脑很不放心。）

misty.meaning: with a lot of mist（多雾的；薄雾笼罩的）；not clear or bright（模糊的；不明晰的）

misunderstand.meaning: to fail to understand sb/sth correctly（误解；误会）

misunderstanding.meaning: a situation in which a comment, an instruction, etc. is not understood correctly（误解；误会）；a slight disagreement or argument（意见不一；不和；争执）

misuse.meaning: (formal) the act of using sth in a dishonest way or for the wrong purpose（误用；滥用；盗用）；to use sth in the wrong way or for the wrong purpose（误用；滥用）；to treat sb badly and/or unfairly（虐待）

mite.meaning: a very small creature like a spider that lives on plants, animals, carpets, etc.（螨（状似蜘蛛的微小动物，在动植物、地毯等上生活））；a small child or animal, especially one that you feel sorry for（（可怜的）小孩子，小动物）；(old-fashioned) a small amount of sth（少量）

mitigate.meaning: (formal) to make sth less harmful, serious, etc.（减轻；缓和）

mitten.meaning: a type of glove that covers the four fingers together and the thumb separately（连指手套）

mix.meaning: if two or more substances mix or you mix them, they combine, usually in a way that means they cannot easily be separated（（使）混合，掺和，融合）；to prepare sth by combining two or more different substances（调配；配制）；if two or more things, people or activities do not mix, they are likely to cause problems or danger if they are combined（相容；平安相处）；to meet and talk to different people, especially at social events（交往；相处；交际）

mixed.meaning: having both good and bad qualities or feelings（混合的；混杂的）；consisting of different kinds of people, for example, people from different races and cultures（人员混杂的；由不同种族的人组成的）；consisting of different types of the same thing（混合的；掺杂在一起的）；of or for both males and females（男女混杂的；男女混合的）

mixer.meaning: a machine or device used for mixing things（搅拌器；混合器）；a drink such as fruit juice that is not alcoholic and that can be mixed with alcohol（调酒用的饮料）；(technical 术语) a device used for mixing together different sound or picture signals in order to produce a single sound or picture; a person whose job is to operate this device（声音（或图像）混合器；声音（或图像）混合操作员）；a person who finds it easy/difficult to talk to people they do not know, for example at a party（擅长/不擅长交际的人）

mixture.meaning: a combination of different things（混合；结合体）；a substance made by mixing other substances together（混合物）；(technical 术语) a combination of two or more substances that mix together without any chemical reaction taking place（混合物；集合体）；the act of mixing different substances together（混合）

moan.meaning: (of a person（人）；to make a long deep sound, usually expressing unhappiness, suffering or sexual pleasure（呻吟）；(informal) to complain about sth in a way that other people find annoying（抱怨）；(especially of the wind（尤指风）

moat.meaning: a deep wide channel that was dug around a castle, etc. and filled with water to make it more difficult for enemies to attack（护城河）；moat·ed /; NAmE/ adj. [usually before noun] a moated manor house（周围有壕沟的庄园宅第）

mob.meaning: a large crowd of people, especially one that may become violent or cause trouble（人群；（尤指）暴民）；(informal) a group of people who are similar in some way（帮派；团伙）；(informal) the people involved in organized crime; the Mafia（犯罪团伙；黑手党）；(AustralE, NZE) a group of animals（（动物的）群）

mobile.meaning: that is not fixed in one place and can be moved easily and quickly（非固定的；可移动的）；(of a person（人）；able to move or travel around easily（行动方便；腿脚灵便）；(of people（人）

mobility.meaning: the ability to move easily from one place, social class, or job to another（（住处、社会阶层、职业方面的）流动能力）；the ability to move or travel around easily（移动的能力；易于行走的能力）

mobilize.meaning: to work together in order to achieve a particular aim; to organize a group of people to do this（组织；鼓动；动员）；to find and start to use sth that is needed for a particular purpose（调动；调用）；if a country mobilizes its army, or if a country or army mobilizes, it makes itself ready to fight in a war（（战时）动员）

moccasin.meaning: a flat shoe that is made from soft leather and has large stitches around the front, of a type originally worn by Native Americans（莫卡辛软皮鞋（原为美洲土著所穿）；软帮皮鞋）

mock.meaning: to laugh at sb/sth in an unkind way, especially by copying what they say or do（嘲笑；（模仿）嘲弄）；(formal) to show no respect for sth（不尊重；蔑视）；mock·er mocker mockers /mɒkə(r); NAmEmɑːkər/ noun adjective [only before noun] 1. not sincere（虚假的；不诚实的）；that is a copy of sth; not real（模仿的；模拟的）

modal.meaning: a verb such as can, may or will that is used with another verb (not a modal) to express possibility, permission, intention, etc.（情态动词（如 can、may 或 will 等，和实义动词连用表示可能、许可、意图等））；modal adj. ➔ compare auxiliary GRAMMAR POINT 语法说明modal verbs■ The modal verbs are can, could, may, might, must, ought to, shall, should, will and would. Dare, need, have to and used to also share some of the features of modal verbs.（*）

mode.meaning: a particular way of doing sth; a particular type of sth（方式；风格；样式）；the way in which a piece of equipment is set to perform a particular task（（设备的）模式，工作状态）；a particular way of feeling or behaving（（情感或行为的）状态，状况）；a particular style or fashion in clothes, art, etc.（（衣着、艺术等的）形式，风格）

model.meaning: a copy of sth, usually smaller than the original object（（依照实物按比例制成的）模型）；a particular design or type of product（样式；设计；型）；a simple description of a system, used for explaining how sth works or calculating what might happen, etc.（（用于示范运作方法等的）模型）；something such as a system that can be copied by other people（样本；范例）

modem.meaning: a device that connects one computer system to another using a telephone line so that data can be sent（调制解调器）

moderate.meaning: that is neither very good, large, hot, etc. nor very bad, small, cold, etc.（适度的；中等的）；having or showing opinions, especially about politics, that are not extreme（温和的；不激烈的；不偏激的）；staying within limits that are considered to be reasonable by most people（适中的；合理的）；(formal) to become or make sth become less extreme, severe, etc.（缓和；使适中）

moderately.meaning: to an average extent; fairly but not very（一般地；勉强地）；within reasonable limits（适度；适量；适中）

moderation.meaning: the quality of being reasonable and not being extreme（适度；适中；合理）；(in education（教育）；the process of making sure that the same standards are used by different people in marking exams, etc.（评分审核制）

moderator.meaning: a person whose job is to help the two sides in a disagreement to reach an agreement（调解人；调停人）；(especially NAmE) a person whose job is to make sure that a discussion or a debate is fair（会议主持；辩论会主席）；(BrE) a person whose job is to make sure that an exam is marked fairly（评分监督）；(computing 计) a person who is responsible for preventing offensive material from being published on a website（（论坛等的）监管员，版主）

modern.meaning: of the present time or recent times（现代的；当代的；近代的）；(of styles in art, music, fashion, etc.（艺术、音乐、时装等的风格）；new and intended to be different from traditional styles（新式的；有别于传统的）；(usually approving) using the latest technology, designs, materials, etc.（时新的；现代化的；最新的）

modern-day.meaning: of the present time（现代的；当代的）；used to describe a modern form of sb/sth, usually sb/sth bad or unpleasant, that existed in the past（现代版的，翻新的（通常用于消极事物））

modernistic.meaning: (of a painting, building, piece of furniture, etc.（绘画、房屋、家具等）；painted, designed, etc. in a very modern style（现代派的；时髦的）

modernize.meaning: to make a system, methods, etc. more modern and more suitable for use at the present time（使（制度、方法等）现代化）；to start using modern equipment, ideas, etc.（使（设备、概念等）现代化）

modest.meaning: not very large, expensive, important, etc.（些许的；不太大（或贵、重要等）的）；(approving) not talking much about your own abilities or possessions（谦虚的；谦逊的）；(of people, especially women, or their clothes（人，尤指妇女或其衣着）；shy about showing much of the body; not intended to attract attention, especially in a sexual way（庄重的；朴素的；不性感的）

modesty.meaning: the fact of not talking much about your abilities or possessions（谦虚；谦逊）；the action of behaving or dressing so that you do not show your body or attract sexual attention（庄重；朴素；贤淑）；the state of being not very large, expensive, important, etc.（不突出；有限）

modicum.meaning: a fairly small amount, especially of sth good or pleasant（少量，一点点（好事或愉快的事））

modification.meaning: the act or process of changing sth in order to improve it or make it more acceptable; a change that is made（修改；改进；改变）

modifier.meaning: a word or group of words that describes a noun phrase or restricts its meaning in some way（修饰语）

modify.meaning: to change sth slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose（调整；稍作修改；使更适合）；to make sth less extreme（缓和；使温和）；(grammar 语法) a word, such as an adjective or adverb, that modifies another word or group of words describes it or restricts its meaning in some way（修饰）

modulate.meaning: (formal) to change the quality of your voice in order to create a particular effect by making it louder, softer, lower, etc.（调节（嗓音的大小、强弱、高低等））；(music 音) to change from one musical key (= set of notes) to another（变调；转调）；(technical 术语) to affect sth so that it becomes more regular, slower, etc.（调整；调节；控制）；(technical 术语) to change the rate at which a sound wave or radio signal vibrates (= the frequency) so that it is clearer（调制（声波或无线电波频率）；调谐）

module.meaning: a unit that can form part of a course of study, especially at a college or university in Britain（单元（尤指英国大学课程的一部分））；(computing 计) a unit of a computer system or program that has a particular function（模块；功能块；程序块）；one of a set of separate parts or units that can be joined together to make a machine, a piece of furniture, a building, etc.（组件；模块；配件）；a unit of a spacecraft that can function independently of the main part（（航天器上独立的）舱）

moisten.meaning: to become or make sth slightly wet（（使）变得潮湿，变得湿润）

moisture.meaning: very small drops of water that are present in the air, on a surface or in a substance（潮气；水汽；水分）

molasses.meaning: a thick black sweet sticky liquid produced when sugar is refined (= made pure), used in cooking（（制糖时产生的）糖浆，糖蜜）

mold.meaning: a container that you pour a liquid or soft substance into, which then becomes solid in the same shape as the container, for example when it is cooled or cooked（模具；铸模）；a particular style showing the characteristics, attitudes or behaviour that are typical of sb/sth（（独特）类型，个性，风格）；a fine soft green, grey or black substance like fur that grows on old food or on objects that are left in warm wet air（霉；霉菌）；to change what people expect from a situation, especially by acting in a dramatic and original way（改变 … 模式；打破 … 模式而自成一格）

moldy.meaning: covered with or containing mold（发霉的；带霉斑的）；old and not in good condition（破旧的）

mole.meaning: a small animal with dark grey fur, that is almost blind and digs tunnels under the ground to live in（鼹鼠（体小，视力极差，居住在挖掘的地道））；a small dark brown mark on the skin, sometimes slightly higher than the skin around it（色素痣）；a person who works within an organization and secretly passes important information to another organization or country（内奸）；(chemistry 化) a unit for measuring the amount of substance（摩尔（计量物质的数量单位））

molecule.meaning: the smallest unit, consisting of a group of atoms, into which a substance can be divided without a change in its chemical nature（分子）；mo·lecu·lar /məˈlekjələ(r); NAmEməˈlekjələr/ adj. [only before noun] molecular structure/biology（分子结构/生物学）

molest.meaning: to attack sb, especially a child, sexually（对（儿童）性骚扰）；(old-fashioned) to attack sb physically（攻击；伤害）；mo·lest·ation molestation molestations /ˌmɒleˈsteɪʃn; NAmEˌmoʊleˈsteɪʃn/ noun [U] mo·lest·er molester molesters /məˈlestə(r); NAmEməˈlestər/ noun a child molester（对儿童性骚扰者）

molt.meaning: (of a bird or an animal（鸟或动物）；to lose feathers or hair before new feathers or hair grow（换羽；蜕毛）

molten.meaning: (of metal, rock, or glass（金属、岩石或玻璃）；heated to a very high temperature so that it becomes liquid（熔化的；熔融的）
