nitrate.meaning: a compound containing nitrogen and oxygen. There are several different nitrates and they are used especially to make soil better for growing crops.（硝酸盐；硝酸盐类化肥）

nitrogen.meaning: a chemical element. Nitrogen is a gas that is found in large quantities in the earth's atmosphere.（氮；氮气）

no.meaning: used to give a negative reply or statement（（用于否定的回答或陈述）不；没有；不是）；used to express shock or surprise at what sb has said（（对某人所说的话感到惊讶）不，不要）；to refuse to accept that sb does not want sth, will not do sth, etc.（非让人接受（或听从））；not one; not any; not a（没有；无）

nobility.meaning: people of high social position who have titles such as that of duke or duchess（贵族）；(formal) the quality of being noble in character（高贵的品质）

noble.meaning: having fine personal qualities that people admire, such as courage, honesty and care for others（崇高的；品质高尚的）；very impressive in size or quality（宏伟的；壮丽的）；belonging to a family of high social rank (= belonging to the nobility)（贵族的；高贵的）；nobly /ˈnəʊbli; NAmEˈnoʊbli/ adv. She bore the disappointment nobly.（她很失望，但表现得很大度。）

nobody.meaning: a person who has no importance or influence（小人物；无足轻重的人）

nod.meaning: if you nod, nod your head or your head nods, you move your head up and down to show agreement, understanding, etc.（点头）；to move your head down and up once to say hello to sb or to give them a sign to do sth（点头致意；点头示意）；to move your head in the direction of sb/sth to show that you are talking about them/it（（朝 … 方向）点头（表示所谈论的人或物））；to let your head fall forward when you are sleeping in a chair（打盹；打瞌睡）

nodule.meaning: a small round lump or swelling, especially on a plant（（尤指植物上的）节结，小瘤）

noise.meaning: a sound, especially when it is loud, unpleasant or disturbing（声音；响声；噪音；吵闹声）；(technical 术语) extra electrical or electronic signals that are not part of the signal that is being broadcast or transmitted and which may damage it（干扰；电子干扰讯号）；information that is not wanted and that can make it difficult for the important or useful information to be seen clearly（杂讯；垃圾信息）；(informal) to complain loudly（大声诉苦；大声抱怨）

noisy.meaning: making a lot of noise（吵闹的；聒噪的；嘈杂的）；full of noise（充满噪音的；吵吵闹闹的）；nois·ily ★ /ˈnɔɪzɪli; NAmEˈnɔɪzɪli/ adv. The children were playing noisily upstairs.（孩子们在楼上吵闹地玩耍。）

nomad.meaning: a member of a community that moves with its animals from place to place（游牧部落的人）；no·mad·ic /nəʊˈmædɪk; NAmEnoʊˈmædɪk/ adj. nomadic tribes（游牧部落）

nominal.meaning: being sth in name only, and not in reality（名义上的；有名无实的；不真实的）；(of a sum of money（款额）；very small and much less than the normal cost or change（很小的；象征性的）；(grammar 语法) connected with a noun or nouns（名词性的；名词的）

nominate.meaning: to formally suggest that sb should be chosen for an important role, prize, position, etc.（提名；推荐）；to choose sb to do a particular job（任命；指派）；to choose a time, date or title for sth（挑选，指定（时间、日期、名称等））

nomination.meaning: the act of suggesting or choosing sb as a candidate in an election, or for a job or an award; the fact of being suggested for this（提名；推荐；任命；指派）

nominee.meaning: a person who has been formally suggested for a job, a prize, etc.（被提名人；被任命者）；(business 商) a person in whose name money is invested in a company, etc.（（投资等的）名义持有人）

non-.meaning: (in nouns, adjectives and adverbs（构成名词、形容词和副词）；not（无；没有）

nonchalant.meaning: behaving in a calm and relaxed way; giving the impression that you are not feeling any anxiety（若无其事的；冷静的；漠不关心的）；non·cha·lance /ˈnɒnʃələns; NAmEˌnɑːnʃəˈlɑːns/ noun [U] an air of nonchalance（一副满不在乎的样子）；non·cha·lant·ly /ˈnɒnʃələntli; NAmEˌnɑːnʃəˈlɑːntli/ adv. He was leaning nonchalantly against the wall.（他漫不经心地斜倚着墙。）

nonconformist.meaning: (in England and Wales) a member of a Protestant Church that does not follow the beliefs and practices of the Church of England（（英格兰和威尔士）不从国教者，不遵奉圣公会的新教教徒）；a person who does not follow normal ways of thinking or behaving（不遵循传统规范的人；不认同主流思想的人）

nonconformity.meaning: the fact of not following normal ways of thinking and behaving（不遵从传统规范；不认同主流思想）；the beliefs and practices of Nonconformist Churches（非国教教义；不信奉英国国教）

none.meaning: not one of a group of people or things; not any（没有一个；毫无）；(literary) only（仅仅；只有）；used to emphasize who or what sb/sth is, when this is surprising（（强调出人意料的人或事）竟然）；to refuse to accept sth（拒绝接受；什么也不要）

nonsense.meaning: ideas, statements or beliefs that you think are ridiculous or not true（谬论；胡扯；胡言乱语）；silly or unacceptable behaviour（愚蠢的行为；冒失；不可接受的行为）；spoken or written words that have no meaning or make no sense（毫无意义的话；没有意义的文章）；to reduce the value of sth by a lot; to make sth seem ridiculous（使 … 的价值大打折扣；使 … 显得荒诞）

noodle.meaning: a long thin strip of pasta, used especially in Chinese and Italian cooking（面条）

noon.meaning: o'clock in the middle of the day（正午；中午）

nor.meaning: and not（也不）；used before a positive verb to agree with sth negative that has just been said（（用于肯定动词前，表示同意刚提及的否定命题）也不）

norm.meaning: a situation or a pattern of behaviour that is usual or expected（常态；正常行为）；standards of behaviour that are typical of or accepted within a particular group or society（规范；行为标准）；a required or agreed standard, amount, etc.（标准；定额；定量）；to adjust sth so that it is of the required standard; to establish a required or agreed standard for sth（规范；规定）

normal.meaning: typical, usual or ordinary; what you would expect（典型的；正常的；一般的）；not suffering from any mental disorder（精神正常的；意识健全的）；the usual or average state, level or standard（常态；通常标准；一般水平）

normalization.meaning: isa·tion AW normalization normalizations /ˌnɔːməlaɪˈzeɪʃn; NAmEˌnɔːrmələˈzeɪʃn/ noun [U] the normalization of relations（关系的正常化）

normalize.meaning: (formal) to fit or make sth fit a normal pattern or condition（（使）正常化，标准化，常规化）；nor·mal·iza·tion, -isa·tion AW normalization normalizations /ˌnɔːməlaɪˈzeɪʃn; NAmEˌnɔːrmələˈzeɪʃn/ noun [U] the normalization of relations（关系的正常化）

normally.meaning: usually; in normal circumstances（通常；正常情况下）；in the usual or ordinary way（正常地；平常地）

norman.meaning: used to describe the style of architecture in Britain in the 11th and 12th centuries that developed from the Romanesque style（诺曼式的；诺曼式建筑风格的）；connected with the Normans (= the people from northern Europe who defeated the English in 1066 and then ruled the country)（诺曼人的）

north.meaning: the direction that is on your left when you watch the sun rise; one of the four main points of the compass（北；北方）；the northern part of a country, a region or the world（北部；北部地区）；the NE states of the US which fought against the South in the American Civil War（（美国南北战争时与南方作战的）北部各州，北方）；the richer and more developed countries of the world, especially in Europe and N America（北方发达国家（尤指欧洲和北美各国））

northern.meaning: located in the north or facing north; connected with or typical of the north part of the world or a region（北方的；向北的；北部的）

northerner.meaning: a person who comes from or lives in the northern part of a country（北方人）

nose.meaning: the part of the face that sticks out above the mouth, used for breathing and smelling things（鼻；鼻子）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；having the type of nose mentioned（有 … 鼻子的）；the front part of a plane, spacecraft, etc.（（飞机、太空船等的）头部，头锥）

nostalgia.meaning: a feeling of sadness mixed with pleasure and affection when you think of happy times in the past（怀旧；念旧）；nos·tal·gic /nɒˈstældʒɪk; NAmEnəˈstældʒɪk; nɑːˈstældʒɪk/ adj. nostalgic memories（引起怀旧之情的回忆）；nos·tal·gic·al·ly /nɒˈstældʒɪkli; NAmEnəˈstældʒɪkli; nɑːˈstældʒɪkli/ adv. to look back nostalgically to your childhood（怀缅童年时光）

nostril.meaning: either of the two openings at the end of the nose that you breathe through（鼻孔）

nosy.meaning: too interested in things that do not concern you, especially other people's affairs（好管闲事的；爱打听的）

not.meaning: used to form the negative of the verbs be, do and have and modal verbs like can or must and often reduced to n't（（构成动词 be、do 和 have 及情态动词 can 或 must 等的否定形式，常缩略为 n't）不，没有）；used to give the following word or phrase a negative meaning, or to reply in the negative（（否定后面的词或短语，或作否定的回答）不，没有）；used after hope, expect, believe, etc. to give a negative reply（（用于 hope、expect、believe 等动词后，作为否定的回答）不，没有）；used to show a negative possibility（（表示否定的可能性）否，不）

notable.meaning: (rather formal) deserving to be noticed or to receive attention; important（值得注意的；显著的；重要的）；(formal) a famous or important person（名人；重要人物）

notably.meaning: used for giving a good or the most important example of sth（尤其；特别）；to a great degree（极大程度上；非常）

notary.meaning: a person, especially a lawyer, with official authority to be a witness when sb signs a document and to make this document valid in law（公证人）

notation.meaning: a system of signs or symbols used to represent information, especially in mathematics, science and music（（数学、科学和音乐中的）符号，记号，谱号）

notch.meaning: a level on a scale, often marking quality or achievement（等级；档次；位阶）；a V-shape or a circle cut in an edge or a surface, sometimes used to keep a record of sth（（表面或边缘的）V 形刻痕，圆形切口）；(informal) to achieve sth such as a win or a high score（赢取；获得）；to make a small V-shaped cut in an edge or a surface（（在表面或边缘）刻 V 形痕，刻下切口）

note.meaning: a short piece of writing to help you remember sth（笔记；记录）；a short informal letter（短笺；便条）；a short comment on a word or passage in a book（注释；按语；批注）；information that you write down when sb is speaking, or when you are reading a book, etc.（（听讲或读书等时的）记录，笔记）

notebook.meaning: a small book of plain paper for writing notes in（笔记本）；a small book for students to write their work in（练习本）；a small computer that can work with a battery and be easily carried（笔记本电脑；便携式电脑）

noted.meaning: well known because of a special skill or feature（（以 … ）见称，闻名，著名）

nothing.meaning: not anything; no single thing（没有什么；没有一件东西）；something that is not at all important or interesting（无关紧要的东西；毫无趣味的事）；to be a person for whom sb has no feelings（对（某人）来说是无所谓的人）；to have no connection with sb/sth（与 … 毫不相干；与 … 无关）

notice.meaning: the fact of sb paying attention to sb/sth or knowing about sth（注意；理会；察觉）；a sheet of paper giving written or printed information, usually put in a public place（通告；布告；通知）；a board or sign giving information, an instruction or a warning（公告牌；警示牌）；a small advertisement or announcement in a newspaper or magazine（启事；声明）

noticeable.meaning: easy to see or notice; clear or definite（显著的；显而易见的）；no·tice·ably /ˈnəʊtɪsəbli; NAmEˈnoʊtɪsəbli/ adv. Her hand was shaking noticeably.（很明显她的手在颤抖。）

notification.meaning: the act of giving or receiving official information about sth（通知；通告；告示）

notify.meaning: to formally or officially tell sb about sth（（正式）通报，通知）

notion.meaning: an idea, a belief or an understanding of sth（观念；信念；理解）

notional.meaning: based on a guess, estimate or theory; not existing in reality（猜测的；估计的；理论上的；想像的）

notoriety.meaning: fame for being bad in some way（恶名；坏名声）

notorious.meaning: well known for being bad（声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的）；no·tori·ous·ly /nəʊˈtɔːriəsli; NAmEnoʊˈtɔːriəsli/ adv. Mountain weather is notoriously difficult to predict.（山地气候难以预料是人所共知的。）

notwithstanding.meaning: (formal) (also used following the noun it refers to（亦用于其所指名词之后）；without being affected by sth; despite sth（虽然；尽管）；(formal) despite this（尽管如此）

nought.meaning: the figure 0（（数码）零）；(literary) used in particular phrases to mean ‘nothing’（（用于某些短语）无，零）

noun.meaning: a word that refers to a person (such as Ann or doctor), a place (such as Paris or city) or a thing, a quality or an activity (such as plant, sorrow or tennis)（名词）

nourish.meaning: to keep a person, an animal or a plant alive and healthy with food, etc.（抚养；滋养；养育）；(formal) to allow a feeling, an idea, etc. to develop or grow stronger（培养，助长（情绪、观点等））；nour·ish·ing /ˈnʌrɪʃɪŋ; NAmEˈnɜːrɪʃɪŋ/ adj. nourishing food（滋补食品）

nourishment.meaning: food that is needed to stay alive, grow and stay healthy（营养；营养品）

novel.meaning: a story long enough to fill a complete book, in which the characters and events are usually imaginary（（长篇）小说）；(often approving) different from anything known before; new, interesting and often seeming slightly strange（新颖的；与众不同的；珍奇的）

novelette.meaning: a short novel, especially a romantic novel that is considered to be badly written（中篇小说（尤指被认为很蹩脚的言情小说））

novelist.meaning: a person who writes novels（小说家）

novelty.meaning: the quality of being new, different and interesting（新奇；新颖；新鲜）；a thing, person or situation that is interesting because it is new, unusual or has not been known before（新奇的事物（或人、环境））；a small cheap object sold as a toy or a decorative object（廉价小饰物；小玩意儿）；different and unusual; intended to be amusing and to catch people's attention（新奇的；风格独特的）

november.meaning: the 11th month of the year, between October and December（十一月）

novice.meaning: a person who is new and has little experience in a skill, job or situation（新手；初学者）；a person who has joined a religious group and is preparing to become a monk or a nun（初学修士（或修女）；（修会等的）初学生）；a horse that has not yet won an important race（尚未赢过大赛的赛马）

now.meaning: (at) the present time（现在；目前；此刻）；at or from this moment, but not before（现在；从现在开始）；(informal) used to show that you are annoyed about sth（（表示厌烦））；used to get sb's attention before changing the subject or asking them to do sth（（改变话题或要对方做某事前，引起对方注意）喂，哎，嗨）

nowadays.meaning: at the present time, in contrast with the past（现今；现在；目前）

nowhere.meaning: not in or to any place（无处；哪里都不）；to make no progress or have no success; to not enable sb to make progress or have success（（让某人）毫无进展）；impossible for anyone to find or see（不可能找到（或看见））

noxious.meaning: poisonous or harmful（有毒的；有害的）

nozzle.meaning: a narrow piece that is attached to the end of a pipe or tube to direct the stream of liquid, air or gas passing through（管口；喷嘴）

nuance.meaning: a very slight difference in meaning, sound, colour or sb's feelings that is not usually very obvious（（意义、声音、颜色、感情等方面的）细微差别）

nuclear.meaning: using, producing or resulting from nuclear energy（原子能的；核能的）；connected with weapons that use nuclear energy（核武器的）；(physics 物) of the nucleus (= central part) of an atom（核子的；原子核的）

nucleus.meaning: (physics 物) the part of an atom that contains most of its mass and that carries a positive electric charge（核；原子核）；(biology 生) the central part of some cells, containing the genetic material（细胞核）；the central part of sth around which other parts are located or collected（核心；中心）

nude.meaning: (especially of a human figure in art（尤指艺术人像）；not wearing any clothes（裸体的）；involving people who are naked（裸体者的）；(of tights/pantyhose, etc.（裤袜等）

nudity.meaning: the state of being naked（裸体；赤裸）

nuisance.meaning: a thing, person or situation that is annoying or causes trouble or problems（麻烦事；讨厌的人（或东西））；(law 律) behaviour by sb that annoys other people and that a court can order the person to stop（非法妨害；滋扰行为）

null.meaning: having the value zero（零值的；等于零的）；(of an election, agreement, etc.（选举、协议等）；having no legal force; not valid（无法律效力的；无效的）

nullify.meaning: to make sth such as an agreement or order lose its legal force（使失去法律效力；废止）；to make sth lose its effect or power（使无效；抵消）

numb.meaning: if a part of your body is numb, you cannot feel anything in it, for example because of cold（麻木的；失去知觉的）；unable to feel, think or react in the normal way（麻木的；迟钝的；呆滞的）；numb·ly /nʌmli; NAmEnʌmli/ adv. Her life would never be the same again, she realized numbly.（她模模糊糊地意识到她的生活不会和过去一样了。）；numb·ness /nʌmnəs; NAmEnʌmnəs/ noun [U] pain and numbness in my fingers（我的手指又疼又麻）

number.meaning: a word or symbol that represents an amount or a quantity（数字；数；数量）；used before a figure to show the position of sth in a series（编号；序数）；(often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a number used to identify sth or communicate by telephone, fax, etc.（（电话、传真等的）号码）

numeral.meaning: a sign or symbol that represents a number（数字；数码）

numerical.meaning: relating to numbers; expressed in numbers（数字的；用数字表示的）；nu·mer·ic·al·ly /njuːˈmerɪkli; NAmEnuːˈmerɪkli/ adv. to express the results numerically（按数字顺序排列结果）

numerous.meaning: existing in large numbers SYN many（众多的；许多的）

nun.meaning: a member of a religious community of women who promise to serve God all their lives and often live together in a convent（修女；尼姑）

nurse.meaning: a person whose job is to take care of sick or injured people, usually in a hospital（护士）；(old-fashioned) (in the past) a woman or girl whose job was to take care of babies or small children in their own homes（（旧时雇主家中的）女保育员，保母，女仆）；to care for sb who is ill/sick or injured（看护，照料（病人或伤者））；to take care of an injury or illness（调治，调养（伤病））

nursery.meaning: (NAmE or old-fashioned) a room in a house where a baby sleeps（婴儿室）；(old-fashioned) a room in a house where young children can play（（供游戏的）儿童室）；a place where young plants and trees are grown for sale or for planting somewhere else（苗圃）；(BrE) connected with the education of children from 2 to 5 years old（幼儿教育的）

nursing.meaning: the job or skill of caring for people who are sick or injured（护理；看护）

nurture.meaning: to care for and protect sb/sth while they are growing and developing（养育；养护；培养）；to help sb/sth to develop and be successful（扶持；帮助；支持）；to have a feeling, an idea, a plan, etc. for a long time and encourage it to develop（滋长；助长）；(formal) care, encouragement and support given to sb/sth while they are growing（养育；培养）

nut.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a small hard fruit with a very hard shell that grows on some trees（坚果）；a small piece of metal with a hole through the centre that is screwed onto a bolt to hold pieces of wood, machinery, etc. together（螺母；螺帽）；(BrE) (slang) a person's head or brain（人的头（或大脑））

nutrient.meaning: a substance that is needed to keep a living thing alive and to help it to grow（营养素；营养物）

nutrition.meaning: the process by which living things receive the food necessary for them to grow and be healthy（营养；滋养；营养的补给）；nu·tri·tion·al /njuˈtrɪʃənl; NAmEnuˈtrɪʃənl/ (also less frequent nu·tri·tive) adj. the nutritional value of milk（牛奶的营养价值）；nu·tri·tion·al·ly /njuˈtrɪʃənəli; NAmEnuˈtrɪʃənəli/ adv. a nutritionally balanced menu（营养均衡的菜谱）

nutritionist.meaning: a person who is an expert on the relationship between food and health（营养学家）

nutritious.meaning: (of food（食物）；very good for you; containing many of the substances which help the body to grow（有营养的；营养丰富的）

nylon.meaning: a very strong artificial material, used for making clothes, rope, brushes, etc.（尼龙）；(old-fashioned) women's stockings or tights/pantyhose made of nylon（（女用）尼龙长袜，尼龙连袜裤）

oak.meaning: a large tree that produces small nuts called acorns. Oaks are common in northern countries and can live to be hundreds of years old.（栎树；橡树）；the hard wood of the oak tree（栎木；橡木）；(saying) something large and successful often begins in a very small way（参天橡树长自小小橡实；合抱之树，生于毫末）

oar.meaning: a long pole with a flat blade at one end that is used for rowing a boat（船桨；桨）；(BrE) (informal) to give your opinion, advice, etc. without being asked and when it is probably not wanted（多管闲事；横插一杠子）

oasis.meaning: an area in the desert where there is water and where plants grow（（沙漠中的）绿洲）；a pleasant place or period of time in the middle of sth unpleasant or difficult（（困苦中）令人快慰的地方（或时刻）；乐土；乐事）

oat.meaning: made from or containing oats（燕麦制的；含燕麦的）

ornament.meaning: (especially BrE) an object that is used as decoration in a room, garden/yard, etc. rather than for a particular purpose（装饰品）；(formal) an object that is worn as jewellery（首饰；饰物）；(formal) the use of objects, designs, etc. as decoration（装饰；摆设；点缀）；(NAmE) a person or thing whose good qualities improve sth（为 … 增添光彩的人（或事物））

ornamental.meaning: used as decoration rather than for a practical purpose（装饰性的；点缀的）

ornamentation.meaning: the use of objects, designs, etc. to decorate sth（装饰；点缀）

ornate.meaning: covered with a lot of decoration, especially when this involves very small or complicated designs（华美的；富丽的；豪华的）；or·nate·ly /ɔːˈneɪtli; NAmEɔːrˈneɪtli/ adv. ornately carved chairs（精雕细刻的椅子）

orogeny.meaning: a process in which the outer layer of the earth is folded to form mountains（造山运动（地层褶皱形成山脉的过程））

orphan.meaning: a child whose parents are dead（孤儿）；to make a child an orphan（使成为孤儿）

orphanage.meaning: a home for children whose parents are dead（孤儿院）

orthodox.meaning: (especially of beliefs or behaviour（尤指信仰或行为）；generally accepted or approved of; following generally accepted beliefs（普遍接受的；正统的；规范的）；following closely the traditional beliefs and practices of a religion（正统信仰的；正宗教义的）；belonging to or connected with the Orthodox Church（正教的；东正教派的）

oscillate.meaning: (formal) to keep changing from one extreme of feeling or behaviour to another, and back again（（情感或行为）摇摆，波动，变化）；(physics 物) to keep moving from one position to another and back again（摆动；振动）；(of an electric current, radio waves, etc.（电流、无线电波等）；to change in strength or direction at regular intervals（波动；振荡）

oscillation.meaning: a regular movement between one position and another or between one amount and another（摆动；摇摆；振动）；a single movement from one position to another of sth that is oscillating（一次波动；浮动；振幅）；a repeated change between different feelings, types of behaviour or ideas（（情感、行为、思想的）摇摆不定，变化无常，犹豫不定）

osprey.meaning: a large bird of prey (= a bird that kills other creatures for food) that eats fish（鹗；鱼鹰）

ostensible.meaning: seeming or stated to be real or true, when this is perhaps not the case（表面的；宣称的；假托的）；os·ten·sibly /ɒˈstensəbli; NAmEɑːˈstensəbli/ adv. Troops were sent in, ostensibly to protect the civilian population.（谎称为保护平民而派驻了军队。）

ostentation.meaning: an exaggerated display of wealth, knowledge or skill that is made in order to impress people（（对财富、知识、技能的）炫耀，卖弄，夸示）

ostracize.meaning: (formal) to refuse to let sb be a member of a social group; to refuse to meet or talk to sb（排挤；排斥）

ostrich.meaning: a very large African bird with a long neck and long legs, that cannot fly but can run very fast（鸵鸟）；(informal) a person who prefers to ignore problems rather than try and deal with them（逃避现实的人；不愿正视现实者）

other.meaning: used to refer to people or things that are additional or different to people or things that have been mentioned or are known about（另外；其他）；used to refer to the second of two people or things（（指两个人或事物中的第二个）那个，另一个）；used to refer to the remaining people or things in a group（（指一组中其余的人或事物）其余的，另外的）；used to refer to a place, direction, etc. that is the opposite to where you are, are going, etc.（（指与说话人所在位置等相反的方向或地点）另一边，对面，相反的方向）

otherwise.meaning: used to state what the result would be if sth did not happen or if the situation were different（否则；不然）；apart from that（除此以外）；in a different way to the way mentioned; differently（以其他方式；另；亦）；used to refer to sth that is different from or the opposite of what has just been mentioned（或其他情况；或相反）

otter.meaning: a small animal that has four webbed feet (= with skin between the toes), a tail and thick brown fur. Otters live in rivers and eat fish.（水獭）

ounce.meaning: a unit for measuring weight, 1/16 of a pound, equal to 28.35 grams（盎司（重量单位，1/16 磅，等于 28.35 克））；(informal) (used especially with negatives（尤与否定词连用）；a very small quantity of sth（少许；少量；一点点；丝毫）

our.meaning: belonging to us; connected with us（我们的）；used to refer to or address God or a holy person（（用于称上帝或圣人））

ours.meaning: the one or ones that belong to us（我们的）；(BrE) (informal) our home（我们的住处）

ourselves.meaning: the reflexive form of we; used when you and another person or other people together cause and are affected by an action（（we 的反身形式）我们自己）；used to emphasize we or us; sometimes used instead of these words（（用于强调或代替 we 或 us）我们自己，亲自）；alone; without anyone else（（我们）独自，单独）；without help（（我们）独立地）

oust.meaning: to force sb out of a job or position of power, especially in order to take their place（剥夺；罢免；革职）

out.meaning: away from the inside of a place or thing（（从 … 里）出来）；(of people（人）；away from or not at home or their place of work（不在家；不在工作地点；外出）；away from the edge of a place（出去；离开（某地）边缘）

outbreak.meaning: the sudden start of sth unpleasant, especially violence or a disease（（暴力、疾病等坏事的）爆发，突然发生）

outbuilding.meaning: a building such as a shed or stable that is built near to, but separate from, a main building（附属建筑物）

outcast.meaning: a person who is not accepted by other people and who sometimes has to leave their home and friends（被抛弃者；被排斥者）

outcome.meaning: the result or effect of an action or event（结果；效果）

outcrop.meaning: a large mass of rock that stands above the surface of the ground（（岩石）露出地面的部分；露头）

outcry.meaning: a reaction of anger or strong protest shown by people in public（呐喊；怒吼；强烈的抗议）

outdated.meaning: no longer useful because of being old-fashioned（过时的；陈旧的）

outdo.meaning: to do more or better than sb else（胜过；优于）

outdoor.meaning: used, happening or located outside rather than in a building（户外的；室外的）

outdoors.meaning: outside, rather than in a building（在户外；在野外）；the countryside, away from buildings and busy places（野外；旷野；郊外）

outer.meaning: on the outside of sth（外表的；外边的）；furthest from the inside or centre of sth（远离中心的；外围的）

outermost.meaning: furthest from the inside or centre（最外边的；最远的）

outfit.meaning: a set of clothes that you wear together, especially for a particular occasion or purpose（全套服装，装束（尤指为某场合或目的））；(informal) a group of people working together as an organization, business, team, etc.（团队；小组；分队）；a set of equipment that you need for a particular purpose（全套装备；成套工具）；(especially NAmE) to provide sb/sth with equipment or clothes for a special purpose（装备；配置设备；供给服装）

outflow.meaning: the movement of a large amount of money, liquid, people, etc. out of a place（外流；流出量）

outgoing.meaning: liking to meet other people, enjoying their company and being friendly towards them（爱交际的；友好的；外向的）；leaving the position of responsibility mentioned（将卸任的；离职的）；going away from a particular place rather than arriving in it（向外的；离开的）

outing.meaning: a trip that you go on for pleasure or education, usually with a group of people and lasting no more than one day（（集体）出外游玩（或学习等）；远足）；(informal) an occasion when sb takes part in a competition（参赛；比赛）；the practice of naming people as homosexuals in public, when they do not want anyone to know（（违背同性恋者本人意愿）对（其）身分的公开挑明）

outlandish.meaning: strange or extremely unusual（古怪的；极不寻常的；奇特的）

outlaw.meaning: to make sth illegal（宣布 … 不合法；使 … 成为非法）；(in the past) to make sb an outlaw（（旧时）剥夺（某人的）法律权益）；(used especially about people in the past) a person who has done sth illegal and is hiding to avoid being caught; a person who is not protected by the law（（尤指过去的人）亡命徒，逃犯，草莽英雄，被剥夺法律权益者）

outlay.meaning: the money that you have to spend in order to start a new project（（启动新项目的）开支，费用）

outlet.meaning: a way of expressing or making good use of strong feelings, ideas or energy（（感情、思想、精力发泄的）出路；表现机会）；(business 商) a shop/store or an organization that sells goods made by a particular company or of a particular type（专营店；经销店）；(especially NAmE) a shop/store that sells goods of a particular make at reduced prices（（某品牌的）折扣店）；a pipe or hole through which liquid or gas can flow out（出口；排放管）

outline.meaning: to give a description of the main facts or points involved in sth（概述；略述）；to show or mark the outer edge of sth（显示，勾勒，描画（事物的轮廓））；a description of the main facts or points involved in sth（概述；梗概）；the line that goes around the edge of sth, showing its main shape but not the details（轮廓线；略图）

outlook.meaning: the attitude to life and the world of a particular person, group or culture（观点；见解；世界观；人生观）；the probable future for sb/sth; what is likely to happen（前景；可能性）；(formal) a view from a particular place（景色；景致；景观）

outlying.meaning: far away from the cities of a country or from the main part of a place（边远的；偏远的；远离市镇的）

outnumber.meaning: to be greater in number than sb/sth（（在数量上）压倒，比 … 多）

outpouring.meaning: a strong and sudden expression of feeling（（感情的）迸发，倾泻）；a large amount of sth produced in a short time（涌现；喷涌）

output.meaning: the amount of sth that a person, a machine or an organization produces（（人、机器、机构的）产量，输出量）；(computing 计) the information, results, etc. produced by a computer（输出）；the power, energy, etc. produced by a piece of equipment（输出功率；输出量）；a place where energy, power, information, etc. leaves a system（输出端）

outrage.meaning: a strong feeling of shock and anger（愤怒；义愤；愤慨）；an act or event that is violent, cruel or very wrong and that shocks people or makes them very angry（暴行；骇人听闻的事）；to make sb very shocked and angry（使震怒；激怒）

outrageous.meaning: very shocking and unacceptable（骇人的；无法容忍的）；very unusual and slightly shocking（反常的；令人惊讶的）；out·ra·geous·ly /aʊtˈreɪdʒəsli; NAmEaʊtˈreɪdʒəsli/ adv. an outrageously expensive meal（贵得吓人的一顿饭）

outrigger.meaning: a wooden structure that is fixed to the side of a boat or ship in order to keep it steady in the water; a boat fitted with such a structure（舷外托架；有舷外托架的小船）

outright.meaning: complete and total（完全的；彻底的；绝对的）；open and direct（公开的；直率的；直截了当的）；in a direct way and without trying to hide anything（公开地；直率地；毫无保留地）；clearly and completely（完全彻底；干净利落）

outset.meaning: at/from the beginning of sth（从开始）

outside.meaning: the outer side or surface of sth（外部；外表）；the area that is near or around a building, etc.（（建筑物等的）周围，外围）；the part of a road nearest to the middle（（靠近路中央的）外侧，外手）；the part of a curving road or track furthest from the inner or shorter side of the curve（（弯曲路面或轨道的）外道，外缘）

outsider.meaning: a person who is not accepted as a member of a society, group, etc.（外人；局外人）；a person who is not part of a particular organization or profession（（组织、行业）外部的人；外来者）；a person or an animal taking part in a race or competition that is not expected to win（（比赛中）不被看好的人（或动物））

outskirts.meaning: the parts of a town or city that are furthest from the centre（（市镇的）边缘地带；市郊）

outspoken.meaning: saying exactly what you think, even if this shocks or offends people（直率的，直言不讳的（不怕得罪人））

outstanding.meaning: extremely good; excellent（优秀的；杰出的；出色的）；very obvious or important（突出的；明显的；重要的）；(of payment, work, problems, etc.（款项、工作、困难等）；not yet paid, done, solved, etc.（未支付的；未完成的；未解决的）

outstrip.meaning: to become larger, more important, etc. than sb/sth（比 … 大（或重要等）；超过；胜过）；to be faster, better or more successful than sb you are competing against（超过，超越（竞争对手））；to run faster than sb in a race so that you pass them（比 … 跑得快；超越）

outward.meaning: connected with the way people or things seem to be rather than with what is actually true（表面的；外表的）；going away from a particular place, especially one that you are going to return to（外出的；向外的）；away from the centre or a particular point（朝外面的；向外的）

outwards.meaning: towards the outside; away from the centre or from a particular point（向外；朝外）

outweigh.meaning: to be greater or more important than sth（重于；大于；超过）

outwit.meaning: to defeat sb/sth or gain an advantage over them by doing sth clever（（智力上）超过，胜过）

outwork.meaning: (BrE) work that is done by people at home（外包活；家庭承揽的活）

oval.meaning: shaped like an egg（椭圆形的；卵形的）；an oval shape（椭圆形；卵形）；(AustralE) a ground for Australian Rules football（澳大利亚式橄榄球球场）

ovation.meaning: enthusiastic clapping by an audience as a sign of their approval（热烈鼓掌；热烈欢迎）

oven.meaning: the part of a cooker/stove shaped like a box with a door on the front, in which food is cooked or heated（烤箱；烤炉）

over.meaning: downwards and away from a vertical position（从直立位置向下；落下；倒下）；from one side to another side（从一侧到另一侧；翻转）；across a street, an open space, etc.（穿过（街道、开阔的空间等））；so as to cover sb/sth completely（完全覆盖（某人或某物））

overall.meaning: including all the things or people that are involved in a particular situation; general（全面的；综合的；总体的）；including everything or everyone; in total（全部；总计）；generally; when you consider everything（一般来说；大致上；总体上）；a loose coat worn over other clothes to protect them from dirt, etc.（外套；罩衣）

overbalance.meaning: (especially BrE) to lose your balance and fall; to make sb/sth lose their balance and fall（（使）失去平衡，摔倒）

overburden.meaning: to give sb/sth more work, worry, etc. than they can deal with（使负担过重）

overcast.meaning: covered with clouds; dull（阴天的；多云的；阴暗的）

overcharge.meaning: to make sb pay too much for sth（多收（某人的）钱）

overcoat.meaning: a long warm coat worn in cold weather（长大衣）

overcome.meaning: to succeed in dealing with or controlling a problem that has been preventing you from achieving sth（克服；解决）；to defeat sb（战胜）；to be extremely strongly affected by sth（受到 … 的极大影响）

overconfident.meaning: too confident（过分自信的；自负的）

overdose.meaning: too much of a drug taken at one time（（一次用药）过量）；to take too much of a drug at one time, so that it is dangerous（一次用药过量）

overdue.meaning: not paid, done, returned, etc. by the required or expected time（（到期）未付的，未做的，未还的；过期的）；that should have happened or been done before now（早该发生的；早应完成的）

overestimate.meaning: to estimate sth to be larger, better, more important, etc. than it really is（高估）；over·esti·mation overestimation overestimations noun [U, C] noun /ˌəʊvərˈestɪmət; NAmEˌoʊvərˈestɪmət/ [usually sing.] an estimate about the size, cost, etc. of sth that is too high（过高的评估）

overflow.meaning: to be so full that the contents go over the sides（漫出；溢出）；(of a place（地方）；to have too many people in it（挤满了人）；to spread beyond the limits of a place or container that is too full（扩展出界；过度延伸）

overgeneralize.meaning: to make a statement that is not accurate because it is too general（做过分概括的陈述；说话过于笼统）

overgraze.meaning: if land is overgrazed, it is damaged by having too many animals feeding on it（在（土地）上过度放牧）

overhang.meaning: to stick out over and above sth else（悬垂；悬挂；突出于某物之上）；the part of sth that sticks out over and above sth else（（ … 上的）伸出物，外伸物，悬垂物）；the amount by which sth hangs over and above sth else（外伸量；突出量）；(especially NAmE) the state of being extra to what is required; the things that are extra（过剩（物）；积压（物））

overhaul.meaning: an examination of a machine or system, including doing repairs on it or making changes to it（检修；大修；改造）；to examine every part of a machine, system, etc. and make any necessary changes or repairs（彻底检修）；to come from behind a person you are competing against in a race and go past them（赶上，超过（赛跑对手））

overhead.meaning: above your head; in the sky（在头上方；在空中）；above your head; raised above the ground（头上方的；地面以上的；高架的）；connected with the general costs of running a business or an organization, for example paying for rent or electricity（经费的；管理费用的）

overhear.meaning: to hear, especially by accident, a conversation in which you are not involved（偶然听到；无意中听到）

overheat.meaning: to become or to make sth become too hot（变得过热；使过热）；(of a country's economy（国家经济）；to be too active, with rising prices（发展过热，过于活跃（以致物价高涨））

overkill.meaning: too much of sth that reduces the effect it has（过犹不及；做得过火的事）

overland.meaning: across the land; by land, not by sea or by air（横跨陆地的；通过陆路的）；over·land adv. to travel overland（作陆上旅行）

overlap.meaning: if one thing overlaps another, or the two things overlap, part of one thing covers part of the other（（物体）部分重叠，交叠）；to make two or more things overlap（使部分重叠）；if two events overlap or overlap each other, the second one starts before the first one has finished（（时间上）部分重叠）；to cover part of the same area of interest, knowledge, responsibility, etc.（（范围方面）部分重叠）

overlie.meaning: (technical 术语) to lie over sth（叠加于；置于 … 上面）

overload.meaning: to put too great a load on sth（使超载；使负荷过重）；to give sb too much of sth（给 … 增加负担）；to put too great a demand on a computer, an electrical system, etc. causing it to fail（使（计算机）超载运行；使（电路）超负荷）；too much of sth（过多；过量；超负荷）

overlook.meaning: to fail to see or notice sth（忽略；未注意到）；to see sth wrong or bad but decide to ignore it（（对不良现象等）不予理会，视而不见）；if a building, etc. overlooks a place, you can see that place from the building（俯视；眺望）；to not consider sb for a job or position, even though they might be suitable（（提拔等时）对（某人）不予考虑）

overly.meaning: (before an adjective（用于形容词前）；too; very（很；十分；过于）

overnight.meaning: during or for the night（在夜间；在晚上）；suddenly or quickly（突然；一夜之间；旋即）；happening during the night; for a night（夜间的；晚上的；只供一夜的）；happening suddenly or quickly（突然的；很快的；一夜之间的）

overpass.meaning: a bridge that carries one road over another one（高架桥；跨线桥；立交桥）

overprint.meaning: to print sth on a document, etc. that already has printing on it（（在印刷品上）套印，加印）

override.meaning: to use your authority to reject sb's decision, order, etc.（（以权力）否决，推翻，不理会）；to be more important than sth（比 … 更重要；凌驾）；to stop a process that happens automatically and control it yourself（超驰控制，超控（使自动控制暂时失效，改用手工控制））

overrule.meaning: to change a decision or reject an idea from a position of greater power（（以权力）否定，拒绝，更改决定）

overrun.meaning: (especially of sth bad or not wanted（尤指坏事或不欲之事）；to fill or spread over an area quickly, especially in large numbers（泛滥；横行；肆虐）；to take more time or money than was intended（多用（时间、钱财等）；超时）；over·run /ˈəʊvərʌn; NAmEˈoʊvərʌn/ noun a cost overrun（超出的成本）

overseas.meaning: connected with foreign countries, especially those separated from your country by the sea or ocean（外国的；海外的）；to or in a foreign country, especially those separated from your country by the sea or ocean（在国外；向海外）

oversee.meaning: to watch sb/sth and make sure that a job or an activity is done correctly（监督；监视）

overshadow.meaning: to make sb/sth seem less important, or successful（使显得逊色；使黯然失色）；to make an event less enjoyable than it should be（使扫兴；使蒙上阴影）；to throw a shadow over sth（掩盖；遮蔽）

oversight.meaning: the fact of making a mistake because you forget to do sth or you do not notice sth（疏忽；忽略；失察）；(formal) the state of being in charge of sb/sth（负责；照管）

overt.meaning: done in an open way and not secretly（公开的；明显的；不隐瞒的）；overt·ly /; NAmE/ adv. overtly political activities（公开的政治活动）

overtake.meaning: (especially BrE) to go past a moving vehicle or person ahead of you because you are going faster than they are（超过；赶上）；to become greater in number, amount or importance than sth else（（在数量或重要性方面）大于，超过）；if sth unpleasant overtakes a person, it unexpectedly starts to happen and to affect them（（不愉快的事情）突然发生，突然降临）

overtax.meaning: to do more than you are able or want to do; to make sb/sth do more than they are able or want to do（使用过度；（使）超负荷工作）；to make a person or an organization pay too much tax（（对人或机构）课税过重，多收税款）

overthrow.meaning: to remove a leader or a government from a position of power by force（推翻；打倒；赶下台）；the act of taking power by force from a leader or government（推翻；打倒）

overtime.meaning: time that you spend working at your job after you have worked the normal hours（加班；加班的时间）；the money sb earns for doing overtime（加班费）；(sport 体) a set period of time that is added to the end of a sports game, etc., if there is no winner at the end of the normal period（（体育比赛等的）加时，加时赛）；(informal) to be very active or too active（非常活跃；过分活跃）

overtone.meaning: an attitude or an emotion that is suggested and is not expressed in a direct way（弦外之音；言外之意；暗示）

overture.meaning: a piece of music written as an introduction to an opera or a ballet（（歌剧或芭蕾舞的）序曲，前奏曲）；a suggestion or an action by which sb tries to make friends, start a business relationship, have discussions, etc. with sb else（友好姿态；建议）

overturn.meaning: if sth overturns, or if sb overturns it, it turns upside down or on its side（倾倒；倾覆；翻掉）；to officially decide that a legal decision, etc. is not correct, and to make it no longer valid（推翻，撤销（判决等））

overweight.meaning: (of people（人）；too heavy and fat（太胖的；超重的）；above an allowed weight（超过限制重量的；过重的）

overwhelm.meaning: to have such a strong emotional effect on sb that it is difficult for them to resist or know how to react（（感情或感觉）充溢，难以禁受）；to defeat sb completely（压倒；击败；征服）；to be so bad or so great that a person cannot deal with it; to give too much of a thing to a person（压垮；使应接不暇）；(of water（水）

overwhelming.meaning: very great or very strong; so powerful that you cannot resist it or decide how to react（巨大的；压倒性的；无法抗拒的）；over·whelm·ing·ly /ˌəʊvəˈwelmɪŋli; NAmEˌoʊvərˈwelmɪŋli/ adv. They voted overwhelmingly against the proposal.（他们以压倒多数票反对这项提案。）

overwrought.meaning: very worried and upset; excited in a nervous way（过度紧张的；过分忧烦的；紧张激动的）

owe.meaning: to have to pay sb for sth that you have already received or return money that you have borrowed（欠（债）；欠（账））；to feel that you ought to do sth for sb or give them sth, especially because they have done sth for you（欠（情））；to exist or be successful because of the help or influence of sb/sth（归因于；归功于；起源于）；(formal) to have to obey or be loyal to sb who is in a position of authority or power（（对位高权重者）忠诚，服从）

owing.meaning: money that is owing has not been paid yet（拖欠；未付；未偿还）

owl.meaning: a bird of prey (= a bird that kills other creatures for food) with large round eyes, that hunts at night. Owls are traditionally thought to be wise.（猫头鹰，鸮（传统上认为是智慧的象征））

own.meaning: used to emphasize that sth belongs to or is connected with sb（（用于强调）自己的，本人的）；Own cannot be used after an article.（*）；done or produced by and for yourself（自己做的；为自己的）；to have the opportunity to show how good or useful you are or sth is（得到充分的发挥）

owner.meaning: a person who owns sth（物主；所有权人；主人）

ownership.meaning: the fact of owning sth（所有权；产权；物主身分）

ox.meaning: a bull (= a male cow) that has been castrated (= had part of its sex organs removed), used, especially in the past, for pulling farm equipment, etc.（（阉割的）公牛；去势公牛）；(old-fashioned) any cow or bull on a farm（饲养的牛）

oxide.meaning: a compound of oxygen and another chemical element（氧化物）

oxidize.meaning: (chemistry 化) to remove one or more electrons from a substance, or to combine or to make sth combine with oxygen, especially when this causes metal to become covered with rust（（使）氧化；（尤指使）生锈）

oxygen.meaning: a chemical element. Oxygen is a gas that is present in air and water and is necessary for people, animals and plants to live.（氧；氧气）

oyster.meaning: a large flat shellfish. Some types of oyster can be eaten and others produce shiny white jewels called pearls.（牡蛎；蚝）

oystercatcher.meaning: a black bird with long legs and a long red beak that lives near the coast and feeds on shellfish（蛎鹬（捕食贝类的滨鸟））

ozone.meaning: (chemistry 化) a poisonous gas with a strong smell that is a form of oxygen（臭氧）；(BrE) (informal) air near the sea that smells fresh and pure（海边的清新空气）

pace.meaning: the speed at which sb/sth walks, runs or moves（（移动的）速度；步速）；the speed at which sth happens（发生的速度；步伐；节奏）；an act of stepping once when walking or running; the distance travelled when doing this（（走或跑时）迈出的一步，一步的距离；步幅）；the fact of sth happening, changing, etc. quickly（迅速出现（或变化等）；快节奏）

pacific.meaning: peaceful or loving peace（平静的；和平的；爱和平的）

pacifier.meaning: a specially shaped rubber or plastic object for a baby to suck（橡皮奶嘴；橡皮奶头）

pacify.meaning: to make sb who is angry or upset become calm and quiet（使平静；平息；抚慰）；to bring peace to an area where there is fighting or a war（平息战争；使实现和平）

pack.meaning: to put clothes, etc. into a bag in preparation for a trip away from home（收拾（行李）；装（箱））；to put sth into a container so that it can be stored, transported or sold（打包；包装）；to protect sth that breaks easily by surrounding it with soft material（（在四周填入软料以）包装（易损物品））；to preserve food in a particular substance（（用某物）保存，保藏）

package.meaning: (NAmE) a box, bag, etc. in which things are wrapped or packed; the contents of a box etc.（包；盒；袋；包装好的东西）；a set of items or ideas that must be bought or accepted together（（必须整体接收的）一套东西，一套建议；一揽子交易）；(computing 计) a set of related programs for a particular type of task, sold and used as a single unit（软件包）；to put sth into a box, bag, etc. to be sold or transported（将 … 包装好）

packaging.meaning: materials used to wrap or protect goods that are sold in shops/stores（包装材料；外包装）；the process of wrapping goods（包装工作；包装）

packer.meaning: a person, machine or company that puts food, goods, etc. into containers to be sold or sent to sb（包装工；包装机；包装公司）

packet.meaning: (BrE) a small paper or cardboard container in which goods are packed for selling（（商品的）小包装纸袋，小硬纸板盒）；a small object wrapped in paper or put into a thick envelope so that it can be sent by mail, carried easily or given as a present（（邮政）小件包裹）；a closed plastic or paper package that contains a very small amount of liquid or a powder（（塑料或纸质）密封小袋）；(BrE) (informal) a large amount of money（一笔巨款）

packing.meaning: the act of putting your possessions, clothes, etc. into bags or boxes in order to take or send them somewhere（打行李；收拾行囊）；material used for wrapping around delicate objects in order to protect them, especially before sending them somewhere（包装材料）

pact.meaning: a formal agreement between two or more people, groups or countries, especially one in which they agree to help each other（条约；协议；公约）

pad.meaning: a thick piece of soft material that is used, for example, for absorbing liquid, cleaning or protecting sth（（吸收液体、保洁或保护用的）软垫，护垫，垫状物）；a number of pieces of paper for writing or drawing on, that are fastened together at one edge（便笺本；拍纸簿）；the soft part under the foot of a cat, dog, etc.（爪垫；肉掌）；a small piece of rough material used for cleaning pans, surfaces, etc.（百洁布，菜瓜布（刷锅等的小块粗糙材料））

paddle.meaning: a short pole with a flat wide part at one or both ends, that you hold in both hands and use for moving a small boat, especially a canoe, through water（桨；船桨）；a tool or part of a machine shaped like a paddle, especially one used for mixing food（（机具的）桨状部分；（尤指）食物搅拌器的桨叶）；(BrE) an act or period of walking in shallow water with no shoes or socks（蹚水；赤脚涉水）；(NAmE) a bat used for playing table tennis（乒乓球拍）

paddock.meaning: a small field in which horses are kept（（牧马的）小围场）；(in horse racing or motor racing（赛马或赛车）；an area where horses or cars are taken before a race and shown to the public（检阅场）；(AustralE, NZE) any field or area of land that has fences around it（设有围栏的一片土地）

paddy.meaning: an offensive word for a person from Ireland（帕迪（对爱尔兰人的蔑称））

page.meaning: one side or both sides of a sheet of paper in a book, magazine, etc.（（书刊或纸张的）页，面，张，版）；a section of data or information that can be shown on a computer screen at any one time（（计算机的）页面，版面）；(literary) an important event or period of history（历史篇章，历史篇页（指历史大事或时期））；(NAmE) a student who works as an assistant to a member of the US Congress（（美国议员的）青年助理（本身为学生））

pageant.meaning: a public entertainment in which people dress in historical costumes and give performances of scenes from history（穿古代服装的游行；再现历史场景的娱乐活动）；(NAmE) a competition for young women in which their beauty, personal qualities and skills are judged（选美比赛）；(literary) something that is considered as a series of interesting and different events（内容繁杂有趣的场面；盛大华丽的情景）

pain.meaning: the feelings that you have in your body when you have been hurt or when you are ill/sick（（身体上的）疼痛）；mental or emotional suffering（痛苦；苦恼；烦恼）；(informal) a person or thing that is very annoying（讨厌的人（或事）；令人头痛的人（或事））；(saying) used to say that you need to suffer if you want to achieve sth（不劳则无获）

painful.meaning: causing you pain（令人疼痛的）；causing you to feel upset or embarrassed（令人痛苦（或难过、难堪）的）；unpleasant or difficult to do（不愉快的；困难的；艰难的）

painstaking.meaning: needing a lot of care, effort and attention to detail（需细心的；辛苦的；需专注的）

paint.meaning: a liquid that is put on surfaces to give them a particular colour; a layer of this liquid when it has dried on a surface（油漆；油漆涂层）；tubes or blocks of paint used for painting pictures（绘画颜料）；to cover a surface or object with paint（在 … 上刷油漆）；to make a picture or design using paints（用颜料画）

painter.meaning: a person whose job is painting buildings, walls, etc.（油漆匠）；an artist who paints pictures（画家）；a rope fastened to the front of a boat, used for tying it to a post, ship, etc.（（系船的）缆绳）

painting.meaning: a picture that has been painted（绘画；油画）；the act or art of using paint to produce pictures（作画；绘画）；the act of putting paint onto the surface of objects, walls, etc.（涂漆；刷油漆）

pair.meaning: two things of the same type, especially when they are used or worn together（一双；一对）；an object consisting of two parts that are joined together（分两个相连接部分的物体）；A plural verb is sometimes used with pair in the singular in senses 1 and 2. In informal NAmE some people use pair as a plural form.（在第 1 及第 2 义中，pair 有时以单数形式与复数动词搭配。在非正式的美式英语中，有些人把 pair 作为复数：）；This is not considered correct in written English.（在书面英语中，这种用法被认为不正确。）

palace.meaning: the official home of a king, queen, president, etc.（王宫；宫殿；总统府）；the people who live in a palace, especially the British royal family（住在王宫里的人；（尤指英国的）王室）；any large impressive house（豪华住宅；宫殿）；(old-fashioned) (sometimes used in the names of buildings（有时用于建筑物名称）

palatable.meaning: (of food or drink（食物或饮料）；having a pleasant or acceptable taste（可口的；味美的）；pleasant or acceptable to sb（宜人的；可意的；可接受的）

pale.meaning: (of a person, their face, etc.（人、面孔等）；having skin that is almost white; having skin that is whiter than usual because of illness, a strong emotion, etc.（灰白的；苍白的；白皙的）；light in colour; containing a lot of white（浅色的；淡色的）；(of light（光线）

palimpsest.meaning: an ancient document from which some or all of the original text has been removed and replaced by a new text（再生羊皮纸卷，重写羊皮书卷（全部或部分原有文字被刮去，在上面另行书写））；(formal) something that has many different layers of meaning or detail（具有多重意义的事物；多层次的东西）

palm.meaning: the inner surface of the hand between the wrist and the fingers（手掌；手心）；a straight tree with a mass of long leaves at the top, growing in tropical countries. There are several types of palm tree, some of which produce fruit.（棕榈树）；to have complete control or influence over sb（完全控制某人；把某人攥在手心里）；to hide a coin, card, etc. in your hand, especially when performing a trick（把 … 藏在手中（尤指玩戏法））

palpitate.meaning: (of the heart（心脏）；to beat rapidly and/or in an irregular way especially because of fear or excitement（急速跳动，悸动（尤指因恐惧或兴奋））

pamper.meaning: (sometimes disapproving) to take care of sb very well and make them feel as comfortable as possible（细心照顾；精心护理；娇惯；纵容）

pamphlet.meaning: a very thin book with a paper cover, containing information about a particular subject（小册子；手册）

pan.meaning: a container, usually made of metal, with a handle or handles, used for cooking food in（平锅；平底锅）；the amount contained in a pan（一锅的量）；a metal container used for cooking food in（（烘煮食物用的）烤盘，烤模）；either of the dishes on a pair of scales that you put things into in order to weigh them（（天平的）称盘）

panacea.meaning: something that will solve all the problems of a particular situation（万灵药；万能之计）

pancreas.meaning: an organ near the stomach that produces insulin and a liquid that helps the body to digest food（胰；胰腺）

panda.meaning: a large black and white animal like a bear, that lives in China and is very rare（大猫熊；大熊猫）；an Asian animal like a raccoon, with reddish-brown fur and a long thick tail（小猫熊，小熊猫（产于亚洲，毛棕红色，尾巴粗长））

pane.meaning: a single sheet of glass in a window（（一片）窗玻璃）

panel.meaning: a square or rectangular piece of wood, glass or metal that forms part of a larger surface such as a door or wall（（门、墙等上面的）嵌板，镶板，方格板块）；a piece of metal that forms part of the outer frame of a vehicle（（车身的）金属板，板金）；a piece of cloth that forms part of a piece of clothing（（衣服上的）镶条，嵌条，饰片）；a group of specialists who give their advice or opinion about sth; a group of people who discuss topics of interest on television or radio（专家咨询组；（广播、电视上的）讨论小组）

pangaea.meaning: an extremely large area of land which existed millions of years ago, made up of all the present continents（泛大陆，泛古陆（原始大陆，由现在的所有大陆组成））

panic.meaning: a sudden feeling of great fear that cannot be controlled and prevents you from thinking clearly（惊恐；恐慌）；a situation in which people are made to feel very anxious, causing them to act quickly and without thinking carefully（人心惶惶的局面；惶恐不安）；(BrE) (informal) a situation in which people feel anxious and there is a lot of confused activity, especially because there is a lot to do in a short period of time（慌乱的状态；（尤指）忙乱的状况）；to suddenly feel frightened so that you cannot think clearly and you say or do sth stupid, dangerous, etc; to make sb do this（（使）惊慌，惊慌失措）

panorama.meaning: a view of a wide area of land（全景）；a description, study or set of pictures that presents all the different aspects or stages of a particular subject, event, etc.（（某专题或事件的）全面叙述，综合研究；全景画卷）；pan·or·am·ic /ˌpænəˈræmɪk; NAmEˌpænəˈræmɪk/ adj. [usually before noun] a panoramic view over the valley（山谷的全景）

pant.meaning: to breathe quickly with short breaths, usually with your mouth open, because you have been doing some physical exercise, or because it is very hot（气喘；喘息）；pant noun [usually pl.] His breath came in short pants.（他气息急促。）；to want sth/sb very much（渴望）

panther.meaning: a black leopard (= a large wild animal of the cat family)（黑豹）

pantomime.meaning: (in Britain) a type of play with music, dancing and jokes, that is based on a fairy tale and is usually performed at Christmas（（英国多在圣诞节期间上演的）童话剧）；the use of movement and the expression of your face to communicate sth or to tell a story（哑剧；默剧）；(BrE) a ridiculous situation, usually with a lot of confusion（滑稽可笑的局面）

pantry.meaning: a cupboard/closet or small room in a house, used for storing food（食品贮藏室；食品贮藏柜）

pants.meaning: (BrE) underpants or knickers（内裤；短衬裤）；(especially NAmE) trousers（裤子）；(BrE, slang) (also used as an adjective（也用作形容词）；something you think is of poor quality（次品；劣质品）

paper.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；the thin material that you write and draw on and that is also used for wrapping and packing things（纸；纸张）；a newspaper（报纸）；pieces of paper with writing on them, such as letters, pieces of work or private documents（文件；文献）

paperback.meaning: a book that has a thick paper cover（平装书；简装书）

par.meaning: (in golf（高尔夫球）；the number of strokes a good player should need to complete a course or to hit the ball into a particular hole（标准杆数）；(business 商) the value that a share in a company had originally（（股票的）面值，票面价值）；less well, good, etc. than is usual or expected（不太好；不佳；不及平常好；不如预期）

parachute.meaning: a device that is attached to people or objects to make them fall slowly and safely when they are dropped from an aircraft. It consists of a large piece of thin cloth that opens out in the air to form an umbrella shape.（降落伞）；to jump from an aircraft using a parachute（跳伞）；to drop sb/sth from an aircraft by parachute（伞降；空投）

parade.meaning: a public celebration of a special day or event, usually with bands in the streets and decorated vehicles（庆祝游行）；a formal occasion when soldiers march or stand in lines so that they can be examined by their officers or other important people（检阅；阅兵）；a series of things or people（一系列（人或事））；(often disapproving) an obvious display of sth, particularly in order to impress other people（夸示；炫耀）

paradigm.meaning: (technical 术语 or formal) a typical example or pattern of sth（典范；范例；样式）；(grammar 语法) a set of all the different forms of a word（词形变化表）

paradise.meaning: (in some religions) a perfect place where people are said to go when they die（（某些宗教所指的）天堂，天国）；a place that is extremely beautiful and that seems perfect, like heaven（天堂，乐土，乐园（指美好的环境））；a perfect place for a particular activity or kind of person（（某类活动或某类人的）乐园，完美去处）；a state of perfect happiness（至福；极乐）

paradox.meaning: a person, thing or situation that has two opposite features and therefore seems strange（矛盾的人（或事物、情况））；a statement containing two opposite ideas that make it seem impossible or unlikely, although it is probably true; the use of this in writing（似非而是的隽语；悖论；悖论修辞）；para·dox·ical /ˌpærəˈdɒksɪkl; NAmEˌpærəˈdɑːksɪkl/ adj. It is paradoxical that some of the poorest people live in some of the richest areas of the country.（某些最贫穷的人却住在这个国家一些最富有的地区，这似乎很矛盾。）；para·dox·ic·al·ly /ˌpærəˈdɒksɪkli; NAmEˌpærəˈdɑːksɪkli/ adv. Paradoxically, the less she ate, the fatter she got.（很矛盾的是，她吃得越少，却变得越胖。）

paragraph.meaning: a section of a piece of writing, usually consisting of several sentences dealing with a single subject. The first sentence of a paragraph starts on a new line.（段；段落）

parakeet.meaning: a small bird of the parrot family, usually with a long tail（长尾小鹦鹉）

parallel.meaning: two or more lines that are parallel to each other are the same distance apart at every point（平行的）；very similar or taking place at the same time（极相似的；同时发生的；相应的；对应的）；(computing 计) involving several computer operations at the same time（并行的）；par·al·lel adv. The road and the canal run parallel to each other.（道路与运河平行。）

paralyse.meaning: to make sb unable to feel or move all or part of their body（使瘫痪；使麻痹）；to prevent sth from functioning normally（使不能正常工作）

paralysis.meaning: a loss of control of, and sometimes feeling in, part or most of the body, caused by disease or an injury to the nerves（麻痹；瘫痪）；a total inability to move, act, function, etc.（（活动、工作等）能力的完全丧失，瘫痪）

parameter.meaning: something that decides or limits the way in which sth can be done（决定因素；规范；范围）

paramount.meaning: more important than anything else（至为重要的；首要的）；(formal) having the highest position or the greatest power（至高无上的；至尊的；权力最大的）

paranoia.meaning: (medical 医) a mental illness in which a person may wrongly believe that other people are trying to harm them, that they are sb very important, etc.（妄想症；偏执狂）；(informal) fear or suspicion of other people when there is no evidence or reason for this（（对别人的）无端恐惧，多疑）

paraphernalia.meaning: a large number of objects or personal possessions, especially the equipment that you need for a particular activity（（尤指某活动所需的）装备，大量用品，私人物品）

paraphrase.meaning: to express what sb has said or written using different words, especially in order to make it easier to understand（（用更容易理解的文字）解释，释义，意译）；a statement that expresses sth that sb has written or said using different words, especially in order to make it easier to understand（解释；释义；意译）

parasite.meaning: a small animal or plant that lives on or inside another animal or plant and gets its food from it（寄生生物；寄生虫；寄生植物）；(disapproving) a person who always relies on or benefits from other people and gives nothing back（寄生虫；依赖他人过活者）

parasitic.meaning: caused by a parasite（寄生生物引起的）；living on another animal or plant and getting its food from it（寄生的；依附性的）；(of a person（人）；always relying on or benefiting from other people and giving nothing back（寄生虫似的；依赖他人的）

parcel.meaning: something that is wrapped in paper or put into a thick envelope so that it can be sent by mail, carried easily, or given as a present（包裹；小包）；a piece of land（一块地；一片地）；(especially BrE) a small amount of food that is wrapped in sth, usually pastry, before it is cooked（油酥包（通常以油酥皮包裹少许食物烹制））；to wrap sth up and make it into a parcel（包；裹好；打包）

pardon.meaning: used to ask sb to repeat sth because you did not hear it or did not understand it（（用于请求别人重复某事）什么，请再说一遍）；used by some people to say ‘sorry’ when they have accidentally made a rude noise, or said or done sth wrong（抱歉；对不起）；an official decision not to punish sb for a crime, or to say that sb is not guilty of a crime（赦免；特赦）；the action of forgiving sb for sth（原谅；宽恕）

parent.meaning: a person's father or mother（父亲；母亲）；an animal or a plant which produces other animals or plants（（动、植物的）亲本，亲代，父本，母本）；(often used as an adjective（常用作形容词）；an organization that produces and owns or controls smaller organizations of the same type（创始机构；母公司；总部）

parental.meaning: connected with a parent or parents（父亲的；母亲的；父母的；双亲的）

parenting.meaning: the process of caring for your child or children（养育；抚养；教养）

parish.meaning: an area that has its own church and that a priest is responsible for（堂区；教区）；(in England) a small country area that has its own elected local government（（英国）乡村的行政小区）；the people living in a particular area, especially those who go to church（教区的居民；（尤指）教区教徒）

park.meaning: an area of public land in a town or a city where people go to walk, play and relax（公园）；(in compounds（构成复合词）；an area of land used for a particular purpose（专用区；园区）；(in Britain) an area of land, usually with fields and trees, attached to a large country house（（英国）庄园，庭院）

parking.meaning: the act of stopping a vehicle at a place and leaving it there for a period of time（停车；泊车）；a space or an area for leaving vehicles（停车场；停车位）

parkway.meaning: a wide road with trees and grass along the sides or middle（（有草木的）大路；绿化道路；林荫大道）

parliament.meaning: the group of people who are elected to make and change the laws of a country（议会；国会）；the parliament of the United Kingdom, consisting of the House of Commons and the House of Lords（英国议会（包括下议院和上议院））；a particular period during which a parliament is working; Parliament as it exists between one general election and the next（一届议会的会期；（两次大选之间的）一届议会）

parliamentary.meaning: connected with a parliament; having a parliament（议会的；国会的；设有议会的）

parody.meaning: a piece of writing, music, acting, etc. that deliberately copies the style of sb/sth in order to be amusing（滑稽模仿作品（文章、音乐作品或表演等的滑稽模仿））；(disapproving) something that is such a bad or unfair example of sth that it seems ridiculous（拙劣的模仿；荒诞不经的事）；to copy the style of sb/sth in an exaggerated way, especially in order to make people laugh（滑稽地模仿；夸张地演绎）

parrot.meaning: a tropical bird with a curved beak. There are several types of parrot, most of which have bright feathers. Some are kept as pets and can be trained to copy human speech.（鹦鹉）；(disapproving) to repeat what sb else has said without thinking about what it means（鹦鹉学舌）

part.meaning: some but not all of a thing（部分）；a section, piece or feature of sth（片段；部分；一点）；a member of sth; a person or thing that, together with others, makes up a single unit（成员；成分）；a piece of a machine or structure（部件；零件）

partake.meaning: (old-fashioned or humorous) to eat or drink sth especially sth that is offered to you（吃，喝，享用（尤指给予的食物））；(old-fashioned) to take part in an activity（参加；参与）；(formal) to have some of a particular quality（具有（部分特性）；有点）

partial.meaning: not complete or whole（部分的；不完全的）；(old-fashioned) liking sb/sth very much（热爱；钟爱）；(disapproving) showing or feeling too much support for one person, team, idea, etc., in a way that is unfair（偏颇；偏袒）

partially.meaning: partly; not completely（部分地；不完全地）

participant.meaning: a person who is taking part in an activity or event（参与者；参加者）

participate.meaning: (rather formal) to take part in or become involved in an activity（参加；参与）

participation.meaning: the act of taking part in an activity or event（参加；参与）

particle.meaning: a very small piece of sth（颗粒；微粒）；(physics 物) a very small piece of matter, such as an electron or proton, that is part of an atom（粒子）；(grammar 语法) an adverb or a preposition that can combine with a verb to make a phrasal verb（小品词（与动词构成短语动词的副词或介词））

particular.meaning: used to emphasize that you are referring to one individual person, thing or type of thing and not others（专指的，特指的（与泛指相对））；greater than usual; special（不寻常的；格外的；特别的）；very definite about what you like and careful about what you choose（讲究；挑剔）；especially or particularly（尤其；特别；格外）

particularly.meaning: especially; more than usual or more than others（特别；尤其）

partisan.meaning: (often disapproving) showing too much support for one person, group or idea, especially without considering it carefully（（对个别人、团体或思想）过分支持的，偏护的，盲目拥护的）；a person who strongly supports a particular leader, group or idea（坚定的支持者；铁杆拥护者）；a member of an armed group that is fighting secretly against enemy soldiers who have taken control of its country（游击队员）

partition.meaning: a wall or screen that separates one part of a room from another（隔断；隔扇；隔板墙）；the division of one country into two or more countries（分割；分治；瓜分）；to divide sth into parts（分割；使分裂）；to separate one area, one part of a room, etc. from another with a wall or screen（（把地方、房间等）分隔，隔开）

partly.meaning: to some extent; not completely（一定程度上；部分地）

partner.meaning: the person that you are married to or having a sexual relationship with（配偶；性伴侣）；one of the people who owns a business and shares the profits, etc.（合伙人）；a person that you are doing an activity with, such as dancing or playing a game（搭档；同伴；舞伴）；a country or an organization that has an agreement with another country（伙伴（与另一国家有协议关系的国家或组织））

partnership.meaning: the state of being a partner in business（伙伴关系；合伙人身分）；a relationship between two people, organizations, etc; the state of having this relationship（合作关系；合作）；a business owned by two or more people who share the profits（合伙企业）

part-time.meaning: for part of the day or week in which people work（部分时间的；兼职的）；ˌpart-ˈtime adv. Liz works part-time from 10 till 2.（利兹的兼职时间是 10 点到 2 点。）

party.meaning: a political organization that you can vote for in elections and whose members have the same aims and ideas（政党；党派）；(especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）；a social occasion, often in a person's home, at which people eat, drink, talk, dance and enjoy themselves（聚会；宴会；联欢会；派对）；a group of people who are doing sth together such as travelling or visiting somewhere（（一起旅行或参观等的）群，队，组）

pass.meaning: to move past or to the other side of sb/sth（通过；走过）；to go or move in the direction mentioned（沿某方向前进；向某方向移动）；to make sth move in the direction or into the position mentioned（使沿某方向移动；使达到某位置）；to give sth to sb by putting it into their hands or in a place where they can easily reach it（给；递；传递）

passable.meaning: fairly good but not excellent（过得去的；尚可的）；if a road or a river is passable, it is not blocked and you can travel along or across it（通行无阻）

passage.meaning: a long narrow area with walls on either side that connects one room or place with another（通道；走廊）；a tube in the body through which air, liquid, etc. passes（（体内通气、输液等的）管路，通道）；a short section from a book, piece of music, etc.（章节；段落；乐段）；(literary) the process of time passing（（时间的）流逝，推移）

passenger.meaning: a person who is travelling in a car, bus, train, plane or ship and who is not driving it or working on it（乘客；旅客）；(informal, disapproving) (especially BrE) a member of a group or team who does not do as much work as the others（白吃饭的人；闲散人员）

passer-by.meaning: a person who is going past sb/sth by chance, especially when sth unexpected happens（路人；过路的人）

passing.meaning: the process of time going by（（时间、岁月的）流逝，推移）；(formal) the fact of sth ending or of sb dying（（事物的）结束，消亡；（人的）亡故，逝世）；the act of making sth become a law（（法律等的）通过）；done or said while you are giving your attention to sth else（顺便；随便）

passion.meaning: a very strong feeling of love, hatred, anger, enthusiasm, etc.（强烈情感；激情）；(formal) a state of being very angry（盛怒；激愤）；a very strong feeling of sexual love（强烈的爱（尤指两性间的））；a very strong feeling of liking sth; a hobby, an activity, etc. that you like very much（酷爱；热衷的爱好（或活动等））

passionate.meaning: having or showing strong feelings of sexual love or of anger, etc.（拥有（或表现出）强烈性爱的；情意绵绵的；怒不可遏的）；having or showing strong feelings of enthusiasm for sth or belief in sth（热诚的；狂热的）；pas·sion·ate·ly /ˈpæʃənətli; NAmEˈpæʃənətli/ adv. He took her in his arms and kissed her passionately.（他把她搂在怀里狂热地亲吻。）

passive.meaning: accepting what happens or what people do without trying to change anything or oppose them（消极的；被动的）；(grammar 语法) connected with the form of a verb used when the subject is affected by the action of the verb, for example He was bitten by a dog. is a passive sentence（（动词形式）被动语态的）；pas·sive·ly AW /ˈpæsɪvli; NAmEˈpæsɪvli/ adv. noun (also ˌpassive ˈvoice) [sing.] (grammar 语法) the form of a verb used when the subject is affected by the action of the verb（动词被动形式；被动语态）

passport.meaning: an official document that identifies you as a citizen of a particular country, and that you may have to show when you enter or leave a country（护照）；a thing that makes sth possible or enables you to achieve sth（途径；路子；手段）

password.meaning: a secret word or phrase that you need to know in order to be allowed into a place（暗语；暗号；口令）；(computing 计) a series of letters or numbers that you must type into a computer or computer system in order to be able to use it（口令；密码）

past.meaning: gone by in time（过去的；昔日的）；gone by recently; just ended（刚过去的；刚结束的）；belonging to an earlier time（从前的；以往的）；(grammar 语法) connected with the form of a verb used to express actions in the past（（动词）过去式的）

paste.meaning: a soft wet mixture, usually made of a powder and a liquid（面团）；(especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）；a smooth mixture of crushed meat, fish, etc. that is spread on bread or used in cooking（肉（或鱼等）酱（作涂抹料或烹饪用））；a type of glue that is used for sticking paper to things（糨糊）

pastime.meaning: something that you enjoy doing when you are not working（消遣；休闲活动）

pastoral.meaning: relating to the work of a priest or teacher in giving help and advice on personal matters, not just those connected with religion or education（牧灵的，牧师的，教牧的（有关圣职人员及教师对个人幸福的关顾））；showing country life or the countryside, especially in a romantic way（田园的；乡村生活的；村野风情的）；relating to the farming of animals（畜牧的）

pastoralism.meaning: a way of keeping animals such as cattle, sheep, etc. that involves moving them from place to place to find water and food（游牧（牧者带着牲口逐水草而居））

pastry.meaning: a mixture of flour, fat and water or milk that is rolled out flat and baked as a base or covering for pies, etc.（油酥面团；油酥面皮）；a small cake made using pastry（油酥糕点）

pasture.meaning: land covered with grass that is suitable for feeding animals on（牧场；牧草地）；the circumstances of your life, work, etc.（生活状况；工作条件；个人发展的机遇）；to put animals in a field to feed on grass（放牧）

pat.meaning: to touch sb/sth gently several times with your hand flat, especially as a sign of affection（（喜爱地）轻拍）；(informal) to praise sb or yourself for doing sth well（表扬，称赞（某人或自己））；a gentle friendly touch with your open hand or with a flat object（（友善的）轻拍，拍打）；a small, soft, flat lump of butter（一小块黄油）

patch.meaning: a small area of sth, especially one which is different from the area around it（色斑；斑点；（与周围不同的）小块，小片）；a small piece of material that is used to cover a hole in sth or to make a weak area stronger, or as decoration（补丁；补块）；a piece of material that you wear over an eye, usually because the eye is damaged（眼罩）；a piece of material that you sew onto clothes as part of a uniform（（制服上的）标记，标识）

patchy.meaning: existing or happening in some places and not others（零散的；散落的；分布不匀的）；not complete; good in some parts, but not in others（不完整的；参差不齐的）

patent.meaning: an official right to be the only person to make, use or sell a product or an invention; a document that proves this（专利权；专利证书）；connected with a patent（有专利的；受专利保护的）；(of a product（产品）；made or sold by a particular company（专利生产的；专利经销的）

paternity.meaning: the fact of being the father of a child（父亲的身分（或地位））

path.meaning: a way or track that is built or is made by the action of people walking（小路；小径）；a line along which sb/sth moves; the space in front of sb/sth as they move（路线；道路）；a plan of action or a way of achieving sth（行动计划；成功的途径）

pathetic.meaning: making you feel pity or sadness（可怜的；可悲的；令人怜惜的）；(informal, disapproving) weak and not successful（无力的；不成功的）；path·et·ic·al·ly /pəˈθetɪkli; NAmEpəˈθetɪkli/ adv. He cried pathetically.（他哭得很悲伤。）

pathogen.meaning: a thing that causes disease（病原体）

pathological.meaning: not reasonable or sensible; impossible to control（不理智的；无道理的；无法控制的）；caused by, or connected with, disease or illness（病态的；与疾病有关的）；(technical 术语) connected with pathology（病理学的；与病理学相关的）；patho·logic·al·ly /ˌpæθəˈlɒdʒɪkli; NAmEˌpæθəˈlɑːdʒɪkli/ adv. pathologically jealous（有嫉妒狂的）

pathology.meaning: (medical 医) the scientific study of diseases（病理学）；an aspect of sb's behaviour that is extreme and unreasonable and that they cannot control（变态；反常）

pathos.meaning: (in writing, speech and plays（文章、讲话和戏剧）；the power of a performance, description, etc. to produce feelings of sadness and sympathy（感染力；令人产生悲悯共鸣的力量）

patience.meaning: the ability to stay calm and accept a delay or sth annoying without complaining（耐心；忍耐力）；the ability to spend a lot of time doing sth difficult that needs a lot of attention and effort（毅力；坚忍；恒心）；a card game for only one player（单人纸牌游戏）

patient.meaning: a person who is receiving medical treatment, especially in a hospital（接受治疗者，病人（尤指医院里的））；a person who receives treatment from a particular doctor, dentist, etc.（（某个医生或牙医等的）病人）；(grammar 语法) the person or thing that is affected by the action of the verb. In the sentence ‘I started the car’, the patient is car.（受动者）；able to wait for a long time or accept annoying behaviour or difficulties without becoming angry（有耐心的；能忍耐的）

patio.meaning: a flat hard area outside, and usually behind, a house where people can sit（（房屋外面或后面的）露台，平台）

patriarch.meaning: the male head of a family or community（（男性）家长，族长，酋长）；an old man that people have a lot of respect for（德高望重的男长者）；the title of a most senior bishop (= a senior priest) in the Orthodox or Roman Catholic Church（（东正教和天主教的）牧首，宗主教）

patriarchal.meaning: ruled or controlled by men; giving power and importance only to men（男人统治的；男性主宰的）；connected with a patriarch（族长的；家长的）

patriot.meaning: a person who loves their country and who is ready to defend it against an enemy（爱国者）

patriotic.meaning: having or expressing a great love of your country（爱国的）

patriotism.meaning: love of your country and willingness to defend it（爱国主义；爱国精神）

patrol.meaning: to go around an area or a building at regular times to check that it is safe and that there is no trouble（巡逻；巡查）；to drive or walk around a particular area, especially in a threatening way（（尤指威胁性地）逛荡，闲逛）；the act of going to different parts of a building, an area, etc. to make sure that there is no trouble or crime（巡逻；巡查）；a group of soldiers, vehicles, etc. that patrol an area（巡逻队；巡逻车队）

patron.meaning: a person who gives money and support to artists and writers（（艺术家的）赞助人，资助者）；a famous person who supports an organization such as a charity and whose name is used in the advertisements, etc. for the organization（名义赞助人（支持慈善组织等的名人，名字常用于有关的广告宣传中））；(formal) a person who uses a particular shop/store, restaurant, etc.（老主顾；顾客；常客）

patronage.meaning: the support, especially financial, that is given to a person or an organization by a patron（资助；赞助）；the system by which an important person gives help or a job to sb in return for their support（（掌权者给予提挈以换取支持的）互惠互利）；(especially NAmE) the support that a person gives a shop/store, restaurant, etc. by spending money there（惠顾；光顾）

pattern.meaning: the regular way in which sth happens or is done（模式；方式）；an excellent example to copy（范例；典范；榜样；样板）；a regular arrangement of lines, shapes, colours, etc. as a design on material, carpets, etc.（图案；花样；式样）；a design, set of instructions or shape to cut around that you use in order to make sth（模型；底样；纸样）

patty.meaning: finely chopped meat, fish, etc. formed into a small round flat shape（碎肉饼；鱼肉饼）

paucity.meaning: (formal) a small amount of sth; less than enough of sth（少量；少许；贫乏）

pause.meaning: to stop talking or doing sth for a short time before continuing（暂停；停顿）；to stop a tape, CD, etc. for a short time using the pause button（（按暂停键）暂停放音，暂停放像）；a period of time during which sb stops talking or stops what they are doing（停顿；停顿的时间）；(music 音) a sign () over a note or a rest to show that it should be longer than usual（延长记号）

pave.meaning: to cover a surface with flat stones or bricks（（用砖石）铺（地））；to create a situation in which sb will be able to do sth or sth can happen（（为 … ）铺平道路，创造条件）

pavement.meaning: a flat part at the side of a road for people to walk on（（马路边的）人行道）；(BrE) any area of flat stones on the ground（石板铺的地面）；(NAmE) the surface of a road（路面）

pavlova.meaning: a cold dessert (= sweet dish) made of meringue, cream and fruit（巴甫洛娃蛋糕（用蛋白酥、奶油和水果制成））

paw.meaning: the foot of an animal that has claws or nails（（动物的）爪）；(informal) a person's hand（（人的）手）；(of an animal（动物）；to scratch or touch sth repeatedly with a paw（（不断地）挠，抓）

pawn.meaning: a chess piece of the smallest size and least value. Each player has eight pawns at the start of a game.（（国际象棋的）兵，卒）；a person or group whose actions are controlled by more powerful people（被利用的人；走卒）；if sth is in pawn, it has been pawned（被抵押；被典当）；to leave an object with a pawnbroker in exchange for money. The object is returned to the owner if he or she pays back the money within an agreed period of time. If not, it can be sold.（质押；典当）

pawnee.meaning: a member of a Native American people, many of whom live in the US state of Oklahoma（波尼人（美洲土著，很多居于美国俄克拉何马州））

pay.meaning: to give sb money for work, goods, services, etc.（付费；付酬）；to give sb money that you owe them（交纳；偿还）；(of a business, etc.（企业等）；to produce a profit（赢利；创收）

payable.meaning: that must be paid or can be paid（应付；可偿付）；when a cheque, etc. is made payable to sb, their name is written on it and they can then pay it into their bank account（应付予（抬头人、收款人等））

payment.meaning: the act of paying sb/sth or of being paid（付款；支付；收款）；a sum of money paid or expected to be paid（（将付或应付的）款额，款项）；a reward or an act of thanks for sth you have done（报答；报偿）；when sth has been paid（付款后）

payroll.meaning: a list of people employed by a company showing the amount of money to be paid to each of them（（公司员工的）工资名单）；the total amount paid in wages by a company（（公司的）工资总支出）

pea.meaning: a small round green seed, eaten as a vegetable. Several peas grow together inside a long thin pod on a climbing plant also called a pea.（豌豆；豌豆粒）

peace.meaning: a situation or a period of time in which there is no war or violence in a country or an area（和平；太平）；the state of being calm or quiet（平静；安静；宁静）；the state of living in friendship with sb without arguing（和睦；融洽；和谐）；(old-fashioned) to say nothing although you would like to give your opinion（（想说却）保持沉默，缄口不语）

peaceful.meaning: not involving a war, violence or argument（不诉诸战争（或暴力、争论）的；和平的）；quiet and calm; not worried or disturbed in any way（安静的；平静的）；trying to create peace or to live in peace; not liking violence or disagreement（爱好和平的；和睦的；寻求和平的）；peace·ful·ly /ˈpiːsfəli; NAmEˈpiːsfəli/ adv. perplexity.meaning: the state of feeling confused and anxious because you do not understand sth（困惑；迷惘）；something that is difficult to understand（难以理解的事物；疑团）
