scent.meaning: the pleasant smell that sth has（香味）；the smell that a person or an animal leaves behind and that other animals such as dogs can follow（（人的）气味，气息；（动物留下的）臭迹，遗臭）；(especially BrE) a liquid with a pleasant smell that you wear on your skin to make it smell nice（香水）；the feeling that sth is present or is going to happen very soon（察觉；预感）

sceptical.meaning: having doubts that a claim or statement is true or that sth will happen（怀疑的）

schedule.meaning: a plan that lists all the work that you have to do and when you must do each thing（工作计划；日程安排）；a list of the television and radio programmes that are on a particular channel and the times that they start（（电视或广播）节目表）；a written list of things, for example prices, rates or conditions（（价格、收费或条款等的）一览表，明细表，清单）；to arrange for sth to happen at a particular time（安排；为 … 安排时间；预定）

scheme.meaning: (BrE) a plan or system for doing or organizing sth（计划；方案；体系；体制）；a plan for getting money or some other advantage for yourself, especially one that involves cheating other people（阴谋；诡计；计谋）；the way things seem to be organized; the way sb wants everything to be organized（格局；心中的安排）；(disapproving) to make secret plans to do sth that will help yourself and possibly harm others（密谋；秘密策划；图谋）

schist.meaning: a type of rock formed of layers of different minerals, that breaks naturally into thin flat pieces（片岩）

scholar.meaning: a person who knows a lot about a particular subject because they have studied it in detail（学者）；a student who has been given a scholarship to study at a school, college or university（奖学金获得者）；(BrE) (informal) a clever person who works hard at school（聪颖勤奋的学生）

scholarly.meaning: (of a person（人）；spending a lot of time studying and having a lot of knowledge about an academic subject（勤奋好学的；有学问的）；connected with academic study（学术的；学术性的）

scholarship.meaning: an amount of money given to sb by an organization to help pay for their education（奖学金）；the serious study of an academic subject and the knowledge and methods involved（学问；学术；学术研究）

scholastic.meaning: connected with schools and education（学校的；教育的；学业的）；connected with scholasticism（经院哲学的）

school.meaning: a place where children go to be educated（（中、小）学校）；(used without the or a（不与 the 和 a 连用）；the process of learning in a school; the time during your life when you go to a school（上学；上学阶段）；the time during the day when children are working in a school（上课（或上学）时间）

schooling.meaning: the education you receive at school（学校教育）

science.meaning: knowledge about the structure and behaviour of the natural and physical world, based on facts that you can prove, for example by experiments（科学；自然科学）；the study of science（自然科学的学习与研究；理科）；a particular branch of science（自然科学学科）；a system for organizing the knowledge about a particular subject, especially one concerned with aspects of human behaviour or society（（尤指人文、社会）学科，学）

scientific.meaning: involving science; connected with science（科学（上）的；关于科学的）；(of a way of doing sth or thinking（做事或思想的方法）；careful and logical（细致严谨的；科学的）；sci·en·tif·ic·al·ly /ˌsaɪənˈtɪfɪkli; NAmEˌsaɪənˈtɪfɪkli/ adv. COLLOCATIONS 词语搭配Scientific research（科学研究）

scientist.meaning: a person who studies one or more of the natural sciences (= for example, physics, chemistry and biology)（科学家）

scissors.meaning: a tool for cutting paper or cloth, that has two sharp blades with handles, joined together in the middle（剪刀）；scis·sor /; NAmE/ adj. [only before noun] The legs move in a scissor action.（两腿像剪刀似地运动。）

sclerosis.meaning: a condition in which soft tissue in the body becomes hard, in a way that is not normal（硬化；硬化症）

scoff.meaning: to talk about sb/sth in a way that makes it clear that you think they are stupid or ridiculous（嘲笑；讥讽）；(informal) to eat a lot of sth quickly（贪婪地吃；狼吞虎咽）

scold.meaning: (formal) to speak angrily to sb, especially a child, because they have done sth wrong（训斥，责骂（尤指孩子））；scold·ing scolding scoldings /skəʊldɪŋ; NAmEskoʊldɪŋ/ noun [usually sing.] I got a scolding from my mother.（我挨了我妈一阵数落。）

scoop.meaning: a tool like a large spoon with a deep bowl, used for picking up substances in powder form like flour, or for serving food like ice cream（勺；铲子）；the amount picked up by a scoop（一勺（的量））；a piece of important or exciting news that is printed in one newspaper before other newspapers know about it（抢先报道的新闻；独家新闻）；(NAmE) (informal) the latest information about sb/sth, especially details that are not generally known（（尤指详情鲜为人知的）最新消息）

scope.meaning: the opportunity or ability to do or achieve sth（（做或实现某事的）机会，能力）；the range of things that a subject, an organization, an activity, etc. deals with（（题目、组织、活动等的）范围）；(in nouns（构成名词）；an instrument for looking through or watching sth with（… 镜（观察仪器））

scorch.meaning: to burn and slightly damage a surface by making it too hot; to be slightly burned by heat（（把 … ）烫坏，烧煳；烤焦（物体表面））；to become or to make sth become dry and brown, especially from the heat of the sun or from chemicals（（使）枯黄，枯萎（尤指因曝晒或化学品的作用））；(BrE) (informal) to move very fast（疾驰；飞驰）

scorching.meaning: very hot（酷热的）；(especially BrE) used to emphasize how strong, powerful, etc. sth is（猛烈的；激烈的；有力的）

score.meaning: the number of points, goals, etc. scored by each player or team in a game or competition（（游戏或比赛中的）得分，比分）；(especially NAmE) the number of points sb gets for correct answers in a test（（考试中的）分数，成绩）；a written or printed version of a piece of music showing what each instrument is to play or what each voice is to sing（总谱）；the music written for a film/movie or play（（电影或戏剧的）配乐）

scorn.meaning: a strong feeling that sb/sth is stupid or not good enough, usually shown by the way you speak（轻蔑；鄙视）；to speak about sb/sth in a way that shows that you do not respect them or have a good opinion of them（嗤之以鼻；不屑一顾）；to feel or show that you think sb/sth is stupid and you do not respect them or it（轻蔑；鄙视）；(formal) to refuse to have or do sth because you are too proud（不屑于（接受或做）；轻蔑地拒绝）

scornful.meaning: showing or feeling scorn（轻蔑的；鄙夷的）；scorn·ful·ly /ˈskɔːnfəli; NAmEˈskɔːrnfəli/ adv. She laughed scornfully.（她轻蔑地大笑。）

scotch.meaning: the type of whisky made in Scotland（苏格兰威士忌）；a glass of Scotch（一杯苏格兰威士忌）；of or connected with Scotland（苏格兰的）

scottish.meaning: of or connected with Scotland or its people（苏格兰的；苏格兰人的）

scour.meaning: to search a place or thing thoroughly in order to find sb/sth（（彻底地）搜寻，搜查，翻找）；to clean sth by rubbing its surface hard with rough material（（用粗糙的物体）擦净，擦亮）；to make a passage, hole, or mark in the ground, rocks, etc. as the result of movement, especially over a long period（冲刷成；冲刷出）

scout.meaning: an organization (officially called the Scout Association) originally for boys, which trains young people in practical skills and does a lot of activities with them, for example camping（童子军）；(BrE) a boy or girl who is a member of the Scouts（童子军成员）；a person, an aircraft, etc. sent ahead to get information about the enemy's position, strength, etc.（侦察员；侦察机）；to search an area or various areas in order to find or discover sth（侦察，搜寻（某处））

scowl.meaning: to look at sb/sth in an angry or annoyed way（怒视（某人或某物））；an angry look or expression（怒容；不悦的神色）

scraggly.meaning: thin and growing in a way that is not even（稀疏凌乱的；散乱的）

scramble.meaning: to move quickly, especially with difficulty, using your hands to help you（（迅速而吃力地）爬，攀登）；to push, fight or compete with others in order to get or to reach sth（争抢；抢占；争夺）；to manage to achieve sth with difficulty, or in a hurry, without much control（艰难地（或仓促地）完成）；to cook an egg by mixing the white and yellow parts together and heating them, sometimes with milk and butter（炒（蛋））

scrap.meaning: a small piece of sth, especially paper, cloth, etc.（碎片，小块（纸、织物等））；(usually with a negative（通常与否定式连用）；a small amount of sth（丝毫；一丁点）；food left after a meal（残羹剩饭）

scrape.meaning: to remove sth from a surface by moving sth sharp and hard like a knife across it（刮掉；削去）；to rub sth by accident so that it gets damaged or hurt（擦坏；擦伤；刮坏；蹭破）；to make an unpleasant noise by rubbing against a hard surface; to make sth do this（（使）发出刺耳的刮擦声）；to manage to win or to get sth with difficulty（艰难取得；勉强获得）

scraping.meaning: a small amount of sth produced by scratching a surface（刮屑；削片）

scratch.meaning: to rub your skin with your nails, usually because it is itching（挠，搔（痒处））；to cut or damage your skin slightly with sth sharp（划破，抓破，划伤，抓伤（皮肤））；to damage the surface of sth, especially by accident, by making thin shallow marks on it（（尤指意外地）擦破，划损，刮坏）；to make or remove a mark, etc. on sth deliberately, by rubbing it with sth hard or sharp（刮出（或刮去）痕迹；划下（或擦去）痕迹）

scream.meaning: to give a loud, high cry, because you are hurt, frightened, excited, etc.（（因伤痛、害怕、激动等）尖叫）；to shout sth in a loud, high voice because of fear, anger, etc.（（向某人或为某事）高声喊，大声叫）；to make a loud, high noise; to move fast, making this noise（发出大而尖的声音；呼啸而过）；to scream loudly and for a long time, especially in order to protest about sth（不停地叫嚷（尤指叫屈、鸣不平））

screech.meaning: to make a loud high unpleasant sound; to say sth using this sound（尖叫；发出尖锐刺耳的声音；尖声地说）；(of a vehicle（车辆）；to make a loud high unpleasant noise as it moves（（行驶时）发出刺耳声）；a loud high unpleasant cry or noise（刺耳的尖叫；尖锐刺耳的声音）

screen.meaning: the flat surface at the front of a television, computer, or other electronic device, on which you see pictures or information（屏幕；荧光屏）；the large flat surface that films/movies or pictures are shown on（银幕）；films/movies or television in general（（统称）电影，电视）；the data or images shown on a computer screen（（电脑屏幕上）一屏的内容；画面）

screening.meaning: the act of showing a film/movie or television programme（（电影的）放映；（电视节目的）播放）；the testing or examining of a large number of people or things for disease, faults, etc.（筛查）

screw.meaning: a thin pointed piece of metal like a nail with a raised spiral line (called a thread ) along it and a line or cross cut into its head. Screws are turned and pressed into wood, metal, etc. with a screwdriver in order to fasten two things together.（螺丝钉；螺丝）；an act of turning a screw（（对螺丝的）旋拧）；(taboo, slang) an act of having sex（性交）；(taboo, slang) a partner in sex（性交对象）

screwdriver.meaning: a tool with a narrow blade that is specially shaped at the end, used for turning screws（螺丝刀；改锥）；a cocktail (= an alcoholic drink) made from vodka and orange juice（伏特加橙汁鸡尾酒；螺丝刀（鸡尾酒））

script.meaning: a written text of a play, film/movie, broadcast, talk, etc.（剧本；电影剧本；广播（或讲话等）稿）；writing done by hand（笔迹）；a set of letters in which a language is written（（一种语言的）字母系统，字母表）；(BrE) a candidate's written answer or answers in an exam（笔试答卷）

scripture.meaning: the Bible（《圣经》）；the holy books of a particular religion（（某宗教的）圣典，经文，经典）；scrip·tural /ˈskrɪptʃərəl; NAmEˈskrɪptʃərəl/ adj. scriptural references（《圣经》引文）

scroll.meaning: a long roll of paper for writing on（（供书写的）长卷纸，卷轴）；a decoration cut in stone or wood with a curved shape like a roll of paper（（石刻或木雕的）涡卷形装饰）；(computing 计) to move text on a computer screen up or down so that you can read different parts of it（滚屏；滚动）

scrub.meaning: to clean sth by rubbing it hard, perhaps with a brush and usually with soap and water（擦洗；刷洗）；(informal) to cancel sth that you have arranged to do（取消（原有安排））；to remove sth from the surface of an object by rubbing it hard with a brush, etc.（（用刷子等）刷掉，擦掉）；to clean the inside of sth by rubbing it hard with a brush and usually with soap and water（（用刷子、肥皂等）把某物从里到外擦洗干净）

scruffy.meaning: dirty or untidy（不整洁的；邋遢的）

scruple.meaning: a feeling that prevents you from doing sth that you think may be morally wrong（（道德上的）顾忌，顾虑）；(formal) to be willing to do sth even if it might be wrong or immoral（无所顾忌地做；肆无忌惮地干）

scrupulous.meaning: careful about paying attention to every detail（仔细的；细致的；一丝不苟的）；careful to be honest and do what is right（审慎正直的；恪守道德规范的）；scru·pu·lous·ly /ˈskruːpjələsli; NAmEˈskruːpjələsli/ adv. Her house is scrupulously clean.（她的家干干净净，纤尘不染。）

scrutiny.meaning: careful and thorough examination（仔细检查；认真彻底的审查）

sculptor.meaning: a person who makes sculptures（雕刻家；雕塑家）

sculpture.meaning: a work of art that is a solid figure or object made by carving or shaping wood, stone, clay, metal, etc.（雕像；雕塑品；雕刻品）；the art of making sculptures（雕刻术；雕塑术）；sculp·tural /ˈskʌlptʃərəl; NAmEˈskʌlptʃərəl/ adj. sculptural decoration（雕饰）

scum.meaning: a layer of bubbles or an unpleasant substance that forms on the surface of a liquid（浮沫；浮垢；浮渣）；(informal) an insulting word for people that you strongly disapprove of（（骂人的话）渣滓，败类）；scummy scummy scummier scummiest /ˈskʌmi; NAmEˈskʌmi/ adj. scummy water（有浮垢的水）

scurry.meaning: to run with quick short steps（碎步疾跑）

sea.meaning: (especially BrE) the salt water that covers most of the earth's surface and surrounds its continents and islands（海；海洋）；(often Sea, especially as part of a name（常作 Sea，尤作名称的一部分）；a large area of salt water that is part of an ocean or surrounded by land（海）；the movement of the waves of the sea（海面情况；海浪状况）

seabed.meaning: the floor of the sea/ocean（海底；海床）

seabird.meaning: a bird that lives close to the sea, for example on cliffs or islands, and gets its food from it（海鸟）

seaboard.meaning: the part of a country that is along its coast（沿海地区；海滨）

seafood.meaning: fish and sea creatures that can be eaten, especially shellfish（海鲜，海味（尤指甲壳类））

seagoing.meaning: (of ships（船只）；built for crossing the sea/ocean（远洋航行的）

seal.meaning: to close an envelope, etc. by sticking the edges of the opening together（封上（信封））；to close a container tightly or fill a crack, etc., especially so that air, liquid, etc. cannot get in or out（密封（容器））；to cover the surface of sth with a substance in order to protect it（封盖 … 的表面）；to make sth definite, so that it cannot be changed or argued about（确定；明确定下来；使成定局）

seam.meaning: a line along which two edges of cloth, etc. are joined or sewn together（（缝合两块布等的）线缝，接缝）；a thin layer of coal or other material, between layers of rock under the ground（矿层；煤层）；a line where two edges meet, for example the edges of wooden boards（（合在一起的两块木板等之间的）接缝，缝隙，裂缝）；(informal) to be very full, especially of people（人满为患；使几乎胀破）

seaman.meaning: a member of the navy or a sailor on a ship below the rank of an officer（水兵；水手；海员）

seaport.meaning: a town with a harbour used by large ships（海港城市）

sear.meaning: to burn the surface of sth in a way that is sudden and powerful（烧灼；灼伤；烤焦；轻煎）；(formal) to cause sb to feel sudden and great pain（使骤然感到剧痛）

search.meaning: an attempt to find sb/sth, especially by looking carefully for them/it（搜索；搜寻；搜查；查找）；(computing 计) an act of looking for information in a computer database or network（搜索；检索）；to look carefully for sth/sb; to examine a particular place when looking for sb/sth（搜索；搜寻；搜查；查找）；(especially of the police（尤指警察）

seashell.meaning: the shell of a small creature that lives in the sea, often found empty when the creature has died（海贝壳）

seashore.meaning: the land along the edge of the sea or ocean, usually where there is sand and rocks（海岸；海滨）

seaside.meaning: an area that is by the sea, especially one where people go for a day or a holiday/vacation（（尤指人们游玩、度假的）海边，海滨）；sea·side adj. [only before noun] a seaside resort（海滨胜地）

season.meaning: any of the four main periods of the year: spring, summer, autumn/fall and winter（季；季节）；a period of the year in tropical countries when it is either very dry or it rains a lot（（热带地区的）旱/雨季）；a period of time during a year when a particular activity happens or is done（（一年中开展某项活动的）季节，旺季）；a period of time in which a play is shown in one place; a series of plays, films/movies or television programmes（（一部戏剧在一地的）演出期，上演期；（一系列的戏剧、电影或电视节目的）会演，荟萃）

seasonal.meaning: happening or needed during a particular season; varying with the seasons（季节性的；随季节变化的）；typical of or suitable for the time of year, especially Christmas（节令性的；适应节日需要的；（尤指）圣诞节的）；sea·son·al·ly /ˈsiːzənəli; NAmEˈsiːzənəli/ adv. seasonally adjusted unemployment figures (= not including the changes that always happen in different seasons)（经季节因素调整的失业统计数字）

seat.meaning: a place where you can sit, for example a chair（座位，坐处（如椅子等））；(in nouns and adjectives（构成名词和形容词）；with the number of seats mentioned（有 … 座位的；有 … 座的）；the part of a chair, etc. on which you actually sit（（椅子等的）座部）

seaway.meaning: a passage from the sea through the land along which large ships can travel（海道（大型海轮可航行的通海河道））

seaweed.meaning: a plant that grows in the sea or ocean, or on rocks at the edge of the sea or ocean. There are many different types of seaweed, some of which are eaten as food.（海草；海藻）

seclude.meaning: (formal) to keep yourself/sb away from contact with other people（（使）与 … 隔离，与 … 隔绝；（使）隐居，独处）

secluded.meaning: (of a place（地方）；quiet and private; not used or disturbed by other people（僻静的；清静的；不受打扰的）；without much contact with other people（隐居的；与世隔绝的）

seclusion.meaning: the state of being private or of having little contact with other people（清静；隐居；与世隔绝）

second.meaning: happening or coming next after the first in a series of similar things or people; 2nd（第二（的））；next in order of importance, size, quality, etc. to one other person or thing（（重要性、规模、质量等）居第二位的）；another; in addition to one that you already own or use（另外的；外加的）；after one other person or thing in order or importance（以第二名；以第二位）

secondary.meaning: less important than sth else（次要的；从属的；辅助的）；happening as a result of sth else（间接引发的；继发性的；次生的）；connected with teaching children of 11-18 years（中等教育的；中学的）；sec·ond·ar·ily /ˈsekəndrəli; NAmEˌsekənˈderəli/ adv. Their clothing is primarily functional and only secondarily decorative.（他们的衣服首重实用，其次才讲花式。）

second-hand.meaning: not new; owned by sb else before（旧的；用过的；二手的）；(of news, information, etc.（消息、信息等）；learned from other people, not from your own experience（间接得来的；二手的）；ˌsecond-ˈhand adv. I bought the camera second-hand.（我买的这架照相机是二手货。）

secondly.meaning: used to introduce the second of a list of points you want to make in a speech or piece of writing（（用于列举）第二，其次）

secrecy.meaning: the fact of making sure that nothing is known about sth; the state of being secret（保密；秘密）

secret.meaning: known about by only a few people; kept hidden from others（秘密的；保密的；外人不得而知的）；used to describe actions and behaviour that you do not tell other people about（（指行为与习惯）暗中进行的，未公开的，隐秘的）；(of a person or their behaviour（人或行为）；liking to have secrets that other people do not know about; showing this（诡秘；神秘）

secretarial.meaning: involving or connected with the work of a secretary（秘书的；文秘工作的）

secretariat.meaning: the department of a large international or political organization which is responsible for running it, especially the office of a Secretary General（（大型国际组织、政治组织的）秘书处，书记处）

secretary.meaning: a person who works in an office, working for another person, dealing with letters and telephone calls, typing, keeping records, arranging meetings with people, etc.（秘书）；an official of a club, society, etc. who deals with writing letters, keeping records, and making business arrangements（（俱乐部、社团等的）干事，文书）；(US) the head of a government department, chosen by the President（部长；大臣）；(in Britain) an assistant of a government minister, an ambassador, etc.（（英国的大臣、大使等的）助理）

secrete.meaning: (of part of the body or a plant（身体或植物器官）；to produce a liquid substance（分泌）；(formal) to hide sth, especially sth small（隐藏，藏匿（小物件））

secretion.meaning: the process by which liquid substances are produced by parts of the body or plants（分泌）；a liquid substance produced by parts of the body or plants（分泌物）

secretive.meaning: tending or liking to hide your thoughts, feelings, ideas, etc. from other people（（思想、情感等）不外露的；惯于掩藏自己的；有城府的）

sect.meaning: a small group of people who belong to a particular religion but who have some beliefs or practices which separate them from the rest of the group（派别；宗派）

section.meaning: any of the parts into which sth is divided（部分；部门）；a separate part of a structure from which the whole can be put together（部件；散件）；a separate part of a document, book, etc.（节；款；项；段；部分）；a separate group within a larger group of people（阶层；界；组）

sectional.meaning: connected with one particular group within a community or an organization（（社团或组织中）某群体的，某阶层的）；made of separate sections（组合式的）；connected with a cross section of sth (= a surface or an image formed by cutting through sth from top to bottom)（剖面的；断面的）

sector.meaning: a part of an area of activity, especially of a country's economy（（尤指一国经济的）部门，领域，行业）；a part of a particular area, especially an area under military control（（尤指军事管制的）区域，地带）；(geometry 几何) a part of a circle lying between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the edge（扇形）

secular.meaning: not connected with spiritual or religious matters（现世的；世俗的；非宗教的）；(of priests（司祭）；living among ordinary people rather than in a religious community（教区的；在俗的）

secure.meaning: feeling happy and confident about yourself or a particular situation（安心的；有把握的）；likely to continue or be successful for a long time（可靠的；牢靠的；稳固的）；that cannot be affected or harmed by sth（安全的；稳妥的）；guarded and/or made stronger so that it is difficult for people to enter or leave（严密把守的；牢固的；坚固的）

security.meaning: the activities involved in protecting a country, building or person against attack, danger, etc.（保护措施；安全工作）；the department of a large company or organization that deals with the protection of its buildings, equipment and staff（保卫部门；保安部门）；protection against sth bad that might happen in the future（担保；保证）；the state of feeling happy and safe from danger or worry（安全；平安）

sedentary.meaning: (of work, activities, etc.（工作、活动等）；in which you spend a lot of time sitting down（需要久坐的）；(of people（人）；spending a lot of time sitting down and not moving（惯于久坐不动的）

sedge.meaning: a plant like grass that grows in wet ground or near water（莎草；苔）

sediment.meaning: the solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid（沉淀物）；(geology 地) sand, stones, mud, etc. carried by water or wind and left, for example, on the bottom of a lake, river, etc.（沉积物）

sedimentary.meaning: connected with or formed from the sand, stones, mud, etc. that settle at the bottom of lakes, etc.（沉积的；沉积形成的）

sedimentation.meaning: the process of depositing sediment（沉积（过程））

seduce.meaning: to persuade sb to have sex with you, especially sb who is younger or who has less experience than you（诱奸）；to persuade sb to do sth that they would not usually agree to do by making it seem very attractive（诱骗；唆使）

seductive.meaning: sexually attractive（诱人的；迷人的；有魅力的；性感的）；attractive in a way that makes you want to have or do sth（有吸引力的；令人神往的）

see.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to become aware of sb/sth by using your eyes（看见；见到；看出）；(not usually used in the progressive tenses（通常不用于进行时）；to have or use the power of sight（看得见；看；有视力）

seed.meaning: the small hard part produced by a plant, from which a new plant can grow（种子；籽）；the beginning of a feeling or a development which continues to grow（起源；起因；萌芽；开端）；(especially in tennis（尤指网球）；one of the best players in a competition. The seeds are given a position in a list to try and make sure that they do not play each other in the early parts of the competition.（种子选手）

seedling.meaning: a young plant that has grown from a seed（秧苗；籽苗；幼苗）

seedy.meaning: dirty and unpleasant, possibly connected with immoral or illegal activities（肮脏的；污七八糟的；乌烟瘴气的；下流的）

seek.meaning: to look for sth/sb（寻找）；to try to obtain or achieve sth（寻求；谋求；争取）；to ask sb for sth（（向人）请求，寻求）；to try to do sth（试图；设法）

seeker.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a person who is trying to find or get the thing mentioned（寻找者；寻求者；追求者；谋求者）

seem.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to give the impression of being or doing sth（（给人印象）好像，似乎，看来）；used to make what you say about your thoughts, feelings or actions less strong（（用以缓和语气）感到好像，觉得似乎）；used to suggest that sth is true when you are not certain or when you want to be polite（（表示不确切或客气）看来好像，似乎）

seeming.meaning: appearing to be sth that may not be true（看似 …（而实际未必）的；表面上的；貌似 … 的）

seemingly.meaning: in a way that appears to be true but may in fact not be（看似；貌似；表面上）；(formal) according to what you have read or heard（据说；听说；看来）

seep.meaning: (especially of liquids（尤指液体）；to flow slowly and in small quantities through sth or into sth（渗；渗透）

seepage.meaning: the process by which a liquid flows slowly and in small quantities through sth; the result of this process（渗；渗透；渗液）

segment.meaning: a part of sth that is separate from the other parts or can be considered separately（部分；份；片；段）；one of the sections of an orange, a lemon, etc.（（柑橘、柠檬等的）瓣）；(geometry 几何) a part of a circle separated from the rest by a single line（弓形；圆缺）；(phonetics 语音) the smallest speech sound that a word can be divided into（音段）

segmental.meaning: relating to the individual sounds that make up speech, as opposed to prosodic features such as stress and intonation（音段的）

segregate.meaning: to separate people of different races, religions or sexes and treat them in a different way（隔离并区别对待（不同种族、宗教或性别的人））；to keep one thing separate from another（（使）分开，分离，隔离）

seismic.meaning: connected with or caused by earthquakes（地震的；地震引起的）；having a very great effect; of very great size（影响深远的；重大的）

seize.meaning: to take sb/sth in your hand suddenly and using force（抓住；捉住；夺）；to take control of a place or situation, often suddenly and violently（（常指通过暴力突然）夺取，攻占，控制）；to arrest or capture sb（逮捕；捉拿；俘获）；to take illegal or stolen goods away from sb（起获；没收；扣押）

seizure.meaning: the use of legal authority to take sth from sb; an amount of sth that is taken in this way（起获；没收；充公；起获的赃物；没收的财产）；the act of using force to take control of a country, town, etc.（夺取；占领；控制）；a sudden attack of an illness, especially one that affects the brain（（疾病，尤指脑病的）突然侵袭，发作）

select.meaning: to choose sb/sth from a group of people or things, usually according to a system（选择；挑选；选拔）；(computing 计) to mark sth on a computer screen; to choose sth, especially from a menu（（在计算机屏幕上）选定；（从菜单中）选择，选取）；carefully chosen as the best out of a larger group of people or things（精选的；作为 … 精华的；优等的）；(of a society, club, place, etc.（社团、俱乐部、地方等）

selection.meaning: the process of choosing sb/sth from a group of people or things, usually according to a system（选择；挑选；选拔）；a number of people or things that have been chosen from a larger group（被挑选的人（或物）；被选中者；入选者）；a collection of things from which sth can be chosen（可供选择的事物）

selective.meaning: affecting or concerned with only a small number of people or things from a larger group（选择性的；有选择的）；tending to be careful about what or who you choose（认真挑选的；严格筛选的）；se·lect·ive·ly AW /sɪˈlektɪvli; NAmEsɪˈlektɪvli/ adv. The product will be selectively marketed in the US (= only in some areas).（这种产品将有选择地投放到美国某些地区的市场。）；se·lect·iv·ity /səˌlekˈtɪvəti; NAmEsəˌlekˈtɪvəti/ noun [U] Schools are tending towards greater selectivity.（学校对新生的选拔有趋严之势。）

selenium.meaning: a chemical element. Selenium is a grey substance that is used in making electrical equipment and coloured glass. A lack of selenium in the human body can lead to illnesses such as depression.（硒（化学元素，用于制造电气设备和有色玻璃，人体缺此元素可致抑郁等病））

self.meaning: the type of person you are, especially the way you normally behave, look or feel（（自己的）通常的行为方式，本来面目，惯常心态）；(formal) a person's personality or character that makes them different from other people（个性；自我）；(formal) your own advantage or pleasure rather than that of other people（个人利益；一己的享乐；私心）；used to refer to a person（（指一个人）自己，本人）

self-.meaning: (in nouns and adjectives（构成名词和形容词）；of, to or by yourself or itself（自身的；对自身；由自身）

self-educated.meaning: having learned things by reading books, etc. rather than at school or college（自我教育的；自学的；自修的）

self-expression.meaning: the expression of your thoughts or feelings, especially through activities such as writing, painting, dancing, etc.（自我表现，自我表达（尤指通过写作、绘画、舞蹈等活动））

self-image.meaning: the opinion or idea you have of yourself, especially of your appearance or abilities（自我形象；自我印象）

selfish.meaning: caring only about yourself rather than about other people（自私的）；self·ish·ly /ˈselfɪʃli; NAmEˈselfɪʃli/ adv. She looked forward, a little selfishly, to a weekend away from her family.（她有点自私，就盼着能够离家在外边度个周末。）

selfless.meaning: thinking more about the needs, happiness, etc. of other people than about your own（无私的）

self-sufficient.meaning: able to do or produce everything that you need without the help of other people（自给自足的；自立的）

self-taught.meaning: having learned sth by reading books, etc., rather than by sb teaching you（自学的；自修的）

sell.meaning: to give sth to sb in exchange for money（出让；转让）；to offer sth for people to buy（出售；售卖）；to be bought by people in the way or in the numbers mentioned; to be offered at the price mentioned（销售得 … ；卖出 … ；售价是 …）；to make people want to buy sth（促销；推销）

seller.meaning: a person who sells sth（卖者；销售者；卖方）；a product that has been sold in the amounts or way mentioned（（畅销、滞销等的）商品）；a situation in which people selling sth have an advantage, because there is not a lot of a particular item for sale, and prices can be kept high（卖方市场）

semblance.meaning: (formal) a situation in which sth seems to exist although this may not, in fact, be the case（表象；假象；外观；外貌）

semester.meaning: one of the two periods that the school or college year is divided into（学期（一学年分两个学期））

semiconductor.meaning: a solid substance that conducts electricity in particular conditions, better than insulators but not as well as conductors（半导体）；a device containing a semiconductor used in electronics（半导体装置）

seminar.meaning: a class at a university or college when a small group of students and a teacher discuss or study a particular topic（（大学教师带领学生作专题讨论的）研讨班）；a meeting for discussion or training（研讨会；培训会）

semitic.meaning: of or connected with the language group that includes Hebrew and Arabic（闪米特语族的，闪语的（包括希伯来语和阿拉伯语））；of or connected with the people who speak Semitic languages, especially Hebrew and Arabic（闪米特人（尤指操希伯来语和阿拉伯语的人）的；闪族的）

senate.meaning: one of the two groups of elected politicians who make laws in some countries, for example in the US, Australia, Canada and France. The Senate is smaller than the other group but higher in rank. Many state parliaments in the US also have a Senate.（参议院（美国、澳大利亚、加拿大、法国等国家的两个立法机构之一；美国许多州议会也设有参议院））；(in some countries) the group of people who control a university（（某些国家的）大学理事会，大学评议会）；(in ancient Rome) the most important council of the government; the building where the council met（（古罗马的）元老院）

senator.meaning: a member of a senate（参议员）；sen·at·or·ial /ˌsenəˈtɔːriəl; NAmEˌsenəˈtɔːriəl/ adj. [only before noun] a senatorial candidate（参议员候选人）

send.meaning: to make sth go or be taken to a place, especially by post/mail, email, radio, etc.（邮寄；发送）；to tell sb sth by sending them a message（传达；转致；告知）；to tell sb to go somewhere or to do sth; to arrange for sb to go somewhere（派遣；打发；安排去）；to make sth/sb move quickly or suddenly（使快速（或猛然）移动）

sender.meaning: a person who sends sth（发送人；邮寄人）

senior.meaning: high in rank or status; higher in rank or status than others（级别（或地位）高的）；for adults or people at a more advanced level（成人的；高级水平的）；for senior citizens (= older people, especially those who have retired from work)（年纪大的；老年的；年老的）；used after the name of a man who has the same name as his son, to avoid confusion（（父子同名时，加在父亲的名字前）老）

seniority.meaning: the fact of being older or of a higher rank than others（年长；级别高）；the rank that you have in a company because of the length of time you have worked there（资历）

sensation.meaning: a feeling that you get when sth affects your body（感觉；知觉）；the ability to feel through your sense of touch（感觉能力；知觉能力）；a general feeling or impression that is difficult to explain; an experience or a memory（直觉；莫名其妙的感觉；经历；回忆）；very great surprise, excitement, or interest among a lot of people; the person or the thing that causes this surprise（轰动；哗然；引起轰动的人（或事物））

sensational.meaning: causing great surprise, excitement, or interest（轰动的；引起哗然的）；(of a newspaper, etc.（报章等）；trying to get your interest by presenting facts or events as worse or more shocking than they really are（哗众取宠的；耸人听闻的）；(informal) extremely good; wonderful（极好的；绝妙的）

sensationalism.meaning: a way of getting people's interest by using shocking words or by presenting facts and events as worse or more shocking than they really are（（指行文或报道）耸人听闻，哗众取宠）；sen·sa·tion·al·ist /senˈseɪʃənəlɪst; NAmEsenˈseɪʃənəlɪst/ adj. sensationalist headlines（耸人听闻的标题）

sense.meaning: one of the five powers (sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch) that your body uses to get information about the world around you（感觉官能（即视、听、嗅、味、触五觉））；a feeling about sth important（（对重大事情的）感觉，意识）；an understanding about sth; an ability to judge sth（理解力；判断力）；good understanding and judgement; knowledge of what is sensible or practical behaviour（见识；良好的判断；清醒的认识）

senseless.meaning: (disapproving) having no meaning or purpose（无意义的；无目的的）；unconscious（失去知觉）；not using good judgement（不明智的；愚蠢的）

sensibility.meaning: the ability to experience and understand deep feelings, especially in art and literature（（尤指文艺方面的）感受能力，鉴赏力，敏感性）；a person's feelings, especially when the person is easily offended or influenced by sth（（尤指易受伤害或影响的）感情）

sensible.meaning: (of people and their behaviour（人及行为）；able to make good judgements based on reason and experience rather than emotion; practical（明智的；理智的；合理的；切合实际的）；(of clothes, etc.（服装等）；useful rather than fashionable（朴素而实用的）

sensitive.meaning: aware of and able to understand other people and their feelings（体贴的；体恤的；善解人意的）；able to understand art, music and literature and to express yourself through them（感觉敏锐的；艺术感觉好的；有悟性的）；easily offended or upset（易生气的；易被惹恼的；神经过敏的）；that you have to treat with great care because it may offend people or make them angry or embarrassed（须谨慎对待的；敏感的）

sensitivity.meaning: the ability to understand other people's feelings（体贴；体恤；体察）；the ability to understand art, music and literature and to express yourself through them（敏锐的感觉；悟性）；a tendency to be easily offended or upset by sth（容易生气；易被惹恼；敏感）；the fact of needing to be treated very carefully because it may offend or upset people（敏感性）

sensor.meaning: a device that can react to light, heat, pressure, etc. in order to make a machine, etc. do sth or show sth（（探测光、热、压力等的）传感器，敏感元件，探测设备）

sensory.meaning: connected with your physical senses（感觉的；感官的）

sentence.meaning: (grammar 语法) a set of words expressing a statement, a question or an order, usually containing a subject and a verb. In written English sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop/period (.), a question mark (?) or an exclamation mark/exclamation point (!).（句子）；the punishment given by a court（判决；宣判；判刑）；to say officially in court that sb is to receive a particular punishment（判决；宣判；判刑）

sentiment.meaning: (formal) a feeling or an opinion, especially one based on emotions（（基于情感的）观点，看法；情绪）；(sometimes disapproving) feelings of pity, romantic love, sadness, etc. which may be too strong or not appropriate（（失之过度或不恰当的）伤感，柔情，哀伤）

sentimental.meaning: connected with your emotions, rather than reason（情感的（而非理性的））；(often disapproving) producing emotions such as pity, romantic love or sadness, which may be too strong or not appropriate; feeling these emotions too much（（失之过度或不恰当地）伤感的，充满柔情的；多愁善感的）

sepal.meaning: a part of a flower, like a leaf, that lies under and supports the petals (= the delicate coloured parts that make up the head of the flower). Each flower has a ring of sepals called a calyx.（萼片）

separable.meaning: that can be separated from sth, or considered separately（可分开的；可分隔的；可分离的）；(of a phrasal verb（短语动词）；that can be used with the object going either between the verb and the particle or after the particle（可分离的；可分开的；可分的）

separate.meaning: forming a unit by itself; not joined to sth else（单独的；独立的；分开的）；different; not connected（不同的；不相关的）；sep·ar·ate·ness noun [U, sing.] Japan's long-standing sense of separateness and uniqueness（日本那种由来已久的自成一体、孑然独立的意识）；to end a relationship with sb（断绝往来；分道扬镳）

separated.meaning: no longer living with your husband, wife or partner（（和某人）分居的）

separately.meaning: as a separate person or thing; not together（单独地；分别地）

separation.meaning: the act of separating people or things; the state of being separate（分离；分开；分割；隔离）；a period of time that people spend apart from each other（离别）；a decision that a husband and wife make to live apart while they are still legally married（分居）

separatist.meaning: a member of a group of people within a country who want to separate from the rest of the country and form their own government（分离主义者；独立主义者）；sep·ar·at·ism /ˈseprətɪzəm; NAmEˈseprətɪzəm/ noun [U] sep·ar·at·ist adj. a separatist movement（分离主义运动）

september.meaning: the 9th month of the year, between August and October（九月）

septic.meaning: (of a wound or part of the body（伤口或身体部分）；infected with harmful bacteria（感染病菌的；脓毒性的；腐败性的）

sequence.meaning: a set of events, actions, numbers, etc. which have a particular order and which lead to a particular result（一系列；一连串）；the order that events, actions, etc. happen in or should happen in（顺序；次序）；a part of a film/movie that deals with one subject or topic or consists of one scene（（电影中表现同一主题或场面的）一组镜头）；(technical 术语) to arrange things into a sequence（按顺序排列）

sequential.meaning: following in order of time or place（按次序的；顺序的；序列的）；se·quen·tial·ly AW /sɪˈkwenʃəli; NAmEsɪˈkwenʃəli/ adv. data stored sequentially on a computer（顺序存贮在计算机里的数据）

sequester.meaning: to keep a jury together in a place, in order to prevent them from talking to other people about a court case, or learning about it in the newspapers, on television, etc.（隔离（避免陪审团与公众接触））

sequoia.meaning: a very tall N American tree, a type of redwood（红杉）

serene.meaning: calm and peaceful（平静的；宁静的；安详的）；se·rene·ly /səˈriːnli; NAmEsəˈriːnli/ adv. serenely beautiful（宁静而美丽）；se·ren·ity serenity serenities /səˈrenəti; NAmEsəˈrenəti/ noun [U, sing.] The hotel offers a haven of peace and serenity away from the bustle of the city.（那家旅馆远离闹市，是一个幽静安谧的好去处。）

serial.meaning: a story on television or the radio, or in a magazine, that is broadcast or published in several separate parts（电视连续剧；广播连续剧；杂志连载小说）；(technical 术语) arranged in a series（顺序排列的；排成系列的）；doing the same thing in the same way several times（连续的；多次的）；(of a story, etc.（小说等）

series.meaning: several events or things of a similar kind that happen one after the other（一系列；连续；接连）；a set of radio or television programmes that deal with the same subject or that have the same characters（（广播或电视上题材或角色相同的）系列节目）；(sport 体) a set of sports games played between the same two teams（（两队之间的）系列比赛）；(technical 术语) an electrical circuit in which the current passes through all the parts in the correct order（串联）

serious.meaning: bad or dangerous（不好的；严重的；有危险的）；needing to be thought about carefully; not only for pleasure（需认真思考的；严肃的）；that must be treated as important（重要的；须重视的）；thinking about things in a careful and sensible way; not silly（严肃的；稳重的）

seriously.meaning: in a serious way（严重地；严肃地；认真地）；used at the beginning of a sentence to show a change from joking to being more serious（（用于句首，表示转为谈正事）说正经的，说实在的）；(informal) very; extremely（非常；极其）；to think that sb/sth is important and deserves your attention and respect（认真对待）

seriousness.meaning: the state of being serious（严重；认真；严肃）；very seriously; not as a joke（非常严肃地；认认真真地；说实在的）

sermon.meaning: a talk on a moral or religious subject, usually given by a religious leader during a service（布道；讲道）；(informal, usually disapproving) moral advice that a person tries to give you in a long talk（冗长的说教）

serpent.meaning: a snake, especially a large one（蛇；（尤指）大蛇）

serpentine.meaning: bending and twisting like a snake（弯弯曲曲的；蜿蜒的；盘旋的；迂回的）

serum.meaning: (biology 生) the thin liquid that remains from blood when the rest has clotted（血清）；(medical 医) serum taken from the blood of an animal and given to people to protect them from disease, poison, etc.（免疫血清）；any liquid like water in body tissue（浆液（体液的水样部分））

servant.meaning: a person who works in another person's house, and cooks, cleans, etc. for them（仆人；用人）；a person who works for a company or an organization（（公司或机构的）雇员，职员）；a person or thing that is controlled by sth（奴仆般受制（或献身）于 … 的人；服务于 … 的事物）

serve.meaning: to give sb food or drink, for example at a restaurant or during a meal（（给某人）提供；端上）；(of an amount of food（食物的量）；to be enough for sb/sth（够 … 吃（或用））；(especially BrE) to help a customer or sell them sth in a shop/store（接待；服务）

server.meaning: (computing 计) a computer program that controls or supplies information to several computers connected in a network; the main computer on which this program is run（服务器；伺服器）；(sport 体) a player who is serving, for example in tennis（发球者）；a kitchen utensil (= tool) used for putting food onto sb's plate（上菜用具（往各人盘子里盛食物的叉、铲、勺等））；(NAmE) a person who serves food in a restaurant; a waiter or waitress（（餐馆给顾客上菜的）侍者）

service.meaning: a system that provides sth that the public needs, organized by the government or a private company（公共服务系统；公共事业）；an organization or a company that provides sth for the public or does sth for the government（公共事业机构（或公司））；a business whose work involves doing sth for customers but not producing goods; the work that such a business does（服务性企业（或行业、业务））；the serving of customers in hotels, restaurants, and shops/stores（（对顾客的）接待，服务）

serving.meaning: an amount of food for one person（（供一个人吃的）一份食物）

session.meaning: a period of time that is spent doing a particular activity（一场；一节；一段时间）；a formal meeting or series of meetings of a court, a parliament, etc; a period of time when such meetings are held（（法庭的）开庭，开庭期；（议会等的）会议，会期）；a school or university year（学年）；an occasion when people meet to play music, especially Irish music, in a pub/bar（（酒吧中）演奏会（尤指演奏爱尔兰音乐））

set.meaning: to put sth/sb in a particular place or position（放；置；使处于）；to cause sb/sth to be in a particular state; to start sth happening（使处于某种状况；使开始）；to place the action of a play, novel or film/movie in a particular place, time, etc.（把故事情节安排在；以 … 为 … 设置背景）；to prepare or arrange sth so that it is ready for use or in position（设置；调整好；安排就绪）

setback.meaning: a difficulty or problem that delays or prevents sth, or makes a situation worse（挫折；阻碍）

setting.meaning: a set of surroundings; the place at which sth happens（环境；背景）；the place and time at which the action of a play, novel, etc. takes place（（戏剧、小说等的）情节背景）；a position at which the controls on a machine can be set, to set the speed, height, temperature, etc.（（机器上调节速度、高度、温度等的）挡，级，点）；(music 音) music written to go with a poem, etc.（（为诗等谱的）曲）

settle.meaning: to put an end to an argument or a disagreement（结束（争论、争端等）；解决（分歧、纠纷等））；to decide or arrange sth finally（（最终）决定，确定，安排好）；to make a place your permanent home（定居）；(of a group of people（一批人）

settlement.meaning: an official agreement that ends an argument between two people or groups（（解决纷争的）协议）；the action of reaching an agreement（解决；处理）；(law 律) the conditions, or a document stating the conditions, on which money or property is given to sb（（关于钱财转让的）协议（书））；the action of paying back money that you owe（（欠款的）支付，偿付，结算）

seven.meaning: (informal, humorous) the desire for new sexual experience that is thought to be felt after seven years of marriage（七年之痒（婚后七年另觅新欢的欲望））

seventeen.meaning: seven·teenth seventeenth seventeenths /ˌsevnˈtiːnθ; NAmEˌsevnˈtiːnθ/ ordinal number, noun HELP There are examples of how to use ordinal numbers at the entry for fifth.（序数词用法示例见 fifth 条。）

seventh.meaning: th（第七）；extremely happy（身处七重天；极乐；极为幸福）；each of seven equal parts of sth（七分之一）

seventy.meaning: numbers, years or temperatures from 70 to 79（七十几；七十年代）；seven·ti·eth seventieth seventieths /ˈsevntiəθ; NAmEˈsevntiəθ/ ordinal number, noun HELP There are examples of how to use ordinal numbers at the entry for fifth.（序数词用法示例见 fifth 条。）；between the ages of 70 and 79（*）

several.meaning: more than two but not very many（几个；数个；一些）；(formal) separate（各自的；分别的）

severe.meaning: extremely bad or serious（极为恶劣的；十分严重的）；punishing sb in an extreme way when they break a particular set of rules（严厉的；重的）；not kind or sympathetic and showing disapproval of sb/sth（严厉的；苛刻的）；extremely difficult and requiring a lot of skill or ability（艰难的；艰巨的；难度很大的）

sew.meaning: to use a needle and thread to make stitches in cloth（缝；做针线活）；to make, repair or attach sth using a needle and thread（缝制；缝补；缝上）；to join or repair sth by sewing（缝合；缝补）；(informal) to arrange sth in an acceptable way（安排妥贴；办好；使万无一失）

sewage.meaning: used water and waste substances that are produced by human bodies, that are carried away from houses and factories through special pipes (= sewers)（（下水道的）污水，污物）

sewer.meaning: an underground pipe that is used to carry sewage away from houses, factories, etc.（污水管；下水道；阴沟）

sewerage.meaning: the system by which sewage is carried away from houses, factories, etc. and is cleaned and made safe by adding chemicals to it（排水系统；污水处理）

sewing.meaning: the activity of making, repairing or decorating things made of cloth using a needle and thread（缝纫）；something that is being sewn（缝制中的衣物）

sex.meaning: the state of being male or female（性别；性）；either of the two groups that people, animals and plants are divided into according to their function of producing young（男性；女性；雄性；雌性）；physical activity between two people in which they touch each other's sexual organs, and which may include sexual intercourse（性行为；性交；性活动）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）

sexual.meaning: connected with the physical activity of sex（性行为的；性的）；connected with the process of producing young（生殖的；有性繁殖的）；connected with the state of being male or female（性别的；性的）；sex·ual·ly ★ AW /ˈsekʃəli; NAmEˈsekʃəli/ adv. sexually abused children（受到性虐待的儿童）

sexuality.meaning: the feelings and activities connected with a person's sexual desires（性征；性感觉；性欲；性行为）

sexy.meaning: (of a person（人）；sexually attractive（性感的）；sexually exciting（引起性欲的；性感的）；sexually excited（性欲发作的；性兴奋的）

shabby.meaning: (of buildings, clothes, objects, etc.（建筑物、衣服、物品等）；in poor condition because they have been used a lot（破旧的；破败的；破烂的）；(of a person（人）；badly dressed in clothes that have been worn a lot（衣着破旧的）

shack.meaning: a small building, usually made of wood or metal, that has not been built well（简陋的小屋；棚屋）；(slang) to start/be living with sb that you have a sexual relationship with, but that you are not married to（和（性伴侣）同居）

shade.meaning: an area that is dark and cool under or behind sth, for example a tree or building, because the sun's light does not get to it（阴凉处；背阴；（树）阴）；a thing that you use to prevent light from coming through or to make it less bright（灯罩）；a particular form of a colour, that is, how dark or light it is（浓淡深浅；色度）；the dark areas in a picture, especially the use of these to produce variety（暗部；阴影部分）

shadow.meaning: the dark shape that sb/sth's form makes on a surface, for example on the ground, when they are between the light and the surface（阴影；影子）；darkness in a place or on sth, especially so that you cannot easily see who or what is there（昏暗处；背光处；阴暗处）；a very small amount of sth（少许；些微；一丁点）；the strong (usually bad) influence of sb/sth（（坏）影响）

shadowy.meaning: dark and full of shadows（阴暗的；幽暗的；阴影中的；多阴的）；difficult to see because there is not much light（昏暗的；朦胧的；模糊的）；that not much is known about（鲜为人知的；神秘莫测的）

shady.meaning: protected from direct light from the sun by trees, buildings, etc.（背阴的；阴凉的；多阴的）；(of a tree, etc.（树等）；providing shade from the sun（成荫的）；(informal) seeming to be dishonest or illegal（可疑的；鬼祟的；非法的）

shaft.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a long, narrow, usually vertical passage in a building or underground, used especially for a lift/elevator or as a way of allowing air in or out（（电梯的）升降机井；通风井；竖井；井筒）；the long narrow part of an arrow, hammer, golf club, etc.（（箭、高尔夫球杆等的）杆；（锤等的）柄）；a metal bar that joins parts of a machine or an engine together, enabling power and movement to be passed from one part to another（（机器的）轴）

shake.meaning: to move or make sb/sth move with short quick movements from side to side or up and down（摇动；抖动；（使）颤动）；to move sth in a particular direction by shaking（摇（出）；抖（掉））；to turn your head from side to side as a way of saying ‘no’ or to show sadness, disapproval, doubt, etc.（摇头）；to take sb's hand and move it up and down as a way of saying hello or to show that you agree about sth（（与某人）握手）

shaky.meaning: shaking and feeling weak because you are ill/sick, emotional or old（颤抖的；颤巍巍的）；not firm or safe; not certain（不稳固的；不牢靠的；摇晃的；不确切的）；not seeming very successful; likely to fail（不大出色的；成问题的；可能失败的）；shaki·ly /ˈʃeɪkɪli; NAmEˈʃeɪkɪli/ adv. ‘Get the doctor,’ he whispered shakily.（“去请大夫。”他颤声低语说。）

shale.meaning: a type of soft stone that splits easily into thin flat layers（页岩）

shall.meaning: (becoming old-fashioned) used with I and we for talking about or predicting the future（（同 I 和 we 连用，表示将来）将要，将会）；used in questions with I and we for making offers or suggestions or asking advice（（在疑问句中同 I 和 we 连用，表示提出或征求意见））；(old-fashioned or formal) used to show that you are determined, or to give an order or instruction（（表示决心、命令或指示）必须，一定，应该）

shallow.meaning: not having much distance between the top or surface and the bottom（浅的）；(of a person, an idea, a comment, etc.（人、观点、评论等）；not showing serious thought, feelings, etc. about sth（肤浅的；浅薄的）；shallow breathing involves taking in only a small amount of air each time（（呼吸）浅的，弱的）

sham.meaning: a situation, feeling, system, etc. that is not as good or true as it seems to be（假象；假情假义；伪善；伪装）；a person who pretends to be sth that they are not（假装 … 的人；冒充者；假冒者）；behaviour, feelings, words, etc. that are intended to make sb/sth seem to be better than they really are（虚假的行为（或感情、言语等）；伪善）；(usually disapproving) not genuine but intended to seem real（虚假的；假装的）

shaman.meaning: a person in some religions and societies who is believed to be able to contact good and evil spirits and cure people of illnesses（萨满（据信能和善恶神灵沟通，能治病的人））

shamble.meaning: to walk in an awkward or lazy way, dragging your feet along the ground（拖着脚走；蹒跚）

shame.meaning: the feelings of sadness, embarrassment and guilt that you have when you know that sth you have done is wrong or stupid（羞耻；羞愧；惭愧）；(formal) (only used in questions and negative sentences（仅用于疑问句和否定句）；the ability to feel shame at sth you have done（羞耻心；羞愧感）；used to say that sth is a cause for feeling sad or disappointed（令人惋惜的事；让人遗憾的事）

shameful.meaning: that should make you feel ashamed（可耻的；丢脸的）

shameless.meaning: not feeling ashamed of sth you have done, although other people think you should（无耻的；没廉耻的；不要脸的）；shame·less·ly /ˈʃeɪmləsli; NAmEˈʃeɪmləsli/ adv. (usually disapproving but sometimes approving) The whole film is shamelessly romantic and glamorous.（张扬的浪漫与华美贯穿整部电影。）

shampoo.meaning: a liquid soap that is used for washing your hair; a similar liquid used for cleaning carpets, furniture covers or a car（洗发剂；香波；（洗地毯、家具罩套、汽车等的）洗涤剂）；an act of washing your hair using shampoo（用洗发剂洗头发）；to wash or clean hair, carpets, etc. with shampoo（用洗发剂洗（头发）；用洗涤剂洗（地毯等））

shanty.meaning: a small house, built of pieces of wood, metal and cardboard, where very poor people live, especially on the edge of a big city（棚屋，简陋小屋（常搭建于城市边缘））；a song that sailors traditionally used to sing while pulling ropes, etc.（水手号子（旧时水手边拉绳索等边唱的歌））

shape.meaning: the form of the outer edges or surfaces of sth; an example of sth that has a particular form（形状；外形；样子；呈 … 形状的事物）；a person or thing that is difficult to see clearly（模糊的影子）；the physical condition of sb/sth（状况；情况）；the particular qualities or characteristics of sth（性质；特点）

shaped.meaning: having the type of shape mentioned（具有（或呈）… 形状的）

shapeless.meaning: not having any definite shape（无定形的；不成形的；样子不好看的）；lacking clear organization（结构混乱的；条理不清的）

share.meaning: to have or use sth at the same time as sb else（共有；合用）；to divide sth between two or more people（分配；分摊）；to give some of what you have to sb else; to let sb use sth that is yours（分享；共享）；to have the same feelings, ideas, experiences, etc. as sb else（有同样的感情（或想法、经历等））

shark.meaning: a large sea fish with very sharp teeth and a pointed fin on its back. There are several types of shark, some of which can attack people swimming.（鲨鱼）；(informal, disapproving) a person who is dishonest in business, especially sb who gives bad advice and gets people to pay too much for sth（坑蒙拐骗的人；诈骗者）

sharp.meaning: having a fine edge or point, especially of sth that can cut or make a hole in sth（锋利的；锐利的；尖的）；sudden and rapid, especially of a change in sth（（变化）急剧的，骤然的）；clear and definite（清楚明确的；清晰的；鲜明的）；(of people or their minds, eyes, etc.（人或人的头脑、眼睛等）

sharpen.meaning: to make sth sharper; to become sharper（（使）变得锋利，变得清晰）；if a sense or feeling sharpens or sth sharpens it, it becomes stronger and/or clearer（（使感觉或感情）加强，加重，变得更明显）；to make a disagreement between people, or an issue on which people disagree, clearer and more likely to produce a result（使尖锐；使明朗）；to become or make sth better, more skilful, more effective, etc. than before（（使）提高，改善）

sharpener.meaning: (usually in compounds（通常构成复合词）；a tool or machine that makes things sharp（磨具；削具）

sharply.meaning: in a critical, rough or severe way（尖刻地；严厉地；猛烈地）；suddenly and by a large amount（急剧地；突然大幅度地）；in a way that clearly shows the differences between two things（鲜明地；明显地）；quickly and suddenly or loudly（迅疾而突然地；急促而大声地）

shatter.meaning: to suddenly break into small pieces; to make sth suddenly break into small pieces（（使）破碎，碎裂）；to destroy sth completely, especially sb's feelings, hopes or beliefs; to be destroyed in this way（（使感情、希望或信念等）粉碎，破灭；被粉碎；被破坏）；to make sb feel extremely shocked and upset（使极为惊愕难过；给予极大打击）

shave.meaning: to cut hair from the skin, especially the face, using a razor（剃（须发）；（尤指）刮脸）；to cut a small amount off a price, etc.（（少量地）削减，调低，降价）；to remove a beard or moustache by shaving（剃掉，刮去（胡须））；to cut very thin pieces from the surface of wood, etc.（削掉；刨去；切掉）

shaver.meaning: an electric tool for shaving（电动剃须刀）

she.meaning: (used as the subject of a verb（用作动词的主语）；a female person or animal that has already been mentioned or is easily identified（她；（指雌性动物）它）；(informal) a female（女性；雌性）；(in compound nouns（构成复合名词）

shear.meaning: to cut the wool off a sheep（给（羊）剪（羊毛））；(formal) to cut off sb's hair（剪（头发））；(especially of metal（尤指金属）；to break under pressure; to cut through sth and make it break（切断；剪切；断）

shed.meaning: a small simple building, usually built of wood or metal, used for keeping things in（简易房，棚（用于贮藏物品））；(BrE) a large industrial building, used for working in or keeping equipment（（工业上用于生产或存放设备的）厂房，工棚，库房）；(AustralE, NZE) a building with open sides where the wool is cut off sheep (= they are sheared) or where cows are milked（剪羊毛棚；挤奶棚）；(often used in newspapers（常用于报章）

sheep.meaning: an animal with a thick coat, kept on farms for its meat (called mutton or lamb ) or its wool（羊；绵羊）；(disapproving) if people behave like sheep, they all do what the others are doing, without thinking for themselves（盲从（不独立思考））；to distinguish people who are good at sth, intelligent, etc. from those who are not（区分能手与常人；分清智者和庸人）

sheepish.meaning: looking or feeling embarrassed because you have done sth silly or wrong（窘迫的；难为情的；不好意思的）

sheepskin.meaning: the skin of a sheep with the wool still on it（带毛绵羊皮）

sheer.meaning: used to emphasize the size, degree or amount of sth（（用来强调事物的大小、程度或数量））；complete and not mixed with anything else（完全的；纯粹的；十足的）；very steep（陡峭的）；(of cloth, etc.（织物等）

sheet.meaning: a large piece of thin cloth used on a bed to lie on or lie under（床单；被单）；a piece of paper for writing or printing on, etc. usually in a standard size（一张（通常指标准尺寸的纸））；a flat thin piece of any material, normally square or rectangular（薄片，薄板（多指正方形或长方形的））；a wide flat area of sth, covering the surface of sth else（一大片（覆盖物））

shelf.meaning: a flat board, made of wood, metal, glass, etc., fixed to the wall or forming part of a cupboard/closet, bookcase, etc., for things to be placed on（（固定在墙上的或橱柜、书架等的）架子，搁板）；(geology 地) a thing shaped like a shelf, especially a piece of rock sticking out from a cliff or from the edge of a mass of land under the sea（（悬崖上或海底）突出的岩石；陆架；陆棚）；not wanted by anyone; not used（（无用而）闲置的；搁置的）；(especially of women（尤指妇女）

shell.meaning: the hard outer part of eggs, nuts, some seeds and some animals（（蛋、坚果、某些种子和某些动物的）壳）；any object that looks like the shell of a snail or sea creature（壳状物）；a metal case filled with explosive, to be fired from a large gun（炮弹）；the walls or outer structure of sth, for example, an empty building or ship after a fire or a bomb attack（（房屋或船舶等的）骨架，框架，壳体）

shellfish.meaning: a creature with a shell, that lives in water, especially one of the types that can be eaten. Oysters and crabs are both shellfish.（（尤指可以吃的）水生有壳动物）

shelter.meaning: the fact of having a place to live or stay, considered as a basic human need（居所；住处）；protection from rain, danger or attack（遮蔽，庇护，避难（避雨、躲避危险或攻击））；(often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a structure built to give protection, especially from the weather or from attack（（尤指用以躲避风雨或攻击的）遮蔽物，庇护处，避难处）

shelve.meaning: to decide not to continue with a plan, either for a short time or permanently（搁置，停止（计划））；to put books, etc. on a shelf（把 … 放在架子（或搁板）上）；(of land（陆地）；to slope downwards（倾斜；成斜坡）

shepherd.meaning: a person whose job is to take care of sheep（牧羊人；羊倌）；to guide sb or a group of people somewhere, making sure they go where you want them to go（带领；引；护送）

sheriff.meaning: (in the US) an elected officer responsible for keeping law and order in a county or town（县治安官，城镇治安官（美国民选地方官员））；(in England and Wales) an officer representing the king or queen in counties, and some cities, who performs some legal duties and attends ceremonies（郡督（英格兰和威尔士官员，为英王在各郡和部分城市的代表））；(in Scotland) a judge（（苏格兰）法官）；(in Canada) an official who works in a court preparing court cases（（加拿大法院准备诉讼案件的）执行员）

shield.meaning: a large piece of metal or leather carried by soldiers in the past to protect the body when fighting（盾（牌））；a person or thing used to protect sb/sth, especially by forming a barrier（保护人；保护物；掩护物；屏障）；a plate or screen that protects a machine or the person using it from damage or injury（（保护机器和操作者的）护罩，防护屏，挡板）；an object in the shape of a shield, given as a prize in a sports competition, etc.（盾形奖牌）

shift.meaning: to move, or move sth, from one position or place to another（转移；挪动）；(BrE) (informal) to move quickly（赶快；快速移动）；(of a situation, an opinion, a policy etc.（情况、意见、政策等）；to change from one state, position, etc. to another（改变；转向）

shilling.meaning: a British coin in use until 1971, worth 12 old pence. There were 20 shillings in one pound.（先令（英国 1971 年以前货币单位，一先令值 12 旧便士，20 先令合一英镑））；the unit of money in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Somalia（先令（肯尼亚、乌干达、坦桑尼亚和索马里货币单位））

shimmer.meaning: to shine with a soft light that seems to move slightly（发出微弱的闪光；闪烁）；a shining light that seems to move slightly（闪烁的光）

shin.meaning: the front part of the leg below the knee（胫；胫部）；(informal) to climb up or down sth quickly, using your hands and legs（爬）

shine.meaning: to produce or reflect light; to be bright（发光；反光；照耀）；to aim or point the light of a lamp, etc. in a particular direction（把 … 照向；使 … 光投向）；to polish sth; to make sth smooth and bright（擦亮；擦光）；to be very good at sth（出色；出类拔萃）

shiny.meaning: smooth and bright; reflecting the light（光亮的；锃亮的；反光的；有光泽的）；(approving) very new and attractive（新颖的；新奇的；新异的）

ship.meaning: a large boat that carries people or goods by sea（（大）船；舰）；to send or transport sb/sth by ship or by another means of transport（船运；运输；运送）；to be available to be bought; to make sth available to be bought（上市；把 … 推向市场）；(of a boat, etc.（船等）

shipment.meaning: the process of sending goods from one place to another（运输；运送；装运）；a load of goods that are sent from one place to another（运输的货物）

shipowner.meaning: a person or company that owns a ship or ships（船主；船东）

shipping.meaning: ships in general or considered as a group（船舶）；the activity of carrying people or goods from one place to another by ship（航运；海运）

shipwreck.meaning: the loss or destruction of a ship at sea because of a storm or because it hits rocks, etc.（船舶失事；海难）；a ship that has been lost or destroyed at sea（失事的船；沉船）；to be left somewhere after the ship that you have been sailing in has been lost or destroyed at sea（遭遇海难；船只失事）；ship·wrecked /; NAmE/ adj. a shipwrecked sailor（遭遇海难的水手）

shipyard.meaning: a place where ships are built or repaired（船坞；造船厂；修船厂）

shirt.meaning: a piece of clothing (usually for men), worn on the upper part of the body, made of light cloth, with sleeves and usually with a collar and buttons down the front（（尤指男式的）衬衫）；(informal) used to tell sb not to get angry（别生气；保持冷静）；(BrE) (informal) to bet all your money on sb/sth（把所有的钱全押在 … 上）；anything that sb has, including the things they really need themselves, that sb else takes from them or they are willing to give（（别人拿走或自愿送掉的）全部家当）

shit.meaning: (taboo, slang) a swear word that many people find offensive, used to show that you are angry or annoyed（（表示气愤或恼怒））；solid waste matter from the bowels（屎；粪便）；an act of emptying solid waste matter from the bowels（拉屎）；stupid remarks or writing; nonsense（胡扯；废话；狗屁）

shiver.meaning: (of a person（人）；to shake slightly because you are cold, frightened, excited, etc.（颤抖，哆嗦（因寒冷、恐惧、激动等））；a sudden shaking movement of your body because you are cold, frightened, excited, etc.（颤抖，哆嗦（因寒冷、恐惧、激动等））；shaking movements of your body because of fear or a high temperature（寒战，寒噤（因恐惧或发高烧））

shoal.meaning: a large number of fish swimming together as a group（鱼群）；a small hill of sand just below the surface of the sea（浅滩；水下沙洲）

shock.meaning: a strong feeling of surprise as a result of sth happening, especially sth unpleasant; the event that causes this feeling（震惊；惊愕；令人震惊的事）；a serious medical condition, usually the result of injury in which a person has lost a lot of blood and they are extremely weak（休克）；a violent shaking movement that is caused by an explosion, earthquake, etc.（（由爆炸、地震等引起的）剧烈震动，剧烈震荡）；a thick mass of hair on a person's head（浓密的一堆（头发））

shocking.meaning: that offends or upsets people; that is morally wrong（令人气愤的；惹人憎恶的；不道德的）；(informal) (especially BrE) very bad（非常糟糕的）；shock·ing·ly /ˈʃɒkɪŋli; NAmEˈʃɑːkɪŋli/ adv. a shockingly high mortality rate（高得惊人的死亡率）

shoe.meaning: one of a pair of outer coverings for your feet, usually made of leather or plastic（鞋）；to be in, or imagine that you are in, another person's situation, especially when it is an unpleasant or difficult one（处于某人的境地；设身处地）；used to introduce a piece of advice you are giving to sb（（引出建议）要是我处在你的境地，换了我是你的话）；if you feel that a remark applies to you, you should accept it and take it as a warning or criticism（有则改之）

shoemaker.meaning: a person whose job is making shoes and boots（鞋匠；制鞋工人）

shoeshine.meaning: the activity of cleaning people's shoes for money（擦鞋（生意））

shoot.meaning: to fire a gun or other weapon; to fire sth from a weapon（开（枪或其他武器）；射击；发射）；to kill or wound a person or an animal with a bullet, etc.（射杀；射伤）；(of a gun or other weapon（枪或其他武器）；to fire bullets, etc.（发射（子弹等））

shooting.meaning: a situation in which a person is shot with a gun（枪击；枪杀）；the sport of shooting animals and birds with guns（狩猎）；the process of filming a film/movie（（电影的）拍摄）

shop.meaning: (especially BrE) a building or part of a building where you can buy goods or services（商店；店铺）；(especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）；a place where things are made or repaired, especially part of a factory where a particular type of work is done（工厂；工场；作坊；（尤指）车间）；(BrE) (informal) an act of going shopping, especially for food and other items needed in the house（购物；采买）

shopkeeper.meaning: a person who owns or manages a shop/store, usually a small one（（通常指小商店的）店主）

shopper.meaning: a person who buys goods from shops/stores（购物者；（商店的）顾客）

shopping.meaning: the activity of going to shops/stores and buying things（购物）；(especially BrE) the things that you have bought from shops/stores（从商店采买的东西）

shore.meaning: the land along the edge of the sea or ocean, a lake or another large area of water（（海洋、湖泊等大水域的）岸，滨）；(especially literary) a country, especially one with a coast（国家（尤指濒海国家））；to support part of a building or other large structure by placing large pieces of wood or metal against or under it so that it does not fall down（用撑柱支撑）；to help to support sth that is weak or going to fail（支撑；稳住）

shoreline.meaning: the edge of the sea, the ocean or a lake（海（或湖）滨线；海（或湖）岸线）

short.meaning: measuring or covering a small length or distance, or a smaller length or distance than usual（短的）；(of a person（人）；small in height（个子矮的）；lasting or taking a small amount of time or less time than usual（短的；短期的；短暂的）

shortage.meaning: a situation when there is not enough of the people or things that are needed（不足；缺少；短缺）

shortcoming.meaning: a fault in sb's character, a plan, a system, etc.（缺点；短处）

shorten.meaning: to make sth shorter; to become shorter（（使）变短，缩短）

shorthand.meaning: a quick way of writing using special signs or abbreviations, used especially to record what sb is saying（速记（法））；a shorter way of saying or referring to sth, which may not be as accurate as the more complicated way of saying it（（对某事）简略的表达方式）

short-lived.meaning: lasting only for a short time（短暂的）

shortly.meaning: a short time; not long（不多时；不久）；soon（立刻；马上）；in an angry and impatient way（没好气地；不耐烦地）

short-range.meaning: (of weapons（武器）；designed to travel only over short distances（短程的；近程的）；(of plans, etc.（计划等）；connected with a short period of time in the future（短期的；近期的）

shorts.meaning: short trousers/pants that end above or at the knee（短裤）

short-term.meaning: lasting a short time; designed only for a short period of time in the future（短期的；近期的）

shoshone.meaning: a member of a Native American people many of whom now live in the US state of Wyoming（肖肖尼人（美洲土著，很多现居于美国怀俄明州））

shot.meaning: the act of firing a gun; the sound this makes（射击；开枪（或炮）；枪（或炮）声）；a person who shoots a gun in a particular way (well, badly, etc.)（优秀（或不高明等的）射手，枪手，炮手）；a large number of small metal balls that you fire together from a shotgun（铅沙弹）；a large stone or metal ball that was shot from a cannon or large gun in the past（（旧时用大炮发射的石质或金属的）弹丸）

should.meaning: used to show what is right, appropriate, etc., especially when criticizing sb's actions（（尤用于纠正别人）应该，应当）；used for giving or asking for advice（（提出或征询建议）该，可以）；used to say that you expect sth is true or will happen（（表示预期）应该会，可能）；used to say that sth that was expected has not happened（（表示与预期相反）本应，本当）

shoulder.meaning: either of the two parts of the body between the top of each arm and the neck（肩；肩膀；肩胛）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；having the type of shoulders mentioned（… 肩膀的）；the part of a piece of clothing that covers the shoulder（（衣服的）肩部）

shout.meaning: to say sth in a loud voice; to speak loudly/angrily to sb（大声说；叫；嚷；斥责；怒骂）；to make a loud noise（呼叫；喊叫）；(AustralE, NZE) to buy drinks or food for sb in a bar, restaurant, etc.（（在酒吧、餐厅等）请人喝饮料（或吃东西））；to shout so that sb who is speaking cannot be heard（用喊叫声盖过某人的讲话）

shove.meaning: to push sb/sth in a rough way（猛推；乱挤；推撞）；(informal) to put sth somewhere roughly or carelessly（乱放；随便放；胡乱丢；随手扔）；(informal) (especially NAmE) used to say rudely that you will not accept or do sth（（粗鲁地表示不接受或不做某事）去他的，没门儿，去他妈的）；(BrE) (informal) used to tell sb rudely to go away（滚；滚开）

shovel.meaning: a tool with a long handle and a broad blade with curved edges, used for moving earth, snow, sand, etc.（铲；铁铲）；the part of a large machine or vehicle that digs or moves earth（（推土机、挖土机等的）铲，铲形部分）；to lift and move earth, stones, coal, etc. with a shovel（铲；铲起）

show.meaning: to make sth clear; to prove sth（表明；证明）；to let sb see sth（给 … 看；出示；展示）；to help sb to do sth by letting them watch you do it or by explaining it（（通过示范）教，解说；演示）；to point to sth so that sb can see where or what it is（指给某人看；指出）

shower.meaning: a piece of equipment producing a spray of water that you stand under to wash yourself; the small room or part of a room that contains a shower（淋浴器；淋浴间）；the act of washing yourself with a shower（淋浴）；a short period of rain or snow（阵雨；阵雪）；a large number of things that arrive or fall together（一大批；一阵；一连串）

showman.meaning: a person who does things in an entertaining way and is good at getting people's attention（善于引起公众注意的人；喜欢出风头的人）；a person who organizes public entertainments, especially at fairgrounds（（尤指露天游乐场的）演出主持人，演出经理人）

showroom.meaning: a large shop/store in which goods for sale, especially cars and electrical goods, are displayed（商品陈列室；展销厅）

showy.meaning: so brightly coloured, large or exaggerated that it attracts a lot of attention（艳丽的；花哨的）

shred.meaning: to cut or tear sth into small pieces（切碎；撕碎）；a small thin piece that has been torn or cut from sth（（撕或切的）细条，碎片）；(used especially in negative sentences（尤用于否定句）；a very small amount of sth（极少量；些许；一丁点）

shrewd.meaning: clever at understanding and making judgements about a situation（精明的；敏锐的；有眼光的；精于盘算的）；showing good judgement and likely to be right（判断得准的；高明的）

shriek.meaning: to give a loud high shout, for example when you are excited, frightened or in pain（尖叫）；to say sth in a loud, high voice（尖声说）；a loud high shout, for example one that you make when you are excited, frightened or in pain（尖叫）

shrill.meaning: (of sounds or voices（声音或嗓音）；very high and loud, in an unpleasant way（刺耳的；尖声的；尖厉的）；loud and determined but often unreasonable（闹着非要 … 不可的；不依不饶的）；shrilly /ˈʃrɪlli; NAmEˈʃrɪlli/ adv. shrill·ness /ʃrɪlnəs; NAmEʃrɪlnəs/ noun [U] verb 1. [I] to make an unpleasant high loud sound（发出刺耳的声音；尖叫）

shrimp.meaning: a small shellfish that can be eaten, like a prawn but smaller. Shrimps turn pink when cooked.（虾；小虾）

shrine.meaning: a place where people come to worship because it is connected with a holy person or event（圣地；圣祠；神庙；神龛）；a place that people visit because it is connected with sb/sth that is important to them（具有重要意义的地方）

shrink.meaning: to become smaller, especially when washed in water that is too hot; to make clothes, cloth, etc. smaller in this way（（使）缩水，收缩，缩小，皱缩）；to become or to make sth smaller in size or amount（（使）缩小，收缩，减少）；to move back or away from sth because you are frightened or shocked（退缩；畏缩）；(humorous) a way of describing a very shy person（（指羞怯的人））

shrinkage.meaning: the process of becoming smaller in size; the amount by which sth becomes smaller（缩小；收缩；收缩量；收缩程度）

shroud.meaning: a piece of cloth that a dead person's body is wrapped in before it is buried（裹尸布；寿衣）；(literary) a thing that covers, surrounds or hides sth（覆盖物；遮蔽物）；(of darkness, clouds, cloth, etc.（黑暗、云、织物等）；to cover or hide sth（覆盖；隐藏；遮蔽）

shrub.meaning: a large plant that is smaller than a tree and that has several stems of wood coming from the ground（灌木）

shrubby.meaning: (of plants（植物）；like a shrub（像灌木的；灌木状的）

shrug.meaning: to raise your shoulders and then drop them to show that you do not know or care about sth（耸肩（表示不知道或不在乎））；an act of raising your shoulders and then dropping them to show that you do not know or care about sth（耸肩（表示不知道或不在乎））；a very short knitted piece of clothing that is open at the front and usually has sleeves made from the same piece as the back and front（（女式）带袖短披肩）；to treat sth as if it is not important（不把 … 当回事；对 … 满不在乎；对 … 不予理睬）

shudder.meaning: to shake because you are cold or frightened, or because of a strong feeling（（因寒冷、害怕或激动）发抖，打颤，战栗）；(of a vehicle, machine, etc.（交通工具、机器等）；to shake very hard（强烈震动；剧烈抖动）；a shaking movement you make because you are cold, frightened or disgusted（（因寒冷、害怕或反感等引起的）发抖，打颤，战栗）

shuffle.meaning: to walk slowly without lifting your feet completely off the ground（拖着脚走）；to move from one foot to another; to move your feet in an awkward or embarrassed way（（笨拙或尴尬地）把脚动来动去；坐立不安）；to mix cards up in a pack/deck of playing cards before playing a game（洗（牌））；to move paper or things into different positions or a different order（把（纸张等）变换位置，打乱次序）

shun.meaning: to avoid sb/sth（避开；回避；避免）

shut.meaning: to make sth close; to become closed（关闭；关上；合上）；(BrE) when a shop/store, restaurant, etc. shuts or when sb shuts it, it stops being open for business and you cannot go into it（（使）停止营业，关门，打烊）；(slang) a rude way of telling sb to be quiet or stop talking（（粗暴地要某人停止说话）住口，闭嘴）；(BrE) (informal) to close a business permanently or to stop working for the day（停业；关张；倒闭；打烊）

shutter.meaning: one of a pair of wooden or metal covers that can be closed over the outside of a window to keep out light or protect the windows from damage（活动护窗；百叶窗）；the part of a camera that opens to allow light to pass through the lens when you take a photograph（（照相机的）快门）；to stop letting sb know what your thoughts or feelings are; to stop letting yourself think about sth（掩藏自己的思想感情；锁上心扉；不再想某件事）

shuttle.meaning: a plane, bus or train that travels regularly between two places（来往于两地之间的航班（或班车、火车））；a pointed tool used in making cloth to pull a thread backwards and forwards over the other threads that pass along the length of the cloth（梭；梭子）；a train service that takes cars and their passengers through the Channel Tunnel between England and France（（英法之间英吉利海峡隧道的）穿梭火车）；to travel between two places frequently（频繁往来（于甲地和乙地之间））

shy.meaning: (of people（人）；nervous or embarrassed about meeting and speaking to other people（羞怯的；腼腆的；怕生的）；showing that sb is nervous or embarrassed about meeting and speaking to other people（显得腼腆的；看着羞怯的）；(of animals（动物）

sibling.meaning: a brother or sister（兄；弟；姐；妹）

sick.meaning: physically or mentally ill（（身体或精神）生病的，有病的）；(especially BrE) feeling that you want to vomit（想呕吐；恶心）；(in compounds（构成复合词）；feeling sick as a result of travelling on a ship, plane, etc.（晕船；晕机；晕车）

sicken.meaning: to make sb feel very shocked and angry（使大为震惊；使愤怒）；to become ill/sick（患病；生病）

sickle.meaning: a tool with a curved blade and a short handle, used for cutting grass, etc.（镰刀）

sickness.meaning: illness; bad health（疾病；不健康）；a particular type of illness or disease（… 病； … 症）；(especially BrE) the feeling that you are likely to vomit (= bring food back up from the stomach to the mouth); the fact of vomiting（恶心；呕吐）；a feeling of great sadness, disappointment or disgust（悲伤；失望；厌恶；反感）

side.meaning: either of the two halves of a surface, an object or an area that is divided by an imaginary central line（（由想像的中线分出的）一边，一侧）；a position or an area to the left or right of sth（（事物左方或右方的）一旁，一边，一侧）；one of the flat surfaces of sth that is not the top or bottom, front or back（侧面）；the vertical or sloping surface around sth, but not the top or bottom of it（斜面；垂直面）

sideline.meaning: an activity that you do as well as your main job in order to earn extra money（兼职；副业；兼营业务）；the lines along the two long sides of a sports field, tennis court, etc. that mark the outer edges; the area just outside these（（球场等的）边线，两侧场外区域）；watching sth but not actually involved in it（从旁观者的角度；置身局外）；to prevent sb from playing in a team, especially because of an injury（使退出比赛，使下场（尤指由于受伤））

sidewalk.meaning: a flat part at the side of a road for people to walk on（（马路边的）人行道）

sideways.meaning: to, towards or from the side（往（或向、从）一侧）；with one side facing forwards（侧着；侧面朝前）；side·ways adj. She slid him a sideways glance.（她斜眼看了他一下。）

siege.meaning: a military operation in which an army tries to capture a town by surrounding it and stopping the supply of food, etc. to the people inside（（军队对城镇的）围困，包围，围攻，封锁）；a situation in which the police surround a building where people are living or hiding, in order to make them come out（（警察对建筑物的）包围，封锁）；surrounded by an army or the police in a siege（被包围；被围困；被封锁）；being criticized all the time or put under pressure by problems, questions, etc.（一再遭到批评的；受 … 困扰的）

sierra.meaning: (especially in place names（尤用于地名）；a long range of steep mountains with sharp points, especially in Spain and America（（尤指西班牙和美洲的）锯齿状山脉）

sieve.meaning: a tool for separating solids from liquids or larger solids from smaller solids, made of a wire or plastic net attached to a ring. The liquid or small pieces pass through the net but the larger pieces do not.（滤器；筛子；笊篱；漏勺）；(informal) to have a very bad memory; to forget things easily（记性差；健忘）；to put sth through a sieve（筛；过筛；滤）

sift.meaning: to put flour or some other fine substance through a sieve/sifter（筛（面粉或颗粒较细的物质））；to examine sth very carefully in order to decide what is important or useful or to find sth important（细查；详审）；to separate sth from a group of things（区分；挑选；精选）；to remove sth that you do not want from a substance by putting it through a sieve（筛除；筛去）

sigh.meaning: to take and then let out a long deep breath that can be heard, to show that you are disappointed, sad, tired, etc.（叹气；叹息）；to say sth with a sigh（叹着气说；叹息道）；(especially of the wind（尤指风）；to make a long sound like a sigh（悲鸣）

sight.meaning: the ability to see（视力；视觉）；the act of seeing sb/sth（看见）；the area or distance within which sb can see or sth can be seen（视力范围；视野）；a thing that you see or can see（看见（或看得见）的事物；景象；情景）
