smoky.meaning: full of smoke（烟雾弥漫的）；producing a lot of smoke（多烟的；冒出大量烟的）；tasting or smelling like smoke（有烟熏味的）；having the colour or appearance of smoke（烟灰色的；似烟的）

smooth.meaning: completely flat and even, without any lumps, holes or rough areas（平整的；平坦的；平滑的；光滑的）；(of a liquid mixture（液体混合物）；without any lumps（无结块的；混合均匀的）；happening or continuing without any problems（顺利的；平稳的）

smoothly.meaning: in an even way, without suddenly stopping and starting again（平稳地；连续而流畅地）；without problems or difficulties（顺利地）；in a calm or confident way（平静地；自信地）；in a way that produces a smooth surface or mixture（平整地；平滑地；均匀地）

smother.meaning: to kill sb by covering their face so that they cannot breathe（使窒息而死；闷死）；to cover sth/sb thickly or with too much of sth（（用某物）厚厚地覆盖）；to prevent sth from developing or being expressed（抑制；扼杀；忍住）；to give sb too much love or protection so that they feel restricted（（因溺爱等）使 … 觉得压抑）

smuggle.meaning: to take, send or bring goods or people secretly and illegally into or out of a country, etc.（走私；私运；偷运）

smuggler.meaning: a person who takes goods into or out of a country illegally（走私者）

smuggling.meaning: the crime of taking, sending or bringing goods secretly and illegally into or out of a country（走私（罪））

snack.meaning: (informal) a small meal or amount of food, usually eaten in a hurry（点心；小吃；快餐）；(AustralE) (informal) a thing that is easy to do（易办到的事；“小菜一碟”）；to eat snacks between or instead of main meals（吃点心（或快餐、小吃））

snag.meaning: (informal) a problem or difficulty, especially one that is small, hidden or unexpected（（尤指潜在的、意外的、不严重的）问题，困难，障碍，麻烦）；an object or a part of an object that is rough or sharp and may cut sth（突出物；尖齿；尖角；尖刺）；(AustralE, NZE) (informal) a sausage（香肠）；to catch or tear sth on sth rough or sharp; to become caught or torn in this way（（在带尖的东西上）钩住，挂破，被钩住，被挂破）

snail.meaning: a small soft creature with a hard round shell on its back, that moves very slowly and often eats garden plants. Some types of snail can be eaten.（蜗牛）；very slowly（非常缓慢）

snake.meaning: a reptile with a very long thin body and no legs. There are many types of snake, some of which are poisonous.（蛇）；(disapproving) a person who pretends to be your friend but who cannot be trusted（阴险的人；潜伏的敌人；虚假的人）；to move like a snake, in long twisting curves; to go in a particular direction in long twisting curves（曲折前行；蛇行；蜿蜒伸展）

snap.meaning: to break sth suddenly with a sharp noise; to be broken in this way（（使咔嚓）断裂，绷断）；to move, or to move sth, into a particular position quickly, especially with a sudden sharp noise（（使啪地）打开，关上，移到某位置）；to speak or say sth in an impatient, usually angry, voice（厉声说；怒气冲冲地说；不耐烦地说）；to try to bite sb/sth（咬）

snatch.meaning: to take sth quickly and often rudely or roughly（一把抓起；一下夺过）；to take sb/sth away from a person or place, especially by force; to steal sth（夺去；抢走；偷窃）；to take or get sth quickly, especially because you do not have much time（抓紧时间做；乘机获得）；to try to take hold of sth with your hands（伸手抓；试图夺）

sneak.meaning: to go somewhere secretly, trying to avoid being seen（偷偷地走；溜）；to do sth or take sb/sth somewhere secretly, often without permission（偷偷地做；偷带；偷拿）；(informal) to secretly take sth small or unimportant（偷走（不重要的或小的东西））；(old-fashioned) (BrE disapproving) to tell an adult that another child has done sth wrong, especially in order to cause trouble（（儿童向成人）打小报告，告状）

sneer.meaning: to show that you have no respect for sb by the expression on your face or by the way you speak（嘲笑；讥讽；嗤笑）；sneer·ing·ly /ˈsnɪərɪŋli; NAmEˈsnɪrɪŋli/ adv. noun [usually sing.] an unpleasant look, smile or comment that shows you do not respect sb/sth（嘲笑；讥讽）

sneeze.meaning: to have air come suddenly and noisily out through your nose and mouth in a way that you cannot control, for example because you have a cold（打喷嚏）；(informal) good enough to be accepted or considered seriously（值得认真对待；不可轻视）；the act of sneezing or the noise you make when you sneeze（喷嚏；喷嚏声）

sniff.meaning: to breathe air in through your nose in a way that makes a sound, especially when you are crying, have a cold, etc.（抽鼻子（尤指哭泣、患感冒等时出声地用鼻子吸气））；to breathe air in through the nose in order to discover or enjoy the smell of sth（（吸着气）嗅，闻）；to say sth in a complaining or disapproving way（抱怨；不以为然地说）；(informal) good enough to be accepted or considered seriously（值得认真对待；不可轻视）

snipe.meaning: to shoot at sb from a hiding place, usually from a distance（狙击；打冷枪）；to criticize sb in an unpleasant way（冷言冷语地指摘；抨击）；snip·ing /snaɪpɪŋ; NAmEsnaɪpɪŋ/ noun [U] Aid workers remain in the area despite continuous sniping.（尽管冷枪不断，但救援人员仍然留在这一地区。）；a bird with a long straight beak that lives on wet ground（沙锥（喙长直，生活在潮湿地区））

snippet.meaning: a small piece of information or news（一小条（消息）；一则（新闻））；a short piece of a conversation, piece of music, etc.（一小段（谈话、音乐等））

snob.meaning: a person who admires people in the higher social classes too much and has no respect for people in the lower social classes（势利小人；谄上欺下的人）；a person who thinks they are much better than other people because they are intelligent or like things that many people do not like（自以为优越的人；自命高雅的人）

snobbery.meaning: the attitudes and behaviour of people who are snobs（势利态度（或行为）；自以为优越的态度（或行为））

snobbish.meaning: thinking that having a high social class is very important; feeling that you are better than other people because you are more intelligent or like things that many people do not like（势利的；自命不凡的）

snore.meaning: to breathe noisily through your nose and mouth while you are asleep（打鼾；打呼噜）；snorer snorer snorers /; NAmE/ noun snor·ing /; NAmE/ noun [U] loud snoring（响亮的鼾声）；noisy breathing while you are asleep（打呼噜（声）；打鼾（声））

snout.meaning: the long nose and area around the mouth of some types of animal, such as a pig（（猪等动物的）口鼻部，吻）；(informal, humorous) a person's nose（（人的）鼻子）；a part of sth that sticks out at the front（吻状突出物）

snow.meaning: small soft white pieces (called flakes ) of frozen water that fall from the sky in cold weather; this substance when it is lying on the ground（雪；雪花；积雪）；(literary) an amount of snow that falls in one particular place or at one particular time（（某地或某时的）降雪量；一场雪）；extremely clean, pure, etc.（冰清玉洁；纯洁无瑕）；when it snows, snow falls from the sky（下雪）

snowbound.meaning: (of a person or vehicle（人或车辆）；trapped in a particular place and unable to move because a lot of snow has fallen（被雪困住的）；(of a road or building（道路或建筑物）；that you cannot use or reach because a lot of snow has fallen（被雪封住的）

snowdrift.meaning: a deep pile of snow that has been blown together by the wind（（风吹成的）雪堆）

snowfall.meaning: an occasion when snow falls; the amount of snow that falls in a particular place in a period of time（下雪；降雪（量））

snowflake.meaning: a small soft piece of frozen water that falls from the sky as snow（雪花；雪片）

snowman.meaning: a figure like a man that people, especially children, make out of snow for fun（（用雪堆成的）雪人）

snowstorm.meaning: a very heavy fall of snow, usually with a strong wind（雪暴；暴风雪）

snowy.meaning: covered with snow（被雪覆盖的）；(of a period of time（一段时间）；when a lot of snow falls（下雪多的）；(literary) very white, like new snow（雪白的）

so.meaning: to such a great degree（（表示程度）这么，这样，那么，那样，如此）；very; extremely（很；极）；(used in comparisons（用于比较）；not to the same degree（不如 …（这么 … ）；不像 …（那样 … ））

soak.meaning: to put sth in liquid for a time so that it becomes completely wet; to become completely wet in this way（浸泡；浸湿；浸透；湿透）；to make sb/sth completely wet（使湿透；把 … 浸湿）；(informal) to obtain a lot of money from sb by making them pay very high taxes or prices（向（某人）敲竹杠；宰（某人）；向（某人）征收重税）；(of a liquid（液体）

soap.meaning: a substance that you use with water for washing your body（肥皂）；to rub yourself/sb/sth with soap（抹肥皂；用肥皂擦洗）

soar.meaning: if the value, amount or level of sth soars, it rises very quickly（急升；猛增）；to rise quickly and smoothly up into the air（升空；升腾）；to fly very high in the air or remain high in the air（高飞；翱翔）；to be very high or tall（高耸；耸立）

sob.meaning: to cry noisily, taking sudden, sharp breaths（抽噎；啜泣；呜咽）；to say sth while you are crying（哭诉；泣诉；抽噎着说）；to cry noisily for a long time because you are very sad（悲切地哭泣；很伤心地哭泣）；an act or the sound of sobbing（抽噎（声）；啜泣（声）；呜咽（声））

sober.meaning: not drunk (= not affected by alcohol)（未醉）；(of people and their behaviour（人及其行为）；serious and sensible（持重的；冷静的）；(of colours or clothes（颜色或服装）

sobriquet.meaning: an informal name or title that you give sb/sth（绰号；外号）

so-called.meaning: used to show that you do not think that the word or phrase that is being used to describe sb/sth is appropriate（（表示不认同）所谓的）；used to introduce the word that people usually use to describe sth（（引出约定俗成的称谓）人称 … 的，号称 … 的）

soccer.meaning: a game played by two teams of 11 players, using a round ball which players kick up and down the playing field. Teams try to kick the ball into the other team's goal.（足球运动）

sociable.meaning: (of people（人）；enjoying spending time with other people（好交际的；合群的；友好的）

social.meaning: connected with society and the way it is organized（社会的）；connected with your position in society（社会上的；社会地位的）；connected with activities in which people meet each other for pleasure（社交的；交际的；联谊的）；(technical 术语) living naturally in groups, rather than alone（群居的）

socialism.meaning: a set of political and economic theories based on the belief that everyone has an equal right to a share of a country's wealth and that the government should own and control the main industries（社会主义）

socialist.meaning: a person who believes in or supports socialism; a member of a political party that believes in socialism（社会主义者；社会党党员）；so·cial·ist adj. [usually before noun] a socialist country（社会主义国家）

socialization.meaning: the process by which sb, especially a child, learns to behave in a way that is acceptable in their society（适应社会的过程；社会化）

socialize.meaning: to meet and spend time with people in a friendly way, in order to enjoy yourself（（和他人）交往，交际）；(formal) to teach people to behave in ways that are acceptable to their society（使适应社会）；to organize sth according to the principles of socialism（使社会主义化；按社会主义原则行事）

society.meaning: people in general, living together in communities（社会（以群体形式生活在一起的人的总称））；a particular community of people who share the same customs, laws, etc.（社会（共同遵守一定的习俗、法律等的特定群体））；(especially in names（尤用于名称）；a group of people who join together for a particular purpose（社团；协会；学会）

sociologist.meaning: a person who studies sociology（社会学家）

sociology.meaning: the scientific study of the nature and development of society and social behaviour（社会学）；socio·logic·al /ˌsəʊsiəˈlɒdʒɪkl; NAmEˌsoʊsiəˈlɑːdʒɪkl/ adj. sociological theories（社会学理论）

sock.meaning: a piece of clothing that is worn over the foot, ankle and lower part of the leg, especially inside a shoe（短袜）；(informal) a strong blow, especially with the fist（（尤指用拳头）猛击，重击）；(informal) to surprise or impress sb very much（使某人万分惊愕；给某人留下深刻印象）；(old-fashioned) (BrE informal) used to tell sb to stop talking or making a noise（（让某人安静）住嘴，别出声）

socket.meaning: a device in a wall that you put a plug into in order to connect electrical equipment to the power supply of a building（（电源）插座）；a device on a piece of electrical equipment that you can fix a plug, a light bulb, etc. into（（电器上的）插口，插孔，管座）；a curved hollow space in the surface of sth that another part fits into or moves around in（托座；孔穴；窝；槽；臼）

sod.meaning: (BrE) (taboo, slang) used to refer to a person, especially a man, that you are annoyed with or think is unpleasant（（指讨厌的人，尤指男人）讨厌鬼）；(BrE) (taboo, slang) used with an adjective to refer to a person, especially a man（（与形容词连用，指人，尤指男人）家伙）；(BrE) (taboo, slang) a thing that is difficult or causes problems（难办的事；惹麻烦的事）；(formal or literary) a layer of earth with grass growing on it; a piece of this that has been removed（长草的土层；（移植的）草皮）

soda.meaning: a sweet fizzy drink (= a drink with bubbles) made with soda water, fruit flavour and sometimes ice cream（苏打汽水（加果味，有时加入冰淇淋））；a chemical substance in common use that is a compound of sodium（苏打；纯碱；无水碳酸钠）

sodium.meaning: a chemical element. Sodium is a soft silver-white metal that is found naturally only in compounds, such as salt.（钠）

sofa.meaning: a long comfortable seat with a back and arms, for two or more people to sit on（长沙发）

soft.meaning: changing shape easily when pressed; not stiff or firm（软的；柔软的）；less hard than average（硬度较低的；较软的）；smooth and pleasant to touch（柔滑的；细滑的；细腻的）；not having sharp angles or hard edges（无棱角的；轮廓不鲜明的；线条柔和的）

softball.meaning: a game similar to baseball but played on a smaller field with a larger, softer ball（垒球运动）；the ball used in softball（垒球）

soften.meaning: to become, or to make sth softer（（使）变软，软化）；to become or to make sth less bright, rough or strong（（使）柔和，和缓）；to become or to make sb/sth more sympathetic and less severe or critical（（使）态度缓和，变温和，变宽厚）；to reduce the force or the unpleasant effects of sth（减轻；减缓；削弱）

softly.meaning: in a soft way（轻轻地；轻柔地；温和地；柔和地）

software.meaning: the programs, etc. used to operate a computer（软件；（台）软体）

softwood.meaning: wood from trees such as pine, that is cheap to produce and can be cut easily（软质木，软木（如松木））

soil.meaning: the top layer of the earth in which plants, trees, etc. grow（土壤）；(literary) a country; an area of land（国土；领土；土地）；(formal) to make sth dirty（弄脏）

solar.meaning: of or connected with the sun（太阳的）；using the sun's energy（太阳能的）

solder.meaning: a mixture of metals that is heated and melted and then used to join metals, wires, etc. together（焊料；焊锡）；to join pieces of metal or wire with solder（焊接；焊合）

soldier.meaning: a member of an army, especially one who is not an officer（军人；（尤指）士兵）；to continue with what you are doing or trying to achieve, especially when this is difficult or unpleasant（坚持；硬挺着）

sole.meaning: only; single（仅有的；唯一的）；belonging to one person or group; not shared（独占的；专有的；全权处理的）；the bottom surface of the foot（脚掌；脚底（板））；the bottom part of a shoe or sock, not including the heel（鞋底；袜底）

solely.meaning: only; not involving sb/sth else（仅；只；唯；单独地）

solemn.meaning: (of a person（人）；not happy or smiling（冷峻的；表情严肃的）；done, said, etc. in a very serious and sincere way（庄严的；严正的；郑重的）；(of a religious ceremony or formal occasion（宗教仪式或正式场合）

solemnity.meaning: the quality of being solemn（庄严；庄重；严肃；郑重）；(formal) formal things that people do at a serious event or occasion（（重大场合的）礼仪，仪式）

solicit.meaning: (formal) to ask sb for sth, such as support, money or information; to try to get sth or persuade sb to do sth（索求，请求 … 给予（援助、钱或信息）；征求；筹集）；(of a prostitute（妓女）；to offer to have sex with people in return for money（招徕（嫖客）；拉（客））；so·lici·ta·tion solicitation solicitations /səˌlɪsɪˈtəɪʃn; NAmEsəˌlɪsɪˈtəɪʃn/ noun [U, C] (especially NAmE) the solicitation of money for election funds（竞选资金筹集活动）

solicitor.meaning: (BrE) a lawyer who prepares legal documents, for example for the sale of land or buildings, advises people on legal matters, and can speak for them in some courts of law（事务律师，诉状律师（代拟法律文书、提供法律咨询等的一般辩护律师））；(NAmE) a person whose job is to visit or telephone people and try to sell them sth（推销员）；(NAmE) the most senior legal officer of a city, town or government department（（城镇或政府部门负责法律事务的）法务官）

solid.meaning: hard or firm; not in the form of a liquid or gas（固体的；坚硬的）；having no holes or spaces inside; not hollow（无空隙的；非中空的；实心的）；strong and made well（结实的；坚固的；牢固的）；that you can rely on; having a strong basis（可靠的；可信赖的；坚实的）

solidarity.meaning: support by one person or group of people for another because they share feelings, opinions, aims, etc.（团结；齐心协力；同心同德；相互支持）

solidify.meaning: to become solid; to make sth solid（（使）凝固，变硬，变得结实）；(of ideas, etc.（观念等）；to become or to make sth become more definite and less likely to change（（使）变得坚定，变得稳固，巩固）

solidity.meaning: the quality or state of being solid（固态；坚固性；可靠性）

solidly.meaning: in a firm and strong way（坚固地；结实地；牢固地）；continuously; without stopping（连续地；不间断地；整整地）；agreeing with or supporting sb/sth completely（一致地；完全支持）

solitary.meaning: done alone; without other people（独自的；单独的）；(of a person or an animal（人或动物）；enjoying being alone; frequently spending time alone（喜欢（或惯于）独处的）；(of a person, thing or place（人、物或处所）

solitude.meaning: the state of being alone, especially when you find this pleasant（独处；独居）

solo.meaning: done by one person alone, without anyone helping them（独自的；单独的）；connected with or played as a musical solo（独唱的；独奏的）；solo adv. She wanted to fly solo across the Atlantic.（她想独自一人驾机飞越大西洋。）；a piece of music, dance or entertainment performed by only one person（独唱；独奏；独舞；单人表演）

soloist.meaning: a person who plays an instrument or performs alone（独奏者；独唱者；单独表演者）

soluble.meaning: that can be dissolved in a liquid（可溶的）；(of a problem（问题）；that can be solved（可解决的；可解的）

solution.meaning: a way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation（解决办法；处理手段）；an answer to a puzzle or to a problem in mathematics（答案；解；谜底）；a liquid in which sth is dissolved（溶液）；the process of dissolving a solid or gas in a liquid（溶解（过程））

solve.meaning: to find a way of dealing with a problem or difficult situation（解决；处理）；to find the correct answer or explanation for sth（解答；破解）

solvency.meaning: the state of not being in debt (= not owing money)（无债务；不负债）

solvent.meaning: a substance, especially a liquid, that can dissolve another substance（溶剂；溶媒）；having enough money to pay your debts; not in debt（有偿付能力；无债务）；(technical 术语) able to dissolve another substance, or be dissolved in another substance（有溶解力的；可溶解的）

some.meaning: used with uncountable nouns or plural countable nouns to mean ‘an amount of’ or ‘a number of’, when the amount or number is not given（（与不可数名词或复数可数名词连用）一些，若干）；In negative sentences and questions any is usually used instead of ‘some’.（在否定句和疑问句中，通常用 any，而不用 some）；However, some is used in questions that expect a positive reply.（但在预料会得到肯定回答的疑问句中仍用 some）；used to refer to certain members of a group or certain types of a thing, but not all of them（（指群体中的某些成员或事物的某些类型）某些，部分，有的）

somehow.meaning: in a way that is not known or certain（以某种方式（或方法））；for a reason that you do not know or understand（由于某种未知的原因；不知为什么；不知怎么地）

someone.meaning: a person who is not known or mentioned by name（某人）；an important person（重要人物）

something.meaning: a thing that is not known or mentioned by name（某事；某物）；(informal) a thing that is thought to be important or worth taking notice of（想来重要（或值得注意）的事物）；(informal) used to show that a description or an amount, etc. is not exact（（表示不确切的描述或数量）大致，左右）；to be successful in life（有所成就；获得成功）

sometime.meaning: at a time that you do not know exactly or has not yet been decided（在某时（不确切或尚未决定））；used to refer to what sb used to be（（指某人曾经是 … ）从前的，一度的）；(NAmE) used to refer to what sb does occasionally（（指某人做某事）偶尔的）

sometimes.meaning: occasionally rather than all of the time（有时；间或）

somewhat.meaning: to some degree（有点；有几分；稍微）

somewhere.meaning: in, at or to a place that you do not know or do not mention by name（在某处；到某处）；some·where (NAmE also some·place) pron. sophisticated.meaning: having a lot of experience of the world and knowing about fashion, culture and other things that people think are socially important（见多识广的；老练的；见过世面的）；(of a machine, system, etc.（机器、体系等）；clever and complicated in the way that it works or is presented（复杂巧妙的；先进的；精密的）；(of a person（人）

spider.meaning: a small creature with eight thin legs. Many spiders spin webs (= nets of thin threads) to catch insects for food.（蜘蛛）

spidery.meaning: long and thin, like the legs of a spider（（像蛛腿一样）细长的）

spike.meaning: a thin object with a sharp point, especially a pointed piece of metal, wood, etc.（尖状物；尖头；尖刺）；a metal point attached to the sole of a sports shoe to prevent you from slipping while running（（防滑）鞋钉）；shoes fitted with these metal spikes, used for running（（赛跑用的）钉鞋）；a long pointed group of flowers that grow together on a single stem（穗；穗状花序）

spiky.meaning: having sharp points（有尖刺的）；(of hair（头发）；sticking straight up from the head（刺猬式的）；(of people（人）

spill.meaning: (especially of liquid（尤指液体）；to flow over the edge of a container by accident; to make liquid do this（（使）洒出，泼出，溢出）；(of people（人）；to come out of a place in large numbers and spread out（涌出；蜂拥而出）

spin.meaning: to turn round and round quickly; to make sth do this（（使）快速旋转）；to turn round quickly once; to make sb do this（（使）急转身，猛转回头，急转弯）；to make thread from wool, cotton, silk, etc. by twisting it（纺（线）；纺（纱））；to produce thread from its body to make a web or cocoon（吐（丝）；作（茧）；结（网））

spinal.meaning: connected with the spine (= the long bone in the back)（脊的；脊柱的；脊髓的）

spine.meaning: the row of small bones that are connected together down the middle of the back（脊柱；脊椎）；any of the sharp pointed parts like needles on some plants and animals（（植物的）刺；（动物的）刺毛）；the narrow part of the cover of a book that the pages are joined to（书脊）

spinet.meaning: a kind of harpsichord (= an early type of musical instrument), played like a piano（斯皮耐琴（小型拨弦键琴））；(US) a small piano/electronic organ（小型钢琴/电子琴）

spiny.meaning: (of animals or plants（动物或植物）；having sharp points like needles（有刺毛的；带刺的；多刺的）

spiral.meaning: a shape or design, consisting of a continuous curved line that winds around a central point, with each curve further away from the centre（螺旋形；螺旋式）；a continuous harmful increase or decrease in sth, that gradually gets faster and faster（逐渐加速上升（或下降））；moving in a continuous curve that winds around a central point（螺旋形的；螺旋式的）；spir·al·ly /ˈspaɪrəli; NAmEˈspaɪrəli/ adv. verb (-ll-, NAmE usually-l-) 1. [I] (+ adv./prep.) to move in continuous circles, going upwards or downwards（螺旋式上升（或下降）；盘旋上升（或下降））

spirit.meaning: the part of a person that includes their mind, feelings and character rather than their body（精神；心灵）；a person's feelings or state of mind（情绪；心境）；(always with an adjective（总是与形容词连用）；a person of the type mentioned（（某种类型的）人）

spiritual.meaning: connected with the human spirit, rather than the body or physical things（精神的；心灵的）；connected with religion（宗教的）；spir·itu·al·ly /ˈspɪrɪtʃuəli; NAmEˈspɪrɪtʃuəli/ adv. a spiritually uplifting book（陶冶性情的书）；the place where you are happiest, especially a country where you feel you belong more than in your own country because you share the ideas and attitudes of the people who live there（在精神上认同的某个地方；精神家园）

spit.meaning: to force liquid, food, etc. out of your mouth（吐，唾（唾沫、食物等））；to force saliva (= the liquid that is produced in the mouth) out of your mouth, often as a sign of anger or lack of respect（啐唾沫（常表示愤怒或鄙视））；to say sth in an angry or aggressive way（怒斥）；to make a short angry sound（（发怒时）发呼噜呼噜声）

spite.meaning: a feeling of wanting to hurt or upset sb（恶意；怨恨）；if you say that sb did sth in spite of a fact, you mean it is surprising that that fact did not prevent them from doing it（不管；尽管）；if you do sth in spite of yourself, you do it although you did not intend or expect to（不由自主地）；to deliberately annoy or upset sb（故意使烦恼；存心使苦恼）

splash.meaning: (of liquid（液体）；to fall noisily onto a surface（泼洒；哗啦哗啦地溅；劈里啪啦地落）；to make sb/sth wet by making water, mud, etc. fall on them/it（把（水、泥等）泼在 … 上，溅在 … 上；朝 … 上泼（或溅））；to move through water making drops fly everywhere（（在水中）溅着水花行走，拍打着水游）

splendid.meaning: (old-fashioned) excellent; very good（极佳的；非常好的）；very impressive; very beautiful（壮丽的；雄伟的；豪华的；华丽的）；splen·did·ly /ˈsplendɪdli; NAmEˈsplendɪdli/ adv. You all played splendidly.（你们都表现得很出色。）；(old-fashioned) (especially BrE) used to show that you approve of sth, or are pleased（（表示赞许或满意）好极了，痛快）

splendour.meaning: grand and impressive beauty（壮丽；雄伟；豪华；华丽）；the beautiful and impressive features or qualities of sth, especially a place（（尤指某地的）壮丽景色，恢弘气势）

splint.meaning: a long piece of wood or metal that is tied to a broken arm or leg to keep it still and in the right position（（固定断肢的）夹板）

splinter.meaning: a small thin sharp piece of wood, metal, glass, etc. that has broken off a larger piece（（木头、金属、玻璃等的）尖碎片，尖细条）；(of wood, glass, stone, etc.（木头、玻璃、石头等）；to break, or to make sth break, into small, thin sharp pieces（（使）裂成碎片）；(of a group of people（团体）

split.meaning: to divide, or to make a group of people divide, into smaller groups that have very different opinions（分裂，使分裂（成不同的派别））；to divide, or to make sth divide, into two or more parts（分开，使分开（成为几个部分））；to divide sth into two or more parts and share it between different people, activities, etc.（分担；分摊；分享）；to tear, or to make sth tear, along a straight line（（使）撕裂）

spoil.meaning: to change sth good into sth bad, unpleasant, useless, etc.（破坏；搞坏；糟蹋；毁掉）；to give a child everything that they ask for and not enough discipline in a way that has a bad effect on their character and behaviour（溺爱；娇惯；宠坏）；to make sb/yourself happy by doing sth special（善待；格外关照）；(of food（食物）

spoilage.meaning: the decay of food which means that it can no longer be used（（食物的）变质，腐败）

spoken.meaning: involving speaking rather than writing; expressed in speech rather than in writing（口语的；口头的；以口头形式表达的）；(following an adverb（用于副词后）；speaking in the way mentioned（说话 … 的）

spokesperson.meaning: a person who speaks on behalf of a group or an organization（发言人）

sponge.meaning: a piece of artificial or natural material that is soft and light and full of holes and can hold water easily, used for washing or cleaning（（或天然或人造、擦洗物品用的）海绵块）；artificial sponge used for filling furniture, cushions, etc.（（用以填充家具、垫子等的）人造海绵）；a simple sea creature with a light body full of holes, from which natural sponge is obtained（海绵动物）；to wash sb/yourself/sth with a wet cloth or sponge（用湿布（或海绵）擦；揩拭）

sponsor.meaning: a person or company that pays for a radio or television programme, or for a concert or sporting event, usually in return for advertising（（广播电视节目、音乐会或运动会的）赞助者，赞助商）；a person who agrees to give sb money for a charity if that person succeeds in completing a particular activity（为慈善活动捐资的人；义赛（或义演等）捐款者）；a person or company that supports sb by paying for their training or education（（培训或教育的）资助者）；a person who introduces and supports a proposal for a new law, etc.（（法案等的）倡议者，发起人，倡导者）

sponsorship.meaning: financial support from a sponsor（资助；赞助款）；the act of sponsoring sb/sth or being sponsored（资助；主办；倡议）

spontaneity.meaning: the quality of being spontaneous（自发性；自然）

spontaneous.meaning: not planned but done because you suddenly want to do it（自发的；非筹划安排的）；often doing things without planning to, because you suddenly want to do them（常心血来潮的）；(technical 术语) happening naturally, without being made to happen（自发的；自然的；自身造成的）；done naturally, without being forced or practised（自然的；非勉强的；无雕饰的）

spoon.meaning: a tool that has a handle with a shallow bowl at the end, used for stirring, serving and eating food（勺；匙；调羹）；to lift and move food with a spoon（用勺舀）

spoonful.meaning: the amount that a spoon can hold（一勺（的量））

sporadic.meaning: happening only occasionally or at intervals that are not regular（偶尔发生的；间或出现的；阵发性的；断断续续的）；spor·ad·ic·al·ly /spəˈrædɪkli; NAmEspəˈrædɪkli/ adv. She attended lectures only sporadically.（她只是偶尔听听课。）

spore.meaning: one of the very small cells that are produced by some plants and that develop into new plants（孢子）

sport.meaning: activity that you do for pleasure and that needs physical effort or skill, usually done in a special area and according to fixed rules（体育运动）；a particular form of sport（（某项）体育运动）；(AustralE, NZE) (informal) used as a friendly way of addressing sb, especially a man（（用作友好称呼，尤指对男子）朋友，老兄，哥们儿）；(formal) enjoyment or fun（乐趣；消遣；玩笑；逗乐）

sportsmanship.meaning: fair, generous and polite behaviour, especially when playing a sport or game（运动员风范，体育精神（多指体育比赛中光明磊落、有气度））

spot.meaning: a small round area that has a different colour or feels different from the surface it is on（斑点）；a small dirty mark on sth（污迹；污渍；脏点）；a small mark or lump on a person's skin, sometimes with a yellow head to it（（皮肤上的）丘疹，疱疹，粉刺；脓疱）；a particular area or place（地点；场所；处所）

spotlight.meaning: a light with a single, very bright beam that can be directed at a particular place or person（聚光灯）；the area of light that is made by a spotlight（聚光灯照亮的地方；聚光灯照明圈）；attention from newspapers, television and the public（媒体和公众的注意）；to shine a spotlight on sb/sth（用聚光灯照）

spouse.meaning: a husband or wife（配偶）；spou·sal /ˈspaʊzl; NAmEˈspaʊzl/ /ˈspaʊsl; NAmEˈspaʊsl/ adj. [only before noun] (formal) spousal consent（配偶的同意）

spout.meaning: a pipe or tube on a container, that you can pour liquid out through（（容器的）嘴）；a stream of liquid coming out of somewhere with great force（（喷出的）水柱，液体柱）；(BrE) (slang) to be/go wrong; to be spoilt or not working（弄错；搞糟；出问题；有毛病）；to send out sth, especially a liquid, in a stream with great force; to come out of sth in this way（喷出；喷射）

sprain.meaning: to injure a joint in your body, especially your wrist or ankle, by suddenly twisting it（扭伤（关节））；sprain noun a bad ankle sprain（踝关节严重扭伤）

sprawl.meaning: to sit or lie with your arms and legs spread out in a relaxed or awkward way（伸开四肢坐（或躺））；to spread in an untidy way; to cover a large area（蔓延；杂乱无序地拓展）；a large area covered with buildings that spreads from the city into the countryside in an ugly way（（城市）杂乱无序拓展的地区）；an act of spreading to cover a large area in an untidy way; sth that spreads like this（随意扩展；蔓延；蔓延物）

spray.meaning: very small drops of a liquid that are sent through the air, for example by the wind（浪花；水花；飞沫）；(especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）；a substance that is forced out of a container such as an aerosol, in very small drops（喷剂；喷雾的液体）；a device or container, for example an aerosol, that you use to apply liquid in fine drops（喷雾器）

spread.meaning: to open sth that has been folded so that it covers a larger area than before（展开；打开）；to arrange objects so that they cover a large area and can be seen easily（摊开；使散开）；to move your arms, legs, fingers, etc. far apart from each other（张开；伸开）；to affect or make sth affect, be known by, or used by more and more people（传播；散布；（使）流传）

spring.meaning: the season between winter and summer when plants begin to grow（春天；春季）；a twisted piece of metal that can be pushed, pressed or pulled but which always returns to its original shape or position afterwards（弹簧；发条）；the ability of a spring to return to its original position（弹性；弹力）；a place where water comes naturally to the surface from under the ground（泉）

springboard.meaning: a strong board that you jump on and use to help you jump high in diving and gymnastics（（跳水或体操中的）跳板）；something that helps you start an activity, especially by giving you ideas（（有助于开展某事的）基础，出发点）；spring·board springboard springboards /ˈsprɪŋbɔːd; NAmEˈsprɪŋbɔːrd/ verb [I, T] springboard~ (sth) (into sth) The company expects that this strategic move would allow it to springboard into the US market.（公司希望这次战略行动会成为公司进入美国市场的跳板。）

springtime.meaning: the season of spring（春季；春天；春令）

sprinkle.meaning: to shake small pieces of sth or drops of a liquid on sth（撒；洒；把 … 撒（或洒）在 … 上）；to include a few of sth in sth else（使某物包含少量的另一物；用 … 点缀）；(NAmE) if it sprinkles, it rains lightly（下小雨）；(especially NAmE) light rain（小雨）

sprint.meaning: to run or swim a short distance very fast（短距离快速奔跑（或游泳））；a race in which the people taking part run, swim, etc. very fast over a short distance（短跑比赛；短距离速度竞赛）；a short period of running, swimming, etc. very fast（短距离快速奔跑（或游泳等）；冲刺）

sprout.meaning: (of plants or seeds（植物或种子）；to produce new leaves or buds; to start to grow（发芽；抽芽；抽条；生长）；to appear; to develop sth, especially in large numbers（出现；（使）涌现出）；to start to grow sth; to start to grow on sb/sth（长出（某物）；（某物）长出）

spruce.meaning: an evergreen forest tree with leaves like needles（云杉）；the soft wood of the spruce, used, for example, in making paper（云杉木）；to make sb/sth/yourself clean and neat（打扮；把 … 收拾整洁）；(of people or places（人或处所）

spur.meaning: a sharp pointed object that riders sometimes wear on the heels of their boots and use to encourage their horse to go faster（马刺；靴刺）；a fact or an event that makes you want to do sth better or more quickly（鞭策；激励；刺激；鼓舞）；an area of high ground that sticks out from a mountain or hill（山嘴；尖坡；支脉）；a road or a railway/railroad track that leads from the main road or line（（公路或铁路的）支线，岔线）

spy.meaning: a person who tries to get secret information about another country, organization or person, especially sb who is employed by a government or the police（间谍；密探）；to collect secret information about another country, organization or person（从事间谍活动；搜集情报）；(literary or formal) to suddenly see or notice sb/sth（突然看见；发现）；to collect information before deciding what to do（（事先）摸清情况，窥察虚实）

squander.meaning: to waste money, time, etc. in a stupid or careless way（浪费，挥霍（金钱、时间等））

square.meaning: (geometry 几何) having four straight equal sides and four angles of 90°（正方形的；四方形的）；forming an angle of 90° exactly or approximately（成直角的；方的）；used after a unit of measurement to say that sth measures the same amount on each of four sides（（用于表示长度的单位后，表示某物四个边等长）… 见方的）；used after a number to give a measurement of area（（用于数字后表示面积）平方）

squarely.meaning: directly; not at an angle or to one side（正对着地；径直地；不偏不倚地）；directly or exactly; without confusion（直接了当；明确无误；毫不含糊地）

squash.meaning: to press sth so that it becomes soft, damaged or flat, or changes shape（压软（或挤软、压坏、压扁等）；把 … 压（或挤）变形）；to push sb/sth or yourself into a space that is too small（（使）挤进；塞入）；to stop sth from continuing; to destroy sth because it is a problem for you（打断；制止；去除；粉碎）；to move so close to sb/sth else that it is uncomfortable（（使）挤在一起）

squat.meaning: to sit on your heels with your knees bent up close to your body（蹲坐；蹲）；to live in a building or on land which is not yours, without the owner's permission（偷住，擅自占用（房子或地方））；(especially BrE) a building that people are living in without permission and without paying rent（偷住的房子）；a squatting position of the body（蹲坐；蹲）

squeak.meaning: to make a short high sound that is not very loud（短促而尖厉地叫；吱吱叫；嘎吱作响）；to speak in a very high voice, especially when you are nervous or excited（（尤指紧张或激动时）尖声说话）；to only just manage to win sth, pass a test, etc.（勉强通过；侥幸成功；险胜）；a short, high cry or sound, that is not usually very loud（短促而尖厉的叫声；吱吱声；尖叫声）

squeal.meaning: to make a long, high sound（尖声长叫；发出长而尖的声音）；to speak in a very high voice, especially when you are excited or nervous（（尤指激动或紧张时）尖声说，高声嚷着说）；(informal, disapproving) to give information, especially to the police, about sth illegal that sb has done（告密；告发）；a long high cry or sound（拖长的尖叫声；长而尖的声音）

squeeze.meaning: to press sth firmly, especially with your fingers（挤压；捏）；to get liquid out of sth by pressing or twisting it hard（（从某物中）榨出，挤出，拧出）；to force sb/sth/yourself into or through a small space（（使）挤入；挤过；塞入）；(informal) to get sth by putting pressure on sb, threatening them, etc.（向 … 勒索（或榨取）；逼迫 … 给）

squirrel.meaning: a small animal with a long thick tail and red, grey or black fur. Squirrels eat nuts and live in trees.（松鼠）；to hide or store sth so that it can be used later（储藏；贮存）

squirt.meaning: to force liquid, gas, etc. in a thin fast stream through a narrow opening; to be forced out of a narrow opening in this way（（使）喷射；喷）；to hit sb/sth with a stream of water, gas, etc.（（用 … ）向 … 喷射）；a thin, fast stream of liquid that comes out of a small opening（喷射出的一股液体）；(informal, disapproving) a word used to refer to a short, young or unimportant person that you do not like or that you find annoying（妄自尊大的年轻人；不知天高地厚的人）

stab.meaning: to push a sharp, pointed object, especially a knife, into sb, killing or injuring them（（用刀等锐器）刺，戳，捅）；to make a short, aggressive or violent movement with a finger or pointed object（（用手指或尖物）戳，捅，刺）；to do or say sth that harms sb who trusts you（在某人背后捅刀子；陷害（或中伤）信任你的人）；an act of stabbing or trying to stab sb/sth; a wound caused by stabbing（刺；戳；捅；刺（或戳、捅）的伤口）

stability.meaning: the quality or state of being steady and not changing or being disturbed in any way (= the quality of being stable)（稳定（性）；稳固（性））

stabilization.meaning: isa·tion AW /ˌsteɪbəlaɪˈzeɪʃn; NAmEˌsteɪbələˈzeɪʃn/ noun [U] economic stabilization（稳定经济的工作）

stabilize.meaning: to become or to make sth become firm, steady and unlikely to change; to make sth stable（（使）稳定，稳固）；sta·bil·iza·tion, -isa·tion AW /ˌsteɪbəlaɪˈzeɪʃn; NAmEˌsteɪbələˈzeɪʃn/ noun [U] economic stabilization（稳定经济的工作）

stabilizer.meaning: a device that keeps sth steady, especially one that stops an aircraft or a ship from rolling to one side（稳定装置；（飞机的）安定面；（船舶的）减摇装置）；small wheels that are fitted at each side of the back wheel on a child's bicycle to stop it from falling over（（儿童自行车后轮两侧的）稳定轮）；(technical 术语) a chemical that is sometimes added to food or paint to stop the various substances in it from becoming separate（稳定剂）

stable.meaning: firmly fixed; not likely to move, change or fail（稳定的；稳固的；牢固的）；(of a person（人）；calm and reasonable; not easily upset（稳重的；沉稳的；持重的）；(of a substance（物质）

stack.meaning: a pile of sth, usually neatly arranged（（通常指码放整齐的）一叠，一摞，一堆）；(informal) (especially BrE) a large number or amount of sth; a lot of sth（大量；许多；一大堆）；a tall chimney, especially on a factory（（尤指工厂的）大烟囱）；the part of a library, sometimes not open to the public, where books that are not often needed are stored（（图书馆中贮藏使用频率较低的书的）书库）

stadium.meaning: a large sports ground surrounded by rows of seats and usually other buildings（体育场；运动场）

staff.meaning: all the workers employed in an organization considered as a group（全体职工（或雇员））；(NAmE) the people who work at a school, college or university, but who do not teach students（（大、中、小学的）管理人员，行政人员）；a group of senior army officers who help a commanding officer（（军队的）全体参谋人员）；(old-fashioned or formal) a long stick used as a support when walking or climbing, as a weapon, or as a symbol of authority（拐杖；棍棒；权杖）

stag.meaning: a male deer（雄鹿）；(of a man（男子）；to go to a party without a partner（不带女伴参加聚会）

stage.meaning: a period or state that sth/sb passes through while developing or making progress（（发展或进展的）时期，阶段，状态）；a separate part that a process, etc. is divided into（段；步；步骤）；a raised area, usually in a theatre, etc. where actors, dancers, etc. perform（（多指剧场中的）舞台）；the theatre and the world of acting as a form of entertainment（戏剧；戏剧表演；戏剧界）

sticky.meaning: made of or covered in a substance that sticks to things that touch it（黏（性）的）；(of paper, labels, etc.（纸、标签等）；with glue on one side so that you can stick it to a surface（一面带黏胶的）；(of the weather（天气）

stiff.meaning: firm and difficult to bend or move（不易弯曲（或活动）的；硬的；挺的）；when a person is stiff, their muscles hurt when they move them（僵硬的；一动就疼的）；thick and almost solid; difficult to stir（稠的；难搅动的）；more difficult or severe than usual（困难的；艰难的；严厉的；激烈的）

stiffen.meaning: to make yourself or part of your body firm, straight and still, especially because you are angry or frightened（（尤指因气愤或害怕，使浑身或身体的一部分）变僵硬，变僵直，绷紧）；(of part of the body（身体的一部分）；to become, or to make sth become, difficult to bend or move（（使）难以弯曲，难以活动，发僵）；to make an attitude or idea stronger or more powerful; to become stronger（（使）变强硬，变坚定）

stifle.meaning: to prevent sth from happening; to prevent a feeling from being expressed（压制；扼杀；阻止；抑制）；to feel unable to breathe, or to make sb unable to breathe, because it is too hot and/or there is no fresh air（（使）窒息，无法自如地呼吸，感觉窒闷）；stif·ling /ˈstaɪflɪŋ; NAmEˈstaɪflɪŋ/ adj. a stifling room（闷得让人透不过气来的房间）；stif·ling·ly /ˈstaɪflɪŋli; NAmEˈstaɪflɪŋli/ adv. The room was stiflingly hot.（房间里热得人喘不上气来。）

stigma.meaning: feelings of disapproval that people have about particular illnesses or ways of behaving（耻辱；羞耻）；(biology 生) the part in the middle of a flower where pollen is received（（花的）柱头）

still.meaning: continuing until a particular point in time and not finishing（还；还是；仍然；依旧）；despite what has just been said（（虽然 … ）还是；但；不过）；used for making a comparison stronger（（加强比较级）还要，更）；even more（还有（更多））

stillness.meaning: the quality of being quiet and not moving（静止；安静；宁静）

stilt.meaning: one of a set of posts that support a building so that it is high above the ground or water（（支撑建筑物高出地面或水面的）桩子，支柱）；one of two long pieces of wood that have a step on the side that you can stand on, so that you can walk above the ground（高跷）

stimulant.meaning: a drug or substance that makes you feel more awake and gives you more energy（兴奋剂）；an event or activity that encourages more activity（有激励作用的事物）

stimulate.meaning: to make sth develop or become more active; to encourage sth（促进；激发；激励）；to make sb interested and excited about sth（刺激；使兴奋）；(technical 术语) to make a part of the body function（促进（身体某部分）的功能）；stimu·la·tion stimulation stimulations /ˌstɪmjuˈleɪʃn; NAmEˌstɪmjuˈleɪʃn/ noun [U] sensory/intellectual/sexual/visual/physical stimulation（感官/智力/性/视觉/身体刺激）

stimulus.meaning: something that helps sb/sth to develop better or more quickly（促进因素；激励因素；刺激物）；something that produces a reaction in a human, an animal or a plant（（使生物产生反应的）刺激，刺激物）

sting.meaning: (of an insect or plant（昆虫或植物）；to touch your skin or make a very small hole in it so that you feel a sharp pain（刺；蜇；叮）；to feel, or to make sb feel, a sharp pain in a part of their body（（使）感觉刺痛，感觉灼痛）；to make sb feel angry or upset（激怒；使不安）

stink.meaning: to have a strong, unpleasant smell（有臭味；有难闻的气味）；to seem very bad, unpleasant or dishonest（让人觉得很糟糕；令人厌恶；似乎有不正当行为）；to fill a place with a strong, unpleasant smell（使充满臭味（或难闻气味））；a very unpleasant smell（恶臭；难闻气味）

stipulate.meaning: to state clearly and firmly that sth must be done, or how it must be done（规定；明确要求）；stipu·la·tion stipulation stipulations /ˌstɪpjuˈleɪʃn; NAmEˌstɪpjuˈleɪʃn/ noun [C, U] The only stipulation is that the topic you choose must be related to your studies.（唯一的要求是所选的题目必须与你的研究科目有关。）

stir.meaning: to move a liquid or substance around, using a spoon or sth similar, in order to mix it thoroughly（搅动；搅和；搅拌）；to move, or to make sth move, slightly（（使）微动）；to move, or to make sb move, in order to do sth（（使）行动，活动）；to make sb excited or make them feel sth strongly（打动；激发）

stock.meaning: a supply of goods that is available for sale in a shop/store（（商店的）现货，存货，库存）；a supply of sth that is available for use（储备物；备用物；供应物）；the value of the shares in a company that have been sold（股本；资本）；a share that sb has bought in a company or business（股份；股票）

stocky.meaning: (of a person（人）；short, with a strong, solid body（矮壮的；敦实的）

stone.meaning: (often used before nouns or in compounds（常用于名词前或构成复合词）；a hard solid mineral substance that is found in the ground, often used for building（石头；石料；岩石）；(especially BrE) a small piece of rock of any shape（石块；石子）；(usually in compounds（通常构成复合词）

stony.meaning: having a lot of stones on it or in it（多石的；石头的）；showing a lack of feeling or sympathy（冷漠的；无情的；铁石心肠的）；to fail to produce the result or the effect that you hope for; to have little success（未产生预期的结果（或效果）；没有开花结果）

stool.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a seat with legs but with nothing to support your back or arms（凳子）；(medical 医) a piece of solid waste from your body（大便；粪便）

stoop.meaning: to bend your body forwards and downwards（俯身；弯腰）；to stand or walk with your head and shoulders bent forwards（（站立或行走时）弓背）；(formal) to drop your moral standards far enough to do sth bad or unpleasant（卑鄙（或堕落）到 … 地步）；to drop your moral standards to do sth bad or unpleasant（卑鄙（或堕落）到做某事）

store.meaning: a large shop that sells many different types of goods（（大型）百货商店）；(NAmE) a shop, large or small（商店；店铺）；a quantity or supply of sth that you have and use（贮存物；备用物）；goods of a particular kind or for a particular purpose（（某类或作某用途的）商品，物品）

stormy.meaning: with strong winds and heavy rain or snow（有暴风雨（或暴风雪）的）；full of strong feelings and angry arguments（群情激愤的；激烈争吵的）

story.meaning: a description of events and people that the writer or speaker has invented in order to entertain people（（虚构的）故事；小说）；an account, often spoken, of what happened to sb or of how sth happened（（真实情况的）叙述，描述）；an account of past events or of how sth has developed（对往事的叙述）；a report in a newspaper, magazine or news broadcast（新闻报道）

stout.meaning: (of a person（人）；rather fat（肥胖的；肥壮的）；strong and thick（粗壮结实的；厚实牢固的）；(formal) brave and determined（顽强的；坚毅的；不屈不挠的）

strategy.meaning: a plan that is intended to achieve a particular purpose（策略；计策；行动计划）；the process of planning sth or putting a plan into operation in a skilful way（策划；规划；部署；统筹安排）；the skill of planning the movements of armies in a battle or war; an example of doing this（战略；战略部署）

straw.meaning: stems of wheat or other grain plants that have been cut and dried. stream.meaning: a small narrow river（小河；溪）；a continuous flow of liquid or gas（流；（液）流；（气）流）；a continuous flow of people or vehicles（（人）流；（车）流）；a large number of things that happen one after the other（一连串，接二连三，源源不断（的事情））

strength.meaning: the quality of being physically strong（体力；力气；力量）；the ability that sth has to resist force or hold heavy weights without breaking or being damaged（强度）；the quality of being brave and determined in a difficult situation（毅力；坚强决心；意志力量）；the power and influence that sb/sth has（实力）

strengthen.meaning: to become stronger; to make sb/sth stronger（加强；增强；巩固）

stress.meaning: pressure or worry caused by the problems in sb's life（精神压力；心理负担；紧张）；pressure put on sth that can damage it or make it lose its shape（压力；应力）；special importance given to sth（强调；重要性）；(phonetics 语音) an extra force used when pronouncing a particular word or syllable（重音；重读）

stretch.meaning: to make sth longer, wider or looser, for example by pulling it; to become longer, etc. in this way（拉长；拽宽；撑大；抻松）；(of cloth（织物）；to become bigger or longer when you pull it and return to its original shape when you stop（有弹性（或弹力））；to pull sth so that it is smooth and tight（拉紧；拉直；绷紧）

strew.meaning: to cover a surface with things（把 … 布满（或散布在）；在 … 上布满（或散播））；to be spread or lying over a surface（布满；撒满；散播在 … 上）

strict.meaning: that must be obeyed exactly（严格的（指必须恪守））；demanding that rules, especially rules about behaviour, should be obeyed（要求严格的；严厉的）；obeying the rules of a particular religion, belief, etc. exactly（恪守教规（或信条等）的）；very exact and clearly defined（严密的；严谨的；精确的）

stringent.meaning: (of a law, rule, regulation, etc.（法律、规则、规章等）；very strict and that must be obeyed（严格的；严厉的）；(of financial conditions（财政状况）；difficult and very strictly controlled because there is not much money（紧缩的；短缺的；银根紧的）

strip.meaning: to take off all or most of your clothes or another person's clothes（脱光衣服；脱掉大部分衣服；扒光 … 的衣服）；to take off your clothes as a form of entertainment; to perform a striptease（进行脱衣表演；表演脱衣舞）；to remove a layer from sth, especially so that it is completely exposed（除去，剥去（一层）；（尤指）剥光）；to remove all the things from a place and leave it empty（从（某处）拿走所有东西；使（某处）空无一物）

stripe.meaning: a long narrow line of colour, that is a different colour from the areas next to it（条纹；线条）；a narrow piece of cloth, often in the shape of a V, that is worn on the uniform of a soldier or police officer to show their rank（（军装或警服上表示等级的）条，杠）；(especially NAmE) a type, category or opinion（种类；类型；观点）

striped.meaning: marked with a pattern of stripes（有条纹的）

strive.meaning: to try very hard to achieve sth（努力；奋斗；力争；力求）；striv·ing /straɪvɪŋ; NAmEstraɪvɪŋ/ noun [U, sing.] our striving for perfection（我们争取完善的努力）

stroke.meaning: an act of hitting a ball, for example with a bat or racket（击球（动作））；a single movement of the arm when hitting sb/sth（（打、击等的）一下，一击）；any of a series of repeated movements in swimming or rowing（划水动作；划桨动作）；(often in compounds（常构成复合词）

stroll.meaning: to walk somewhere in a slow relaxed way（散步；遛达；闲逛）；a slow relaxed walk（散步；遛达；闲逛）

strong.meaning: (of people, animals, etc.（人、动物等）；having a lot of physical power so that you can lift heavy weights, do hard physical work, etc.（强壮的；强健的）；(of a natural or physical force（自然力或物理力）；having great power（强的；强劲的）

stronghold.meaning: an area in which there is a lot of support for a particular belief or group of people, especially a political party（有广泛支持的地方；势力强大的地方）；a castle or a place that is strongly built and difficult to attack（堡垒；要塞；据点）；an area where there are a large number of a particular type of animal（（某种动物的）主要栖息地）

structural.meaning: connected with the way in which sth is built or organized（结构（或构造）上的）；struc·tur·al·ly AW /ˈstrʌktʃərəli; NAmEˈstrʌktʃərəli/ adv. The building is structurally sound.（这座房子结构完好。）

structure.meaning: the way in which the parts of sth are connected together, arranged or organized; a particular arrangement of parts（结构；构造）；a thing that is made of several parts, especially a building（结构体；（尤指）建筑物）；the state of being well organized or planned with all the parts linked together; a careful plan（精心组织；周密安排；体系）；to arrange or organize sth into a system or pattern（使形成体系；系统安排；精心组织）

struggle.meaning: to try very hard to do sth when it is difficult or when there are a lot of problems（奋斗；努力；争取）；to move somewhere or do sth with difficulty（艰难地行进；吃力地进行）；to fight against sb/sth in order to prevent a bad situation or result（斗争；抗争）；to fight sb or try to get away from them（搏斗；扭打；挣扎脱身）

stud.meaning: a small piece of jewellery with a part that is pushed through a hole in your ear, nose, etc.（钉状首饰；耳钉；鼻钉）；a small round piece of metal that is attached to the surface of sth, especially for decoration（（尤指装饰用的）饰钉，嵌钉）；(BrE) one of several small metal or plastic objects that are fixed to the bottom part of a football boot or running shoe（（足球鞋或跑鞋上的）鞋钉）；a small metal object used in the past for fastening a collar onto a shirt（领扣）

stuffy.meaning: (of a building, room, etc.（建筑物、房间等）；warm in an unpleasant way and without enough fresh air（闷热的；闷人的；通风不畅的）；(informal, disapproving) very serious, formal, boring or old-fashioned（一本正经的；古板的；无聊的；保守的）；(especially NAmE) if you have a stuffy nose, your nose is blocked because you have a cold（（鼻子）不通的，堵住的；鼻塞的）

stump.meaning: the bottom part of a tree left in the ground after the rest has fallen or been cut down（树墩；树桩）；the end of sth or the part that is left after the main part has been cut, broken off or worn away（残余部分；残根；残段）；the short part of sb's leg or arm that is left after the rest has been cut off（残肢）；(in cricket（板球）

stun.meaning: to make a person or an animal unconscious for a short time, especially by hitting them on the head（使昏迷；（尤指）打昏）；to surprise or shock sb so much that they cannot think clearly or speak（使震惊（或惊愕、目瞪口呆））；to impress sb very much（给（某人）以深刻印象；使深深感动）；stunned /; NAmE/ adj. stupid.meaning: showing a lack of thought or good judgement（欠考虑的；糊涂的）；(of a person（人）；slow to learn or understand things; not clever or intelligent（笨的；傻的；脑子不好使的）；(informal) used to emphasize that you are annoyed with sb/sth（（用以加强语气）讨厌的，恼人的）

sturdy.meaning: (of an object（物品）；strong and not easily damaged（结实的；坚固的）；(of people and animals, or their bodies（人、动物或身体）；physically strong and healthy（强壮的；健壮的）

sty.meaning: an infection of the eyelid (= the skin above or below the eye) which makes it red and sore（麦粒肿；睑腺炎）

subdue.meaning: to bring sb/sth under control, especially by using force（制伏；征服；控制）；to calm or control your feelings（抑制，压制，克制（感情））

subject.meaning: a thing or person that is being discussed, described or dealt with（主题；题目；话题；题材；问题）；an area of knowledge studied in a school, college, etc.（学科；科目；课程）；a person or thing that is the main feature of a picture or photograph, or that a work of art is based on（表现对象；绘画（或拍摄）题材）；a person or thing being used to study sth, especially in an experiment（接受试验者；实验对象）

submit.meaning: to give a document, proposal, etc. to sb in authority so that they can study or consider it（提交，呈递（文件、建议等））；(formal) to accept the authority, control or greater strength of sb/sth; to agree to sth because of this（顺从；屈服；投降；不得已接受）；(law 律 or formal) to say or suggest sth（表示；认为；主张；建议）

subscription.meaning: an amount of money you pay, usually once a year, to receive regular copies of a newspaper or magazine, etc; the act of paying this money（（报刊等的）订阅费，订购款，订阅，订购）；(BrE) a sum of money that you pay regularly to a charity, or to be a member of a club or to receive a service; the act of paying this money（（向慈善机构的）定期捐款；（俱乐部的）会员费；（服务的）用户费；会员费（或服务费）的交纳）；the act of people paying money for sth to be done（集体资助；集体捐助）

subsequent.meaning: happening or coming after sth else（随后；后来；之后；接后）

subside.meaning: to become calmer or quieter（趋于平静；平息；减弱；消退）；(of water（水）；to go back to a normal level（回落；减退）；(of land or a building（地面或建筑物）

subsidiary.meaning: connected with sth but less important than it（辅助的；附带的；次要的）；(of a business company（公司）；owned or controlled by another company（附属的；隶属的）；a business company that is owned or controlled by another larger company（附属公司；子公司）

subsist.meaning: to manage to stay alive, especially with limited food or money（（尤指靠有限的食物或钱）维持生活，度日）；(formal) to exist; to be valid（存在；有效）

substantial.meaning: large in amount, value or importance（大量的；价值巨大的；重大的）；(formal) large and solid; strongly built（大而坚固的；结实的；牢固的）

substantive.meaning: (formal) dealing with real, important or serious matters（实质性的；本质上的；重大的；严肃认真的）；(old-fashioned) (grammar 语法) a noun（名词）

substitute.meaning: a person or thing that you use or have instead of the one you normally use or have（代替者；代替物；代用品）；a player who replaces another player in a sports game（替补（运动员））；to take the place of sb/sth else; to use sb/sth instead of sb/sth else（（以 … ）代替；取代）；sub·sti·tu·tion AW substitution substitutions /ˌsʌbstɪˈtjuːʃn; NAmEˈsʌbstɪˈtuːʃn/ noun [U, C] the substitution of low-fat spreads for butter（用低脂的面包抹酱代替黄油）

substrate.meaning: a substance or layer which is under sth or on which sth happens, for example the surface on which a living thing grows and feeds（底层；基底；基层）

subtle.meaning: (often approving) not very noticeable or obvious（不易察觉的；不明显的；微妙的）；(of a person or their behaviour（人或其行为）；behaving in a clever way, and using indirect methods, in order to achieve sth（机智的；机巧的；狡猾的）；organized in a clever way（巧妙的）

subtlety.meaning: the quality of being subtle（细微；微妙；狡猾；巧妙；敏锐）；the small but important details or aspects of sth（细小但重要的地方；微妙之处）

subtract.meaning: to take a number or an amount away from another number or amount（减；减去）

subtropical.meaning: in or connected with regions that are near tropical parts of the world（亚热带的；副热带的）

suburb.meaning: an area where people live that is outside the centre of a city（郊区；城外）

suburban.meaning: in or connected with a suburb（郊区的；城外的）；(disapproving) boring and ordinary（平淡乏味的；呆板的）

suburbia.meaning: the suburbs and the way of life, attitudes, etc. of the people who live there（郊区及其居民的生活方式（或态度等））

subway.meaning: (NAmE) an underground railway/railroad system in a city（地下铁道；地铁交通）；(BrE) a path that goes under a road, etc. which people can use to cross to the other side（（穿越马路等的）地下人行道）

succeed.meaning: to achieve sth that you have been trying to do or get; to have the result or effect that was intended（达到目的；实现目标；办到；做成）；to be successful in your job, earning money, power, respect, etc.（成功；有成就；有作为）；to come next after sb/sth and take their/its place or position（接替；继任；随后出现）；to gain the right to a title, property, etc. when sb dies（继承）

success.meaning: the fact that you have achieved sth that you want and have been trying to do or get; the fact of becoming rich or famous or of getting a high social position（成功；胜利；发财；成名）；a person or thing that has achieved a good result and been successful（成功的人（或事物））

successful.meaning: achieving your aims or what was intended（达到目的的；有成效的）；having become popular and/or made a lot of money（获得成功的；有成就的）；suc·cess·ful·ly ★ /səkˈsesfəli; NAmEsəkˈsesfəli/ adv. SYNONYMS 同义词辨析successfulprofitable ◇ commercial ◇ lucrative ◇ economicThese words all describe sb/sth that is making or is likely to make money.（以上各词均指赚钱的、赢利的、有利可图的。）

succession.meaning: a number of people or things that follow each other in time or order（一连串；一系列；连续的人（或事物））；the regular pattern of one thing following another thing（交替；更迭）；the act of taking over an official position or title; the right to take over an official position or title, especially to become the king or queen of a country（继承；继任；（尤指王位的）继承权）

successive.meaning: following immediately one after the other（连续的；接连的；相继的）；suc·ces·sively AW /səkˈsesɪvli; NAmEsəkˈsesɪvli/ adv. This concept has been applied successively to painting, architecture and sculpture.（这一概念相继应用于绘画、建筑和雕塑中。）

successor.meaning: a person or thing that comes after sb/sth else and takes their/its place（接替者；继任者；接替的事物；后继的事物）

succinct.meaning: expressed clearly and in a few words（简明的；言简意赅的）；suc·cinct·ly /səkˈsɪŋktli; NAmEsəkˈsɪŋktli/ adv. You put that very succinctly.（你说得十分简明扼要。）

succulent.meaning: (of fruit, vegetables and meat（水果、蔬菜和肉）；containing a lot of juice and tasting good（汁多味美的）；(of plants（植物）；having leaves and stems that are thick and contain a lot of water（肉质的；多汁的）

succumb.meaning: to not be able to fight an attack, an illness, a temptation, etc.（屈服；屈从；抵挡不住（攻击、疾病、诱惑等））

such.meaning: of the type already mentioned（（指上文）这样的，那样的，类似的）；of the type that you are just going to mention（（指后文）这样的，那样的，下述一类的）；used to emphasize the great degree of sth（（强调程度）这样，非常，如此程度）；and similar things or people（诸如此类的事物（或人））

suck.meaning: to take liquid, air, etc. into your mouth by using the muscles of your lips（吮吸；吸；咂；啜）；to keep sth in your mouth and pull on it with your lips and tongue（含在嘴里吸食）；to take liquid, air, etc. out of sth（抽吸；抽取）；to pull sb/sth with great force in a particular direction（（以巨大的力量）吸，吸引，使卷入）

sudden.meaning: happening or done quickly and unexpectedly（突然的；忽然的；骤然的）；sud·den·ness /; NAmE/ noun [U] IDM ˌall of a ˈsudden quickly and unexpectedly（突然；猛地）

suddenly.meaning: quickly and unexpectedly（突然；忽然；猛地；骤然）

sue.meaning: to make a claim against sb in court about sth that they have said or done to harm you（控告；提起诉讼）；(formal) to formally ask for sth, especially in court（（尤指在法庭上）提出请求）

suffer.meaning: to be badly affected by a disease, pain, sadness, a lack of sth, etc.（（因疾病、痛苦、悲伤等）受苦，受难，受折磨）；to experience sth unpleasant, such as injury, defeat or loss（遭受；蒙受）；to become worse（变差；变糟）；to have very little patience with people that you think are stupid（不愿迁就笨人；不能容忍愚蠢者）

suffering.meaning: physical or mental pain（疼痛；痛苦；折磨；苦难）；feelings of pain and unhappiness（痛苦；苦恼）

suffice.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to be enough for sb/sth（足够；足以）；used to suggest that although you could say more, what you do say will be enough to explain what you mean（无须多说；只需说 … 就够了）

sufficiency.meaning: (formal) an amount of sth that is enough for a particular purpose（足量；充足）

sufficient.meaning: enough for a particular purpose; as much as you need（足够的；充足的）；suf·fi·cient·ly ★ AW /səˈfɪʃntli; NAmEsəˈfɪʃntli/ adv. The following day she felt sufficiently well to go to work.（第二天，她感觉好转，完全可以去上班了。）

suffix.meaning: a letter or group of letters added to the end of a word to make another word, such as -ly in quickly or -ness in sadness（后缀，词尾（加在词尾，用以构成新词，如 quickly 中的 -ly 或 sadness 中的 -ness））

sugar.meaning: a sweet substance, often in the form of white or brown crystals, made from the juices of various plants, used in cooking or to make tea, coffee, etc. sweeter（食糖）；the amount of sugar that a small spoon can hold or that is contained in a small cube, added to tea, coffee, etc.（一匙糖；一块方糖）；(technical 术语) any of various sweet substances that are found naturally in plants, fruit, etc.（（植物、水果等所含的）糖）；(informal) (especially NAmE) a way of addressing sb that you like or love（（爱称）宝贝儿，亲爱的）

suggest.meaning: to put forward an idea or a plan for other people to think about（建议；提议）；to tell sb about a suitable person, thing, method, etc. for a particular job or purpose（推荐；举荐）；to put an idea into sb's mind; to make sb think that sth is true（使想到；使认为；表明）；to state sth indirectly（暗示；言下之意是说）

suggestion.meaning: an idea or a plan that you mention for sb else to think about（建议；提议）；a reason to think that sth, especially sth bad, is true（使人作（尤其是不好的事情的）推测的理由）；a slight amount or sign of sth（微量；些微；迹象）；putting an idea into people's minds by connecting it with other ideas（暗示；联想）

suggestive.meaning: reminding you of sth or making you think about sth（使人想起 … 的；引起联想的）；making people think about sex（性暗示的；性挑逗的）；sug·gest·ive·ly /; NAmE/ adv. He leered suggestively.（他色迷迷地斜瞟一眼。）

suicide.meaning: the act of killing yourself deliberately（自杀）；a course of action that is likely to ruin your career, position in society, etc.（自杀性行为；自毁；自取灭亡的行为）；(formal) a person who commits suicide（自杀者）

suit.meaning: a set of clothes made of the same cloth, including a jacket and trousers/pants or a skirt（西服；西装；套装）；a set of clothing worn for a particular activity（（从事特定活动时穿的）成套服装）；any of the four sets that form a pack/deck of cards（（扑克牌中）所有同花色的牌）；(informal) a person with an important job as a manager in a company or organization, especially one thought of as being mainly concerned with financial matters or as having a lot of influence（（具影响力的）高级行政人员（尤指财务方面的））

suitable.meaning: right or appropriate for a particular purpose or occasion（合适的；适宜的；适当的；适用的）；suit·abil·ity /ˌsuːtəˈbɪləti; ˌsjuːtəˈbɪləti; NAmEˌsuːtəˈbɪləti/ noun [U] There is no doubt about her suitability for the job.（毫无疑问，她适合做这个工作。）

suitably.meaning: in a way that is right or appropriate for a particular purpose or occasion（合适地；适宜地；适当地）；showing the feelings, etc. that you would expect in a particular situation（如你所料地；自然）

suitcase.meaning: a case with flat sides and a handle, used for carrying clothes, etc. when you are travelling（（旅行用的）行李箱，手提箱）

suite.meaning: a set of rooms, especially in a hotel（（尤指旅馆的）一套房间，套房）；a set of matching pieces of furniture（一套家具）；a piece of music made up of three or more related parts, for example pieces from an opera（组曲（由三个或更多相关部分组成））；(computing 计) a set of related computer programs（套；套装软件）

suited.meaning: right or appropriate for sb/sth（合适；适宜；适当）；if two people are suited or well suited, they are likely to make a good couple（般配的）；wearing a suit, or a suit of the type mentioned（穿西装的；穿 … 套装的）

sullen.meaning: bad-tempered and not speaking, either on a particular occasion or because it is part of your character（面有愠色的；闷闷不乐的；郁郁寡欢的）；(of the sky or weather（天空或天气）；dark and unpleasant（阴沉的）

sully.meaning: to spoil or reduce the value of sth（败坏；有损于）；to make sth dirty（弄脏；玷污）

sulphide.meaning: a compound of sulphur and another chemical element（硫化物）

sulphur.meaning: a chemical element. Sulphur is a pale yellow substance that produces a strong unpleasant smell when it burns and is used in medicine and industry.（硫；硫磺）；sul·phur·ous (BrE) (US sul·fur·ous) /ˈsʌlfərəs; NAmEˈsʌlfərəs/ adj. sulphurous fumes（燃烧硫磺产生的烟雾）

sultry.meaning: (of the weather or air（天气或空气）；very hot and uncomfortable（闷热的）；(of a woman or her appearance（女子或其外表）；sexually attractive; seeming to have strong sexual feelings（姿色迷人的；风情万种的；性感的）

sum.meaning: an amount of money（金额；款项）；the number you get when you add two or more numbers together（和；总和；总数）；all of sth, especially when you think that it is not very much（全部，一切（尤指数量不大））；a simple problem that involves calculating numbers（算术；（数字的）简单计算）

summarize.meaning: to give a summary of sth (= a statement of the main points)（总结；概括；概述）

summary.meaning: a short statement that gives only the main points of sth, not the details（总结；概括；概要）；(formal) giving only the main points of sth, not the details（总结性的；概括的；概要的）；(sometimes disapproving) done immediately, without paying attention to the normal process that should be followed（从速从简的；即决的；草草的）；sum·mar·ily /ˈsʌmərəli; NAmEsəˈmerəli/ adv. to be summarily dismissed/executed（被草草开除/处决）

summer.meaning: the warmest season of the year, coming between spring and autumn/fall（夏天；夏季）

summertime.meaning: the season of summer（夏季；夏天；夏令）

summit.meaning: the highest point of sth, especially the top of a mountain（最高点；顶点；山顶）；an official meeting or series of meetings between the leaders of two or more governments at which they discuss important matters（（政府间的）首脑会议；峰会）

summon.meaning: (formal) to order sb to appear in court（传唤，传讯（出庭））；(formal) to order sb to come to you（召唤）；(formal) to arrange an official meeting（召集，召开（会议））；(formal) to call for or try to obtain sth（吁求；请求；争取）

sumptuous.meaning: very expensive and looking very impressive（华贵的；豪华的；奢华的）

sun.meaning: the star that shines in the sky during the day and gives the earth heat and light（太阳；日）；the light and heat from the sun（太阳的光和热；阳光；日光）；(technical 术语) any star around which planets move（恒星）；used to emphasize that you are talking about a very large number of things（（强调事物数量很大）天下，世上，全世界）

sunburn.meaning: the condition of having painful red skin because you have spent too much time in the sun（晒斑；晒伤）

sunburst.meaning: an occasion when the sun appears from behind the clouds and sends out bright streams of light（云开日出；阳光突现）

sunday.meaning: the day of the week after Saturday and before Monday, thought of as either the first or the last day of the week（星期日；星期天）；(BrE) (informal) a newspaper published on a Sunday（每逢星期日出版的报纸；星期日报）；(informal, humorous) your best clothes（自己最好的衣服）

sundial.meaning: a device used outdoors, especially in the past, for telling the time when the sun is shining. A pointed piece of metal throws a shadow on a flat surface that is marked with the hours like a clock, and the shadow moves around as the sun moves across the sky.（日规；日晷）

sun-dried.meaning: (especially of food（尤指食物）；dried naturally by the heat of the sun（晒干的）

sunflower.meaning: a very tall plant with large yellow flowers, grown in gardens or for its seeds and their oil that are used in cooking（向日葵；葵花）

sunlight.meaning: the light from the sun（阳光；日光）

sunlit.meaning: receiving light from the sun（阳光照耀的）

sunny.meaning: with a lot of bright light from the sun（阳光充足的）；cheerful and happy（欢乐的；快乐的）

sunrise.meaning: the time when the sun first appears in the sky in the morning（日出）；the colours in the part of the sky where the sun first appears in the morning（朝霞）

sunset.meaning: the time when the sun goes down and night begins（日落；傍晚）；the colours in the part of the sky where the sun slowly goes down in the evening（晚霞）；a fixed period of time after which a law or the effect of a law will end（（法律的）自动废止期，效力消减期）；used to describe a colour that is like one of the colours in a sunset（霞红色的；浅橘红色的）

sunshine.meaning: the light and heat of the sun（阳光；日光）；(informal) happiness（欢乐；幸福）；(BrE) (informal) used for addressing sb in a friendly, or sometimes a rude way（（友好地称呼某人，有时显得不礼貌）朋友，老兄）

super.meaning: (informal, becoming old-fashioned) extremely good（顶好的；超级的；顶呱呱的）；(informal) especially; particularly（特别；格外）；(BrE) (informal) a superintendent in the police（（英国的）警官；（美国的）警长）；(NAmE) a superintendent of a building（（大楼的）管理人）

superb.meaning: excellent; of very good quality（极佳的；卓越的；质量极高的）；su·perb·ly /; NAmE/ adv. a superbly illustrated book（一部配有精美插图的书）

supercontinent.meaning: any of the very large areas of land, for example Gondwana or Laurasia, that existed millions of years ago（超大陆（存在于几百万年之前，如冈瓦纳古陆或劳亚古陆））

superficial.meaning: (often disapproving) not studying or looking at sth thoroughly; seeing only what is obvious（粗略的；肤浅的；粗枝大叶的；浅薄的）；appearing to be true, real or important until you look at it more carefully（表面的；外面的；外表的）；(of a wound or damage（伤口或损坏）；only affecting the surface and therefore not serious（表层的；表皮的）

superfluous.meaning: more than you need or want（过剩的；过多的；多余的）

superintend.meaning: (formal) to be in charge of sth and make sure that everything is working, being done, etc. as it should be（主管；监督；监管）

superintendent.meaning: a person who has a lot of authority and manages and controls an activity, a place, a group of workers, etc.（主管人；负责人；监管人；监督人）；(in Britain（英国）；a police officer just above the rank of chief inspector（中级警官，警司（官阶仅高于巡长））；(in the US（美国）

superior.meaning: better in quality than sb/sth else; greater than sb/sth else（（在品质上）更好的；占优势的；更胜一筹的）；higher in rank, importance or position（（在级别、重要性或职位上）更高的）；(disapproving) showing by your behaviour that you think you are better than others（有优越感的；高傲的）；(used especially in advertisements（尤用于广告）

superiority.meaning: the state or quality of being better, more skilful, more powerful, greater, etc. than others（优越（性）；优势）；behaviour that shows that you think you are better than other people（优越感；神气活现的样子；盛气凌人的行为）

supermarket.meaning: a large shop/store that sells food, drinks and goods used in the home. People choose what they want from the shelves and pay for it as they leave.（超级市场；超市）

supermodel.meaning: a very famous and highly paid fashion model（超级名模）

supernatural.meaning: that cannot be explained by the laws of science and that seems to involve gods or magic（超自然的；神奇的；神灵魔怪的）；events, forces or powers that cannot be explained by the laws of science and that seem to involve gods or magic（超自然物；超自然力量；神奇怪异的事）

supersede.meaning: to take the place of sth/sb that is considered to be old-fashioned or no longer the best available（取代，替代（已非最佳选择或已过时的事物））

supersonic.meaning: faster than the speed of sound（超音速的；超声速的）

superstition.meaning: the belief that particular events happen in a way that cannot be explained by reason or science; the belief that particular events bring good or bad luck（迷信；迷信观念（或思想））

superstitious.meaning: believing in superstitions（迷信的；有迷信观念的）

superstructure.meaning: a structure that is built on top of sth, for example the upper parts of a ship or the part of a building above the ground（（船舶的）上层结构；（建筑物的）上部结构）；(formal) the systems and beliefs in a society that have developed from more simple ones（（社会的）上层建筑）

supervise.meaning: to be in charge of sb/sth and make sure that everything is done correctly, safely, etc.（监督；管理；指导；主管）；super·vi·sion supervision supervisions /ˌsuːpəˈvɪʒn; ˌsjuːpəˈvɪʒn; NAmEˌsuːpərˈvɪʒn/ noun [U, C] Very young children should not be left to play without supervision.（不能让幼儿在没人照看的情况下独自玩耍。）

supervisor.meaning: a person who supervises sb/sth（监督人；指导者；主管人）；super·vis·ory /ˌsuːpəˈvaɪzəri; ˌsjuːpəˈvaɪzəri; NAmEˌsuːpərˈvaɪzəri/ adj. She has a supervisory role on the project.（她负责这个项目的监督工作。）

supper.meaning: the last meal of the day, either a main meal, usually smaller and less formal than dinner, or a snack eaten before you go to bed（晚饭；晚餐；夜宵）

supplant.meaning: (formal) to take the place of sb/sth (especially sb/sth older or less modern)（取代，替代（尤指年老者或落后于时代的事物））

supplement.meaning: a thing that is added to sth else to improve or complete it（增补（物）；补充（物）；添加物）；an extra separate section, often in the form of a magazine, that is sold with a newspaper（（报纸的）增刊）；a book or a section at the end of a book that gives extra information or deals with a special subject（（书籍的）补编，补遗，附录）；(BrE) an amount of money that you pay for an extra service or item, especially in addition to the basic cost of a holiday/vacation（额外费用，附加费（尤指度假服务的））

supplementary.meaning: provided in addition to sth else in order to improve or complete it（增补性的；补充性的；额外的；外加的）

supplier.meaning: a person or company that supplies goods（供应者；供货商；供货方）

supply.meaning: an amount of sth that is provided or available to be used（供应量；供给量；储备）；the things such as food, medicines, fuel, etc. that are needed by a group of people, for example an army or expedition（（军队或探险队等的）补给，补给品）；the act of supplying sth（供应；供给；提供；补给）；to provide sb/sth with sth that they need or want, especially in large quantities（（尤指大量）供应，供给，提供）

support.meaning: to help or encourage sb/sth by saying or showing that you agree with them/it（支持；拥护；鼓励）；to give or be ready to give help to sb if they need it（帮助；援助）；to help or encourage sth to be successful by giving it money（资助；赞助）；to provide everything necessary, especially money, so that sb/sth can live or exist（养活；赡养；扶养；维持）

supporter.meaning: a person who supports a political party, an idea, etc.（支持者；拥护者）；(BrE) a person who supports a particular sports team（（运动队的）支持者）

supportive.meaning: giving help, encouragement or sympathy to sb（给予帮助的；支持的；鼓励的；同情的）

suppose.meaning: to think or believe that sth is true or possible (based on the knowledge that you have)（（根据所知）认为，推断，料想）；to pretend that sth is true; to imagine what would happen if sth were true（假定；假设；设想）；used to make a statement, request or suggestion less direct or less strong（（婉转表达）我看，要我说，要不）；to be expected or required to do/be sth according to a rule, a custom, an arrangement, etc.（（按规定、习惯、安排等）应当，应，该，须）

supposedly.meaning: according to what is generally thought or believed but not known for certain（据信；据传；据说）

supposing.meaning: used to ask sb to pretend that sth is true or to imagine that sth will happen（假定；假设；设想）

supposition.meaning: an idea that you think is true although you may not be able to prove it（推测的想法；推断的结论）；the act of believing or claiming that sth is true even though it cannot be proved（推测；推断）

suppress.meaning: (of a government, ruler, etc.（政府、统治者等）；to put an end, often by force, to a group or an activity that is believed to threaten authority（镇压；（武力）平定；压制）；(usually disapproving) to prevent sth from being published or made known（禁止（发表）；查禁；封锁）；to prevent yourself from having or expressing a feeling or an emotion（抑制；控制；忍住）

suppression.meaning: the act of suppressing sth（镇压；压制；抑制）

supremacy.meaning: a position in which you have more power, authority or status than anyone else（至高无上；最大权力；最高权威；最高地位）

supreme.meaning: highest in rank or position（（级别或地位）最高的，至高无上的）；very great or the greatest in degree（（程度）很大的，最大的）

surcharge.meaning: an extra amount of money that you must pay in addition to the usual price（额外费用；附加费；增收费）；to make sb pay a surcharge（向（某人）收取额外费用）

sure.meaning: confident that you know sth or that you are right（确信；确知；肯定；有把握）；certain that you will receive sth or that sth will happen（一定，必定，无疑（将会得到或发生））；certain to do sth or to happen（一定，必定，无疑（会做或会发生））；that can be trusted or relied on（不容置疑的；确切的；可靠的；保险的）

surely.meaning: used to show that you are almost certain of what you are saying and want other people to agree with you（（对自己的话很有把握，希望他人同意）想必）；used with a negative to show that sth surprises you and you do not want to believe it（（用于否定句，表示难以置信））；(formal) without doubt; certainly（无疑；必定）；(old-fashioned) (NAmE informal) used to say ‘yes’ to sb or to agree to sth（（表示肯定或同意）当然）

surf.meaning: large waves in the sea or ocean, and the white foam that they produce as they fall on the beach, on rocks, etc.（激浪；拍岸浪花）；to take part in the sport of riding on waves on a surfboard（进行冲浪运动；冲浪）；to use the Internet（（互联网上）冲浪，漫游，浏览）

surface.meaning: the outside or top layer of sth（表面；表层；面）；the top layer of an area of water or land（水面；地面；液面）；the flat upper part of a piece of furniture, that is used for working on（（家具的）顶面，操作台）；the outer appearance of a person, thing or situation; the qualities that you see or notice, that are not hidden（表面；外表；外观）

surfing.meaning: the sport of riding on waves while standing on a narrow board called a surfboard（冲浪运动）；the activity of looking at different things on the Internet in order to find sth interesting, or of changing between TV channels in order to find an interesting programme（（互联网上）冲浪，漫游，浏览；来回转换电视频道（以寻找有趣节目））

surge.meaning: to move quickly and with force in a particular direction（涌；汹涌；涌动）；to fill sb with a strong feeling（使强烈地感到）；(of prices, profits, etc.（物价、利润等）；to suddenly increase in value（急剧上升；飞涨；激增）

surgeon.meaning: a doctor who is trained to perform surgery (= medical operations that involve cutting open a person's body)（外科医生）

surgery.meaning: medical treatment of injuries or diseases that involves cutting open a person's body and often removing or replacing some parts; the branch of medicine connected with this treatment（外科手术；外科学）；In American English the countable form can be used.（美式英语可用可数形式）；(BrE) the time during which a doctor, dentist or vet is available to see patients（应诊时间）；a place where a doctor, dentist or vet sees patients（诊室；门诊处）

surgical.meaning: used in or connected with surgery（外科的；外科手术的）；sur·gi·cal·ly /ˈsɜːdʒɪkli; NAmEˈsɜːrdʒɪkli/ adv. The lumps will need to be surgically removed.（这些肿块需手术切除。）

surmise.meaning: (formal) to guess or suppose sth using the evidence you have, without definitely knowing（推测；猜测）；(formal) a guess based on some facts that you know already（推测；猜测）

surmount.meaning: to deal successfully with a difficulty（克服；解决）；to be placed on top of sth（处于（某物）上面；置于（某物）顶端）

surname.meaning: a name shared by all the members of a family (written last in English names)（姓）

surpass.meaning: (formal) to do or be better than sb/sth（超过；胜过；优于）

surplus.meaning: an amount that is extra or more than you need（过剩；剩余；过剩量；剩余额）；the amount by which the amount of money received is greater than the amount of money spent（盈余；顺差）；more than is needed or used（过剩的；剩余的；多余的）

surprise.meaning: an event, a piece of news, etc. that is unexpected or that happens suddenly（意想不到（或突然）的事；令人惊奇的事（或消息等））；a feeling caused by sth happening suddenly or unexpectedly（惊奇；惊讶；意外）；the use of methods that cause feelings of surprise（出人意表的做事方式；出奇制胜的策略）；(ironic, often disapproving) used to show that sth is not a surprise to you, as you could easily have predicted that it would happen or be true（（认为不足为怪时说）这有什么好奇怪的）

surprised.meaning: feeling or showing surprise（惊奇的；惊讶的；觉得奇怪的；感觉意外的）

surprising.meaning: causing surprise（令人吃惊的；使人惊奇的；出人意料的；奇怪的）；sur·pris·ing·ly ★ /səˈpraɪzɪŋli; NAmEsərˈpraɪzɪŋli/ adv. She looked surprisingly well.（她看上去身体出奇地好。）

surrender.meaning: to admit that you have been defeated and want to stop fighting; to allow yourself to be caught, taken prisoner, etc.（投降）；(formal) to give up sth/sb when you are forced to（（被迫）放弃，交出）；(formal) to stop trying to prevent yourself from having a feeling, habit, etc. and allow it to control what you do（听任（感情、习惯等）摆布（或发展））；an act of admitting that you have been defeated and want to stop fighting（投降）

surround.meaning: to be all around sth/sb（围绕；环绕）；to move into position all around sb/sth, especially so as to prevent them from escaping; to move sb/sth into position in this way（包围；围住）；to be closely connected with sth/sb（与 … 紧密相关；围绕）；to choose to have particular people or things near you all the time（喜欢结交（某类人）；喜欢身边总有（某类东西））

surrounding.meaning: that is near or around sth（周围的；附近的）

surroundings.meaning: everything that is around or near sb/sth（环境）

survey.meaning: an investigation of the opinions, behaviour, etc. of a particular group of people, which is usually done by asking them questions（民意调查；民意测验）；the act of examining and recording the measurements, features, etc. of an area of land in order to make a map or plan of it（测量；勘测；测绘）；(BrE) an examination of the condition of a house, etc., usually done for sb who is thinking of buying it（（尤指为欲购房者所做的）房屋鉴定）；a general study, view or description of sth（总体研究；全面评述；概述）

surveyor.meaning: a person whose job is to examine and record the details of a piece of land（（土地）测量员，勘测员）；a person whose job is to examine a building to make sure it is in good condition, usually done for sb who is thinking of buying it（（建筑物）鉴定人）；(BrE) an official whose job is to check that sth is accurate, of good quality, etc.（检验员；检验官）

survival.meaning: the state of continuing to live or exist, often despite difficulty or danger（生存；存活；幸存）；something that has continued to exist from an earlier time（残存物；幸存事物）；the principle that only the people or things that are best adapted to their surroundings will continue to exist（适者生存）

survive.meaning: to continue to live or exist（生存；存活；继续存在）；to continue to live or exist despite a dangerous event or time（幸存；幸免于难；渡过难关）；to live or exist longer than sb/sth（比 … 活（或存在）的时间长）

survivor.meaning: a person who continues to live, especially despite being nearly killed or experiencing great danger or difficulty（幸存者；生还者；挺过困难者）

susceptible.meaning: very likely to be influenced, harmed or affected by sb/sth（易受影响（或伤害等）；敏感；过敏）；easily influenced by feelings and emotions（好动感情的；感情丰富的；善感的）；(formal) allowing sth; capable of sth（容许 … 的；可能 … 的；可以 … 的）

suspect.meaning: to have an idea that sth is probably true or likely to happen, especially sth bad, but without having definite proof（疑有，觉得（尤指坏事可能属实或发生））；to have an idea that sb is guilty of sth, without having definite proof（怀疑（某人有罪））；to be suspicious about sth; to not trust sth（怀疑；感觉有问题；不信任）；sus·pected adj. a suspected broken arm（怀疑骨折的胳膊）

suspend.meaning: (formal) to hang sth from sth else（悬；挂；吊）；to officially stop sth for a time; to prevent sth from being active, used, etc. for a time（暂停；中止；使暂停发挥作用（或使用等））；to officially delay sth; to arrange for sth to happen later than planned（延缓；暂缓；推迟）；to officially prevent sb from doing their job, going to school, etc. for a time（使暂时停职（或停学等））

suspender.meaning: a short circle of elastic for holding up a sock or stocking（吊袜带）；long narrow pieces of cloth, leather, etc. for holding trousers/pants up. They are fastened to the top of the trousers/pants at the front and back and passed over the shoulders.（吊裤带；背带）

suspense.meaning: a feeling of worry or excitement that you have when you feel that sth is going to happen, sb is going to tell you some news, etc.（（对即将发生的事等的）担心；焦虑；兴奋；悬念）
