suspension.meaning: the act of officially removing sb from their job, school, team, etc. for a period of time, usually as a punishment（暂令停职（或停学、停赛等））；the act of delaying sth for a period of time, until a decision has been taken（暂缓；推迟；延期）；the system by which a vehicle is supported on its wheels and which makes it more comfortable to ride in when the road surface is not even（（车辆减震用的）悬架）；(technical 术语) a liquid with very small pieces of solid matter floating in it; the state of such a liquid（悬浮液；悬浮）

suspicion.meaning: a feeling that sb has done sth wrong, illegal or dishonest, even though you have no proof（怀疑；嫌疑）；a feeling or belief that sth is true, even though you have no proof（感觉；看法）；the feeling that you cannot trust sb/sth（猜疑；怀疑；不放心）；(formal) a small amount of sth（少许；一点儿）

suspicious.meaning: feeling that sb has done sth wrong, illegal or dishonest, without having any proof（感觉可疑的；怀疑的）；making you feel that sth is wrong, illegal or dishonest（令人怀疑的；可疑的）；not willing or able to trust sb/sth（不信任的；持怀疑态度的）

sustain.meaning: to provide enough of what sb/sth needs in order to live or exist（维持（生命、生存））；to make sth continue for some time without becoming less（使保持；使稳定持续）；(formal) to experience sth bad（遭受；蒙受；经受）；to provide evidence to support an opinion, a theory, etc.（证明；证实）

sustainable.meaning: involving the use of natural products and energy in a way that does not harm the environment（（对自然资源和能源的利用）不破坏生态平衡的，合理利用的）；that can continue or be continued for a long time（可持续的）

sustenance.meaning: the food and drink that people, animals and plants need to live and stay healthy（食物；营养；养料）；the process of making sth continue to exist（维持；保持）

swallow.meaning: to make food, drink, etc. go down your throat into your stomach（吞下；咽下）；to move the muscles of your throat as if you were swallowing sth, especially because you are nervous（（由于紧张等）做吞咽动作）；to take sb/sth in or completely cover it so that they cannot be seen or no longer exist separately（吞没；淹没；侵吞）；to use up sth completely, especially an amount of money（用尽，耗尽，花光（钱等））

swamp.meaning: an area of ground that is very wet or covered with water and in which plants, trees, etc. are growing（沼泽（地））；swampy swampy swampier swampiest /; NAmE/ adj. swampy ground（沼泽地）；to make sb have more of sth than they can deal with（使不堪承受；使疲于应对；使应接不暇）；to fill or cover sth with a lot of water（淹；淹没）

swan.meaning: a large bird that is usually white and has a long thin neck. Swans live on or near water.（天鹅）；(BrE) (informal, disapproving) to go around enjoying yourself in a way that annoys other people or makes them jealous（悠游；悠然闲逛）

swarm.meaning: a large group of insects, especially bees, moving together in the same direction（一大群（蜜蜂等昆虫））；a large group of people, especially when they are all moving quickly in the same direction（一大群，一大批（向同方向移动的人））；(of people, animals, etc.（人、动物等）；to move around in a large group（成群地来回移动）

sway.meaning: to move slowly from side to side; to move sth in this way（（使）摇摆，摇动）；to persuade sb to believe sth or do sth（说服；使相信；使动摇）；a movement from side to side（摇摆；摆动）；(literary) power or influence over sb（统治；势力；支配；控制；影响）

swear.meaning: to use rude or offensive language, usually because you are angry（咒骂；诅咒；说脏话）；to make a serious promise to do sth（郑重承诺；发誓要；表示决心要）；to promise that you are telling the truth（赌咒发誓地说；肯定地说）；to make a public or official promise, especially in court（（尤指在法庭上）发誓，郑重承诺）

swearing.meaning: rude or offensive language（诅咒语；骂人的话；脏话）

sweat.meaning: drops of liquid that appear on the surface of your skin when you are hot, ill/sick or afraid（汗）；the state of being covered with sweat（出汗；流汗；一身汗）；hard work or effort（繁重的工作；艰苦的劳动；累活儿；艰苦努力）；(informal) (especially NAmE) a sweatsuit or sweatpants（运动服；运动裤）

sweater.meaning: a knitted piece of clothing made of wool or cotton for the upper part of the body, with long sleeves. In British English the word is used to describe a piece of clothing with no buttons. In American English a sweater can have buttons and be like a jacket.（毛衣，线衣（英式英语指套头无扣的；美式英语可指开襟有扣的））

sweatshop.meaning: a place where people work for low wages in poor conditions（血汗工厂，血汗工场（工资低廉、劳动条件恶劣））

sweaty.meaning: covered or damp with sweat（满是汗的；汗津津的；汗水湿透的）；making you become hot and covered with sweat（热得让人出汗的）

swede.meaning: a large round yellow root vegetable（大头菜）

sweep.meaning: to clean a room, surface, etc. using a broom (= a type of brush on a long handle)（扫；打扫；清扫）；to remove sth from a surface using a brush, your hand, etc.（扫去；清除）；to move or push sb/sth suddenly and with a lot of force（（迅猛地）推送，吹走，冲走，带走）；(of weather, fire, etc.（风、雨、雪、火等）

sweet.meaning: containing, or tasting as if it contains, a lot of sugar（含糖的；甜的）；having a pleasant smell（香的；芳香的；芬芳的）；having a pleasant sound（悦耳的；好听的）；pleasant and not containing any harmful substances（纯净的；清新的；新鲜的）

sweeten.meaning: to make food or drinks taste sweeter by adding sugar, etc.（使变甜；加糖于）；(informal) to try to make sb more willing to help you, agree to sth, etc. by giving them money, praising them, etc.（讨好；拉拢；哄；收买；恭维）；to make sth more pleasant or acceptable（使令人愉快；使更合心意；改善；缓和）

sweetheart.meaning: (informal) used to address sb in a way that shows affection（（用作称呼语）亲爱的，宝贝儿）；(becoming old-fashioned) a person with whom sb is having a romantic relationship（恋人；爱人；心上人）

sweetness.meaning: the quality of being pleasant（令人愉快；讨人喜欢）；the quality of tasting or smelling sweet（甜；芬芳）；(of a person（人）；to be pleasant, friendly and polite（和蔼可亲；温文尔雅）

swell.meaning: to become bigger or rounder（膨胀；肿胀）；to curve out or make sth curve out（（使）凸出，鼓出）；to increase or make sth increase in number or size（（使）增加，增大，扩大）；(of a sound（声音）

swelling.meaning: the condition of being larger or rounder than normal (= of being swollen)（膨胀；肿胀）；a place on your body that has become larger or rounder than normal as the result of an illness or injury（肿胀处；浮肿处）

swerve.meaning: (especially of a vehicle（尤指车辆等）；to change direction suddenly, especially in order to avoid hitting sb/sth（突然转向；急转弯）

swift.meaning: happening or done quickly and immediately; doing sth quickly（迅即发生的；马上做出的；迅速的）；moving very quickly; able to move very quickly（速度快的；敏捷的；矫健的）；swift·ly /swɪftli; NAmEswɪftli/ adv. She moved swiftly to the rescue.（她迅速赶来营救。）；swift·ness /swɪftnəs; NAmEswɪftnəs/ noun [U, sing.] noun a small bird with long narrow wings, similar to a swallow（雨燕）

swim.meaning: (of a person（人）；to move through water in a horizontal position using the arms and legs（游水；游泳）；to spend time swimming for pleasure（游泳（作为娱乐））；(of a fish, etc.（鱼等）

swimmer.meaning: a person who can swim; a person who is swimming（会游泳者；游泳者）

swimming.meaning: the sport or activity of swimming（游泳；游泳运动）

swing.meaning: to move backwards or forwards or from side to side while hanging from a fixed point; to make sth do this（（使）摆动，摇摆，摇荡）；to move from one place to another by holding sth that is fixed and pulling yourself along, up, etc.（纵身跃向；荡向；悬吊到）；to move or make sth move with a wide curved movement（（使）弧线运动，转弯，转动）；to turn or change direction suddenly; to make sth do this（（使）突然转向，突然转身）

swipe.meaning: to hit or try to hit sb/sth with your hand or an object by swinging your arm（挥拳打；扬起巴掌打；挥起（物体）击打）；(informal) to steal sth（偷窃）；to pass a plastic card, such as a credit card, through a special machine that is able to read the information that is stored on it（刷（磁卡））；an act of hitting or trying to hit sb/sth by swinging your arm or sth that you are holding（抡打；挥击）

swirl.meaning: to move around quickly in a circle; to make sth do this（（使）打旋，旋动，起漩涡）；the movement of sth that twists and turns in different directions and at different speeds（打旋；旋动；漩涡）；a pattern or an object that twists in circles（螺旋形；漩涡状（物体））

swiss.meaning: from or connected with Switzerland（瑞士的）；a person from Switzerland（瑞士人）

switch.meaning: a small device that you press or move up and down in order to turn a light or piece of electrical equipment on and off（（电路的）开关，闸，转换器）；a change from one thing to another, especially when this is sudden and complete（（尤指突然彻底的）改变，转变）；(NAmE) the points on a railway/railroad line（（铁路的）转辙器，道岔）；a thin stick that bends easily（（细软）枝条；鞭子）

swollen.meaning: (of a part of the body（身体的一部分）；larger than normal, especially as a result of a disease or an injury（肿胀的；肿起来的）；(of a river（河流）；containing more water than normal（涨水的；上涨的）

sword.meaning: a weapon with a long metal blade and a handle（剑；刀）；(old-fashioned or literary) to kill sb with a sword（用剑刺死某人）；(literary) a bad or unpleasant thing that might happen to you at any time and that makes you feel worried or frightened（达摩克利斯剑（喻指令人忧虑或畏惧的、随时可能降临的灾祸））；(literary) to stop fighting and return to peaceful activities（铸剑为犁；化干戈为玉帛；偃武修文）

swordfish.meaning: a large sea fish with a very long thin pointed upper jaw（箭鱼；剑鱼）

syllable.meaning: any of the units into which a word is divided, containing a vowel sound and usually one or more consonants（音节）

syllabus.meaning: a list of the topics, books, etc. that students should study in a particular subject at school or college（教学大纲）

symbiosis.meaning: (biology 生) the relationship between two different living creatures that live close together and depend on each other in particular ways, each getting particular benefits from the other（共生（关系））；a relationship between people, companies, etc. that is to the advantage of both（合作关系；互惠互利的关系）；sym·bi·ot·ic /ˌsɪmbaɪˈɒtɪk; NAmEˌsɪmbaɪˈɑːtɪk/ adj. a symbiotic relationship（一种互惠互利的关系）

symbol.meaning: a person, an object, an event, etc. that represents a more general quality or situation（象征）；a sign, number, letter, etc. that has a fixed meaning, especially in science, mathematics and music（符号；代号；记号）

symbolic.meaning: containing symbols, or being used as a symbol（使用象征的；作为象征的；象征性的）；sym·bol·ic·al·ly AW /sɪmˈbɒlɪkli; NAmEsɪmˈbɑːlɪkli/ adv. a symbolically significant gesture（有象征意义的举动）

symbolism.meaning: the use of symbols to represent ideas, especially in art and literature（（尤指文艺中的）象征主义，象征手法）；sym·bol·ist symbolist symbolists /ˈsɪmbəlɪst; NAmEˈsɪmbəlɪst/ adj., noun the symbolist poet Rimbaud（象征主义诗人兰波）

symbolize.meaning: to be a symbol of sth（象征；是 … 的象征；代表）

symmetrical.meaning: (of a body, a design, an object, etc.（身体、图案、物体等）；having two halves, parts or sides that are the same in size and shape（对称的）

symmetry.meaning: the exact match in size and shape between two halves, parts or sides of sth（对称）；the quality of being very similar or equal（相似；相仿；相等）

sympathetic.meaning: kind to sb who is hurt or sad; showing that you understand and care about their problems（同情的；有同情心的；表示同情的）；showing that you approve of sb/sth or that you share their views and are willing to support them（赞同的；支持的）；(of a person（人）；easy to like（让人喜欢的；招人喜爱的）

sympathize.meaning: to feel sorry for sb; to show that you understand and feel sorry about sb's problems（同情）；to support sb/sth（赞同；支持）

sympathy.meaning: the feeling of being sorry for sb; showing that you understand and care about sb's problems（同情）；the act of showing support for or approval of an idea, a cause, an organization, etc.（赞同；支持）；friendship and understanding between people who have similar opinions or interests（意气相投；志同道合）；happening because sth else has happened（因 … 而出现；相应发生）

symphony.meaning: a long complicated piece of music for a large orchestra, in three or four main parts (called movements )（交响乐；交响曲）；sym·phon·ic /sɪmˈfɒnɪk; NAmEsɪmˈfɑːnɪk/ adj. Mozart's symphonic works（莫扎特的交响乐作品）

symposium.meaning: a meeting at which experts have discussions about a particular subject; a small conference（专题讨论会；研讨会；小型讨论会）

symptom.meaning: a change in your body or mind that shows that you are not healthy（症状）；a sign that sth exists, especially sth bad（征候；征兆）

synchronize.meaning: to happen at the same time or to move at the same speed as sth; to make sth do this（（使）同步，在时间上一致，同速进行）

syndrome.meaning: a set of physical conditions that show you have a particular disease or medical problem（综合征；综合症状）；a set of opinions or a way of behaving that is typical of a particular type of person, attitude or social problem（典型意见；典型表现）

synonym.meaning: a word or expression that has the same or nearly the same meaning as another in the same language（同义词）

synonymous.meaning: (of words or expressions（词语）；having the same, or nearly the same, meaning（同义的）；so closely connected with sth that the two things appear to be the same（等同于 … 的）

synopsis.meaning: a summary of a piece of writing, a play, etc.（（著作、剧本等的）大纲，提要，概要，梗概）

syntax.meaning: (linguistics 语言) the way that words and phrases are put together to form sentences in a language; the rules of grammar for this（句法；句法规则）；(computing 计) the rules that state how words and phrases must be used in a computer language（句法；语构）

synthesis.meaning: the act of combining separate ideas, beliefs, styles, etc; a mixture or combination of ideas, beliefs, styles, etc.（综合；结合；综合体）；(technical 术语) the natural chemical production of a substance in animals and plants（（物质在动植物体内的）合成）；(technical 术语) the artificial production of a substance that is present naturally in animals and plants（（人工的）合成）；(technical 术语) the production of sounds, music or speech by electronic means（（用电子手段对声音、音乐或语音的）合成）

synthesize.meaning: (technical 术语) to produce a substance by means of chemical or biological processes（（通过化学手段或生物过程）合成）；to produce sounds, music or speech using electronic equipment（（音响）合成）；to combine separate ideas, beliefs, styles, etc.（综合）

synthesizer.meaning: an electronic machine for producing different sounds. Synthesizers are used as musical instruments, especially for copying the sounds of other instruments, and for copying speech sounds.（音响合成器）

synthetic.meaning: artificial; made by combining chemical substances rather than being produced naturally by plants or animals（人造的；（人工）合成的）；(of languages（语言）；using changes to the ends of words rather than separate words to show the functions of words in a sentence（综合（型）的）；syn·thet·ic·al·ly /sɪnˈθetɪkli; NAmEsɪnˈθetɪkli/ adv. noun an artificial substance or material（合成物；合成纤维（织物）；合成剂）

syrup.meaning: a sweet liquid made from sugar and water, often used in cans of fruit（糖水（罐头水果常用））；any thick sweet liquid made with sugar, used especially as a sauce（糖浆）

system.meaning: an organized set of ideas or theories or a particular way of doing sth（（思想或理论）体系；方法；制度；体制）；a group of things, pieces of equipment, etc. that are connected or work together（系统）；a human or an animal body, or a part of it, when it is being thought of as the organs and processes that make it function（身体；（器官）系统）；(informal, usually disapproving) the rules or people that control a country or an organization, especially when they seem to be unfair because you cannot change them（（尤指不公正的统治或管理）制度，体系，集团）

systematic.meaning: done according to a system or plan, in a thorough, efficient or determined way（成体系的；系统的；有条理的；有计划有步骤的）；sys·tem·at·ic·al·ly /ˌsɪstəˈmætɪkli; NAmEˌsɪstəˈmætɪkli/ adv. The search was carried out systematically.（搜查已按照部署执行。）

systematize.meaning: (formal) to arrange sth according to a system（使系统化；使成体系；使条理化）

table.meaning: a piece of furniture that consists of a flat top supported by legs（桌子；台子；几）；the people sitting at a table for a meal or to play cards, etc.（（就餐或玩牌等的）一桌人）；a list of facts or numbers arranged in a special order, usually in rows and columns（表；一览表）；a list of sports teams, countries, schools, etc. that shows their position in a competition, etc.（（竞赛等的）名次表，排名榜，积分表）

tableland.meaning: a large area of high flat land（台地；高原）

tablet.meaning: (especially BrE) a small round solid piece of medicine that you swallow（药片；片剂）；an amount of another substance in a small round solid piece（丸）；a flat piece of stone that has words written on it, especially one that has been fixed to a wall in memory of an important person or event（（固定于墙上作纪念的）牌，碑，匾）；(old-fashioned, formal) a piece of soap（一块肥皂）

taboo.meaning: a cultural or religious custom that does not allow people to do, use or talk about a particular thing as people find it offensive or embarrassing（（文化或宗教习俗方面的）禁忌，忌讳，戒律）；a general agreement not to do sth or talk about sth（禁止；避讳）；taboo adj. in the days when sex was a taboo subject（在谈性色变的时代）

tabulate.meaning: to arrange facts or figures in columns or lists so that they can be read easily（列成表格；列表显示）

tacit.meaning: that is suggested indirectly or understood, rather than said in words（心照不宣的；不言而喻的；默示的）

tack.meaning: the way in which you deal with a particular situation; the direction of your words or thoughts（方针；方法；思路）；(technical 术语) the direction that a boat with sails takes as it sails at an angle to the wind in order to fill its sails（（帆船的）抢风调向，抢风行驶）；a small nail with a sharp point and a flat head, used especially for fixing a carpet to the floor（（尤指把地毯钉在地板上的）平头钉，大头钉）；a long loose stitch used for holding pieces of cloth together temporarily, before you sew them finally（粗线脚缝；假缝）

tackle.meaning: to make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem or situation（应付，处理，解决（难题或局面））；to speak to sb about a problem or difficult situation（与某人交涉；向某人提起（问题或困难情况））；(in football (soccer), hockey, etc.（足球、曲棍球等）；to try and take the ball from an opponent（抢球；抢断；抢截；铲断）

tact.meaning: the ability to deal with difficult or embarrassing situations carefully and without doing or saying anything that will annoy or upset other people（（处事、言谈等的）老练，圆通，得体，乖巧）

tactful.meaning: careful not to say or do anything that will annoy or upset other people（圆通的；得体的；不得罪人的）；tact·ful·ly /ˈtæktfəli; NAmEˈtæktfəli/ adv. a tactfully worded reply（措辞得体的答复）

tactic.meaning: the particular method you use to achieve sth（策略；手段；招数）；the art of moving soldiers and military equipment around during a battle or war in order to use them in the most effective way（战术；兵法）

tadpole.meaning: a small creature with a large head and a small tail, that lives in water and is the young form of a frog or toad（蝌蚪）

tag.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a small piece of paper, cloth, plastic, etc. attached to sth to identify it or give information about it（标签；标牌）；a name or phrase that is used to describe a person or thing in some way（称呼；诨名）；(linguistics 语言) a word or phrase that is added to a sentence for emphasis, for example I do in Yes, I do（附加语（为加强语气，如 Yes, I do 一句中的 I do））

tail.meaning: the part that sticks out and can be moved at the back of the body of a bird, an animal or a fish（尾；尾巴）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；having the type of tail mentioned（有 … 尾巴的）；the back part of a plane, spacecraft, etc.（尾部；后部）

tailor.meaning: a person whose job is to make men's clothes, especially sb who makes suits, etc. for individual customers（（尤指为顾客个别订制男装的）裁缝）；to make or adapt sth for a particular purpose, a particular person, etc.（专门制作；订做）

taint.meaning: (formal) to damage or spoil the quality of sth or the opinion that people have of sb/sth（使腐坏；污染；玷污，败坏（名声））；taint·ed /; NAmE/ adj. tainted drinking water（污染的饮用水）；the effect of sth bad or unpleasant that spoils the quality of sb/sth（腐坏；污染；玷污）

take.meaning: to carry or move sth from one place to another（携带；拿走；取走；运走）；to go with sb from one place to another, especially to guide or lead them（带去；引领）；to make sb/sth go from one level, situation, etc. to another（使达到，把 … 推向，把 … 带到（另一个层次、层面等））；to put your hands or arms around sb/sth and hold them/it; to reach for sb/sth and hold them/it（拿；抱；握；取；接）

take-off.meaning: the moment at which an aircraft leaves the ground and starts to fly（（飞机的）起飞）；the moment when your feet leave the ground when you jump（起跳）；if you do a take-off of sb, you copy the way they speak or behave, in a humorous way to entertain people（（对他人言行的）滑稽模仿）

tale.meaning: a story created using the imagination, especially one that is full of action and adventure（（尤指充满惊险的）故事；历险记）；an exciting spoken description of an event, which may not be completely true（（精彩但不一定完全真实的）讲述，叙述）

talent.meaning: a natural ability to do sth well（天才；天资；天赋）；people or a person with a natural ability to do sth well（有才能的人；人才；天才）；(BrE) (slang) people who are sexually attractive（（统称）性感的人）

talented.meaning: having a natural ability to do sth well（有才能的；天才的；有才干的）

talk.meaning: to say things; to speak in order to give information or to express feelings, ideas, etc.（说话；讲话；谈话）；to discuss sth, usually sth serious or important（讨论，谈论，商谈，洽谈（通常指重大的事））；to say words in a language（（用某种语言）讲，说）；to say things that are/are not sensible（说，讲（有理、无理的话））

talkative.meaning: liking to talk a lot（爱多说话的；多嘴的；饶舌的；健谈的）

tall.meaning: (of a person, building, tree, etc.（人、建筑物、树木等）；having a greater than average height（高的；高大的）；used to describe or ask about the height of sb/sth（（用以表示或询问高度）有 … 高，身高）；tall·ness /tɔːlnəs; NAmEtɔːlnəs/ noun [U] IDM stand ˈtall (especially NAmE) to show that you are proud and able to deal with anything（趾高气扬；昂然挺立）

tally.meaning: a record of the number or amount of sth, especially one that you can keep adding to（记录；积分表；账）；to be the same as or to match another person's account of sth, another set of figures, etc.（（说法、数字等）与 … 符合（或一致）；吻合）；to calculate the total number, cost, etc. of sth（计算（总的数目、成本等）；合计）

tambourine.meaning: a musical instrument that has a round wooden frame, sometimes covered with plastic or skin, with metal discs around the edge. To play it you shake it or hit it with your hand.（铃鼓（蒙有塑料或皮面，鼓帮装有金属圆片，摇动或用手击打发声））

tame.meaning: (of animals, birds, etc.（动物、鸟等）；not afraid of people, and used to living with them（养驯的；驯服的）；(informal) not interesting or exciting（平淡无奇的；枯燥乏味的）；(of a person（人）

tamper.meaning: to make changes to sth without permission, especially in order to damage it（篡改，擅自改动，胡乱摆弄（尤指有意破坏））

tan.meaning: if a person or their skin tans or is tanned, they become brown as a result of spending time in the sun（（使）晒成褐色，晒黑）；to make animal skin into leather by treating it with chemicals（鞣（革）；硝（皮））；a yellowish-brown colour（棕黄色；黄褐色）；the brown colour that sb with pale skin goes when they have been in the sun（晒成棕褐肤色；晒成的棕褐色）

tang.meaning: a strong sharp taste or smell（强烈味道；刺鼻气味）；tangy tangy tangier tangiest /ˈtæŋi; NAmEˈtæŋi/ adj. a refreshing tangy lemon flavour（清新浓郁的柠檬香味）

tangible.meaning: that can be clearly seen to exist（有形的；实际的；真实的）；that you can touch and feel（可触摸的；可触知的；可感知的）

tangle.meaning: a twisted mass of threads, hair, etc. that cannot be easily separated（（线、毛发等的）缠结的一团，乱团，乱糟糟的一堆）；a state of confusion or lack of order（混乱；纷乱）；(informal) a disagreement or fight（纠纷；不和；争执；打架）；to twist sth into an untidy mass; to become twisted in this way（使缠结；纠结；乱作一团）

tank.meaning: a large container for holding liquid or gas（（贮放液体或气体的）箱，槽，罐）；the contents of a tank or the amount it will hold（箱（或桶等）所装之物；一箱（或一桶等）的量）；a military vehicle covered with strong metal and armed with guns. It can travel over very rough ground using wheels that move inside metal belts.（坦克）；(IndE) an artificial pool, lake or reservoir（（人工）水池，湖，水库）

tanker.meaning: a ship or lorry/truck that carries oil, gas or petrol/gas in large quantities（运送大量液体或气体的轮船（或卡车）；油轮；罐车；油槽车）

tannin.meaning: a yellowish or brownish substance found in the bark of some trees and the fruit of many plants, used especially in making leather, ink and wine（单宁；单宁酸；鞣质）

tantalize.meaning: to make a person or an animal want sth that they cannot have or do（（以可望而不可即之物）逗引，招惹，使干着急）；tan·tal·iz·ing, -is·ing /ˈtæntəlaɪzɪŋ; NAmEˈtæntəlaɪzɪŋ/ adj. The tantalizing aroma of fresh coffee wafted towards them.（新鲜咖啡那诱人的香味向他们飘来。）；tan·tal·iz·ing·ly, -is·ing·ly /ˈtæntəlaɪzɪŋli; NAmEˈtæntəlaɪzɪŋli/ adv. The branch was tantalizingly out of reach.（够不到那树枝，让人干着急。）

tantamount.meaning: (formal) having the same bad effect as sth else（无异于；等于；效果与 … 一样坏）

tap.meaning: to hit sb/sth quickly and lightly（轻敲；轻拍；轻叩）；if you tap your fingers, feet, etc. or they tap, you hit them gently against a table, the floor, etc., for example to the rhythm of music（（用 … ）轻轻叩击）；to make use of a source of energy, knowledge, etc. that already exists（利用，开发，发掘（已有的资源、知识等））；(especially BrE) to fit a device to a telephone so that sb's calls can be listened to secretly（（在电话上）安装窃听器，搭线窃听）

tape.meaning: a long narrow strip of magnetic material that is used for recording sounds, pictures or information（磁带；录音带；录像带）；a cassette that contains sounds, or sounds and pictures, that have been recorded（录了音的盒式磁带；录了像的盒式磁带）；a long narrow strip of material with a sticky substance on one side that is used for sticking things together（胶带；胶条）；a narrow strip of material that is used for tying things together or as a label（（捆、系物品或作标记的）狭带，带子，线带，窄布条）

tapestry.meaning: a picture or pattern that is made by weaving coloured wool onto heavy cloth; the art of doing this（壁毯；挂毯；织锦；绣帷）；tap·es·tried /; NAmE/ adj. tapestried walls（挂有绣帷的墙）

tapeworm.meaning: a long flat worm that lives in the intestines of humans and animals（绦虫）

tapir.meaning: an animal like a pig with a long nose, that lives in Central and S America and SE Asia（貘（生活在中南美洲和东南亚的长鼻猪状动物））

taproot.meaning: the main root of a plant that grows straight downwards and produces smaller side roots（（植物的）直根，主根）

tar.meaning: a thick black sticky liquid that becomes hard when cold. Tar is obtained from coal and is used especially in making roads.（焦油；焦油沥青；柏油）；a substance similar to tar that is formed by burning tobacco（（烟草点燃后产生的）烟碱，尼古丁）；to cover sth with tar（用沥青涂抹；用柏油铺）；to put tar on sb then cover them with feathers, as a punishment（把 … 浑身涂上沥青并粘上羽毛（作为惩罚）；严惩）

tare.meaning: a plant growing where you do not want it（莠草；杂草；杂生植物）

target.meaning: a result that you try to achieve（目标；指标）；an object, a person or a place that people aim at when attacking（（攻击的）目标，对象）；an object that people practise shooting at, especially a round board with circles on it（靶；靶子）；to aim an attack or a criticism at sb/sth（把 … 作为攻击目标；把 … 作为批评的对象）

tariff.meaning: a tax that is paid on goods coming into or going out of a country（关税）；a list of fixed prices that are charged by a hotel or restaurant for rooms, meals, etc., or by a company for a particular service（（旅馆、餐厅或服务公司的）价目表，收费表）；(BrE) (law 律) a level of punishment for sb who has been found guilty of a crime（量刑标准）

tarnish.meaning: if metal tarnishes or sth tarnishes it, it no longer looks bright and shiny（（使）失去光泽，暗淡）；to spoil the good opinion people have of sb/sth（玷污，败坏，损坏（名声等））；a thin layer on the surface of a metal that makes it look dull and not bright（（金属表面上的）暗锈）

task.meaning: a piece of work that sb has to do, especially a hard or unpleasant one（（尤指艰巨或令人厌烦的）任务，工作）；an activity which is designed to help achieve a particular learning goal, especially in language teaching（（尤指语言教学中旨在帮助达到某一学习目的的）活动）；to criticize sb strongly for sth they have done（严厉地责备；申斥；训斥）；(formal) to give sb a task to do（交给某人（任务）；派给某人（工作））

taste.meaning: the particular quality that different foods and drinks have that allows you to recognize them when you put them in your mouth（味道；滋味）；the sense you have that allows you to recognize different foods and drinks when you put them in your mouth（味觉）；a small quantity of food or drink that you try in order to see what it is like（少许尝的东西；一口；一点儿）；a short experience of sth（体验；尝试）

tasteful.meaning: (especially of clothes, furniture, decorations, etc.（尤指衣服、家具、装饰等）；attractive and of good quality and showing that the person who chose them can recognize good things（高雅的；雅致的；优美的）；taste·ful·ly /ˈteɪstfəli; NAmEˈteɪstfəli/ adv. The bedroom was tastefully furnished.（这卧室布置得很雅致。）

tasty.meaning: (approving) having a strong and pleasant flavour（美味的；可口的；好吃的）；(BrE) (informal, sometimes offensive) a word that some men use about women that they think are sexually attractive（风骚的，有味道的，性感的（男子用以形容性感女子））

taut.meaning: stretched tightly（拉紧的；绷紧的）；showing that you are anxious or tense（显得紧张的（或焦虑的、不安的等））；(of a person or their body（人或人体）；with firm muscles; not fat（肌肉结实的；不虚胖的）

tavern.meaning: a pub or an inn（酒馆；小旅店；客栈）

tax.meaning: money that you have to pay to the government so that it can pay for public services. People pay tax according to their income and businesses pay tax according to their profits. Tax is also often paid on goods and services.（税；税款）；to put a tax on sb/sth; to make sb pay tax（对 … 征税；课税；使纳税）；(BrE) to pay tax on a vehicle so that you may use it on the roads（缴纳车辆牌照税）；to need a great amount of physical or mental effort（使负重担；使受压力；使大伤脑筋）

taxation.meaning: money that has to be paid as taxes（税；税款；税金；税收）；the system of collecting money by taxes（税制；征税；课税）

taxi.meaning: a car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere. Taxis usually have meters which show how much money you have to pay.（出租汽车；计程车；的士）；in some places in Africa, a small bus with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere. Taxis usually have fixed routes and stop wherever passengers need to get on or off.（（非洲某些地方行走固定路线、乘客可随时上下的）小公共汽车，小巴士）；(of a plane（飞机）；to move slowly along the ground before taking off or after landing（（起飞前或降落后在地面上）滑行）

taxonomy.meaning: the scientific process of classifying things (= arranging them into groups)（分类学）；a particular system of classifying things（分类法；分类系统）

tea.meaning: the dried leaves (called tea leaves ) of the tea bush（茶叶）；a hot drink made by pouring boiling water onto tea leaves. It may be drunk with milk or lemon and/or sugar added.（（沏好的）茶）；a cup of tea（一杯茶）；the name used by some people in Britain for the cooked meal eaten in the evening, especially when it is eaten early in the evening（晚点，便餐（英国人傍晚时吃））

teach.meaning: to give lessons to students in a school, college, university, etc; to help sb learn sth by giving information about it（教（课程）；讲授；教授）；to show sb how to do sth so that they will be able to do it themselves（教；训练）；to make sb feel or think in a different way（教育；教导；使懂得（情理））；(informal) to persuade sb not to do sth again by making them suffer so much that they are afraid to do it（使引以为戒；惩戒）

teacher.meaning: a person whose job is teaching, especially in a school（教师；教员；老师；先生）

teaching.meaning: the work of a teacher（教学；授课；指导）；the ideas of a particular person or group, especially about politics, religion or society, that are taught to other people（教导；学说；教义；教诲）

teacup.meaning: a cup in which tea is served（茶杯）

team.meaning: a group of people who play a particular game or sport against another group of people（（游戏或运动的）队）；a group of people who work together at a particular job（（一起工作的）组，班）；two or more animals that are used together to pull a cart, etc.（（同拉一辆车等的）一组牲畜，联畜）；to put two or more things or people together in order to do sth or to achieve a particular effect（使互相配合；使协作；使合作）

teapot.meaning: a container with a spout, a handle and a lid, used for making and serving tea（茶壶）

tear.meaning: to damage sth by pulling it apart or into pieces or by cutting it on sth sharp; to become damaged in this way（撕裂；撕碎；扯破；戳破）；to make a hole in sth by force（撕开，划成，刺出，扯开（裂口或洞））；to remove sth from sth else by pulling it roughly or violently（拉掉；撕掉；拔掉；扯掉）；to pull yourself/sb away by force from sb/sth that is holding you or them（挣开；拽开；夺去；揪走）

tease.meaning: to laugh at sb and make jokes about them, either in a friendly way or in order to annoy or embarrass them（取笑；戏弄；揶揄；寻开心）；to annoy an animal, especially by touching it, pulling its tail, etc.（招惹，逗弄（动物））；(disapproving) to make sb sexually excited, especially when you do not intend to have sex with them（挑逗，撩拨（异性））；to pull sth gently apart into separate pieces（梳理）

technical.meaning: connected with the practical use of machinery, methods, etc. in science and industry（技术的；技能的；工艺的）；connected with the skills needed for a particular job, sport, art, etc.（专门技术的；技巧的；技艺的）；connected with a particular subject and therefore difficult to understand if you do not know about that subject（专科的；专业的）；connected with the details of a law or set of rules（诉讼程序性的；技术性的）

technician.meaning: a person whose job is keeping a particular type of equipment or machinery in good condition（技术员；技师）；a person who is very skilled at the technical aspects of an art, a sport, etc.（（艺术、体育等的）技巧精湛者，精于技巧者）

technique.meaning: a particular way of doing sth, especially one in which you have to learn special skills（技巧；技艺；工艺）；the skill with which sb is able to do sth practical（技术；技能）

technology.meaning: scientific knowledge used in practical ways in industry, for example in designing new machines（科技；工艺；工程技术；技术学；工艺学）；machinery or equipment designed using technology（技术性机器（或设备））；tech·no·logic·al AW /ˌteknəˈlɒdʒɪkl; NAmEˌteknəˈlɑːdʒɪkl/ adj. technological advances（科技进步）；tech·no·logic·al·ly AW /ˌteknəˈlɒdʒɪkli; NAmEˌteknəˈlɑːdʒɪkli/ adv. technologically advanced（技术上先进的）

tectonic.meaning: connected with the structure of the earth's surface（地壳构造的）

tedious.meaning: lasting or taking too long and not interesting（冗长的；罗嗦的；单调乏味的；令人厌烦的）

tedium.meaning: the quality of being boring（单调乏味；冗长；罗嗦）

teem.meaning: (of rain（雨）；to fall heavily（倾注；倾泻）；to be full of people, animals, etc. moving around（充满，遍布，到处都是（移动着的人、动物等））

teenager.meaning: a person who is between 13 and 19 years old（（13 至 19 岁之间的）青少年，少年，少女）

teens.meaning: the years of a person's life when they are between 13 and 19 years old（十几岁（13 至 19 岁之间））

telecommunications.meaning: the technology of sending signals, images and messages over long distances by radio, telephone, television, satellite, etc.（电信；电讯）；tele·com·mu·ni·ca·tion /ˌtelikəˌmjuːnɪˈkeɪʃn; NAmEˌtelikəˌmjuːnɪˈkeɪʃn/ (also informal tele·com /ˈtelikɒm; NAmEˈtelikɑːm/) adj. [only before noun] a telecommunication company（电信公司）

telegram.meaning: a message sent by telegraph and then printed and given to sb（电报（用电信号传递的信息））

telegraph.meaning: a method of sending messages over long distances, using wires that carry electrical signals（电报（通信方式））；to send a message by telegraph（打电报；用电报发送（电文）；电告）；to make it clear to people what you are going to do, often without intending to（（无意中）流露（思想），泄露（动机））

telephone.meaning: a system for talking to sb else over long distances, using wires or radio; a machine used for this（电话；电话系统；电话机）；the part of the telephone that you hold in your hand and speak into（电话听筒）；to be using the telephone（在打电话；在通电话）；(BrE) to have a telephone in your home or place of work（（在家里或工作单位）装有电话机的）

telescope.meaning: a piece of equipment shaped like a tube, containing lenses, that you look through to make objects that are far away appear larger and nearer（望远镜）；to become shorter, or make sth shorter, by sliding sections inside one another（（使）叠套缩短，叠缩）；to reduce sth so that it happens in less time（缩短，精简，压缩（成 … ））

telescopic.meaning: connected with or using a telescope; making things look larger as a telescope does（望远镜的；望远的；放大的）；made of sections that can slide into each other to make the object longer or shorter（可伸缩的；套叠的；套筒的）

televise.meaning: to broadcast sth on television（用电视播送）

television.meaning: a piece of electrical equipment with a screen on which you can watch programmes with moving pictures and sounds（电视机）；the programmes broadcast on television（电视节目；电视）；the system, process or business of broadcasting television programmes（电视系统；电视学；电视广播业）；being broadcast by television; appearing in a television programme（电视播放的；上电视的；在电视上露面的）

televisual.meaning: relating to or suitable for television（电视的；适于电视的）

telex.meaning: an international system of communication in which messages are typed on a special machine and sent by the telephone system（电传系统）；a message sent or received by telex（电传；用户电报）；(informal) a machine for sending and receiving messages by telex（电传机；电传收发机）；to send a message by telex（发电传；以电传发出（电文））

tell.meaning: (of a person（人）；to give information to sb by speaking or writing（告诉；告知）；(of some writing, an instrument, a sign, etc.（文章、仪器、标记等）；to give information about sth（提供（情况）；说明；显示）

teller.meaning: a person whose job is to receive and pay out money in a bank（（银行的）出纳，出纳员）；a machine that pays out money automatically（出纳机；提款机）；a person whose job is to count votes, especially in a parliament（（尤指议会投票时的）计票员）；(usually in compounds（通常构成复合词）

telling.meaning: having a strong or important effect; effective（强有力的；有明显效果的；显著的）；showing effectively what sb/sth is really like, but often without intending to（生动的；显露真实面目的，说明问题的（通常并非有意））

telltale.meaning: showing that sth exists or has happened（暴露实情的；能说明问题的）；(informal, disapproving) a child who tells an adult what another child has done wrong（向大人告另一个孩子状的小孩儿；小告密者）

tellurium.meaning: a chemical element. Tellurium is a shiny silver-white substance that breaks easily, found in sulphide ores.（碲）

temper.meaning: if sb has a temper, they become angry very easily（脾气；易怒的性情）；a short period of feeling very angry（怒气；火气；阵怒）；the way that you are feeling at a particular time（心情；情绪；性情；心境）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）

tempera.meaning: a kind of paint in which the colour is mixed with egg and water; a method of painting that uses this kind of paint（蛋彩画颜料（用颜料与鸡蛋和水调和而成）；蛋彩画法）

temperament.meaning: a person's or an animal's nature as shown in the way they behave or react to situations or people（（人或动物的）气质，性情，性格，禀性）；the tendency to get emotional and excited very easily and behave in an unreasonable way（易冲动；（性情）暴躁；喜怒无常）

temperate.meaning: (of a climate or region（气候或地区）；having a mild temperature without extremes of heat or cold（气候温和的；温带的）；(formal) behaving in a calm and controlled way（温和的；心平气和的；自我克制的）

temperature.meaning: the measurement in degrees of how hot or cold a thing or place is（温度；气温）；the measurement of how hot sb's body is（体温）；to increase/decrease the amount of excitement, emotion, etc. in a situation（升/降温；增加/减少热烈程度等）

temple.meaning: a building used for the worship of a god or gods, especially in religions other than Christianity（（尤指非基督教的）庙宇，寺院，神殿，圣堂）；each of the flat parts at the sides of the head, at the same level as the eyes and higher（太阳穴；鬓角；颞颥；颞部）

tempo.meaning: the speed or rhythm of a piece of music（（乐曲的）速度，拍子，节奏）；the speed of any movement or activity（（运动或活动的）速度，节奏）

temporal.meaning: (formal) connected with the real physical world, not spiritual matters（世间的；世俗的；现世的）；(formal) connected with or limited by time（时间的）；(anatomy 解) near the temple(s) at the side of the head（太阳穴的；颞的）

temporary.meaning: lasting or intended to last or be used only for a short time; not permanent（短暂的；暂时的；临时的）；tem·por·ar·ily ★ AW /ˈtemprərəli; NAmEˌtempəˈrerəli/ adv. We regret this service is temporarily unavailable.（我们很抱歉暂时不能提供这一服务。）

tempt.meaning: to attract sb or make sb want to do or have sth, even if they know it is wrong（引诱；诱惑）；to persuade or try to persuade sb to do sth that you want them to do, for example by offering them sth（劝诱；鼓动；怂恿；利诱）；to do sth too confidently in a way that might mean that your good luck will come to an end（玩命；冒险；鲁莽）

temptation.meaning: the desire to do or have sth that you know is bad or wrong（引诱；诱惑）；a thing that makes sb want to do or have sth that they know is bad or wrong（煽诱人的事物）

ten.meaning: (BrE) (often ironic) used to say that sb has guessed sth correctly or done sth very well（完全正确；得满分）；very probably（十之八九；非常可能）

tenable.meaning: (of a theory, an opinion, etc.（理论、想法等）；easy to defend against attack or criticism（说得过去的；站得住脚的）；(of a job, position, etc., especially in a university（尤指大学中的工作、职位等）；that can be held for a particular period of time（可保有，可保持，可担任（一段时间））

tenacious.meaning: that does not stop holding sth or give up sth easily; determined（紧握的；不松手的；坚持的）；continuing to exist, have influence, etc. for longer than you might expect（顽强的；坚忍不拔的）；ten·acious·ly /təˈneɪʃəsli; NAmEtəˈneɪʃəsli/ adv. Though seriously ill, he still clings tenaciously to life.（他虽然病情严重，但仍然顽强地活着。）；ten·acity /təˈnæsəti; NAmEtəˈnæsəti/ noun [U] They competed with skill and tenacity.（他们竞争靠的是技术和顽强意志。）

tenancy.meaning: (BrE) a period of time that you rent a house, land, etc. for（（房屋、土地等的）租用期限，租赁期限，租期）；the right to live or work in a building or on land that you rent（（房屋或土地的）租用，租赁）

tenant.meaning: a person who pays rent for the use of a room, building, land, etc. to the person who owns it（房客；租户；佃户）；to live or work in a place as a tenant（（作为租赁者）居住，工作）

tend.meaning: to be likely to do sth or to happen in a particular way because this is what often or usually happens（往往会；常常就）；to take a particular direction or often have a particular quality（趋向；走向；倾向；趋于）；to care for sb/sth（照料；照管；护理）；(NAmE) to serve customers in a store, bar, etc.（招待，侍候，照顾，照料（商店、酒吧等的顾客））

tendency.meaning: if sb/sth has a particular tendency, they are likely to behave or act in a particular way（倾向；偏好；性情）；a new custom that is starting to develop（趋势；趋向）；(BrE) a group within a larger political group, whose views are more extreme than those of the rest of the group（（政党内的）极端派别）

tender.meaning: kind, gentle and loving（和善的；温柔的；亲切的；慈爱的）；(of food（食物）；easy to bite through and cut（嫩的；柔软的）；(of part of the body（身体部位）

tendon.meaning: a strong band of tissue in the body that joins a muscle to a bone（腱）

tenement.meaning: a large building divided into flats/apartments, especially in a poor area of a city（（尤指城市贫困区的）经济公寓，廉租公寓）

tenet.meaning: one of the principles or beliefs that a theory or larger set of beliefs is based on（原则；信条；教义）

tennis.meaning: a game in which two or four players use rackets to hit a ball backwards and forwards across a net on a specially marked court（网球）

tenon.meaning: an end of a piece of wood that has been cut to fit into a mortise so that the two are held together（雄榫；凸榫；榫舌）

tenor.meaning: a man's singing voice with a range just below the lowest woman's voice; a man with a tenor voice（男高音；男高音歌手）；a musical part written for a tenor voice（男高音部）；(formal) the general character or meaning of sth（大意；要旨；要领）；(of a musical instrument（乐器）

tense.meaning: (of a person（人）；nervous or worried, and unable to relax（神经紧张的；担心的；不能松弛的）；(of a situation, an event, a period of time, etc.（形势、事件、时期等）；in which people have strong feelings such as worry, anger, etc. that often cannot be expressed openly（令人紧张的（或焦虑的、满腹愤懑的等））

tension.meaning: a situation in which people do not trust each other, or feel unfriendly towards each other, and which may cause them to attack each other（紧张局势（或关系、状况））；a situation in which the fact that there are different needs or interests causes difficulties（矛盾；对立）；a feeling of anxiety and stress that makes it impossible to relax（（情绪上的）紧张，烦躁）；the feeling of fear and excitement that is created by a writer or a film/movie director（（作家或电影导演制造的）紧张气氛）

tent.meaning: a shelter made of a large sheet of canvas, nylon, etc. that is supported by poles and ropes fixed to the ground, and is used especially for camping（帐篷；帐棚）

tentacle.meaning: a long thin part of the body of some creatures, such as squid, used for feeling or holding things, for moving or for getting food（触角；触手；触须）；(usually disapproving) the influence that a large place, organization or system has and that is hard to avoid（（大的地方、组织或系统难以避免的）影响，束缚，约束）

tentative.meaning: (of an arrangement, agreement, etc.（安排、协议等）；not definite or certain because you may want to change it later（不确定的；不肯定的；暂定的）；not behaving or done with confidence（踌躇的；犹豫不定的；不果断的）

tenth.meaning: th（第十）；each of ten equal parts of sth（十分之一）

tenuous.meaning: so weak or uncertain that it hardly exists（脆弱的；微弱的；缥缈的）；extremely thin and easily broken（纤细的；薄的；易断的）

tepee.meaning: a type of tall tent shaped like a cone, used by Native Americans in the past（（美洲印第安人旧时使用的）圆锥形帐篷）

term.meaning: a word or phrase used as the name of sth, especially one connected with a particular type of language（词语；术语；措辞）；(especially in Britain) one of the three periods in the year during which classes are held in schools, universities, etc.（学期（尤用于英国，学校一年分三个学期））；a period of time for which sth lasts; a fixed or limited time（期；期限；任期）；(formal) the end of a particular period of time, especially one for which an agreement, etc. lasts（到期；期满）

terminal.meaning: a building or set of buildings at an airport where air passengers arrive and leave（航空站；航空终点站）；a place, building or set of buildings where journeys by train, bus or boat begin or end（（火车、公共汽车或船的）终点站）；(computing 计) a piece of equipment, usually consisting of a keyboard and a screen that joins the user to a central computer system（终端；终端机）；(technical 术语) a point at which connections can be made in an electric circuit（（电路的）端子，线接头）

terminate.meaning: to end; to make sth end（（使）停止，结束，终止）；(of a bus or train（公共汽车或火车）；to end a journey/trip（到达终点站）

termination.meaning: (formal) the act of ending sth; the end of sth（结束；终止；末端；端）；(medical 医) a medical operation to end a pregnancy at an early stage（终止妊娠）

terminology.meaning: the set of technical words or expressions used in a particular subject（（某学科的）术语）；words used with particular meanings（有特别含义的用语；专门用语）

termite.meaning: an insect that lives in organized groups, mainly in hot countries. Termites do a lot of damage by eating the wood of trees and buildings.（白蚁）

tern.meaning: a bird with long pointed wings and a tail with two points that lives near the sea（燕鸥）

terrace.meaning: (BrE) (often in the names of streets（常用于街名）；a continuous row of similar houses that are joined together in one block（（相同的一排）排房，排屋）；a flat, hard area, especially outside a house or restaurant, where you can sit, eat and enjoy the sun（（尤指房屋或餐馆外的）露天平台，阳台）；(BrE) the wide steps at a football (soccer) ground where people can stand to watch the game（（足球场的）阶梯看台）

terrain.meaning: used to refer to an area of land when you are mentioning its natural features, for example, if it is rough, flat, etc.（地形；地势；地带）

terrestrial.meaning: (of animals and plants（动植物）；living on the land or on the ground, rather than in water, in trees or in the air（陆地的；陆栖的；陆生的）；connected with the planet Earth（地球的；地球上的）；(of television and broadcasting systems（电视和广播系统）

terrible.meaning: very unpleasant; making you feel very unhappy, upset or frightened（非常讨厌的；令人极不快的；可怕的）；causing great harm or injury; very serious（危害极大的；造成极大伤害的；非常严重的）；unhappy or ill/sick（不痛快；身体不舒服）；(informal) of very bad quality; very bad（劣质的；劣等的；拙劣的）

terribly.meaning: (especially BrE) very（非常；很）；very much; very badly（非常地；很厉害地）

terrific.meaning: (informal) excellent; wonderful（极好的；绝妙的；了不起的）；(informal) very large; very great（很大的；巨大的；异乎寻常的）

terrify.meaning: to make sb feel extremely frightened（使恐惧；使十分害怕；使惊吓）；ter·ri·fy·ing /; NAmE/ adj. It was a terrifying experience.（那是一次可怕的经历。）

territorial.meaning: (in Britain) a member of the Territorial Army（（英国）本土防卫义勇军士兵）

territory.meaning: land that is under the control of a particular country or ruler（领土；版图；领地）；an area that one person, group, animal, etc. considers as their own and defends against others who try to enter it（（个人、群体、动物等占据的）领域，管区，地盘）；an area of a town, country, etc. that sb has responsibility for in their work or another activity（（某人负责的）地区）；a particular type of land（（某类）地区；（某种）地方）

terror.meaning: a feeling of extreme fear（惊恐；恐惧；惊骇）；a person, situation or thing that makes you very afraid（可怕的人；恐怖的事；可怕的情况）；violent action or the threat of violent action that is intended to cause fear, usually for political purposes（（通常出于政治目的）恐怖行动，恐怖）；(informal) a person (usually a child) or an animal that causes you trouble or is difficult to control（讨厌鬼；小捣蛋）

terrorism.meaning: the use of violent action in order to achieve political aims or to force a government to act（恐怖主义）

terrorist.meaning: a person who takes part in terrorism（恐怖主义者；恐怖分子）

terse.meaning: using few words and often not seeming polite or friendly（简要的；简短生硬的）

tertiary.meaning: third in order, rank or importance（第三的；第三位的；第三级的）

terylene.meaning: a light strong artificial material, used for making clothes, etc.（涤纶；聚酯纤维）

test.meaning: an examination of sb's knowledge or ability, consisting of questions for them to answer or activities for them to perform（测验；考查）；a medical examination to discover what is wrong with you or to check the condition of your health（（医疗上的）检查，化验，检验）；an experiment to discover whether or how well sth works, or to find out more information about it（试验；测试）；a situation or an event that shows how good, strong, etc. sb/sth is（检验；考验）

testify.meaning: to make a statement that sth happened or that sth is true, especially as a witness in court（（尤指出庭）作证）；(formal) to say that you believe sth is true because you have evidence of it（证实；证明）；(especially NAmE) to express your belief in God publicly（见证（上帝的存在））；(formal) to show or be evidence that sth is true（作为某事的证明；表明；说明）

testimony.meaning: (formal) a thing that shows that sth else exists or is true（证据；证明）；a formal written or spoken statement saying what you know to be true, usually in court（证词；证言；口供）

tether.meaning: to tie an animal to a post so that it cannot move very far（拴（牲畜））；a rope or chain used to tie an animal to sth, allowing it to move around in a small area（（拴牲畜的）拴绳，拴链）

text.meaning: the main printed part of a book or magazine, not the notes, pictures, etc.（（书籍或杂志的）正文，本文（并非附注、图片等））；any form of written material（文本；文档）；the written form of a speech, a play, an article, etc.（演讲稿；剧本；文稿）；a book, play, etc., especially one studied for an exam（（尤指为了考试而学习的）课本，教科书，剧本）

textbook.meaning: a book that teaches a particular subject and that is used especially in schools and colleges（教科书；课本；教材）；used to describe sth that is done exactly as it should be done, in the best possible way（规范的；标准的）

textile.meaning: any type of cloth made by weaving or knitting（纺织品）；the industry that makes cloth（纺织业）

textual.meaning: connected with or contained in a text（文本的；篇章的）

textural.meaning: relating to texture（质地的；纹理的）

texture.meaning: the way a surface, substance or piece of cloth feels when you touch it, for example how rough, smooth, hard or soft it is（质地；手感）；the way food or drink tastes or feels in your mouth, for example whether it is rough, smooth, light, heavy, etc.（口感）；the way that different parts of a piece of music or literature are combined to create a final impression（（音乐或文学的）谐和统一感，神韵）

than.meaning: used to introduce the second part of a comparison（（用以引出比较的第二部分）比）；used for comparing amounts, numbers, distances, etc.（（比较数量、距离等）多于，小于，少于）；used in expressions showing that one thing happens straight after another（（表示一事紧跟另一事发生）就）

thank.meaning: to tell sb that you are grateful for sth（谢谢，感谢（某人）；（为某事）道谢）；used when you are saying who is responsible for sth（责怪；由 … 负责；多亏；归功于）；(formal) used to tell sb that you are annoyed and do not want them to do sth（（用以表示恼火，不让人做某事）请你 …）；used to say that you are pleased about sth（谢天谢地）

thankful.meaning: pleased about sth good that has happened, or sth bad that has not happened（感谢；感激；欣慰）

thanks.meaning: used to show that you are grateful to sb for sth they have done（（表示感激）感谢，谢谢）；a polite way of accepting sth that sb has offered you（（接受好意）好的，谢谢）；a polite way of refusing sth that sb has offered you（（婉言谢绝）不用了，谢谢）；words or actions that show that you are grateful to sb for sth（感谢；感激；谢意）

thanksgiving.meaning: a public holiday in the US (on the fourth Thursday in November) and in Canada (on the second Monday in October), originally to give thanks to God for the harvest and for health（感恩节（美国定为十一月的第四个星期四，加拿大定为十月的第二个星期一，均为公休日））；(formal) the expression of thanks to God（感恩（于上帝））

that.meaning: used for referring to a person or thing that is not near the speaker or as near to the speaker as another（（指较远的人或事物）那，那个）；used for referring to sb/sth that has already been mentioned or is already known about（（指已提到过或已知的人或事物）那，那个）；(formal) used for referring to people or things of a particular type（（特指）那，那种，那些）；used as a relative pronoun to introduce a part of a sentence which refers to the person, thing or time you have been talking about（（用作关系代词，引导从句））

thaw.meaning: (of ice and snow（冰雪）；to turn back into water after being frozen（（结冰后）解冻，融化，融解）；when it thaws or is thawing, the weather becomes warm enough to melt snow and ice（天气暖和得使冰雪融化（或解冻））；to become, or to let frozen food become, soft or liquid ready for cooking（（使冷冻食品）化冻）

the.meaning: used to refer to sb/sth that has already been mentioned or is easily understood（（指已提到或易领会到的人或事物））；used to refer to sb/sth that is the only, normal or obvious one of their kind（（指独一无二的、正常的或不言而喻的人或事物））；used when explaining which person or thing you mean（（解说时用））；used to refer to a thing in general rather than a particular example（（用以泛指））

theatre.meaning: a building or an outdoor area where plays and similar types of entertainment are performed（戏院；剧场；露天剧场）；a building in which films/movies are shown（电影院；影厅）；plays considered as entertainment（戏剧）；the work of writing, producing and acting in plays（戏剧工作；剧作；演出；上演）

theatrical.meaning: connected with the theatre（戏剧的；演剧的；剧场的）；(of behaviour（举止）；exaggerated in order to attract attention or create a particular effect（演戏似的；夸张的；戏剧性的）

theft.meaning: the crime of stealing sth from a person or place（偷；偷窃；盗窃罪）

their.meaning: of or belonging to them（他们的；她们的；它们的）；used instead of his or her to refer to a person whose sex is not mentioned or not known（（在提及性别不详的人时，用以代替 his 或 her））

theirs.meaning: (the possessive form of they（*）；of or belonging to them（他们的，她们的，它们的（所有物））

them.meaning: used when referring to people, animals or things as the object of a verb or preposition, or after the verb be（他们；她们；它们）；used instead of him or her to refer to a person whose sex is not mentioned or not known（（指性别不详的人时，用以代替 him 或 her））

theme.meaning: the subject or main idea in a talk, piece of writing or work of art（（演讲、文章或艺术作品的）题目，主题，主题思想）；(music 音) a short tune that is repeated or developed in a piece of music（（乐曲的）主题，主旋律）；(old-fashioned) (NAmE) a short piece of writing on a particular subject, done for school（（学生的）作文）；(linguistics 语言) the part of a sentence or clause that contains information that is not new to the reader or audience（（句子的）主位；词干；主题）

themselves.meaning: (the reflexive form of they（*）；used to emphasize they or a plural subject（（用以强调 they 或复数主语）他们（或她们、它们）亲自，他们（或她们、它们）本身）；used instead of himself or herself to refer to a person whose sex is not mentioned or not known（（指性别不详的人时，用以代替 himself 或 herself））；alone; without anyone else（（他们）独自，单独）

then.meaning: used to refer to a particular time in the past or future（（指过去）当时，那时；（指将来）到那时，届时）；used to introduce the next item in a series of actions, events, instructions, etc.（然后；接着；其后；后来）；used to show the logical result of a particular statement or situation（那么；因此；既然如此）；used to introduce additional information（另外；还有；再者；而且）

theoretical.meaning: concerned with the ideas and principles on which a particular subject is based, rather than with practice and experiment（理论上的）；that could possibly exist, happen or be true, although this is unlikely（理论上存在的；假设的）；the·or·etic·al·ly AW /ˌθɪəˈretɪkli; NAmEˌθiːəˈretɪkli/ adv. theoretically sound conclusions（理论上无懈可击的结论）

theorist.meaning: a person who develops ideas and principles about a particular subject in order to explain why things happen or exist（理论家；理论工作者）

theorize.meaning: to suggest facts and ideas to explain sth; to form a theory or theories about sth（从理论上说明；形成理论；理论化）

theory.meaning: a formal set of ideas that is intended to explain why sth happens or exists（学说；论；说）；the principles on which a particular subject is based（理论；原理；原则）；an opinion or idea that sb believes is true but that is not proved（（未证明的）意见；看法；推测）；used to say that a particular statement is supposed to be true but may in fact be wrong（理论上；按理说）

therapeutic.meaning: designed to help treat an illness（治疗的；医疗的；治病的）；helping you to relax（有助于放松精神的）

therapist.meaning: (especially in compounds（尤用于构成复合词）；a specialist who treats a particular type of illness or problem, or who uses a particular type of treatment（（某治疗法的）治疗专家）

therapy.meaning: the treatment of a physical problem or an illness（治疗；疗法）

there.meaning: used to show that sth exists or happens（（表示存在或发生））；in, at or to that place or position（在那里；到那里；往那里）；existing or available（存在的；现有的；可得到的）；at that point (in a story, an argument, etc.)（（故事、辩论等）在那一点上）

thereafter.meaning: after the time or event mentioned（之后；此后；以后）

thereby.meaning: used to introduce the result of the action or situation mentioned（因此；由此；从而）

therefore.meaning: used to introduce the logical result of sth that has just been mentioned（因此；所以；因而）

therefrom.meaning: from the thing mentioned（由此；从那里）

therein.meaning: in the place, object, document, etc. mentioned（在那里，在其中（指提及的地点、物体、文件等））；used to emphasize the result or consequence of a particular situation（那一点就是；那方面便是； … 就在那里）

thereof.meaning: of the thing mentioned（在其中；由此）

thereon.meaning: on the thing mentioned（以 … 为根据；由 … 而产生）

therewith.meaning: with or in the thing mentioned（与此；与之）；soon or immediately after that（随即；立即）

thermal.meaning: (technical 术语) connected with heat（热的；热量的）；(of clothing（衣服）；designed to keep you warm by preventing heat from escaping from the body（保暖的；防寒的）；(of streams, lakes, etc.（溪水、湖泊等）

thermometer.meaning: an instrument used for measuring the temperature of the air, a person's body, etc.（温度计；寒暑表；体温计）

thermostat.meaning: a device that measures and controls the temperature of a machine or room, by switching the heating or cooling system on and off as necessary（温度自动调节器；恒温器）

thesaurus.meaning: a book that lists words in groups that have similar meanings（分类词典；同义词词典）

thesis.meaning: a long piece of writing completed by a student as part of a university degree, based on their own research（论文；毕业论文；学位论文）；a statement or an opinion that is discussed in a logical way and presented with evidence in order to prove that it is true（命题；论题）

they.meaning: people, animals or things that have already been mentioned or are easily identified（他们；她们；它们）；used instead of he or she to refer to a person whose sex is not mentioned or not known（（用以代替 he 或 she，指性别不详的人））；people in general（（泛指）人们，人人，众人）；people in authority or experts（权威人士；上面（指负责人）；专家）

thick.meaning: having a larger distance between opposite sides or surfaces than other similar objects or than normal（厚的；粗的）；used to ask about or state the distance between opposite sides or surfaces（（询问或说明厚度）有 … 厚）；growing closely together in large numbers（浓密的；稠密的；茂密的）；not flowing very easily（浓的；黏稠的）

thicken.meaning: to become thicker; to make sth thicker（（使）变厚，变浓，变稠）

thickly.meaning: in a way that produces a wide piece or deep layer of sth（厚厚地）；having a lot of trees, people, etc. close together（（树木、人口等）茂密，稠密）；in a deep voice that is not as clear as normal, especially because of illness or emotion（声音不清地，沙哑地（尤指因疾病或激动））

thickness.meaning: the size of sth between opposite surfaces or sides（厚；厚度；粗）；a layer of sth（层）

thief.meaning: a person who steals sth from another person or place（贼；小偷；窃贼）

thigh.meaning: the top part of the leg between the knee and the hip（大腿；股）；the top part of the leg of a chicken, etc., cooked and eaten（食用的鸡（等的）大腿）

thimble.meaning: a small metal or plastic object that you wear on the end of your finger to protect it when sewing（顶针；针箍）

thin.meaning: having a smaller distance between opposite sides or surfaces than other similar objects or than normal（薄的；细的）；(of a person or part of the body（人或身体部位）；(sometimes disapproving) not covered with much flesh（瘦的）；not growing closely together or in large amounts（稀少的；稀疏的）

thing.meaning: an object whose name you do not use because you do not need to or want to, or because you do not know it（东西；物）；an object that is not alive in the way that people and plants are（物件；物品；事物）；(rather informal) objects, clothing or tools that belong to sb or are used for a particular purpose（（个人的）用品，衣服；（某种）用具）；used with negatives to mean ‘anything’ in order to emphasize what you are saying（任何东西（用于否定句，加强语气））

think.meaning: (not used in the progressive tenses（不用于进行时）；to have a particular idea or opinion about sth/sb; to believe sth（认为；以为）；to use your mind to consider sth, to form connected ideas, to try to solve problems, etc.（想；思考；思索；思想）；(usually used in the progressive tenses（通常用于进行时）

thinker.meaning: a person who thinks seriously, and often writes about important things, such as philosophy or science（思想家）；a person who thinks in a particular way（思想 … 的人）

thinking.meaning: the process of thinking about sth（思想；思考；思维）；ideas or opinions about sth（想法；见解）；intelligent and able to think seriously about things（思想的；有理智的；有思考力的）

thinly.meaning: in a way that produces a thin piece or layer of sth（细；瘦；薄）；with only a few things or people spread over a place so that there is a lot of space between them（稀疏；稀少）；in a way that is not sincere or enthusiastic（冷淡；冷漠）；in a way that does not hide the truth very well（容易识破的；显而易见的）

thinner.meaning: a substance that is added to paint, varnish, etc. to make it less thick（（涂料、清漆等的）稀料，稀释剂）

third.meaning: rd（第三）；used when you have failed to do sth twice and hope that you will succeed the third time（（但愿）第三次交好运；过一过二不过三）；each of three equal parts of sth（三分之一）；a level of university degree at British universities, that is lower than average（三等学位（英国大学中低于平均水平的学位））

thirdly.meaning: used to introduce the third of a list of points you want to make in a speech or piece of writing（（用于讲话或文章中列举事项）第三，第三点）

thirst.meaning: the feeling of needing or wanting a drink（口渴；干渴感）；the state of not having enough water to drink（渴；干渴）；a strong desire for sth（渴望；渴求）；(old use) to be thirsty（渴；想喝水）

thirsty.meaning: needing or wanting to drink（渴的；口渴的）；having a strong desire for sth（渴望；渴求；热望）；(of plants, fields, etc.（植物、田地等）；dry; in need of water（干旱的；缺水的）

thirteen.meaning: thir·teenth ★ /ˌθɜːˈtiːnθ; NAmEˌθɜːrˈtiːnθ/ ordinal number, noun HELP There are examples of how to use ordinal numbers at the entry for fifth.（序数词用法示例见 fifth 条。）

thirty.meaning: numbers, years or temperatures from 30 to 39（三十几；三十年代）；thir·ti·eth ★ thirtieth thirtieths /ˈθɜːtiəθ; NAmEˈθɜːrtiəθ/ ordinal number, noun HELP There are examples of how to use ordinal numbers at the entry for fifth.（序数词用法示例见 fifth 条。）；between the ages of 30 and 39（*）

this.meaning: used to refer to a particular person, thing or event that is close to you, especially compared with another（（指较近的人或事物）这，这个）；used to refer to sth/sb that has already been mentioned（（指已提到过的人或事物）这，这个）；used for introducing sb or showing sth to sb（（介绍人或展示事物时用）这，这样）；used with periods of time related to the present（（与和现在有关的一段时间连用）今，本，这个，现在）

thorn.meaning: a small sharp pointed part on the stem of some plants, such as roses（（玫瑰之类植物的）刺，棘刺）；a tree or bush that has thorns（带刺的树；荆棘）；(phonetics 语音) the letter that was used in Old English and Icelandic to represent the sounds /θ/ and /ð/ and later written as th（刺形符，字母 ð（古英语和古冰岛语用的字母，表示 /）；a person or thing that repeatedly annoys sb or stops them from doing sth（不断让人烦心的人（或事）；肉中刺；眼中钉）

thorny.meaning: causing difficulty or disagreement（棘手的；麻烦的；引起争议的）；having thorns（有刺的；多刺的）

thorough.meaning: done completely; with great attention to detail（彻底的；完全的；深入的；细致的）；(of a person（人）；doing things very carefully and with great attention to detail（仔细周到；工作缜密）；(BrE) (informal) used to emphasize how bad or annoying sb/sth is（十足的；彻头彻尾的；完完全全的）

thoroughly.meaning: very much; completely（非常；极其；彻底；完全）；completely and with great attention to detail（彻底；仔细；缜密）

though.meaning: despite the fact that（虽然；尽管；即使）；used to add a fact or an opinion that makes the previous statement less strong or less important（（用于主句后，引出补充说明，使语气变弱）不过，可是，然而）；used especially at the end of a sentence to add a fact or an opinion that makes the previous statement less strong or less important（（尤用于句末补充说明，使语气减弱）不过，可是，然而）

thought.meaning: something that you think of or remember（想法；看法；主意；记忆）；a person's mind and all the ideas that they have in it when they are thinking（心思；思想）；the power or process of thinking（思考能力；思维过程；思考；思维）；the act of thinking seriously and carefully about sth（考虑；深思）

thoughtful.meaning: quiet, because you are thinking（沉思的；深思的；思考的）；(approving) showing that you think about and care for other people（体贴的；关心别人的；关切的）；showing signs of careful thought（缜密思考过的；深思熟虑的）；thought·ful·ly /ˈθɔːtfəli; NAmEˈθɔːtfəli/ adv. Martin looked at her thoughtfully.（马丁若有所思地望着她。）

thoughtless.meaning: not caring about the possible effects of your words or actions on other people（粗心大意的；欠考虑的；轻率的）

thousand.meaning: You say a, one, two, etc. thousand without a final ‘s’ on ‘thousand’. Thousands (of … ) can be used if there is no number or quantity before it. Always use a plural verb with thousand or thousands, except when an amount of money is mentioned.（*）；(usually informal) a large number（数以千计的；成千上万的；许许多多的）；the numbers from 1 000 to 9 999（*）

thousandth.meaning: th（第一千）；each of one thousand parts of sth（千分之一）

thrash.meaning: to hit a person or an animal many times with a stick, etc. as a punishment（（作为惩罚用棍子等）抽打，连续击打）；to move or make sth move in a violent or uncontrolled way（（使）激烈扭动，翻来覆去）；(informal) (especially BrE) to defeat sb very easily in a game（（赛事中）轻易击败，一举战胜）；(informal) to discuss a situation or problem thoroughly in order to decide sth（彻底讨论，反复讨论（以便作出决定））

thread.meaning: a thin string of cotton, wool, silk, etc. used for sewing or making cloth（（棉、毛、丝等的）线）；an idea or a feature that is part of sth greater; an idea that connects the different parts of sth（线索；脉络；思绪；思路；贯穿的主线）；a long thin line of sth（线状物；细细的一条）；(computing 计) a series of connected messages on a message board on the Internet which have been sent by different people（（互联网留言板上帖子的）系列相关信息，链式消息）

threat.meaning: a statement in which you tell sb that you will punish or harm them, especially if they do not do what you want（威胁；恐吓）；the possibility of trouble, danger or disaster（坏事发生的可能）；a person or thing that is likely to cause trouble, danger, etc.（构成威胁的人；形成威胁的事物）

threaten.meaning: to say that you will cause trouble, hurt sb, etc. if you do not get what you want（扬言要；威胁；恐吓）；to seem likely to happen or cause sth unpleasant（预示凶兆；有 … 危险）；to be a danger to sth（危及；对 … 构成威胁）

threatening.meaning: expressing a threat of harm or violence（威胁的；恐吓的）；(of the sky, clouds, etc.（天空、云等）；showing that bad weather is likely（阴沉沉的；乌云密布的）；threat·en·ing·ly /ˈθretnɪŋli; NAmEˈθretnɪŋli/ adv. He glared at her threateningly.（他气势汹汹地瞪着她。）

three.meaning: (old-fashioned) reading, writing and arithmetic, thought to be the most important parts of a child's education（初等教育三要素（被视为儿童教育最重要部分的读、写、算））

three-dimensional.meaning: having, or appearing to have, length, width and depth（三维的；立体的；三度空间的；有立体感的）

thresh.meaning: to separate grains of rice, wheat, etc. from the rest of the plant using a machine or, especially in the past, by hitting it with a special tool（（用机器）使脱粒；（尤指旧时手持工具）打稻，打麦）；to make, or cause sth to make, uncontrolled movements（（使）剧烈扭动，翻滚）；thresh·ing /θreʃɪŋ; NAmEθreʃɪŋ/ noun [U] a threshing machine（脱粒机）

threshold.meaning: the floor or ground at the bottom of a doorway, considered as the entrance to a building or room（门槛；门口）；the level at which sth starts to happen or have an effect（阈；界；起始点）；the point just before a new situation, period of life, etc. begins（开端；起点；入门）

thrift.meaning: (approving) the habit of saving money and spending it carefully so that none is wasted（节约；节俭）；a wild plant with bright pink flowers that grows by the sea/ocean（海石竹（海边野生植物，花鲜艳，呈粉红色））

thrifty.meaning: careful about spending money and not wasting things（节约的；节俭的）

thrill.meaning: a strong feeling of excitement or pleasure; an experience that gives you this feeling（震颤感；兴奋感；兴奋；激动；令人兴奋的经历）；a sudden strong feeling that produces a physical effect（一阵强烈的感觉）；(informal) the excitement that is involved in dangerous activities, especially sports（（危险活动，尤指体育运动的）紧张和刺激）；to excite or please sb very much（使非常兴奋；使非常激动）

thriller.meaning: a book, play or film/movie with an exciting story, especially one about crime or spying（（尤指关于罪案或间谍的）惊险小说（或戏剧、电影））

thrive.meaning: to become, and continue to be, successful, strong, healthy, etc.（兴旺发达；繁荣；蓬勃发展；旺盛；茁壮成长）；thriv·ing /θraɪvɪŋ; NAmEθraɪvɪŋ/ adj. a thriving industry（兴盛的行业）；to enjoy sth or be successful at sth, especially sth that other people would not like（以某事为乐，因某事而有成（尤指别人不喜欢的事物））

throat.meaning: a passage in the neck through which food and air pass on their way into the body; the front part of the neck（咽喉；喉咙；颈前部）；(in adjectives（构成形容词）；having the type of throat mentioned（有 … 喉咙的；嗓子 … 的）；(of two or more people, groups, etc.（两个以上的人或群体等）

throne.meaning: a special chair used by a king or queen to sit on at ceremonies（（国王、女王的）御座，宝座）；the position of being a king or queen（王位；王权；帝位）

throng.meaning: (literary) a crowd of people（聚集的人群；一大群人）；(literary) to go somewhere or be present somewhere in large numbers（群集；拥塞；拥向）；to be full of people, cars, etc.（挤满（人、汽车等））

through.meaning: from one end or side of sth/sb to the other（从 … 一端至另一端；穿过；贯穿）；to see, hear, etc. sth from the other side of an object or a substance（透过 … 看到；隔着 … 听到）；from the beginning to the end of an activity, a situation or a period of time（自始至终；从头到尾）；past a barrier, stage or test（通过（障碍、阶段或测试）；穿过）

throughout.meaning: in or into every part of sth（各处；遍及）；during the whole period of time of sth（自始至终；贯穿整个时期）；through·out adv. The house was painted white throughout.（这所房子全都粉刷成了白色。）

throw.meaning: to send sth from your hand through the air by moving your hand or arm quickly（投；掷；抛；扔）；to put sth in a particular place quickly and carelessly（摔；丢；扔）；to move sth suddenly and with force（猛推；使劲撞）；to move your body or part of it quickly or suddenly（猛动（头、臂、腿）；挺起（胸）；仰起（头）；挥动（拳头、手臂））

thrust.meaning: to push sth/sb suddenly or violently in a particular direction; to move quickly and suddenly in a particular direction（猛推；冲；搡；挤；塞）；to make a sudden strong forward movement at sb with a weapon, etc.（刺；戳）；to refuse to listen to sb's complaints, comments, etc.（置之一旁；置之不理）；to force sb to accept or deal with sth/sb that they do not want（把 … 强加于；强迫 … 接受；强人所难）

thumb.meaning: the short thick finger at the side of the hand, slightly apart from the other four（拇指）；the part of a glove that covers the thumb（（手套的）拇指部分）；to be awkward with your hands so that you drop things or are unable to do sth（笨手笨脚；笨拙；手指不灵活）；(SAfrE) to hope that your plans will be successful or that sth will take place in the way that you want it to（希望（计划）成功；期望如愿以偿）

thumbtack.meaning: a short pin with a large round flat head, used especially for fastening paper to a board or wall（图钉）

thunder.meaning: the loud noise that you hear after a flash of lightning, during a storm（雷；雷声）；a loud noise like thunder（雷鸣般的响声；轰隆声）；when it thunders, there is a loud noise in the sky during a storm（打雷）；to make a very loud deep noise（发出雷鸣般响声；轰隆隆地响）

thunderous.meaning: very loud（雷鸣般的；声音很大的）；looking very angry（怒容满面的；面色阴沉的；怒气冲冲的）

thunderstorm.meaning: a storm with thunder and lightning and usually very heavy rain（雷雨；雷暴；雷雨交加）

thursday.meaning: the day of the week after Wednesday and before Friday（星期四）

thus.meaning: in this way; like this（以此方式；如此；这样）；as a result of sth just mentioned（因此；从而；所以）

thwart.meaning: to prevent sb from doing what they want to do（阻止；阻挠；对 … 构成阻力）

thyroid.meaning: a small organ at the front of the neck that produces hormones that control the way in which the body grows and functions（甲状腺）

tick.meaning: (of a clock, etc.（钟表等）；to make short, light, regular repeated sounds to mark time passing（发出滴答声；滴答地走时）；to put a mark (✓) next to an item on a list, an answer, etc.（标记号；打上钩；打对号）；(BrE) (informal) to do exactly the right things to please sb（投其所好；迎合众人/某人的喜好）

ticket.meaning: a printed piece of paper that gives you the right to travel on a particular bus, train, etc. or to go into a theatre, etc.（票；券；车票；戏票；入场券）；a printed piece of paper with a number or numbers on it, that you buy in order to have the chance of winning a prize if the number or numbers are later chosen（奖券；彩票）；a label that is attached to sth in a shop/store giving details of its price, size, etc.（（商店中标明货物价格、尺码等的）标签）；an official notice that orders you to pay a fine because you have done sth illegal while driving or parking your car（（交通违章）通知单，罚款单）

tickle.meaning: to move your fingers on a sensitive part of sb's body in a way that makes them laugh（呵痒；胳肢）；to produce a slightly uncomfortable feeling in a sensitive part of the body; to have a feeling like this（（使）发痒）；to amuse and interest sb（逗乐；使高兴；使感兴趣；使满足）；(informal) to be very pleased or amused（高兴极了；非常开心）

tidal.meaning: connected with tides (= the regular rise and fall of the sea)（潮汐的；有潮的）

tide.meaning: a regular rise and fall in the level of the sea, caused by the pull of the moon and sun; the flow of water that happens as the sea rises and falls（潮；潮汐；潮水）；the direction in which the opinion of a large number of people seems to be moving（潮流；趋势；动向）；a large amount of sth unpleasant that is increasing and is difficult to control（（难以控制的）恶潮，怒潮）；a feeling that you suddenly have that gets stronger and stronger（高涨的情绪）

tidy.meaning: (especially BrE) arranged neatly and with everything in order（整洁的；整齐的；井然有序的；井井有条的）；(especially BrE) keeping things neat and in order（爱整洁的；爱整齐的）；(informal) a tidy amount of money is fairly large（高额的；可观的）；tidi·ly /; NAmE/ adv. The room was very tidily arranged.（这房间布置得整整齐齐。）

tie.meaning: to attach or hold two or more things together using string, rope, etc; to fasten sb/sth with string, rope, etc.（（用线、绳等）系，拴，绑，捆，束）；to fasten sth to or around sth else（将 … 系在 … 上；束紧；系牢；捆绑）；to make a knot in a piece of string, rope, etc.（（在线、绳上）打结，系扣）；to be closed or fastened with a knot, etc.（打结系牢；系上）

tie-up.meaning: (BrE) an agreement between two companies to join together（（两家公司的）联合，合作）；(BrE) a connection between two or more things（联系；关系；关联）；(especially NAmE) a situation in which sth stops working or moving forward（停顿；停滞不前）

tiger.meaning: a large wild animal of the cat family, that has yellowish fur with black lines (= stripes) and lives in parts of Asia（虎；老虎）

tight.meaning: held or fixed in position firmly; difficult to move or undo（牢固的；紧的；不松动的；难解开的）；fitting closely to your body and sometimes uncomfortable（紧身的；紧贴的）；very strict and firm（严密的；严格的；严厉的）；stretched or pulled so that it cannot stretch much further（拉紧的；绷紧的）

tighten.meaning: to become or make sth become tight or tighter（（使）变紧，更加牢固）；to make sth become stricter（使更加严格；加强）；to spend less money because there is less available（勒紧腰带（省吃俭用））；to become stricter or more careful（变得更加严格（或小心））

tightly.meaning: closely and firmly; in a tight manner（紧紧地；牢固地；紧密地）

tile.meaning: a flat, usually square, piece of baked clay, carpet or other material that is used in rows for covering walls and floors（（贴墙或铺地用的）瓷砖，地砖，小方地毯，片状材料）；a piece of baked clay that is used in rows for covering roofs（（铺屋顶的）瓦，瓦片）；any of the small flat pieces that are used in particular board games（（棋盘游戏的）棋子）；to cover a surface with tiles（铺瓦；铺地砖；贴瓷砖）

till.meaning: (BrE) (informal) the place where you pay for goods in a large shop/store（（大商店中的）交款处，收银台）；(especially NAmE) the drawer where the money is put in a cash register（（现金出纳机的）放钱的抽屉）；(old use) to prepare and use land for growing crops（耕作；犁地）

tilt.meaning: to move, or make sth move, into a position with one side or end higher than the other（（使）倾斜，倾侧）；to make sth/sb change slightly so that one particular opinion, person, etc. is preferred or more likely to succeed than another; to change in this way（使倾向于；使向 … 倾斜；偏向）；to waste your energy attacking imaginary enemies（攻击假想敌；庸人自扰）；(BrE) to attack sb/sth in speech or writing（抨击；攻击）

timber.meaning: trees that are grown to be used in building or for making things（（用于建筑或制作物品的）树木，林木；用材林）；wood that is prepared for use in building, etc.（（建筑等用的）木材，木料）；a long heavy piece of wood used in building a house or ship（（建造房屋用的）大木料，栋木；（造船用的）肋材）；used to warn people that a tree that has been cut is about to fall（（砍伐树木时说）倒啦，小心大树倒下）

time.meaning: what is measured in minutes, hours, days, etc.（（以分钟、小时、天等计量的）时间）；the time shown on a clock in minutes and hours（（钟表所显示的）时间，钟点，时刻）；the time measured in a particular part of the world（（世界某一地区所计量的）时，时间）；the time when sth happens or when sth should happen（（某事发生或应该发生的）时间，时候）

timely.meaning: happening at exactly the right time（及时的；适时的）

timer.meaning: (often in compounds（常构成复合词）；a device that is used to measure the time that sth takes; a device that starts or stops a machine working at a particular time（时计；计时器；跑表；定时器）

timescale.meaning: the period of time that it takes for sth to happen or be completed（（事情发生或完成所需要的）一段时间，期限）

timetable.meaning: a list showing the times at which particular events will happen（时间表；时刻表）；a plan of when you expect or hope particular events to happen（预定计划；时间安排）；(especially BrE) to arrange for sth to take place at a particular time（为 … 安排时间）

timid.meaning: shy and nervous; not brave（羞怯的；胆怯的；缺乏勇气的）

timing.meaning: the act of choosing when sth happens; a particular point or period of time when sth happens or is planned（定时；时间的选择；（事情发生或计划安排的）特定时间）；the skill of doing sth at exactly the right time（时机的掌握；火候的把握）；the repeated rhythm of sth; the skill of producing this（节奏；掌握节奏的技巧）；(technical 术语) the rate at which an electric spark is produced in a vehicle's engine in order to make it work（（汽车发动机的）点火时间控制）

tin.meaning: a chemical element. Tin is a soft silver-white metal that is often mixed with other metals or used to cover them to prevent them from rusting.（锡）；a metal container in which food and drink is sold; the contents of one of these containers（罐；罐头盒；罐头）；a metal container with a lid, in the shape of a cylinder, in which paint, glue, etc. is sold and stored; the contents of one of these containers（（盛涂料、胶水等的）马口铁罐，白铁桶；罐装物）；a metal container with a lid used for keeping food in（金属食品盒）

tine.meaning: any of the points or sharp parts of, for example, a fork or the antlers of a deer（（叉子等的）尖头，尖齿；（鹿角的）分叉）

tinge.meaning: to add a small amount of colour to sth（（轻微地）给 … 着色，给 … 染色）；to add a small amount of a particular emotion or quality to sth（使略带 … 感情（或性质））；a small amount of a colour, feeling or quality（微量，少许，一丝，几分（颜色、感情或性质））

tingle.meaning: (of a part of your body（身体部位）；to feel as if a lot of small sharp points are pushing into it（感到刺痛）；to feel an emotion strongly（强烈地感到）；a slight stinging or uncomfortable feeling in a part of your body（刺痛感）

tinker.meaning: (in the past) a person who travelled from place to place, selling or repairing things（（旧时走街串巷的）小炉匠，补锅匠，白铁匠）；to make small changes to sth in order to repair or improve it, especially in a way that may not be helpful（（尤指不起作用地）小修补，小修理）

tinplate.meaning: a metal material made from iron and steel and covered with a layer of tin（镀锡铁皮；马口铁）

tint.meaning: a shade or small amount of a particular colour; a faint colour covering a surface（色调；淡色彩；（一层）淡色，浅色）；an artificial colour used to change the colour of your hair; the act of colouring the hair with a tint（染发剂；染发）；to add a small amount of colour to sth（为 … 轻微染色；给 … 略微着色）；to change the colour of sb's hair with a tint（染（发））

tiny.meaning: very small in size or amount（极小的；微小的；微量的）

tip.meaning: the thin pointed end of sth（尖端；尖儿；端）；a small part that fits on or over the end of sth（（装在顶端的）小部件）；a small piece of advice about sth practical（指点；实用的提示）；(informal) a secret or expert piece of advice about what the result of a competition, etc. is likely to be, especially about which horse is likely to win a race（（尤指有关赛马的）内幕消息，指点）

tiptoe.meaning: standing or walking on the front part of your foot, with your heels off the ground, in order to make yourself taller or to move very quietly（踮着脚；蹑手蹑脚）；to walk using the front parts of your feet only, so that other people cannot hear you（踮着脚走；蹑手蹑脚地走）

tire.meaning: to become tired and feel as if you want to sleep or rest; to make sb feel this way（（使）疲劳，疲倦，困倦）；to do sth a lot, especially in a way that annoys people（不厌其烦地做）；to become bored with sth/sb or begin to enjoy it/them less（对 … 感到厌倦；对 … 腻烦）；to make sb/yourself feel very tired（使感到筋疲力尽；使感到疲惫不堪）

tired.meaning: feeling that you would like to sleep or rest; needing rest（疲倦的；疲劳的；困倦的）；feeling that you have had enough of sb/sth because you no longer find them/it interesting or because they make you angry or unhappy（厌倦；厌烦）；boring because it is too familiar or has been used too much（陈旧的；陈腐的；陈词滥调的）；tired·ly /ˈtaɪədli; NAmEˈtaɪərdli/ adv. He shook his head tiredly.（他厌倦地摇了摇头。）

tireless.meaning: putting a lot of hard work and energy into sth over a long period of time（不知疲倦的；不觉疲劳的；精力充沛的）

tiresome.meaning: making you feel annoyed（讨厌的；令人厌烦的；烦人的）

tiring.meaning: making you feel the need to sleep or rest（令人困倦的；使人疲劳的；累人的）

tissue.meaning: a collection of cells that form the different parts of humans, animals and plants（（人、动植物细胞的）组织）；a piece of soft paper that absorbs liquids, used especially as a handkerchief（（尤指用作手帕的）纸巾，手巾纸）；very thin paper used for wrapping and packing things that break easily（（用于包装易碎物品的）薄纸，绵纸）；(literary) a story, an excuse, etc. that is full of lies（一派谎言）

titanium.meaning: a chemical element. Titanium is a silver-white metal used in making various strong light materials.（钛）
